---

EmblemWeave plays *Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave* natively on Windows, from your
own copy of the game, with no emulator. The game's machine code is recompiled
ahead of time into native PC code, and the launcher brings everything around it
together: building the game from your dump, save profiles and a save editor,
mods from GameBanana, cheats, and an in-game menu.

You supply the game from your own legally obtained copy. EmblemWeave contains no
game code, no assets and no keys, and it only ever reads your files.

> **Current status: playable.** Download the [latest release](https://github.com/XiONDiGiTaL/EmblemWeave/releases/latest),
> point it at your dump, press **Build the game** once and then **Play**. On an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT the game runs at about
> 60 fps with sound. EmblemWeave's own Rust runtime, which will take over running the game, now executes the game's code
> natively; see [Development status](#development-status) and [docs/ENGINE.md](docs/ENGINE.md).

> **AI-assisted development.** EmblemWeave is designed and directed by [XiØN](https://github.com/XiONDiGiTaL) and developed
> with the help of AI coding tools. Every change is tested against the real game and the project's own test suite before it
> is published.

## What EmblemWeave does

EmblemWeave plays *Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave* natively on Windows, built from your own dump, with no emulator. For now the game is
built and run by a bundled third-party engine in `engine/` (GPL-3.0, with its own licence and notices in that folder), while
EmblemWeave's own runtime is completed: it translates the game's code to C++ and compiles it into `fefw.exe`, which draws with
Vulkan and plays audio through XAudio2. The EmblemWeave launcher finds and
checks your dump, builds the game with the engine, keeps your saves (including imports from Switch emulators), and starts it.

EmblemWeave also has its own recompiler and runtime in Rust, used for research and verification:

| Stage | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Read** | Your extracted ExeFS, RomFS and title metadata are located and validated. |
| **Decode** | The game's executable is decompressed into its code and data segments. |
| **Recompile** | Every AArch64 instruction is decoded, functions and control flow are recovered, and the code is emitted as portable C and compiled natively. |
| **Run** | The runtime maps the game, starts it the way the console's SDK does, and serves its system calls with native implementations. |

The launcher wraps all of this in one application: it shows exactly what is
ready, what is running and where the runtime stops, and it never presents a
feature as working before it is.

## Features

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Play natively** | Build the game once from your own dump, then play it at 60 fps with sound, windowed or full screen. |
| **In-game menu** | F10 or Back + RB while playing: pause, screenshot, restart, stop and return, cheats and display settings. |
| **Saves** | Save profiles to switch between, imports from yuzu, suyu, sudachi, citron, eden and torzu, and a save editor (gold, renown, level, experience, stats, weapon masteries, items and spells). |
| **Mods** | Install RomFS mods from GameBanana (browse the game's list or paste a link), a .zip, .7z or .rar archive, or a folder, and switch each on or off. |
| **Cheats** | Quick per-unit cheats (infinite HP, quick level-up, max stats), Atmosphere cheat codes, and Cheat Engine tables with live, editable, freezable values. |
| **Launcher** | Game-data detection and validation, three colour schemes (XiØN, Arcade, FE), diagnostics, and a recompilation pipeline you can watch run. |

## Development status

Measured on the retail game (version 1.1.0, update 131072) on 10 November 2026.

**Playable through the engine.** On an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT the game runs at about 60 fps, with sound, from the launcher's
**Build the game** and **Play**. The first build takes a while (the game code is compiled and about 12,000 shaders are translated);
later builds only redo what changed.

EmblemWeave's own Rust runtime, which is being completed to replace the bundled engine ([docs/ENGINE.md](docs/ENGINE.md)):

| Area | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Instruction decoding | **99.97%** of 6,714,569 instruction words, including the Advanced SIMD (vector) unit, system registers and supervisor calls |
| Control-flow recovery | 304,909 basic blocks in 3,620 complete functions (4,000-function pass); 151 switch tables resolved |
| Emitted C verified | 400 recovered functions and 2,400 vector-instruction runs identical to the reference interpreter |
| Independent CPU check | Execution compared instruction by instruction against Unicorn (QEMU's AArch64 model) |
| Program modules | `main` plus the title's own `sdk`, loaded side by side; the C++ standard library and other library code run as the title's own code |
| Graphics | NVN device on the host GPU through Vulkan; queues, memory pools, buffers, textures (block-linear sizes, BC and ASTC formats), samplers, render state, shaders, swap chain, command buffers and the DLSS upscaler are served; draws are recorded and counted, not yet rendered |
| Input | Player 1 is a Pro Controller fed by the first XInput gamepad |
| Audio | The audio renderer opens and runs on its 5 ms clock; voices are not yet mixed to the speakers |
| Content | Content index, shader archives (`.bfsha`), texture archives (`.bntx`) and graphics presets load from RomFS |
| Own runtime | Runs the frame loop past the autosave notice and the opening movie into the first map load (27.9 billion instructions); draws are counted, not rendered |
| Native execution | The whole main module (807,604 functions, 10.6 million instructions) compiled ahead of time into one library; identical to the reference interpreter over the boot's first billion instructions, and about twice as fast |

The full compatibility matrix, the list of verified host services and the
known limitations live in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## Key capabilities

- **Static recompiler** for AArch64: integer, floating point, Advanced SIMD,
  atomics and exclusives, with an independent reference interpreter for every
  instruction.
- **Three layers of verification:** the emitted C against the interpreter, the
  vector unit against seeded edge cases (NaNs, infinities, signed zeros), and the
  interpreter against an independent CPU model.
- **Guest thread scheduler** with real blocking waits: mutexes, condition
  variables, events, timers, joins and sleeps, plus deadlock detection that names
  every waiting thread.
- **Native platform services:** the SDK's startup sequence, heap and frame-heap
  allocators, a read-only RomFS filesystem with a separate save directory, the
  musl C library (formatted I/O, parsing, a bit-exact math library), libc++
  runtime pieces, and system settings such as language and profile.
- **Native execution:** the recompiled code compiled ahead of time into one
  library, entered at any block, checked call by call against the interpreter
  (`EW_NATIVE_CHECK=1`).
- **A complete launcher** with game-data detection, save profiles and editing,
  mods and cheats, an in-game menu, a staged recompilation pipeline, diagnostics
  with search and export, and three themes.

## System requirements

| Component | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Operating system | Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit |
| Graphics | A GPU with a Vulkan 1.3 driver |
| Processor | Any x86-64 processor; recompilation benefits from more cores |
| Memory | 8 GB minimum, 16 GB recommended |
| Storage | About 30 GB for the extracted game data, plus space for build output |
| Game | Your own legally obtained copy of *Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave* |

Building the game needs these tools (all from winget): LLVM 23 (`LLVM.LLVM`), CMake (`Kitware.CMake`), Ninja
(`Ninja-build.Ninja`), the .NET 10 SDK (`Microsoft.DotNet.SDK.10`), uv, Git and PowerShell 7, plus Visual Studio Build Tools with
"Desktop development with C++". NASM (`NASM.NASM`) is optional and speeds up movie decoding. The launcher says which are missing.

To build the launcher from source you also need the tools listed in [Building from source](#building-from-source).

## Installation

Download `EmblemWeave-<version>-windows-x64.zip` from the [releases page](https://github.com/XiONDiGiTaL/EmblemWeave/releases),
unzip it anywhere and run `EmblemWeave.exe`. Choose your game on **Game Setup**, then press **Build the game** on the
Overview page (once; it lists any build tools you still need) and **Play**. To build the launcher yourself, see
[Building from source](#building-from-source).

Settings are saved to `%APPDATA%\EmblemWeave\config.json`. Decoded modules and
build output go to `%APPDATA%\EmblemWeave\work`, and save data to
`%APPDATA%\EmblemWeave\save`. Your game folder is never written to.

## Preparing your game data

The simplest way is a **`.nup` dump** of your own copy of the game. On the
**Game Setup** page, choose **Choose .nup…** and select the file. EmblemWeave
then does the rest:

- it checks the container's table of contents and every file it reads against
  their SHA-256 hashes, so a damaged dump is reported rather than used;
- it copies the small ExeFS (about 70 MB) once into its work folder;
- it reads the RomFS (26 GB) **in place** from the `.nup`, so nothing has to be
  extracted, and it takes the title and version from the dump's own metadata.

The `.nup` is only ever read.

You can also use an extracted copy. EmblemWeave then needs:

| Item | What it is | Where it usually is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ExeFS | The game's executable modules (`main`, `sdk`, `main.npdm`, ...) | `exefs\` |
| RomFS | The game's assets (`Fs.bin.zst` and the asset folders) | `romfs\` |
| `control.nacp` | Title metadata, including the version | `data\control\control.nacp` in an NSP extraction |

Choose the containing folder with **Folder…** on Game Setup. Plain dumps and NSP
extractions are both detected automatically, and every location can be set
individually. NSP files themselves are not read: a store NSP is encrypted, and
EmblemWeave does not handle console keys.

The game's `main` module is compressed with ZBIC, a Zstandard variant. Decode it
once with **Decode main module** on Game Setup. This currently uses a small
helper script and the Python `zbic` package:

```powershell
python -m pip install zbic
```

## Using the launcher

| Page | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Overview** | **Build the game** compiles it from your dump; **Play** starts it. Load a save profile and jump to the save editor, mods and cheats. Also readiness, the boot test of the Rust runtime, and recent activity. |
| **Game Setup** | Choose and validate your game data (a `.nup` or a folder) and set the language and profile. |
| **Saves** | Save profiles: keep the current save under a name and load any profile later (the save it replaces goes to the backups folder). Lists the slots in the current save, with an editor for gold, renown and each unit's level, experience, max HP, stat gains, weapon masteries, items and spells; names come from your own game data. Imports saves from yuzu, suyu, sudachi, citron, eden and torzu, from any folder, and exports to the emulator layout. |
| **Mods** | Installed RomFS mods, switched on and off with a toggle. Installs from a .zip, .7z or .rar archive, a folder, a GameBanana link, or the game's GameBanana list browsed in the launcher. Mods that only patch the game's code (exefs) are recognised and not installed, since they cannot apply to a recompiled game. |
| **Cheats** | Atmosphere cheat codes, pasted or imported as `.txt`, each switched on and off and applied about 60 times a second while the game runs (data writes, pointer chains, conditionals, loops and controller-button tests work; instruction patches do not). Cheat Engine tables (`.CT`): `aobscan`/`aobscanregion` entries search the game's memory, and the values below them show live, can be typed in, and can be frozen. |
| **In-game menu** | While the game runs, F10 (or Back + RB on a controller) opens EmblemWeave's menu on top of it: pause and resume, a screenshot of the game window (saved to Pictures\EmblemWeave), restart at the title screen, stop and return to the launcher, quick cheats, cheat codes and tables, display settings (window mode, picture size, frame rate counter) and the controls in use. |
| **Quick cheats** | Per-unit switches for the units found in the game's memory: infinite HP, quick level-up (experience held at 99) and max stats. Experimental: the units are found by the record layout Cheat Engine tables for this game use. |
| **Recompilation** | Run the nine-stage pipeline (parse, decompress, decode, recover, analyse, emit C, compile, verify, prepare) with live progress. |
| **Graphics, Audio, Controls** | Options for EmblemWeave's own runtime, saved now and marked until its renderer, mixer and input are in place. While playing, the display settings are in the in-game menu and full rebinding is in the game engine's F1 menu. |
| **Appearance** | Choose between the [XiØN](https://github.com/XiONDiGiTaL) scheme (the xiondigital.net palette), Arcade (a retro video-game palette of hot pink, arcade yellow and cyan on violet, over a neon grid) and FE (gold, white silver and royal blue). The logo artwork changes with the scheme. |
| **Diagnostics** | Stop reason, guest threads, host events, imports reached and the final events before a stop, with search and export. |
| **About** | Version, build revision, credits and legal information. |

Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>1</kbd> to <kbd>9</kbd> to jump between pages. From the command line,
`EmblemWeave.exe --page Diagnostics` opens a page, `--build-engine` builds the game as soon as your game data is detected,
`--boot-test` runs the boot test, and `--screenshot <file.png>` saves the launcher's own frame and closes.

The game runs from `%APPDATA%\EmblemWeave\play`, where the launcher writes its `fefw.ini`. RomFS mods go in that folder's `mods`
folder, one folder per mod holding `romfs/` (the layout emulators use). Every engine option is described in
`engine/fefw-recomp/runtime/docs/CONFIG.md`.

## How the recompilation works

```
  your ExeFS ──► ew-format ──► decoded segments
                                   │
                                   ▼
                              ew-lift: decode ─► recover functions ─► emit C ─► native code
                                   │                                               │
                                   ▼                                               ▼
                         reference interpreter ◄── differential verification ──► compiled C
                                   │
                                   ▼
  your RomFS ──► ew-boot: module image, SDK startup, scheduler, host services ──► the game runs
```

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `ew-format` | NSO0, ExeFS and RomFS parsing, LZ4 segments, module validation |
| `ew-lift` | AArch64 decoder, control-flow and jump-table recovery, C emitter, reference interpreter, Advanced SIMD |
| `ew-boot` | Module image and imports, SDK startup sequence, guest thread scheduler, and the host services (`nn::os`, `nn::fs`, `nn::oe`, `nn::lmem`, C and C++ runtime) |
| `ew-gfx` | The host Vulkan device behind the NVN layer |
| `ew-runtime` | Guest memory bus and service readiness |
| `apps/eblemweave` | The EmblemWeave launcher |

Design details are in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), and the
reasoning behind static recompilation is in [docs/FEASIBILITY.md](docs/FEASIBILITY.md).

## Building from source

| Tool | Version | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Rust](https://rustup.rs) | stable, 1.85 or newer | everything |
| Python | 3.10 or newer | the ZBIC decode helper and verification tools |
| `ziglang` (Python package) | any recent | compiling the emitted C during verification |

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/XiONDiGiTaL/EmblemWeave.git
cd EmblemWeave
cargo build --release
```

The launcher is `target\release\EmblemWeave.exe`. The command-line tools are
built alongside it:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ew-inspect` | Inspect an ExeFS and RomFS |
| `ew-lift` | Run the recompiler and emit C, verification campaigns and reports |
| `ew-run` | Run the game in the console and print a detailed stop report (`--native` runs the compiled library) |
| `ew-native` | Lift, emit and compile the whole main module into `ew_native.dll` |

For example, to run the game from the command line:

```powershell
target\release\ew-run --module work\decoded\main --romfs D:\Games\FortunesWeave\romfs --nacp D:\Games\FortunesWeave\data\control\control.nacp
```

## Testing and verification

```powershell
cargo test --workspace
```

The repository also carries end-to-end checks that run on your own game data:

| Script | What it proves |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/verify_cfg.sh` | 400 recovered functions produce identical registers in the interpreter and in the compiled C |
| `tools/verify_simd.sh` | every distinct vector encoding behaves identically in both, across edge-case inputs |
| `tools/oracle_lockstep.py` | the interpreter agrees with an independent CPU model instruction by instruction, from a snapshot taken by `ew-run --snapshot-at` |

The verification tools need `pip install ziglang unicorn`.

## Project structure

```
apps/eblemweave/     the EmblemWeave launcher (egui)
assets/branding/     the EmblemWeave logo
crates/ew-format/    container and asset formats
crates/ew-lift/      decoder, recompiler and reference interpreter
crates/ew-boot/      runtime: image, startup, scheduler, host services
crates/ew-gfx/       host Vulkan device for the NVN layer
crates/ew-runtime/   guest memory and service registry
docs/                status, architecture, feasibility, legal
tools/               decoding helper and verification scripts
```

`apps/eblemweave/build.rs`:

```rs
//! Build metadata and Windows executable branding.
//!
//! Records the git revision for the About page and, on Windows, embeds the
//! EmblemWeave icon and version information into the executable.

fn main() {
    let rev = std::process::Command::new("git")
        .args(["rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"])
        .output()
        .ok()
        .filter(|o| o.status.success())
        .map(|o| String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).trim().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into());
    println!("cargo:rustc-env=EW_GIT_REV={rev}");
    // HEAD names the branch; the branch ref (or packed-refs) moves on every commit.
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=../../.git/HEAD");
    if let Ok(head) = std::fs::read_to_string("../../.git/HEAD") {
        if let Some(r) = head.trim().strip_prefix("ref: ") {
            println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=../../.git/{r}");
        }
    }
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=../../.git/packed-refs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=assets/icon.ico");

    if std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").as_deref() == Ok("windows") {
        let mut res = winresource::WindowsResource::new();
        res.set_icon("assets/icon.ico")
            .set("ProductName", "EmblemWeave")
            .set("FileDescription", "EmblemWeave: native PC recompilation launcher")
            .set("CompanyName", "XiØN")
            .set("LegalCopyright", "XiØN. Not affiliated with Nintendo or Intelligent Systems.");
        if let Err(e) = res.compile() {
            println!("cargo:warning=could not embed the Windows resources: {e}");
        }
    }
}

```

`apps/eblemweave/src/cheats.rs`:

```rs
//! Cheats: Atmosphere cheat codes and Cheat Engine tables, applied to the
//! running game.
//!
//! The engine maps the game's memory at the addresses the game itself uses
//! (main module at 0x71_0000_0000, heap at 0x78_0000_0000), so EmblemWeave
//! reads and writes it from outside the process with ReadProcessMemory and
//! WriteProcessMemory, the way Cheat Engine does.
//!
//! * Atmosphere codes (`[name]` followed by hex words, the dmnt cheat VM) run
//!   about 60 times a second while switched on. Code patches to the main
//!   module's instructions have no effect, because the game's code is compiled
//!   ahead of time; data writes, pointer chains and conditionals work.
//! * Cheat Engine tables (`.CT`): `aobscanregion` scripts find their pattern in
//!   the game's memory (the range in the table belongs to the emulator it was
//!   made for, so the game's own memory is scanned instead), and the entries
//!   below show live values that can be edited or frozen.

use std::collections::HashMap;

pub const MAIN_BASE: u64 = 0x71_0000_0000;
pub const HEAP_BASE: u64 = 0x78_0000_0000;
pub const ALIAS_BASE: u64 = 0x60_0000_0000;
/// The game's memory, scanned for patterns: alias views, the main module,
/// the heap; stacks start at 0x7C_0000_0000.
pub const GUEST_RANGE: (u64, u64) = (0x60_0000_0000, 0x7C_0000_0000);

/// The engine's process name.
pub const GAME_EXE: &str = "fefw.exe";

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ process

pub trait Memory {
    fn read(&self, addr: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> bool;
    fn write(&self, addr: u64, data: &[u8]) -> bool;
    /// Committed, readable and writable regions within `[lo, hi)`.
    fn regions(&self, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> Vec<(u64, u64)>;
}

#[cfg(windows)]
pub mod process {
    use super::Memory;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, HANDLE};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{ReadProcessMemory, WriteProcessMemory};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Process32FirstW, Process32NextW, PROCESSENTRY32W, TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{VirtualQueryEx, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_GUARD, PAGE_READWRITE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
        GetExitCodeProcess, OpenProcess, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, PROCESS_VM_OPERATION, PROCESS_VM_READ, PROCESS_VM_WRITE,
    };

    pub struct Process {
        handle: HANDLE,
        pub pid: u32,
    }

    unsafe impl Send for Process {}
    unsafe impl Sync for Process {}

    impl Drop for Process {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            unsafe { CloseHandle(self.handle) };
        }
    }

    pub fn find(exe: &str) -> Option<u32> {
        unsafe {
            let snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0);
            if snap.is_null() || snap as isize == -1 {
                return None;
            }
            let mut e: PROCESSENTRY32W = std::mem::zeroed();
            e.dwSize = std::mem::size_of::<PROCESSENTRY32W>() as u32;
            let mut found = None;
            let mut ok = Process32FirstW(snap, &mut e);
            while ok != 0 {
                let len = e.szExeFile.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(e.szExeFile.len());
                if String::from_utf16_lossy(&e.szExeFile[..len]).eq_ignore_ascii_case(exe) {
                    found = Some(e.th32ProcessID);
                    break;
                }
                ok = Process32NextW(snap, &mut e);
            }
            CloseHandle(snap);
            found
        }
    }

    impl Process {
        pub fn open(pid: u32) -> Option<Process> {
            let h = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_VM_WRITE | PROCESS_VM_OPERATION | PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, 0, pid) };
            (!h.is_null()).then_some(Process { handle: h, pid })
        }

        pub fn alive(&self) -> bool {
            let mut code = 0u32;
            unsafe { GetExitCodeProcess(self.handle, &mut code) != 0 && code == 259 }
        }
    }

    impl Memory for Process {
        fn read(&self, addr: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> bool {
            let mut n = 0usize;
            unsafe { ReadProcessMemory(self.handle, addr as _, buf.as_mut_ptr() as _, buf.len(), &mut n) != 0 && n == buf.len() }
        }

        fn write(&self, addr: u64, data: &[u8]) -> bool {
            let mut n = 0usize;
            unsafe { WriteProcessMemory(self.handle, addr as _, data.as_ptr() as _, data.len(), &mut n) != 0 && n == data.len() }
        }

        fn regions(&self, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> Vec<(u64, u64)> {
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            let mut a = lo;
            while a < hi {
                let mut m: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
                let n = unsafe { VirtualQueryEx(self.handle, a as _, &mut m, std::mem::size_of::<MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION>()) };
                if n == 0 {
                    break;
                }
                let (base, size) = (m.BaseAddress as u64, m.RegionSize as u64);
                if size == 0 {
                    break;
                }
                let rw = m.Protect & (PAGE_READWRITE | PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE) != 0 && m.Protect & PAGE_GUARD == 0;
                if m.State == MEM_COMMIT && rw {
                    out.push((base.max(lo), (base + size).min(hi)));
                }
                a = base + size;
            }
            out
        }
    }
}

/// Find `pattern` (None = wildcard) in readable memory within `[lo, hi)`.
pub fn aob_scan(mem: &dyn Memory, lo: u64, hi: u64, pattern: &[Option<u8>]) -> Option<u64> {
    if pattern.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    const CHUNK: u64 = 4 << 20;
    let first = pattern.iter().position(|b| b.is_some())?;
    let key = pattern[first].unwrap();
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    for (s, e) in mem.regions(lo, hi) {
        let mut a = s;
        while a < e {
            let len = (e - a).min(CHUNK + pattern.len() as u64 - 1);
            buf.resize(len as usize, 0);
            if mem.read(a, &mut buf) {
                let mut i = 0;
                while i + pattern.len() <= buf.len() {
                    match buf[i + first..].iter().position(|&b| b == key) {
                        None => break,
                        Some(k) => i += k,
                    }
                    if i + pattern.len() > buf.len() {
                        break;
                    }
                    if pattern.iter().zip(&buf[i..]).all(|(p, b)| p.is_none_or(|p| p == *b)) {
                        return Some(a + i as u64);
                    }
                    i += 1;
                }
            }
            a += CHUNK;
        }
    }
    None
}

/// `aob_scan` split across the CPU's cores, returning the lowest match.
pub fn aob_scan_parallel(mem: &(dyn Memory + Sync), lo: u64, hi: u64, pattern: &[Option<u8>]) -> Option<u64> {
    const PIECE: u64 = 64 << 20;
    let mut pieces = Vec::new();
    for (s, e) in mem.regions(lo, hi) {
        let mut a = s;
        while a < e {
            let b = (a + PIECE).min(e);
            // Overlap so a match across the boundary is still seen.
            pieces.push((a, (b + pattern.len() as u64).min(e)));
            a = b;
        }
    }
    let next = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let best = std::sync::Mutex::new(None::<u64>);
    let threads = std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|n| n.get()).unwrap_or(4).min(16);
    std::thread::scope(|sc| {
        for _ in 0..threads {
            sc.spawn(|| loop {
                let i = next.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                let Some(&(a, b)) = pieces.get(i) else { return };
                if best.lock().unwrap().is_some_and(|x| x < a) {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(found) = aob_scan(&Window(mem, a, b), a, b, pattern) {
                    let mut g = best.lock().unwrap();
                    if g.is_none_or(|x| found < x) {
                        *g = Some(found);
                    }
                }
            });
        }
    });
    best.into_inner().unwrap()
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ unit records

/// Offsets in a unit's in-memory record, as Cheat Engine tables for this
/// game use them: the record starts with five growth-rate bytes and three
/// zero bytes; max HP and the eight stats follow as u16s.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub mod unit {
    pub const MAX_HP: u64 = 0x08;
    pub const STATS: u64 = 0x08; // nine u16: max HP, Str, Mag, Dex, Spd, Lck, Def, Res, Cha
    pub const HP: u64 = 0x20;
    pub const LEVEL: u64 = 0x26;
    pub const EXP: u64 = 0x2C;
    pub const LEN: usize = 0x30;
}

/// Whether `b` (at least `unit::LEN` bytes) looks like a unit record.
pub fn looks_like_unit(b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    // The five signature bytes are non-zero multiples of 5 in every record
    // the community tables name (50 50 20 90 80, 5 5 90 35 90, ...).
    if b.len() < unit::LEN || b[5..8] != [0, 0, 0] || b[0..5].iter().any(|&g| g == 0 || g > 100 || g % 5 != 0) {
        return false;
    }
    let u16_at = |o: usize| u16::from_le_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1]]);
    let max_hp = u16_at(8);
    if !(10..=99).contains(&max_hp) || (0..9).any(|i| u16_at(8 + 2 * i) > 99) {
        return false;
    }
    let hp = u16_at(0x20);
    let level = b[0x26];
    let exp = u32::from_le_bytes(b[0x2C..0x30].try_into().unwrap());
    (1..=max_hp).contains(&hp) && (1..=40).contains(&level) && exp <= 99
}

/// Every unit record in the game's memory, lowest address first.
pub fn scan_units(mem: &(dyn Memory + Sync)) -> Vec<u64> {
    const PIECE: u64 = 64 << 20;
    let mut pieces = Vec::new();
    for (s, e) in mem.regions(GUEST_RANGE.0, GUEST_RANGE.1) {
        let mut a = s;
        while a < e {
            pieces.push((a, (a + PIECE + unit::LEN as u64).min(e)));
            a += PIECE;
        }
    }
    let next = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let found = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new());
    let threads = std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|n| n.get()).unwrap_or(4).min(16);
    std::thread::scope(|sc| {
        for _ in 0..threads {
            sc.spawn(|| {
                let mut buf = Vec::new();
                loop {
                    let i = next.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                    let Some(&(a, b)) = pieces.get(i) else { return };
                    buf.resize((b - a) as usize, 0);
                    if !mem.read(a, &mut buf) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let mut local = Vec::new();
                    let mut o = 0usize;
                    while o + unit::LEN <= buf.len() {
                        if buf[o + 5] == 0 && buf[o + 6] == 0 && buf[o + 7] == 0 && looks_like_unit(&buf[o..o + unit::LEN]) {
                            local.push(a + o as u64);
                        }
                        o += 8;
                    }
                    found.lock().unwrap().extend(local);
                }
            });
        }
    });
    let mut v = found.into_inner().unwrap();
    v.sort_unstable();
    v.dedup();
    v
}

/// One piece of a memory, as its only region.
struct Window<'a>(&'a (dyn Memory + Sync), u64, u64);

impl Memory for Window<'_> {
    fn read(&self, a: u64, b: &mut [u8]) -> bool {
        self.0.read(a, b)
    }
    fn write(&self, a: u64, d: &[u8]) -> bool {
        self.0.write(a, d)
    }
    fn regions(&self, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> Vec<(u64, u64)> {
        let (s, e) = (self.1.max(lo), self.2.min(hi));
        if s < e { vec![(s, e)] } else { vec![] }
    }
}

pub fn parse_aob(s: &str) -> Option<Vec<Option<u8>>> {
    let compact: String = s.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
    let toks: Vec<String> = if compact.contains(' ') {
        compact.split(' ').map(String::from).collect()
    } else {
        compact.as_bytes().chunks(2).map(|c| String::from_utf8_lossy(c).into_owned()).collect()
    };
    toks.iter()
        .map(|t| if t.chars().all(|c| c == '?' || c == '*') { Some(None) } else { u8::from_str_radix(t, 16).ok().map(Some) })
        .collect()
}

// -------------------------------------------------------- Cheat Engine tables

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VarType {
    Byte,
    Bytes2,
    Bytes4,
    Bytes8,
    Float,
    Double,
}

impl VarType {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<VarType> {
        Some(match s.trim() {
            "Byte" => VarType::Byte,
            "2 Bytes" => VarType::Bytes2,
            "4 Bytes" => VarType::Bytes4,
            "8 Bytes" => VarType::Bytes8,
            "Float" => VarType::Float,
            "Double" => VarType::Double,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }

    pub fn size(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            VarType::Byte => 1,
            VarType::Bytes2 => 2,
            VarType::Bytes4 | VarType::Float => 4,
            VarType::Bytes8 | VarType::Double => 8,
        }
    }

    pub fn format(self, b: &[u8], signed: bool) -> String {
        let mut w = [0u8; 8];
        w[..self.size()].copy_from_slice(&b[..self.size()]);
        let u = u64::from_le_bytes(w);
        match self {
            VarType::Float => format!("{}", f32::from_bits(u as u32)),
            VarType::Double => format!("{}", f64::from_bits(u)),
            _ if signed => {
                let bits = self.size() * 8;
                format!("{}", ((u << (64 - bits)) as i64) >> (64 - bits))
            }
            _ => format!("{u}"),
        }
    }

    pub fn encode(self, text: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        let t = text.trim();
        let b = match self {
            VarType::Float => t.parse::<f32>().ok()?.to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
            VarType::Double => t.parse::<f64>().ok()?.to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
            _ => {
                let v: i128 = if let Some(h) = t.strip_prefix("0x") { i128::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok()? } else { t.parse().ok()? };
                (v as u64).to_le_bytes()[..self.size()].to_vec()
            }
        };
        Some(b)
    }
}

/// An `aobscanregion(name, from, to, bytes)` from an entry's script.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AobScan {
    pub symbol: String,
    pub pattern: Vec<Option<u8>>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Entry {
    pub id: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub var: Option<VarType>,
    pub address: String,
    pub signed: bool,
    pub group: bool,
    pub scans: Vec<AobScan>,
    /// The script uses something other than `aobscan*`/`registersymbol`
    /// (code injection), which EmblemWeave cannot run.
    pub unsupported_script: bool,
    pub children: Vec<Entry>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Table {
    pub name: String,
    pub entries: Vec<Entry>,
}

fn parse_scans(script: &str) -> (Vec<AobScan>, bool) {
    let enable = script.split("[DISABLE]").next().unwrap_or(script);
    let mut scans = Vec::new();
    let mut unsupported = false;
    for line in enable.lines() {
        let l = line.split("//").next().unwrap_or("").trim();
        let lower = l.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if l.is_empty() || lower.starts_with("[enable]") || lower.starts_with("registersymbol") || lower.starts_with("{") {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(args) = lower.strip_prefix("aobscanregion(").or_else(|| lower.strip_prefix("aobscan(")).or_else(|| lower.strip_prefix("aobscanmodule(")) {
            let region = lower.starts_with("aobscanregion") || lower.starts_with("aobscanmodule");
            let original = &l[l.len() - args.len()..];
            let inner = original.trim_end_matches(')');
            let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect();
            let (sym, bytes) = match (region, parts.as_slice()) {
                (true, [s, _, _, b, ..]) if lower.starts_with("aobscanregion") => (s, b),
                (true, [s, _, b, ..]) => (s, b),
                (false, [s, b, ..]) => (s, b),
                _ => {
                    unsupported = true;
                    continue;
                }
            };
            match parse_aob(bytes) {
                Some(pattern) => scans.push(AobScan { symbol: sym.to_string(), pattern }),
                None => unsupported = true,
            }
        } else {
            unsupported = true;
        }
    }
    (scans, unsupported)
}

fn parse_entry(n: roxmltree::Node) -> Entry {
    let text = |tag: &str| n.children().find(|c| c.has_tag_name(tag)).and_then(|c| c.text()).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let vt = text("VariableType");
    let (scans, unsupported) = if vt == "Auto Assembler Script" { parse_scans(&text("AssemblerScript")) } else { (Vec::new(), false) };
    let children = n
        .children()
        .find(|c| c.has_tag_name("CheatEntries"))
        .map(|c| c.children().filter(|e| e.has_tag_name("CheatEntry")).map(parse_entry).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    Entry {
        id: text("ID"),
        description: text("Description").trim().trim_matches('"').to_string(),
        var: VarType::parse(&vt),
        address: text("Address").trim().to_string(),
        signed: text("ShowAsSigned").trim() == "1",
        group: text("GroupHeader").trim() == "1",
        scans,
        unsupported_script: unsupported,
        children,
    }
}

pub fn parse_table(name: &str, xml: &str) -> Result<Table, String> {
    let doc = roxmltree::Document::parse(xml).map_err(|e| format!("not a Cheat Engine table: {e}"))?;
    let root = doc.root_element();
    if !root.has_tag_name("CheatTable") {
        return Err("not a Cheat Engine table (no <CheatTable>)".into());
    }
    let entries = root
        .children()
        .find(|c| c.has_tag_name("CheatEntries"))
        .map(|c| c.children().filter(|e| e.has_tag_name("CheatEntry")).map(parse_entry).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    Ok(Table { name: name.to_string(), entries })
}

/// Resolve a CE address: `symbol`, `symbol+44`, `+26+6` (relative to the
/// parent), `7800001000`. Terms are hex; symbols are matched ignoring case.
pub fn resolve(expr: &str, parent: Option<u64>, symbols: &HashMap<String, u64>) -> Option<u64> {
    let e: String = expr.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
    if e.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let relative = e.starts_with('+') || e.starts_with('-');
    let mut total: i128 = if relative { parent? as i128 } else { 0 };
    let mut sign = 1i128;
    let mut term = String::new();
    let flush = |term: &mut String, sign: i128, total: &mut i128| -> Option<()> {
        if term.is_empty() {
            return Some(());
        }
        let v = match u64::from_str_radix(term.trim_start_matches("0x"), 16) {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(_) => *symbols.get(&term.to_ascii_lowercase())?,
        };
        *total += sign * v as i128;
        term.clear();
        Some(())
    };
    for c in e.chars() {
        match c {
            '+' | '-' => {
                flush(&mut term, sign, &mut total)?;
                sign = if c == '+' { 1 } else { -1 };
            }
            _ => term.push(c),
        }
    }
    flush(&mut term, sign, &mut total)?;
    (total >= 0).then_some(total as u64)
}

// ------------------------------------------------------ Atmosphere cheat VM

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Code {
    pub name: String,
    pub master: bool,
    pub words: Vec<u32>,
}

/// Parse an Atmosphere cheat file: `[name]` or `{master}` headers, each
/// followed by hex words.
pub fn parse_codes(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Code>, String> {
    let mut out: Vec<Code> = Vec::new();
    for (n, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
        let l = line.trim();
        if l.is_empty() || l.starts_with("//") || l.starts_with('#') {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(name) = l.strip_prefix('[').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix(']')) {
            out.push(Code { name: name.trim().to_string(), master: false, words: Vec::new() });
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(name) = l.strip_prefix('{').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix('}')) {
            out.push(Code { name: name.trim().to_string(), master: true, words: Vec::new() });
            continue;
        }
        let Some(cur) = out.last_mut() else {
            return Err(format!("line {}: code before any [name]", n + 1));
        };
        for w in l.split_whitespace() {
            cur.words.push(u32::from_str_radix(w, 16).map_err(|_| format!("line {}: {w:?} is not a hex word", n + 1))?);
        }
    }
    Ok(out.into_iter().filter(|c| !c.words.is_empty() || c.master).collect())
}

/// The game's Switch buttons in the bit order cheats use.
pub mod keys {
    pub const A: u32 = 1 << 0;
    pub const B: u32 = 1 << 1;
    pub const X: u32 = 1 << 2;
    pub const Y: u32 = 1 << 3;
    pub const LSTICK: u32 = 1 << 4;
    pub const RSTICK: u32 = 1 << 5;
    pub const L: u32 = 1 << 6;
    pub const R: u32 = 1 << 7;
    pub const ZL: u32 = 1 << 8;
    pub const ZR: u32 = 1 << 9;
    pub const PLUS: u32 = 1 << 10;
    pub const MINUS: u32 = 1 << 11;
    pub const LEFT: u32 = 1 << 12;
    pub const UP: u32 = 1 << 13;
    pub const RIGHT: u32 = 1 << 14;
    pub const DOWN: u32 = 1 << 15;
}

/// Buttons held on the first Xbox-style controller, as Switch buttons by
/// position (the east face button is A).
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn held_keys() -> u32 {
    use windows_sys::Win32::UI::Input::XboxController::*;
    let mut st: XINPUT_STATE = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    if unsafe { XInputGetState(0, &mut st) } != 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    let g = st.Gamepad;
    let b = g.wButtons;
    let map = [
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_B, keys::A),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_A, keys::B),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_Y, keys::X),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_X, keys::Y),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_LEFT_THUMB, keys::LSTICK),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_RIGHT_THUMB, keys::RSTICK),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_LEFT_SHOULDER, keys::L),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_RIGHT_SHOULDER, keys::R),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_START, keys::PLUS),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_BACK, keys::MINUS),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_LEFT, keys::LEFT),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_UP, keys::UP),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_RIGHT, keys::RIGHT),
        (XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_DOWN, keys::DOWN),
    ];
    let mut k = map.iter().filter(|(x, _)| b & *x != 0).fold(0, |a, (_, s)| a | s);
    if g.bLeftTrigger > 128 {
        k |= keys::ZL;
    }
    if g.bRightTrigger > 128 {
        k |= keys::ZR;
    }
    k
}

/// Registers that persist between runs, as in Atmosphere.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct VmState {
    pub regs: [u64; 16],
    pub saved: [u64; 16],
    pub statics: [u64; 128],
}

impl Default for VmState {
    fn default() -> Self {
        VmState { regs: [0; 16], saved: [0; 16], statics: [0; 128] }
    }
}

fn mem_base(m: u32) -> u64 {
    match m {
        0 => MAIN_BASE,
        1 => HEAP_BASE,
        2 => ALIAS_BASE,
        _ => MAIN_BASE,
    }
}

fn mask(width: u32) -> u64 {
    if width >= 8 { u64::MAX } else { (1u64 << (width * 8)) - 1 }
}

fn rd(mem: &dyn Memory, a: u64, w: u32) -> u64 {
    let mut b = [0u8; 8];
    let w = (w as usize).clamp(1, 8);
    if !mem.read(a, &mut b[..w]) {
        return 0;
    }
    u64::from_le_bytes(b)
}

fn wr(mem: &dyn Memory, a: u64, w: u32, v: u64) {
    let w = (w as usize).clamp(1, 8);
    mem.write(a, &v.to_le_bytes()[..w]);
}

fn cmp(c: u32, a: u64, b: u64) -> bool {
    match c {
        1 => a > b,
        2 => a >= b,
        3 => a < b,
        4 => a <= b,
        5 => a == b,
        6 => a != b,
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn nib(w: u32, i: u32) -> u32 {
    (w >> (28 - 4 * i)) & 0xF
}

/// Decoded opcode with its length in words.
fn op_len(words: &[u32], i: usize) -> usize {
    let w = words[i];
    let t = nib(w, 0);
    let width = nib(w, 1);
    match t {
        0 | 1 => if width == 8 { 4 } else { 3 },
        2 => 1,
        3 => if nib(w, 1) == 0 { 2 } else { 1 },
        4 => 3,
        5 => 2,
        6 => 3,
        7 => 2,
        8 => 1,
        9 => {
            if nib(w, 5) == 1 { if width == 8 { 3 } else { 2 } } else { 1 }
        }
        0xA => {
            let o = nib(w, 5);
            if o == 2 || o == 4 || o == 5 { 2 } else { 1 }
        }
        0xC => match nib(w, 1) {
            0 => match nib(w, 5) {
                0 | 2 => 2,
                4 => if nib(w, 2) == 8 { 3 } else { 2 },
                _ => 1,
            },
            _ => 1,
        },
        _ => 1,
    }
}

/// Skip from just after a false conditional at `i` to the instruction after
/// its matching end (or just after its else). Returns the new index.
fn skip_block(words: &[u32], mut i: usize, stop_at_else: bool) -> usize {
    let mut depth = 0;
    while i < words.len() {
        let w = words[i];
        let t = nib(w, 0);
        let n = op_len(words, i);
        if t == 1 || t == 8 || (t == 0xC && nib(w, 1) == 0) {
            depth += 1;
        } else if t == 2 {
            if depth == 0 {
                if nib(w, 1) == 0 || stop_at_else {
                    return i + 1;
                }
            } else if nib(w, 1) == 0 {
                depth -= 1;
            }
        }
        i += n;
    }
    i
}

/// Run one cheat's opcodes once.
pub fn run(words: &[u32], st: &mut VmState, mem: &dyn Memory, keys_held: u32) {
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut loops: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new(); // (start index, register)
    let mut guard = 0u32;
    let w = |i: usize| words.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    let addr40 = |hi: u32, lo: u32| ((hi as u64 & 0xFF) << 32) | lo as u64;
    while i < words.len() {
        guard += 1;
        if guard > 1_000_000 {
            return;
        }
        let op = words[i];
        let t = nib(op, 0);
        let width = nib(op, 1);
        let n = op_len(words, i);
        match t {
            0 => {
                let (m, r) = (nib(op, 2), nib(op, 3) as usize);
                let a = mem_base(m).wrapping_add(st.regs[r]).wrapping_add(addr40(op, w(i + 1)));
                let v = if width == 8 { ((w(i + 3) as u64) << 32) | w(i + 2) as u64 } else { w(i + 2) as u64 };
                wr(mem, a, width, v);
            }
            1 => {
                let (m, c) = (nib(op, 2), nib(op, 3));
                let a = mem_base(m).wrapping_add(addr40(op, w(i + 1)));
                let v = if width == 8 { ((w(i + 3) as u64) << 32) | w(i + 2) as u64 } else { w(i + 2) as u64 };
                if !cmp(c, rd(mem, a, width) & mask(width), v) {
                    i = skip_block(words, i + n, true);
                    continue;
                }
            }
            2 => {
                if nib(op, 1) == 1 {
                    // Reached an else while the branch ran: skip to the end.
                    i = skip_block(words, i + 1, false);
                    continue;
                }
            }
            3 => {
                let r = nib(op, 3) as usize;
                if nib(op, 1) == 0 {
                    st.regs[r] = w(i + 1) as u64;
                    loops.push((i + n, r));
                } else if let Some(&(start, lr)) = loops.last() {
                    if st.regs[lr] > 1 {
                        st.regs[lr] -= 1;
                        i = start;
                        continue;
                    }
                    st.regs[lr] = 0;
                    loops.pop();
                }
            }
            4 => {
                st.regs[nib(op, 3) as usize] = ((w(i + 1) as u64) << 32) | w(i + 2) as u64;
            }
            5 => {
                let (m, r, mode) = (nib(op, 2), nib(op, 3) as usize, nib(op, 4));
                let off = addr40(op, w(i + 1));
                let a = match mode {
                    1 => st.regs[r].wrapping_add(off),
                    2 => mem_base(m).wrapping_add(st.regs[r]).wrapping_add(off),
                    _ => mem_base(m).wrapping_add(off),
                };
                st.regs[r] = rd(mem, a, width) & mask(width);
            }
            6 => {
                let (r, inc, use_off, ro) = (nib(op, 3) as usize, nib(op, 4), nib(op, 5), nib(op, 6) as usize);
                let v = ((w(i + 1) as u64) << 32) | w(i + 2) as u64;
                let a = st.regs[r].wrapping_add(if use_off != 0 { st.regs[ro] } else { 0 });
                wr(mem, a, width, v);
                if inc != 0 {
                    st.regs[r] = st.regs[r].wrapping_add(width as u64);
                }
            }
            7 => {
                let (r, c) = (nib(op, 3) as usize, nib(op, 4));
                let v = w(i + 1) as u64;
                let x = st.regs[r];
                st.regs[r] = match c {
                    0 => x.wrapping_add(v),
                    1 => x.wrapping_sub(v),
                    2 => x.wrapping_mul(v),
                    3 => x.wrapping_shl(v as u32),
                    4 => x.wrapping_shr(v as u32),
                    _ => x,
                } & mask(width);
            }
            8 => {
                let k = op & 0x0FFF_FFFF;
                if keys_held & k != k {
                    i = skip_block(words, i + n, true);
                    continue;
                }
            }
            9 => {
                let (c, d, s1, imm) = (nib(op, 2), nib(op, 3) as usize, nib(op, 4) as usize, nib(op, 5));
                let a = st.regs[s1];
                let b = if imm == 1 {
                    if width == 8 { ((w(i + 1) as u64) << 32) | w(i + 2) as u64 } else { w(i + 1) as u64 }
                } else {
                    st.regs[nib(op, 6) as usize]
                };
                let r = match c {
                    0 => a.wrapping_add(b),
                    1 => a.wrapping_sub(b),
                    2 => a.wrapping_mul(b),
                    3 => a.wrapping_shl(b as u32),
                    4 => a.wrapping_shr(b as u32),
                    5 => a & b,
                    6 => a | b,
                    7 => !a,
                    8 => a ^ b,
                    _ => a,
                };
                st.regs[d] = r & mask(width);
            }
            0xA => {
                let (s, r, inc, o, x) = (nib(op, 2) as usize, nib(op, 3) as usize, nib(op, 4), nib(op, 5), nib(op, 6));
                let a40 = ((op as u64 & 0xF) << 32) | w(i + 1) as u64;
                let a = match o {
                    1 => st.regs[r].wrapping_add(st.regs[x as usize]),
                    2 => st.regs[r].wrapping_add(a40),
                    3 => mem_base(x).wrapping_add(st.regs[r]),
                    4 => mem_base(x).wrapping_add(a40),
                    5 => mem_base(x).wrapping_add(st.regs[r]).wrapping_add(a40),
                    _ => st.regs[r],
                };
                wr(mem, a, width, st.regs[s]);
                if inc != 0 {
                    st.regs[r] = st.regs[r].wrapping_add(width as u64);
                }
            }
            0xC => match nib(op, 1) {
                0 => {
                    let (width, c, s, x) = (nib(op, 2), nib(op, 3), nib(op, 4) as usize, nib(op, 5));
                    let a = st.regs[s] & mask(width);
                    let p6 = nib(op, 6);
                    let p7 = nib(op, 7);
                    let a40 = ((p7 as u64) << 32) | w(i + 1) as u64;
                    let b = match x {
                        0 => rd(mem, mem_base(p6).wrapping_add(a40), width),
                        1 => rd(mem, mem_base(p6).wrapping_add(st.regs[p7 as usize]), width),
                        2 => rd(mem, st.regs[p6 as usize].wrapping_add(a40), width),
                        3 => rd(mem, st.regs[p6 as usize].wrapping_add(st.regs[p7 as usize]), width),
                        4 => if width == 8 { ((w(i + 1) as u64) << 32) | w(i + 2) as u64 } else { w(i + 1) as u64 },
                        _ => st.regs[p6 as usize],
                    } & mask(width);
                    if !cmp(c, a, b) {
                        i = skip_block(words, i + n, true);
                        continue;
                    }
                }
                1 => {
                    let (d, s, x) = (nib(op, 3) as usize, nib(op, 5) as usize, nib(op, 6));
                    match x {
                        0 => st.regs[d] = st.saved[s],
                        1 => st.saved[d] = st.regs[s],
                        2 => st.saved[d] = 0,
                        3 => st.regs[d] = 0,
                        _ => {}
                    }
                }
                2 => {
                    let (x, m) = (nib(op, 2), op & 0xFFFF);
                    for k in 0..16 {
                        if m & (1 << k) != 0 {
                            match x {
                                0 => st.regs[k] = st.saved[k],
                                1 => st.saved[k] = st.regs[k],
                                2 => st.saved[k] = 0,
                                3 => st.regs[k] = 0,
                                _ => {}
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                3 => {
                    let idx = ((op >> 4) & 0xFF) as usize;
                    let r = (op & 0xF) as usize;
                    if idx < 0x80 {
                        st.regs[r] = st.statics[idx];
                    } else {
                        st.statics[idx & 0x7F] = st.regs[r];
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            },
            _ => {}
        }
        i += n;
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ runner

/// What the cheat thread applies, shared with the launcher's UI.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Shared {
    /// Atmosphere codes switched on (master codes first).
    pub codes: Vec<Code>,
    /// Frozen values: address and the bytes kept there.
    pub freezes: Vec<(u64, Vec<u8>)>,
    /// The game's process id while attached.
    pub attached: Option<u32>,
    pub stop: bool,
}

pub type Handle = std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Shared>>;

#[cfg(windows)]
thread_local! {
    static OPEN: std::cell::RefCell<Option<std::sync::Arc<process::Process>>> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
}

/// The game's process, opened for reading and writing, while it runs.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn game() -> Option<std::sync::Arc<process::Process>> {
    OPEN.with(|o| {
        let mut o = o.borrow_mut();
        if o.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| !p.alive()) {
            *o = None;
        }
        if o.is_none() {
            *o = process::find(GAME_EXE).and_then(process::Process::open).map(std::sync::Arc::new);
        }
        o.clone()
    })
}

/// Start the thread that applies codes and freezes about 60 times a second
/// while the game runs.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn start() -> Handle {
    let h: Handle = Default::default();
    let shared = h.clone();
    std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("cheats".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let mut vm = VmState::default();
            let mut idle = 0u32;
            loop {
                let (codes, freezes) = {
                    let s = shared.lock().unwrap();
                    if s.stop {
                        return;
                    }
                    (s.codes.clone(), s.freezes.clone())
                };
                if codes.is_empty() && freezes.is_empty() {
                    // Only look for the game now and then when there is nothing to apply.
                    idle += 1;
                    if idle % 60 == 0 {
                        let pid = game().map(|p| p.pid);
                        shared.lock().unwrap().attached = pid;
                    }
                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(16));
                    continue;
                }
                let proc = game();
                shared.lock().unwrap().attached = proc.as_ref().map(|p| p.pid);
                if let Some(p) = proc {
                    let k = held_keys();
                    for c in &codes {
                        run(&c.words, &mut vm, p.as_ref(), k);
                    }
                    for (a, b) in &freezes {
                        p.write(*a, b);
                    }
                } else {
                    vm = VmState::default();
                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500));
                }
                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(16));
            }
        })
        .expect("starting the cheat thread");
    h
}

/// Where cheats are kept: Atmosphere `.txt` files and Cheat Engine `.CT` tables.
pub fn dir() -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
    crate::engine::run_dir().map(|d| d.join("cheats"))
}

/// The names of the codes switched on, per file, kept in `cheats/enabled.json`.
pub fn load_enabled(dir: &std::path::Path) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("enabled.json")).ok().and_then(|t| serde_json::from_str(&t).ok()).unwrap_or_default()
}

pub fn save_enabled(dir: &std::path::Path, e: &HashMap<String, Vec<String>>) {
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(dir);
    let _ = std::fs::write(dir.join("enabled.json"), serde_json::to_string_pretty(e).unwrap_or_default());
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    /// A flat memory for tests: the heap's first 64 KiB.
    struct Fake(Mutex<Vec<u8>>);
    impl Memory for Fake {
        fn read(&self, a: u64, b: &mut [u8]) -> bool {
            let m = self.0.lock().unwrap();
            let Some(o) = a.checked_sub(HEAP_BASE).map(|o| o as usize) else { return false };
            if o + b.len() > m.len() {
                return false;
            }
            b.copy_from_slice(&m[o..o + b.len()]);
            true
        }
        fn write(&self, a: u64, d: &[u8]) -> bool {
            let mut m = self.0.lock().unwrap();
            let Some(o) = a.checked_sub(HEAP_BASE).map(|o| o as usize) else { return false };
            if o + d.len() > m.len() {
                return false;
            }
            m[o..o + d.len()].copy_from_slice(d);
            true
        }
        fn regions(&self, lo: u64, hi: u64) -> Vec<(u64, u64)> {
            let (s, e) = (HEAP_BASE, HEAP_BASE + self.0.lock().unwrap().len() as u64);
            if e <= lo || s >= hi { vec![] } else { vec![(s.max(lo), e.min(hi))] }
        }
    }

    fn fake() -> Fake {
        Fake(Mutex::new(vec![0; 0x10000]))
    }

    #[test]
    fn static_store_and_pointer_chain() {
        let m = fake();
        // [heap+0x100] = heap+0x2000 (a pointer); then write 999 at [ptr]+0x10.
        m.write(HEAP_BASE + 0x100, &(HEAP_BASE + 0x2000).to_le_bytes());
        let codes = parse_codes(
            "[Gold]\n04100000 00000040 0000270F\n[Chain]\n58100000 00000100\n78000000 00000010\n64000000 00000000 000003E7\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(codes.len(), 2);
        let mut st = VmState::default();
        for c in &codes {
            run(&c.words, &mut st, &m, 0);
        }
        assert_eq!(rd(&m, HEAP_BASE + 0x40, 4), 9999);
        assert_eq!(rd(&m, HEAP_BASE + 0x2010, 4), 999);
    }

    #[test]
    fn conditionals_and_keys() {
        let m = fake();
        m.write(HEAP_BASE + 0x10, &5u32.to_le_bytes());
        // if [heap+0x10] == 5 { [heap+0x20] = 1 } else { [heap+0x20] = 2 }
        let c = parse_codes("[c]\n14150000 00000010 00000005\n04100000 00000020 00000001\n21000000\n04100000 00000020 00000002\n20000000\n").unwrap();
        run(&c[0].words, &mut VmState::default(), &m, 0);
        assert_eq!(rd(&m, HEAP_BASE + 0x20, 4), 1);
        m.write(HEAP_BASE + 0x10, &6u32.to_le_bytes());
        run(&c[0].words, &mut VmState::default(), &m, 0);
        assert_eq!(rd(&m, HEAP_BASE + 0x20, 4), 2);
        // while A is held, [heap+0x30] = 7
        let k = parse_codes("[k]\n80000001\n04100000 00000030 00000007\n20000000\n").unwrap();
        run(&k[0].words, &mut VmState::default(), &m, 0);
        assert_eq!(rd(&m, HEAP_BASE + 0x30, 4), 0);
        run(&k[0].words, &mut VmState::default(), &m, keys::A);
        assert_eq!(rd(&m, HEAP_BASE + 0x30, 4), 7);
    }

    #[test]
    fn loops_write_runs() {
        let m = fake();
        // r1 = heap+0x400; loop 4 { [r1] = 0x63 (1 byte), r1 += 1 }
        let c = parse_codes("[l]\n40010000 00000078 00000400\n30000000 00000004\n61011000 00000000 00000063\n31000000\n").unwrap();
        run(&c[0].words, &mut VmState::default(), &m, 0);
        let mut b = [0u8; 5];
        m.read(HEAP_BASE + 0x400, &mut b);
        assert_eq!(b, [0x63, 0x63, 0x63, 0x63, 0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ce_tables_resolve_and_scan() {
        let xml = r#"<?xml version="1.0"?><CheatTable><CheatEntries>
          <CheatEntry><ID>37</ID><Description>"Dietrich Stats"</Description><VariableType>Auto Assembler Script</VariableType>
            <AssemblerScript>[ENABLE]
aobscanregion(diet, 20000000000, 30000000000, 32 32 14 5A 50 00 00 00)
registersymbol(diet)
[DISABLE]
unregistersymbol(diet)
</AssemblerScript>
            <CheatEntries><CheatEntry><ID>93</ID><Description>"Base"</Description><VariableType>4 Bytes</VariableType><Address>diet</Address>
              <CheatEntries><CheatEntry><ID>45</ID><Description>"XP"</Description><VariableType>4 Bytes</VariableType><Address>+26+6</Address></CheatEntry>
              <CheatEntry><ID>51</ID><Description>"Str"</Description><VariableType>Byte</VariableType><Address>+A</Address></CheatEntry></CheatEntries>
            </CheatEntry></CheatEntries></CheatEntry>
        </CheatEntries></CheatTable>"#;
        let t = parse_table("t", xml).unwrap();
        let e = &t.entries[0];
        assert_eq!(e.description, "Dietrich Stats");
        assert_eq!(e.scans.len(), 1);
        assert!(!e.unsupported_script);
        let base = &e.children[0];
        assert_eq!(base.children[0].var, Some(VarType::Bytes4));

        let m = fake();
        m.write(HEAP_BASE + 0x1234, &[0x32, 0x32, 0x14, 0x5A, 0x50, 0, 0, 0]);
        let at = aob_scan(&m, GUEST_RANGE.0, GUEST_RANGE.1, &e.scans[0].pattern).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(at, HEAP_BASE + 0x1234);
        let mut syms = HashMap::new();
        syms.insert("diet".to_string(), at);
        let b = resolve(&base.address, None, &syms).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(resolve("+26+6", Some(b), &syms), Some(at + 0x2C));
        assert_eq!(resolve("DIET +44", None, &syms), Some(at + 0x44));
        assert_eq!(resolve("+A", None, &syms), None);
        assert_eq!(VarType::Bytes2.format(&[0xFF, 0xFF], true), "-1");
        assert_eq!(VarType::Byte.encode("200"), Some(vec![200]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn finds_unit_records() {
        let m = fake();
        // growth 50 50 20 90 80, then max HP 30 and stats, HP 25, level 7, exp 42
        let mut r = vec![0u8; unit::LEN];
        r[..5].copy_from_slice(&[50, 50, 20, 90, 80]);
        for (i, v) in [30u16, 12, 3, 10, 9, 6, 8, 4, 7].iter().enumerate() {
            r[8 + 2 * i..10 + 2 * i].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
        r[0x20..0x22].copy_from_slice(&25u16.to_le_bytes());
        r[0x26] = 7;
        r[0x2C] = 42;
        m.write(HEAP_BASE + 0x800, &r);
        assert_eq!(scan_units(&m), vec![HEAP_BASE + 0x800]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn aob_patterns() {
        assert_eq!(parse_aob("19 00 ?? 4E"), Some(vec![Some(0x19), Some(0), None, Some(0x4E)]));
        assert_eq!(parse_aob("19004E"), Some(vec![Some(0x19), Some(0), Some(0x4E)]));
        assert_eq!(parse_aob("zz"), None);
    }

    /// Attaches to a running game: its memory is where the cheats expect it.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn live_game_memory() {
        let pid = process::find(GAME_EXE).expect("start the game first");
        let p = process::Process::open(pid).expect("open the game");
        let regions = p.regions(GUEST_RANGE.0, GUEST_RANGE.1);
        let total: u64 = regions.iter().map(|(a, b)| b - a).sum();
        println!("{} regions, {} MiB in the guest range", regions.len(), total >> 20);
        let heap: u64 = regions.iter().filter(|(a, _)| *a >= HEAP_BASE && *a < HEAP_BASE + (1 << 36)).map(|(a, b)| b - a).sum();
        let main: u64 = regions.iter().filter(|(a, _)| *a >= MAIN_BASE && *a < HEAP_BASE).map(|(a, b)| b - a).sum();
        println!("heap {} MiB, main module data {} KiB", heap >> 20, main >> 10);
        assert!(heap > 0);
        let (a, _) = regions.iter().find(|(a, _)| *a >= HEAP_BASE).copied().unwrap();
        let mut b = [0u8; 16];
        assert!(p.read(a, &mut b));
        assert!(p.write(a, &b), "write back the same bytes");
        let t = std::time::Instant::now();
        let none = aob_scan_parallel(&p, GUEST_RANGE.0, GUEST_RANGE.1, &parse_aob("DE AD BE EF 13 37 C0 DE 55 AA").unwrap());
        println!("parallel scan {:?} in {:?}", none, t.elapsed());
        p.write(a, &[0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF, 0x13, 0x37, 0xC0, 0xDE, 0x55, 0xAA]);
        let found = aob_scan_parallel(&p, GUEST_RANGE.0, GUEST_RANGE.1, &parse_aob("DE AD BE EF 13 37 C0 DE 55 AA").unwrap());
        p.write(a, &b);
        assert_eq!(found, Some(a));
    }

    /// Lists the unit records found in a running game.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn live_units() {
        let pid = process::find(GAME_EXE).expect("start the game first");
        let p = process::Process::open(pid).unwrap();
        let t = std::time::Instant::now();
        let units = scan_units(&p);
        println!("{} unit records in {:?}", units.len(), t.elapsed());
        for a in units.iter().take(40) {
            let mut b = [0u8; unit::LEN];
            p.read(*a, &mut b);
            let u16s: Vec<u16> = (0..9).map(|i| u16::from_le_bytes([b[8 + 2 * i], b[9 + 2 * i]])).collect();
            println!("{a:#x} growth {:?} stats {:?} hp {} lv {} exp {}", &b[..5], u16s, u16::from_le_bytes([b[0x20], b[0x21]]), b[0x26], b[0x2C]);
        }
    }
}

`apps/eblemweave/src/config.rs`:

```rs
//! Persistent launcher settings.
//!
//! Stored as JSON at `%APPDATA%\EmblemWeave\config.json`. Every section has a
//! serde default, so a file written by an older build loads with the new
//! fields filled in instead of being discarded. Writes go to a temporary file
//! first and are renamed into place, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a
//! truncated config behind.

use crate::theme::Scheme;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::path::PathBuf;

/// Where the user's own game data lives. Every path is optional: the setup
/// page detects what it can from `game_root` and the user may override any
/// individual location.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Paths {
    /// The folder the user picked: an extracted dump, an NSP extraction, or a
    /// folder holding `exefs` and `romfs`.
    pub game_root: String,
    pub exefs: String,
    pub romfs: String,
    pub nacp: String,
    /// Decompressed `main` segments (`text.bin`, `rodata.bin`, `data.bin`).
    pub decoded: String,
}

/// Values the runtime reports to the game as system settings. These are live:
/// the boot passes them to `nn::oe` and `nn::account`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct System {
    pub language: String,
    pub user_name: String,
}

impl Default for System {
    fn default() -> Self {
        System { language: "en-US".into(), user_name: "Player".into() }
    }
}

/// Run parameters for the guest execution.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]

    pub max_steps: u64,
    /// Guest heap arena, in MiB.
    pub heap_mib: u64,
}

impl Default for Runtime {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Runtime { max_steps: 50_000_000, heap_mib: 4096 }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Config {
    pub paths: Paths,
    pub system: System,
    pub runtime: Runtime,
    pub graphics: Graphics,
    pub audio: Audio,
    pub input: Input,
    pub theme: Scheme,
}

impl Config {
    pub fn dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
        std::env::var_os("APPDATA").map(|base| PathBuf::from(base).join("EmblemWeave"))
    }

    pub fn path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
        Self::dir().map(|d| d.join("config.json"))
    }

    /// Load the config. A missing file is a fresh install; a file that cannot
    /// be parsed is reported, kept on disk under a `.bad` name, and replaced
    /// by defaults so the launcher still starts.
    pub fn load() -> (Config, Option<String>) {
        let Some(path) = Self::path() else {
            return (Config::default(), Some("APPDATA is not set; settings will not persist".into()));
        };
        match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
            Ok(text) => match serde_json::from_str(&text) {
                Ok(cfg) => (cfg, None),
                Err(e) => {
                    let _ = std::fs::rename(&path, path.with_extension("json.bad"));
                    (Config::default(), Some(format!("config.json could not be read ({e}); it was kept as config.json.bad")))
                }
            },
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => (Config::default(), None),
            Err(e) => (Config::default(), Some(format!("config.json could not be opened: {e}"))),
        }
    }

    pub fn save(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
        let path = Self::path().ok_or("APPDATA is not set")?;
        let dir = path.parent().ok_or("config path has no parent")?;
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(|e| format!("creating {}: {e}", dir.display()))?;
        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let tmp = path.with_extension("json.tmp");
        std::fs::write(&tmp, json).map_err(|e| format!("writing {}: {e}", tmp.display()))?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, &path).map_err(|e| format!("replacing {}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    /// Writable directory for save data, kept apart from the user's dump.
    pub fn save_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
        Self::dir().map(|d| d.join("save"))
    }

    /// Writable directory for decoded modules and lift output.
    pub fn work_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
        Self::dir().map(|d| d.join("work"))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn an_old_config_without_new_sections_still_loads() {
        let cfg: Config = serde_json::from_str(r#"{"theme":"emblem"}"#).unwrap();
