`crates/ew-boot/src/alloc.rs`:

```rs
//! `nn::mem::StandardAllocator`, the legacy nnSdk heap interface.
//!
//! The game hands each allocator object a heap region and expects pointers
//! back. The properties callers can observe are kept: returns are aligned, live
//! blocks never overlap, `GetSizeOf` reports what was asked for, freed memory is
//! reused, and a heap never hands out memory outside the region it was given.
//!
//! Every allocator object is its own heap, keyed by its address. A title
//! creates several (a main heap, then sub-heaps carved out of it), so one
//! shared heap would let a later `Initialize` overwrite an earlier one.
//!
//! **Assumption, stated plainly:** this is a first-fit free list, not nnSdk's
//! dlmalloc. Block headers live out of band on the host, so a program that
//! reads the allocator's own metadata out of the heap would see nothing where
//! nnSdk puts its headers. Everything the game can do through the API behaves
//! as specified.
//!
//! A zero size returns a null pointer, as the interface specifies.
//!
//! One boot-order fact shapes the rest of this module. The title allocates
//! through a **static** `StandardAllocator` that nnSdk initialises inside its
//! own code, which this host does not run. Rather than fail a call whose
//! contract the host can honour, an allocator that was never initialised serves
//! from the dispatcher's reserved guest heap.

use crate::hle::{HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// Default alignment when the caller passes zero.
const DEFAULT_ALIGN: u64 = 16;

/// One allocator object's heap.
#[derive(Default, Clone)]
pub struct Heap {
    pub base: u64,
    pub end: u64,
    /// Live blocks: address to (requested size, span start, span end).
    live: BTreeMap<u64, (u64, u64, u64)>,
    /// Free spans: start to length, coalesced.
    free: BTreeMap<u64, u64>,
    /// Spans are rounded up to this many units so free spans stay aligned.
    granule: u64,
}

impl Heap {
    pub fn new(base: u64, size: u64) -> Heap {
        let mut free = BTreeMap::new();
        free.insert(base, size);
        Heap { base, end: base + size, live: BTreeMap::new(), free, granule: DEFAULT_ALIGN }
    }

    /// An empty number line with unit granularity; ranges join with `add_range`.
    pub fn number_line() -> Heap {
        Heap { granule: 1, ..Heap::default() }
    }

    /// Make `[start, start + len)` available. Overlap with a live block or an
    /// existing free span is refused.
    pub fn add_range(&mut self, start: u64, len: u64) -> bool {
        let end = start + len;
        let overlaps = self.free.iter().any(|(&s, &l)| s < end && start < s + l)
            || self.live.values().any(|&(_, s, e)| s < end && start < e);
        if len == 0 || overlaps {
            return false;
        }
        self.free.insert(start, len);
        self.base = if self.end == 0 { start } else { self.base.min(start) };
        self.end = self.end.max(end);
        true
    }

    /// First fit. Padding in front of an aligned block stays free; the span a
    /// block holds runs from its address to its end rounded to the granule.
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, size: u64, align: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let (start, len, at) = self.free.iter().find_map(|(&start, &len)| {
            let at = start.div_ceil(align) * align;
            (at + size <= start + len).then_some((start, len, at))
        })?;
        self.free.remove(&start);
        // Round the span up so the next free span stays 16-byte aligned.
        let g = self.granule.max(1);
        let span_end = (at + size).div_ceil(g).saturating_mul(g).min(start + len);
        if span_end < start + len {
            self.free.insert(span_end, start + len - span_end);
        }
        // Alignment padding in front of the block stays free.
        if at > start {
            self.free.insert(start, at - start);
        }
        self.live.insert(at, (size, at, span_end));
        Some(at)
    }

    pub fn release(&mut self, ptr: u64) -> bool {
        let Some((_, mut start, mut end)) = self.live.remove(&ptr) else { return false };
        if let Some((&prev, &len)) = self.free.range(..start).next_back() {
            if prev + len == start {
                self.free.remove(&prev);
                start = prev;
            }
        }
        if let Some(len) = self.free.remove(&end) {
            end += len;
        }
        self.free.insert(start, end - start);
        true
    }

    pub fn size_of(&self, ptr: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.live.get(&ptr).map(|b| b.0)
    }

    pub fn largest_free(&self) -> u64 {
        self.free.values().copied().max().unwrap_or(0)
    }

    pub fn total_free(&self) -> u64 {
        self.free.values().sum()
    }
}

/// Every allocator object's heap, plus blocks served from the reserved guest
/// heap for allocators nnSdk would have initialised.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Heaps {
    pub by_object: BTreeMap<u64, Heap>,
    pub static_blocks: BTreeMap<u64, u64>,
}

fn heaps<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Heaps) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<Heaps, R>(f)
}

fn initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (this, base, size) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    if base == 0 || size == 0 {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "StandardAllocator::Initialize got base 0x{base:x} and size 0x{size:x}"
        ));
    }
    state.host.log.push(format!("heap: StandardAllocator 0x{this:x} given 0x{size:x} bytes at 0x{base:x}"));
    heaps(state, |h| h.by_object.insert(this, Heap::new(base, size)));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn allocate(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (this, size) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let align = if state.x[2] == 0 { DEFAULT_ALIGN } else { state.x[2] };
    if size == 0 {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    let align = align.max(DEFAULT_ALIGN).next_power_of_two();
    let served = heaps(state, |h| {
        h.by_object.get_mut(&this).map(|heap| (heap.allocate(size, align), heap.largest_free()))
    });
    match served {
        Some((Some(ptr), _)) => HostResult::Returned(ptr),
        Some((None, largest)) => HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "StandardAllocator 0x{this:x} is exhausted: asked for 0x{size:x} bytes aligned {align}, largest free span 0x{largest:x}"
        )),
        None => {
            // Never initialised on this host: nnSdk set it up in code that is
            // not executed here. The reserved guest heap keeps the pointer
            // valid, aligned and inside guest memory.
            match state.host.allocate(size, align) {
                Ok(ptr) => {
                    heaps(state, |h| h.static_blocks.insert(ptr, size));
                    HostResult::Returned(ptr)
                }
                Err(message) => HostResult::Unavailable(message),
            }
        }
    }
}

fn free(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (this, ptr) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    heaps(state, |h| {
        let released = h.by_object.get_mut(&this).is_some_and(|heap| heap.release(ptr));
        if !released {
            h.static_blocks.remove(&ptr);
        }
    });
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn size_of(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (this, ptr) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let size = heaps(state, |h| {
        h.by_object
            .get(&this)
            .and_then(|heap| heap.size_of(ptr))
            .or_else(|| h.static_blocks.get(&ptr).copied())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    });
    HostResult::Returned(size)
}

fn allocatable_size(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let this = state.x[0];
    let reserved = state.host.alloc_end.saturating_sub(state.host.alloc_next);
    HostResult::Returned(heaps(state, |h| h.by_object.get(&this).map(Heap::largest_free)).unwrap_or(reserved))
}

fn total_free_size(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let this = state.x[0];
    let reserved = state.host.alloc_end.saturating_sub(state.host.alloc_next);
    HostResult::Returned(heaps(state, |h| h.by_object.get(&this).map(Heap::total_free)).unwrap_or(reserved))
}

fn finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let this = state.x[0];
    heaps(state, |h| h.by_object.remove(&this));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

// nn::mem::NumberLineAllocator: sub-allocation of integer ranges (the game uses
// it for offsets inside memory pools). Each object is its own number line.

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct NumberLines(pub BTreeMap<u64, Heap>);

fn lines<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut BTreeMap<u64, Heap>) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<NumberLines, R>(|n| f(&mut n.0))
}

fn nl_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let this = state.x[0];
    lines(state, |l| l.insert(this, Heap::number_line()));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn nl_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let this = state.x[0];
    lines(state, |l| l.remove(&this));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn nl_set_mode(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `AddRange(int begin, int size)`.
fn nl_add_range(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (this, begin, size) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u32 as u64, state.x[2] as u32 as u64);
    match lines(state, |l| l.get_mut(&this).map(|h| h.add_range(begin, size))) {
        Some(ok) => HostResult::Returned(ok as u64),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("NumberLineAllocator 0x{this:x} used before Initialize")),
    }
}

fn nl_allocate_impl(state: &mut State, align: u64) -> HostResult {
    let (this, out, size) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2] as u32 as u64);
    if size == 0 {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    let got = lines(state, |l| l.get_mut(&this).map(|h| h.allocate(size, align.max(1))));
    match got {
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("NumberLineAllocator 0x{this:x} used before Initialize")),
        Some(None) => HostResult::Returned(0),
        Some(Some(at)) => match crate::hle::write_bytes(state, out, &(at as u32).to_le_bytes()) {
            Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(1),
            Err(e) => e,
        },
    }
}

/// `Allocate(int* out, int size)`.
fn nl_allocate(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    nl_allocate_impl(state, 1)
}

/// `Allocate(int* out, int size, int alignment)`.
fn nl_allocate_aligned(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let align = state.x[3] as u32 as u64;
    nl_allocate_impl(state, align)
}

/// `Free(int begin)`.
fn nl_free(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (this, begin) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u32 as u64);
    lines(state, |l| l.get_mut(&this).map(|h| h.release(begin)));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// The allocator object itself lives in the guest's `.bss`. Every field it would
/// carry is held by the host arena instead, so construction and teardown have no
/// guest-visible effect beyond what `Initialize` and `Finalize` already do.
fn constructor(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn clear_thread_cache(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

pub fn register(services: &mut HostServices) {
    let nl: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult, &'static str)] = &[
        ("_ZN2nn3mem19NumberLineAllocator10InitializeEPFPvmS2_ES2_PFvS2_S2_ES2_b", nl_initialize, "an empty number line held on the host"),
        ("_ZN2nn3mem19NumberLineAllocator8FinalizeEv", nl_finalize, "forgets the number line"),
        ("_ZN2nn3mem19NumberLineAllocator17SetAllocationModeENS1_14AllocationModeE", nl_set_mode, "first fit serves every mode's contract"),
        ("_ZN2nn3mem19NumberLineAllocator8AddRangeEii", nl_add_range, "adds a free range, refusing overlap"),
        ("_ZN2nn3mem19NumberLineAllocator8AllocateEPii", nl_allocate, "first-fit range allocation"),
        ("_ZN2nn3mem19NumberLineAllocator8AllocateEPiii", nl_allocate_aligned, "aligned first-fit range allocation"),
        ("_ZN2nn3mem19NumberLineAllocator4FreeEi", nl_free, "returns the range, coalescing neighbours"),
    ];
    for (name, handler, claim) in nl {
        services.register(name, *handler, claim);
    }
    services.register(
        "_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocatorC1Ev",
        constructor as _,
        "the allocator's state is held by the host arena, so construction writes nothing",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator10InitializeEPvm",
        initialize as _,
        "gives this allocator object its own heap over the region the game provides",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator10InitializeEPvmb",
        initialize as _,
        "gives this allocator object its own heap over the region the game provides",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator8AllocateEmm",
        allocate as _,
        "aligned first-fit allocation from this allocator's own heap once Initialize has run, and from the reserved guest heap for the static allocator nnSdk would have initialised",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator4FreeEPv",
        free as _,
        "returns the block to its heap's free list, coalescing neighbours",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZNK2nn3mem17StandardAllocator9GetSizeOfEPKv",
        size_of as _,
        "returns the size the block was allocated with, or 0 for an unknown pointer",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZNK2nn3mem17StandardAllocator18GetAllocatableSizeEv",
        allocatable_size as _,
        "largest free span in this allocator's heap, or the reserved guest heap when it was never initialised",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator8FinalizeEv",
        finalize as _,
        "forgets this allocator's heap",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZNK2nn3mem17StandardAllocator16GetTotalFreeSizeEv",
        total_free_size as _,
        "sum of the free spans in this allocator's heap",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZNK2nn3mem17StandardAllocator16ClearThreadCacheEv",
        clear_thread_cache as _,
        "the host heap keeps no per-thread cache",
    );
    services.register(
        "_ZNK2nn3mem17StandardAllocator21CleanUpManagementAreaEv",
        clear_thread_cache as _,
        "no management area is reserved, so there is nothing to clean",
    );
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn init(s: &mut State, base: u64, size: u64) {
        s.x[0] = 0x10;
        s.x[1] = base;
        s.x[2] = size;
        assert_eq!(initialize(s), HostResult::Returned(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn allocations_are_aligned_and_do_not_overlap() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        init(&mut s, 0x1000, 0x100);
        let mut seen = Vec::new();
        for (size, align) in [(1u64, 0u64), (7, 32), (3, 0)] {
            s.x[0] = 0x10;
            s.x[1] = size;
            s.x[2] = align;
            let ptr = match allocate(&mut s) {
                HostResult::Returned(p) => p,
                other => panic!("{other:?}"),
            };
            assert_eq!(ptr % align.max(DEFAULT_ALIGN), 0);
            assert!(ptr >= 0x1000 && ptr + size <= 0x1100);
            for (other, other_size) in &seen {
                assert!(ptr + size <= *other || *other + other_size <= ptr, "blocks overlap");
            }
            seen.push((ptr, size));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn size_of_and_free_track_the_block() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        init(&mut s, 0x2000, 0x80);
        s.x[1] = 24;
        s.x[2] = 8;
        let ptr = match allocate(&mut s) {
            HostResult::Returned(p) => p,
            other => panic!("{other:?}"),
        };
        s.x[1] = ptr;
        assert_eq!(size_of(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(24));
        assert_eq!(free(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        assert_eq!(size_of(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_zero_size_returns_null_and_exhaustion_is_reported() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        init(&mut s, 0x3000, 0x20);
        s.x[1] = 0;
        s.x[2] = 0;
        assert_eq!(allocate(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));

        s.x[1] = 0x1000;
        s.x[2] = 16;
        assert!(matches!(allocate(&mut s), HostResult::Unavailable(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_static_allocator_serves_from_the_reserved_heap() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        s.mem = vec![0u8; 0x20000];
        s.host.alloc_next = 0x10000;
        s.host.alloc_end = 0x20000;
        // No Initialize: this is the object nnSdk would have set up.
        s.x[1] = 48;
        s.x[2] = 16;
        let ptr = match allocate(&mut s) {
            HostResult::Returned(p) => p,
            other => panic!("expected the reserved heap to serve the call, got {other:?}"),
        };
        assert!(ptr >= 0x10000 && ptr + 48 <= 0x20000, "0x{ptr:x} is outside the guest heap");
        assert_eq!(ptr % 16, 0);
        s.x[1] = ptr;
        assert_eq!(size_of(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(48));
        assert_eq!(allocatable_size(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0x10000 - 48));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_number_line_allocates_aligned_ranges_and_reuses_them() {
        let mut h = Heap::number_line();
        assert!(h.add_range(0, 100));
        assert!(!h.add_range(50, 10), "overlap must be refused");
        assert_eq!(h.allocate(10, 1), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(h.allocate(10, 32), Some(32));
        assert_eq!(h.allocate(5, 1), Some(10));
        assert!(h.release(0));
        assert!(h.release(10));
        assert_eq!(h.allocate(15, 1), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(h.allocate(200, 1), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_allocator_object_has_its_own_heap_and_reuses_freed_memory() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        init(&mut s, 0x1000, 0x1000);
        s.x[0] = 0x20;
        s.x[1] = 0x8000;
        s.x[2] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(initialize(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        let alloc = |s: &mut State, this: u64, size: u64| {
            s.x[0] = this;
            s.x[1] = size;
            s.x[2] = 16;
            match allocate(s) {
                HostResult::Returned(p) => p,
                other => panic!("{other:?}"),
            }
        };
        let a = alloc(&mut s, 0x10, 0x400);
        let b = alloc(&mut s, 0x20, 0x40);
        assert!((0x1000..0x2000).contains(&a));
        assert!((0x8000..0x8100).contains(&b), "second heap served from the first: 0x{b:x}");
        let c = alloc(&mut s, 0x10, 0x400);
        s.x[0] = 0x10;
        s.x[1] = a;
        assert_eq!(free(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.x[1] = c;
        assert_eq!(free(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        // Everything was returned and coalesced, so the whole heap fits again.
        assert_eq!(alloc(&mut s, 0x10, 0x1000), 0x1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn allocating_before_initialize_is_reported() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        s.x[1] = 16;
        s.x[2] = 16;
        match allocate(&mut s) {
            HostResult::Unavailable(message) => {
                assert!(message.contains("no guest page arena"), "{message}")
            }
            other => panic!("expected a reported fault, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }
}

`crates/ew-boot/src/audio.rs`:

```rs
//! `nn::audio` at the renderer service boundary.
//!
//! The title's renderer configuration (voices, mixes, effects, wave buffers)
//! is built by nnSdk's own code in `sdk`, which works entirely on game memory.
//! What reaches the system audio service is served here: opening, starting
//! and stopping the renderer, and its update and rendering requests. The
//! renderer's system event fires every 5 ms, the console's audio frame, so
//! the game's audio thread runs at its real cadence.
//!
//! An update runs nnSdk's own `RequestUpdateAudioRenderer`, which reaches the
//! renderer service through the handle: a guest object whose vtable the host
//! fills. Its update call is served by [`crate::audio_update`], which plays
//! voices forward in time and releases their wave buffers. The voices are not
//! mixed to the PC's speakers yet.

use crate::hle::{write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const OK: u64 = 0;
/// The audio frame: 5 ms.
const FRAME_NS: u64 = 5_000_000;
/// The device name every output reports.
const DEVICE_NAME: &[u8] = b"AudioTvOutput";

#[derive(Default)]
struct Renderers {
    /// Handle to the guest address of its system event.
    events: BTreeMap<u64, u64>,
    next: u64,
    updates: u64,
}

fn renderers<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Renderers) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<Renderers, R>(f)
}

/// The renderer service's vtable: 64 slots, the update call at +64.
const VTABLE_SLOTS: u64 = 64;
const SLOT_REQUEST_UPDATE: u64 = 8;

/// A renderer object for the handle: a vtable pointer, then the vtable.
fn renderer_object(state: &mut State) -> Result<u64, HostResult> {
    let object = state.host.allocate(16 + VTABLE_SLOTS * 8, 16).map_err(HostResult::Unavailable)?;
    let update = crate::hle::dynamic_stub(state, "audio:IAudioRenderer::RequestUpdate")?;
    let other = crate::hle::dynamic_stub(state, "audio:IAudioRenderer::unimplemented")?;
    let vtable = object + 16;
    write_bytes(state, object, &vtable.to_le_bytes())?;
    for slot in 0..VTABLE_SLOTS {
        let f = if slot == SLOT_REQUEST_UPDATE { update } else { other };
        write_bytes(state, vtable + slot * 8, &f.to_le_bytes())?;
    }
    Ok(object)
}

fn unimplemented_service(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
        "the audio renderer service was called at 0x{:x} through a vtable slot the host does not serve",
        state.x[30].wrapping_sub(4)
    ))
}

/// `OpenAudioRenderer(AudioRendererHandle*, os::SystemEvent*, const
/// AudioRendererParameter&, void* workBuffer, size_t)`.
fn open(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (out, event) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let handle = match renderer_object(state) {
        Ok(h) => h,
        Err(e) => return e,
    };
    renderers(state, |r| {
        r.next += 1;
        r.events.insert(handle, event);
    });
    // The event is a 5 ms periodic timer that auto-clears on wait.
    if let Err(e) = crate::threads::init_timer_event(state, event, true) {
        return e;
    }
    state.host.log.push(format!(
        "audio: renderer 0x{handle:x} opened; its event fires every 5 ms, voices play forward in time but are not mixed to the speakers yet"
    ));
    match write_bytes(state, out, &handle.to_le_bytes()) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(OK),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn event_of(state: &State, handle: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    renderers(state, |r| r.events.get(&handle).copied())
}

/// `StartAudioRenderer(handle)`: the frame clock starts.
fn start(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let handle = state.x[0];
    match event_of(state, handle) {
        Some(e) => match crate::threads::start_timer_event(state, e, FRAME_NS, FRAME_NS) {
            Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(OK),
            Err(err) => err,
        },
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("StartAudioRenderer on handle {handle}, which is not open")),
    }
}

/// `StopAudioRenderer(handle)`.
fn stop(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let handle = state.x[0];
    if let Some(e) = event_of(state, handle) {
        if let Err(err) = crate::threads::stop_timer_event(state, e) {
            return err;
        }
    }
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

fn close(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let handle = state.x[0];
    renderers(state, |r| r.events.remove(&handle));
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// `RequestUpdateAudioRenderer(handle, const AudioRendererConfig*)`: nnSdk's
/// own implementation, which calls the renderer object's update.
fn request_update(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    renderers(state, |r| r.updates += 1);
    let export = "_ZN2nn5audio26RequestUpdateAudioRendererENS0_19AudioRendererHandleEPKNS0_19AudioRendererConfigE";
    match state.host.named.get(&format!("export.{export}")) {
        Some(&addr) => HostResult::Jump(addr),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable("RequestUpdateAudioRenderer needs the sdk module, which is not loaded".into()),
    }
}

/// `GetAudioRendererWorkBufferSize(const AudioRendererParameter&)`: the work
/// buffer belongs to the audio service, which the host renderer replaces, so
/// the game reserves a single 64 KiB block for it.
fn work_buffer_size(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0x1_0000)
}

fn ok(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// `AcquireAudioOutputDeviceNotification(os::SystemEvent*)`: the output
/// device never changes on the host, so the event is never signalled.
fn device_notification(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    match crate::threads::init_timer_event(state, state.x[0], true) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(OK),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn write_name(state: &mut State, out: u64) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    let mut name = [0u8; 256];
    name[..DEVICE_NAME.len()].copy_from_slice(DEVICE_NAME);
    write_bytes(state, out, &name)
}

/// `ListAudioOutputDeviceName(AudioDeviceName*, int count)`: one device.
fn list_devices(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (out, count) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as i32);
    if count < 1 {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    match write_name(state, out) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(1),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

/// `GetActiveAudioOutputDeviceName(AudioDeviceName*)`.
fn active_device(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    match write_name(state, state.x[0]) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(OK),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult, &'static str)] = &[
        ("_ZN2nn5audio17OpenAudioRendererEPNS0_19AudioRendererHandleEPNS_2os11SystemEventERKNS0_22AudioRendererParameterEPvm", open, "a renderer whose event fires every 5 ms; no mixing to the speakers yet"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio30GetAudioRendererWorkBufferSizeERKNS0_22AudioRendererParameterE", work_buffer_size, "64 KiB; the host renderer does not use the service's work buffer"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio18StartAudioRendererENS0_19AudioRendererHandleE", start, "starts the 5 ms frame clock"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio17StopAudioRendererENS0_19AudioRendererHandleE", stop, "stops the frame clock"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio18CloseAudioRendererENS0_19AudioRendererHandleE", close, "forgets the renderer"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio26RequestUpdateAudioRendererENS0_19AudioRendererHandleEPKNS0_19AudioRendererConfigE", request_update, "nnSdk's own update, served by the host renderer"),
        ("audio:IAudioRenderer::RequestUpdate", crate::audio_update::request_update, "voices play forward in time; wave buffers are released as they finish"),
        ("audio:IAudioRenderer::unimplemented", unimplemented_service, "any other renderer service call stops the run"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio29ExecuteAudioRendererRenderingENS0_19AudioRendererHandleE", ok, "accepted; nothing is mixed yet"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio36AcquireAudioOutputDeviceNotificationEPNS_2os11SystemEventE", device_notification, "never signalled: the output device does not change"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio25ListAudioOutputDeviceNameEPNS0_15AudioDeviceNameEi", list_devices, "one output device"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio30GetActiveAudioOutputDeviceNameEPNS0_15AudioDeviceNameE", active_device, "the one output device"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio26SetAudioDeviceOutputVolumeEPKNS0_15AudioDeviceNameEf", ok, "accepted"),
        ("_ZN2nn5audio40SetDeviceOutputVolumeAutoTuneModeEnabledEb", ok, "accepted"),
    ];
    for (name, handler, claim) in table {
        s.register(name, *handler, claim);
    }
}

`crates/ew-boot/src/audio_update.rs`:

```rs
//! The audio renderer's update request, served on the host.
//!
//! nnSdk's own `RequestUpdateAudioRenderer` (in `sdk`) serialises the game's
//! renderer configuration into an input buffer, calls the renderer service
//! through the handle's vtable, and hands the output buffer to its managers,
//! which check every section's size against the output header. The host
//! implements that one service call.
//!
//! Input: a 64-byte header of section sizes, then behaviour, memory pools,
//! voice channel resources, voices, effects, splitters, mixes, sinks and
//! performance, in that order. Output: a 64-byte header, then memory pool,
//! voice, effect and sink statuses, performance, behaviour and render info.
//! The header offsets are the ones nnSdk's code reads and writes.
//!
//! Voices advance by the time that passes between updates, at their sample
//! rate and pitch: a wave buffer is consumed when its samples have played,
//! and a stopped voice releases all of its buffers. That is what lets the
//! game reuse a sound's handle. Nothing is mixed to the speakers yet.

use crate::hle::{read_bytes, write_bytes, HostResult};
use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::HashMap;

const HEADER: u64 = 64;

/// Input header: byte offsets of each section's size.
mod input {
    pub const BEHAVIOR: u64 = 4;
    pub const MEMORY_POOLS: u64 = 8;
    pub const VOICES: u64 = 12;
    pub const VOICE_RESOURCES: u64 = 16;
    pub const EFFECTS: u64 = 20;
    pub const MIXES: u64 = 24;
    pub const SINKS: u64 = 28;
    pub const PERFORMANCE: u64 = 32;
    pub const SPLITTERS: u64 = 36;
}

/// Output header: byte offsets of each section's size, as nnSdk checks them.
mod output {
    pub const BEHAVIOR: usize = 4;
    pub const MEMORY_POOLS: usize = 8;
    pub const VOICES: usize = 12;
    pub const EFFECTS: usize = 20;
    pub const SINKS: usize = 28;
    pub const PERFORMANCE: usize = 32;
    pub const RENDER_INFO: usize = 40;
    pub const TOTAL: usize = 60;
}

/// Entry sizes of the renderer's IPC structures.
const POOL_IN: u64 = 0x20;
const POOL_OUT: usize = 0x10;
/// This SDK's voice parameter: biquad coefficients are floats, so the wave
/// buffers start at 0x78 (read from nnSdk's `UpdateVoiceInParameter`).
const VOICE_IN: u64 = 0x188;
const VOICE_WAVE_BUFFERS: usize = 0x78;
const VOICE_FLUSH_COUNT: usize = 0x171;
const VOICE_OUT: usize = 0x10;
const EFFECT_IN: u64 = 0xC0;
/// Effect statuses carry a result-state block: 0x90 bytes (the sdk checks the
/// total against its own buffer size).
const EFFECT_OUT: usize = 0x90;
const SINK_IN: u64 = 0x140;
const SINK_OUT: usize = 0x20;
const PERFORMANCE_OUT: usize = 0x10;
const BEHAVIOR_OUT: usize = 0xB0;
const RENDER_INFO_OUT: usize = 0x10;

/// Memory pool states, as the renderer protocol numbers them.
const POOL_REQUEST_DETACH: u32 = 2;
const POOL_DETACHED: u32 = 3;
const POOL_REQUEST_ATTACH: u32 = 4;
const POOL_ATTACHED: u32 = 5;

/// Voice play states.
const PLAY_STARTED: u8 = 0;
const PLAY_STOPPED: u8 = 1;

/// One wave buffer slot as the voice parameter carries it (0x38 bytes).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct WaveBuffer {
    /// Sample data address; 0 is an empty slot.
    pub address: u64,
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
    pub looping: bool,
    pub sent: bool,
}

/// What a voice parameter says, reduced to what playback needs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct VoiceIn {
    pub id: u32,
    pub is_new: bool,
    pub in_use: bool,
    pub play_state: u8,
    pub sample_rate: u32,
    pub pitch: f32,
    pub flush: u8,
    pub buffers: [WaveBuffer; 4],
}

/// The renderer's own playback state for a voice.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Voice {
    /// Slots the renderer holds and has not finished.
    valid: [bool; 4],
    /// The slot playing now.
    index: usize,
    /// Samples played of the current slot.
    offset: u64,
    /// Fractional samples carried between updates.
    carry: f64,
    pub played_samples: u64,
    pub consumed: u32,
}

impl Voice {
    /// Take in this update's parameter and play `seconds` of it.
    pub fn update(&mut self, p: &VoiceIn, seconds: f64) {
        if p.is_new {
            *self = Voice::default();
        }
        // A filled slot the client has not sent before is a newly appended
        // buffer; empty slots (no address) are skipped.
        for (i, b) in p.buffers.iter().enumerate() {
            if !b.sent && b.address != 0 && !self.valid[i] {
                self.valid[i] = true;
            }
        }
        for _ in 0..p.flush {
            self.release_current();
        }
        match p.play_state {
            PLAY_STOPPED => {
                while self.valid.iter().any(|v| *v) {
                    self.release_current();
                }
                self.carry = 0.0;
            }
            PLAY_STARTED => {
                let rate = p.sample_rate as f64 * if p.pitch > 0.0 { p.pitch as f64 } else { 1.0 };
                let want = rate * seconds + self.carry;
                let mut samples = want.floor() as u64;
                self.carry = want - samples as f64;
                // Every slot is visited at most once a pass; a looping buffer
                // plays on and never finishes.
                let mut idle = 0;
                while samples > 0 && idle < 4 {
                    if !self.valid[self.index] {
                        self.index = (self.index + 1) % 4;
                        idle += 1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    idle = 0;
                    let b = p.buffers[self.index];
                    let length = b.end.saturating_sub(b.start) as u64;
                    let left = length.saturating_sub(self.offset);
                    if b.looping && length > 0 {
                        self.played_samples += samples;
                        self.offset = (self.offset + samples) % length;
                        samples = 0;
                    } else if samples >= left {
                        samples -= left;
                        self.played_samples += left;
                        self.release_current();
                    } else {
                        self.offset += samples;
                        self.played_samples += samples;
                        samples = 0;
                    }
                }
                if !self.valid.iter().any(|v| *v) {
                    self.carry = 0.0;
                }
            }
            // Paused: nothing plays.
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Finish the slot being played (or the next held one) and move on.
    fn release_current(&mut self) {
        for _ in 0..4 {
            if self.valid[self.index] {
                self.valid[self.index] = false;
                self.consumed += 1;
                self.offset = 0;
                self.index = (self.index + 1) % 4;
                return;
            }
            self.index = (self.index + 1) % 4;
        }
    }
}

/// Parse one voice parameter (0x188 bytes).
pub fn parse_voice(b: &[u8]) -> VoiceIn {
    let u32_at = |o: usize| u32::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 4].try_into().unwrap());
    let mut buffers = [WaveBuffer::default(); 4];
    for (i, w) in buffers.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        let o = VOICE_WAVE_BUFFERS + i * 0x38;
        *w = WaveBuffer { address: u64::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 8].try_into().unwrap()), start: u32_at(o + 0x10), end: u32_at(o + 0x14), looping: b[o + 0x18] != 0, sent: b[o + 0x1A] != 0 };
    }
    VoiceIn {
        id: u32_at(0),
        is_new: b[8] != 0,
        in_use: b[9] != 0,
        play_state: b[10],
        sample_rate: u32_at(0x0C),
        pitch: f32::from_bits(u32_at(0x1C)),
        flush: b[VOICE_FLUSH_COUNT],
        buffers,
    }
}

/// Per-renderer state kept between updates.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Server {
    voices: HashMap<u32, Voice>,
    last_tick: Option<u64>,
    frames: u64,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Servers(HashMap<u64, Server>);

fn r32(state: &State, a: u64) -> Result<u32, HostResult> {
    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes(read_bytes(state, a, 4)?.try_into().unwrap()))
}

fn r64(state: &State, a: u64) -> Result<u64, HostResult> {
    Ok(u64::from_le_bytes(read_bytes(state, a, 8)?.try_into().unwrap()))
}

fn put32(out: &mut [u8], at: usize, v: u32) {
    out[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
}

/// `IAudioRenderer::RequestUpdate(this, {out, size}*, {performance, size}*,
/// {in, size}*)`, reached through the renderer handle's vtable.
pub fn request_update(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let renderer = state.x[0];
    match update(state, renderer, state.x[1], state.x[3]) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(0),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn update(state: &mut State, renderer: u64, out_span: u64, in_span: u64) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    let (out, out_size) = (r64(state, out_span)?, r64(state, out_span + 8)?);
    let (inp, in_size) = (r64(state, in_span)?, r64(state, in_span + 8)?);
    let size = |field: u64| r32(state, inp + field).map(|v| v as u64);
    let (behavior, pools, resources, voices) = (size(input::BEHAVIOR)?, size(input::MEMORY_POOLS)?, size(input::VOICE_RESOURCES)?, size(input::VOICES)?);
    let (effects, splitters, mixes, sinks) = (size(input::EFFECTS)?, size(input::SPLITTERS)?, size(input::MIXES)?, size(input::SINKS)?);
    let _performance = size(input::PERFORMANCE)?;
    for (name, bytes, entry) in [("memory pool", pools, POOL_IN), ("voice", voices, VOICE_IN), ("effect", effects, EFFECT_IN), ("sink", sinks, SINK_IN)] {
        if bytes % entry != 0 {
            return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
                "audio update: {name} section of {bytes} bytes is not a whole number of 0x{entry:x}-byte entries"
            )));
        }
    }
    let pool_at = inp + HEADER + behavior;
    let voice_at = pool_at + pools + resources;
    let effect_at = voice_at + voices;
    let sink_at = effect_at + effects + splitters + mixes;
    if sink_at + sinks > inp + in_size {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("audio update: sections run past the {in_size}-byte input")));
    }

    let (n_pools, n_voices, n_effects, n_sinks) =
        ((pools / POOL_IN) as usize, (voices / VOICE_IN) as usize, (effects / EFFECT_IN) as usize, (sinks / SINK_IN) as usize);
    let sizes = [n_pools * POOL_OUT, n_voices * VOICE_OUT, n_effects * EFFECT_OUT, n_sinks * SINK_OUT, PERFORMANCE_OUT, BEHAVIOR_OUT, RENDER_INFO_OUT];
    let total = HEADER as usize + sizes.iter().sum::<usize>();
    if total as u64 > out_size {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("audio update: {total} bytes of output do not fit the {out_size}-byte buffer")));
    }
    let mut o = vec![0u8; total];
    o[0..4].copy_from_slice(&read_bytes(state, inp, 4)?);
    put32(&mut o, output::MEMORY_POOLS, sizes[0] as u32);
    put32(&mut o, output::VOICES, sizes[1] as u32);
    put32(&mut o, output::EFFECTS, sizes[2] as u32);
    put32(&mut o, output::SINKS, sizes[3] as u32);
    put32(&mut o, output::PERFORMANCE, sizes[4] as u32);
    put32(&mut o, output::BEHAVIOR, sizes[5] as u32);
    put32(&mut o, output::RENDER_INFO, sizes[6] as u32);
    put32(&mut o, output::TOTAL, total as u32);

    // Memory pools: a requested attach or detach takes effect.
    let mut at = HEADER as usize;
    for i in 0..n_pools {
        let s = r32(state, pool_at + i as u64 * POOL_IN + 16)?;
        let next = match s {
            POOL_REQUEST_ATTACH => POOL_ATTACHED,
            POOL_REQUEST_DETACH => POOL_DETACHED,
            other => other,
        };
        put32(&mut o, at, next);
        at += POOL_OUT;
    }

    // Voices: advance by the time since this renderer's last update.
    let now = crate::threads::now_ticks();
    let parsed: Vec<VoiceIn> = (0..n_voices)
        .map(|i| read_bytes(state, voice_at + i as u64 * VOICE_IN, VOICE_IN).map(|b| parse_voice(&b)))
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    let statuses = state.host.ext.with::<Servers, _>(|s| {
        let server = s.0.entry(renderer).or_default();
        let seconds = server.last_tick.map(|t| now.saturating_sub(t) as f64 / crate::threads::TICK_FREQ as f64).unwrap_or(0.0);
        server.last_tick = Some(now);
        server.frames += 1;
        let statuses: Vec<(u64, u32)> = parsed
            .iter()
            .map(|p| {
                if !p.in_use {
                    server.voices.remove(&p.id);
                    return (0, 0);
                }
                let v = server.voices.entry(p.id).or_default();
                v.update(p, seconds.min(0.25));
                (v.played_samples, v.consumed)
            })
            .collect();
        (statuses, server.frames)
    });
    let (statuses, frames) = statuses;
    if frames == 1 {
        state.host.log.push(format!(
            "audio: first update: {n_pools} memory pools, {n_voices} voices, {n_effects} effects, {n_sinks} sinks; {total} bytes out of {out_size}"
        ));
    }
    for (played, consumed) in statuses {
        o[at..at + 8].copy_from_slice(&played.to_le_bytes());
        put32(&mut o, at + 8, consumed);
        at += VOICE_OUT;
    }
    // Effects, sinks, performance and behaviour report nothing to say: no
    // errors, no history. Render info carries the elapsed frame count.
    at += sizes[2] + sizes[3] + sizes[4] + sizes[5];
    o[at..at + 8].copy_from_slice(&frames.to_le_bytes());
    write_bytes(state, out, &o)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn voice(state: u8, buffers: &[(u32, u32, bool)]) -> VoiceIn {
        let mut v = VoiceIn { id: 1, in_use: true, play_state: state, sample_rate: 48_000, pitch: 1.0, ..Default::default() };
        for (i, (start, end, sent)) in buffers.iter().enumerate() {
            v.buffers[i] = WaveBuffer { address: 0x1000 * (i as u64 + 1), start: *start, end: *end, looping: false, sent: *sent };
        }
        v
    }

    #[test]
    fn buffers_are_consumed_as_their_samples_play() {
        let mut v = Voice::default();
        // Two 4800-sample buffers (0.1 s each) appended.
        let p = voice(PLAY_STARTED, &[(0, 4800, false), (0, 4800, false)]);
        v.update(&p, 0.05);
        assert_eq!((v.played_samples, v.consumed), (2400, 0));
        let sent = voice(PLAY_STARTED, &[(0, 4800, true), (0, 4800, true)]);
        v.update(&sent, 0.1);
        assert_eq!((v.played_samples, v.consumed), (7200, 1));
        v.update(&sent, 1.0);
        assert_eq!((v.played_samples, v.consumed), (9600, 2));
        // Nothing more to play.
        v.update(&sent, 1.0);
        assert_eq!(v.consumed, 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_stopped_voice_releases_everything() {
        let mut v = Voice::default();
        v.update(&voice(PLAY_STARTED, &[(0, 48_000, false), (0, 48_000, false), (0, 48_000, false)]), 0.01);
        v.update(&voice(PLAY_STOPPED, &[(0, 48_000, true), (0, 48_000, true), (0, 48_000, true)]), 0.01);
        assert_eq!(v.consumed, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_reused_slot_is_a_new_buffer_and_new_voices_restart() {
        let mut v = Voice::default();
        v.update(&voice(PLAY_STARTED, &[(0, 480, false)]), 0.01);
        assert_eq!(v.consumed, 1);
        // The client appends again into slot 0.
        v.update(&voice(PLAY_STARTED, &[(0, 480, false)]), 0.005);
        assert_eq!((v.consumed, v.played_samples), (1, 720));
        let mut fresh = voice(PLAY_STARTED, &[]);
        fresh.is_new = true;
        v.update(&fresh, 0.0);
        assert_eq!((v.consumed, v.played_samples), (0, 0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn looping_buffers_never_finish() {
        let mut v = Voice::default();
        let mut p = voice(PLAY_STARTED, &[(0, 1000, false)]);
        p.buffers[0].looping = true;
        v.update(&p, 10.0);
        assert_eq!(v.consumed, 0);
        assert_eq!(v.played_samples, 480_000);
    }
}

`crates/ew-boot/src/bin/ew-native.rs`:

```rs
//! `ew-native`: lift a whole decoded module, emit it as C, compile it in
//! parallel and link one native library (`ew_native.dll`) that `ew-run
//! --native` loads in place of the reference interpreter.
//!
//! ```text
//! ew-native --module work/decoded/main --out build/native [--opt 1] [--limit N] [--cc clang]
//! ```
//!
//! The library exports `ew_native_shards()` and `ew_native_shard(i, &count)`,
//! which hand the runtime each shard's block table: every block start of every
//! lifted function, with the function to call there.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;

struct Args {
    module: PathBuf,
    out: PathBuf,
    opt: String,
    limit: usize,
    cc: PathBuf,
}

fn parse() -> Result<Args, String> {
    let mut a = Args {
        module: PathBuf::from("work/decoded/main"),
        out: PathBuf::from("build/native"),
        opt: "1".into(),
        limit: usize::MAX,
        cc: default_cc(),
    };
    let mut it = std::env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(k) = it.next() {
        let mut v = || it.next().ok_or(format!("{k} needs a value"));
        match k.as_str() {
            "--module" => a.module = PathBuf::from(v()?),
            "--out" => a.out = PathBuf::from(v()?),
            "--opt" => a.opt = v()?,
            "--limit" => a.limit = v()?.parse().map_err(|e| format!("--limit: {e}"))?,
            "--cc" => a.cc = PathBuf::from(v()?),
            "-h" | "--help" => {
                println!("ew-native --module <decoded main> --out <dir> [--opt 0|1|2] [--limit functions] [--cc clang]");
                std::process::exit(0);
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("unknown argument {k}")),
        }
    }
    Ok(a)
}

fn default_cc() -> PathBuf {
    let llvm = PathBuf::from(r"C:\Program Files\LLVM\bin\clang.exe");
    if llvm.is_file() { llvm } else { PathBuf::from("clang") }
}

/// Contiguous groups of functions of roughly equal instruction count.
fn shards(funcs: &[ew_lift::LiftedFunction], n: usize) -> Vec<&[ew_lift::LiftedFunction]> {
    let total: usize = funcs.iter().map(|f| f.insn_count()).sum();
    let target = (total / n.max(1)).max(1);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let (mut start, mut acc) = (0, 0);
    for (i, f) in funcs.iter().enumerate() {
        acc += f.insn_count();
        if acc >= target {
            out.push(&funcs[start..=i]);
            start = i + 1;
            acc = 0;
        }
    }
    if start < funcs.len() {
        out.push(&funcs[start..]);
    }
    out
}

/// Compiler processes to run at once: half the cores, and no more than one
/// per 3 GiB of physical memory, so the machine stays usable.
fn jobs() -> usize {
    let cores = std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|n| n.get()).unwrap_or(4);
    let mem_gib = physical_memory_gib().unwrap_or(16);
    (cores / 2).min((mem_gib / 3) as usize).max(1)
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn physical_memory_gib() -> Option<u64> {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::{GlobalMemoryStatusEx, MEMORYSTATUSEX};
    let mut m: MEMORYSTATUSEX = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    m.dwLength = std::mem::size_of::<MEMORYSTATUSEX>() as u32;
    (unsafe { GlobalMemoryStatusEx(&mut m) } != 0).then_some(m.ullTotalPhys >> 30)
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn physical_memory_gib() -> Option<u64> {
    None
}

/// Give every block to one function: the one with the highest entry at or
/// below it (else the lowest). The lifter follows control flow from every
/// entry, so the same code turns up in many functions; a branch into code
/// another function owns now leaves the native function, and the run loop
/// enters the owner at that block.
fn own_blocks(funcs: &mut Vec<ew_lift::LiftedFunction>) {
    funcs.sort_by_key(|f| f.addr);
    funcs.dedup_by_key(|f| f.addr);
    let mut owner: std::collections::HashMap<u64, u64> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for f in funcs.iter() {
        for b in &f.blocks {
            let e = owner.entry(b.addr).or_insert(f.addr);
            let cur = *e;
            let better = match (f.addr <= b.addr, cur <= b.addr) {
                (true, true) => f.addr > cur,
                (true, false) => true,
                (false, true) => false,
                (false, false) => f.addr < cur,
            };
            if better {
                *e = f.addr;
            }
        }
    }
    for f in funcs.iter_mut() {
        let a = f.addr;
        f.blocks.retain(|b| owner.get(&b.addr) == Some(&a));
    }
    funcs.retain(|f| !f.blocks.is_empty());
}

fn compile_all(cc: &Path, opt: &str, out: &Path, sources: &[PathBuf]) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, String> {
    let threads = jobs();
    eprintln!("compiling {} files, {threads} at a time", sources.len());
    let next = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let failed = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new());
    let done = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
    std::thread::scope(|s| {
        for _ in 0..threads {
            s.spawn(|| loop {
                let i = next.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                let Some(src) = sources.get(i) else { return };
                let obj = src.with_extension("o");
                let mtime = |p: &Path| std::fs::metadata(p).and_then(|m| m.modified()).ok();
                if matches!((mtime(&obj), mtime(src)), (Some(o), Some(c)) if o >= c) {
                    done.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                    continue;
                }
                let mut cmd = Command::new(cc);
                #[cfg(windows)]
                {
                    use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
                    // Below normal priority, so the desktop stays responsive.
                    cmd.creation_flags(0x0000_4000);
                }
                let r = cmd
                    .args(["-std=c11", &format!("-O{opt}"), "-c", "-w", "-fno-strict-aliasing", "-I"])
                    .arg(out)
                    .arg(src)
                    .arg("-o")
                    .arg(&obj)
                    .output();
                match r {
                    Ok(o) if o.status.success() => {}
                    Ok(o) => failed.lock().unwrap().push(format!("{}: {}", src.display(), String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stderr).lines().take(4).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" | "))),
                    Err(e) => failed.lock().unwrap().push(format!("{}: {e}", src.display())),
                }
                let n = done.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) + 1;
                if n % 16 == 0 || n == sources.len() {
                    eprintln!("compiled {n} of {}", sources.len());
                }
            });
        }
    });
    let failed = failed.into_inner().unwrap();
    if !failed.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("{} shards failed:\n{}", failed.len(), failed.join("\n")));
    }
    Ok(sources.iter().map(|s| s.with_extension("o")).collect())
}

/// Write `text` to `path` unless it already holds exactly that. Returns
/// whether it wrote.
fn write_if_changed(path: &Path, text: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {
    if std::fs::read(path).ok().as_deref() == Some(text.as_bytes()) {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    std::fs::write(path, text).map_err(|e| format!("writing {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(true)
}

fn main() {
    if let Err(e) = run() {
        eprintln!("ew-native: {e}");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

fn run() -> Result<(), String> {
    let a = parse()?;
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    let module = ew_boot::Module::from_dir(&a.module).map_err(|e| format!("{e:#}"))?;
    let segments: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = vec![(module.rodata_addr, &module.rodata), (module.data_addr, &module.data)];
    let opts = ew_lift::LiftOptions { module: "app".into(), max_functions: a.limit, max_insns: 4096, own_blocks: true, ..Default::default() };
    let (report, mut funcs) = ew_lift::lift_text_in(&module.text, &segments, &opts);
    let lifted: usize = funcs.iter().map(|f| f.insn_count()).sum();
    own_blocks(&mut funcs);
    let insns: usize = funcs.iter().map(|f| f.insn_count()).sum();
    eprintln!(
        "lifted {lifted} instructions; kept {} functions ({} complete), {} blocks, {} instructions in {:.1?}",
        funcs.len(),
        report.complete_functions,
        funcs.iter().map(|f| f.blocks.len()).sum::<usize>(),
        insns,
        t0.elapsed()
    );

    std::fs::create_dir_all(&a.out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    // Incremental: a file is only rewritten when its text changes, and only
    // compiled when it is newer than its object. A changed header rebuilds all.
    let header_changed = write_if_changed(&a.out.join("ew_aarch64.h"), ew_lift::RUNTIME_HEADER)?;
    write_if_changed(&a.out.join("ew_dispatch.h"), ew_lift::dispatch_header())?;
    if header_changed {
        for old in std::fs::read_dir(&a.out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.flatten() {
            if old.file_name().to_string_lossy().ends_with(".o") {
                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(old.path());
            }
        }
    }
    // Shards of about 20,000 instructions: a few MiB of C each, which clang
    // compiles in bounded memory.
    let parts = shards(&funcs, (insns / 20_000).max(1));
    let mut sources = Vec::new();
    let mut table = String::from("#include \"ew_dispatch.h\"\n\n");
    for (i, chunk) in parts.iter().enumerate() {
        let name = format!("app_{i:04}");
        let path = a.out.join(format!("{name}.c"));
        write_if_changed(&path, &ew_lift::emit_module(&name, chunk))?;
        sources.push(path);
        table.push_str(&format!("extern const ew_func_entry {name}_blocks[];\nextern const unsigned {name}_block_count;\n"));
    }
    table.push_str(&format!("\n__declspec(dllexport) unsigned ew_native_shards(void) {{ return {}u; }}\n\n", parts.len()));
    table.push_str("__declspec(dllexport) const ew_func_entry *ew_native_shard(unsigned i, unsigned *count)\n{\n    switch (i) {\n");
    for i in 0..parts.len() {
        table.push_str(&format!("    case {i}u: *count = app_{i:04}_block_count; return app_{i:04}_blocks;\n"));
    }
    table.push_str("    default: *count = 0; return 0;\n    }\n}\n");
    let table_path = a.out.join("app_table.c");
    write_if_changed(&table_path, &table)?;
    sources.push(table_path);
    // Shards left over from a larger build.
    for old in std::fs::read_dir(&a.out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.flatten() {
        let p = old.path();
        let keep = sources.iter().any(|s| *s == p || s.with_extension("o") == p);
        let n = old.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        if n.starts_with("app_") && !keep && (n.ends_with(".c") || n.ends_with(".o")) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(p);
        }
    }
    eprintln!("emitted {} C files in {:.1?}", sources.len(), t0.elapsed());

    let objects = compile_all(&a.cc, &a.opt, &a.out, &sources)?;
    eprintln!("compiled in {:.1?}", t0.elapsed());
    let dll = a.out.join("ew_native.dll");
    let o = Command::new(&a.cc)
        .args(["-shared", "-fuse-ld=lld", "-o"])
        .arg(&dll)
        .args(&objects)
        .output()
        .map_err(|e| format!("linking: {e}"))?;
    if !o.status.success() {
        return Err(format!("linking failed: {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stderr).lines().take(10).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n")));
    }
    eprintln!("linked {} in {:.1?}", dll.display(), t0.elapsed());
    Ok(())
}

`crates/ew-boot/src/bin/ew-run.rs`:

```rs
//! `ew-run` — run the recovered module and report where it stops.
//!
//! This is the closest thing the project has to starting the game. It maps the
//! module image, enters at the module's text start, dispatches recovered
//! functions until control leaves the translated code, and prints a typed reason
//! for every stop with the address that caused it.
//!
//! It is a diagnostic runner, not the product runtime: it executes the reference
//! interpreter so the report cannot disagree with the lifter about what a block
//! does.

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use ew_boot::{boot, BootOptions, Module, Stop};
use std::path::PathBuf;

struct Args {
    module_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    text: Option<PathBuf>,
    rodata: Option<PathBuf>,
    data: Option<PathBuf>,
    entry: Option<u64>,
    romfs: Option<PathBuf>,
    libs: Vec<PathBuf>,
    save: Option<PathBuf>,
    nacp: Option<PathBuf>,
    language: Option<String>,
    snapshot_at: Option<u64>,
    snapshot_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    snapshot_steps: usize,
    max_steps: u64,
    max_seconds: Option<u64>,
    watch: Vec<u64>,
    trace: usize,
    x0: u64,
    json: Option<PathBuf>,
    verbose: bool,
    all_calls: bool,
    presses: Vec<ew_boot::hid::Press>,
    dump: Option<(u64, usize)>,
    /// Print the module's named imports whose mangled name contains this text.
    imports: Option<String>,
    /// `--native <ew_native.dll>`: run the game's code from the library built
    /// by `ew-native` wherever it has it.
    native: Option<PathBuf>,
}

fn main() {
    if let Err(e) = run() {
        eprintln!("ew-run: {e:#}");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

fn run() -> Result<()> {
    let mut args = Args {
        module_dir: None,
        text: None,
        rodata: None,
        data: None,
        entry: None,
        romfs: None,
        libs: Vec::new(),
        save: None,
        nacp: None,
        language: None,
        snapshot_at: None,
        snapshot_dir: None,
        snapshot_steps: 20_000,
        max_steps: 20_000_000,
        max_seconds: None,
        watch: Vec::new(),
        trace: 64,
        x0: 0,
        native: None,
        json: None,
        verbose: false,
        all_calls: false,
        presses: Vec::new(),
        dump: None,
        imports: None,
    };

    let mut it = std::env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--module" => args.module_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--module")?)),
            "--text" => args.text = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--text")?)),
            "--rodata" => args.rodata = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--rodata")?)),
            "--data" => args.data = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--data")?)),
            "--entry" => args.entry = Some(hex(&value(&mut it, "--entry")?)?),
            "--max-steps" => args.max_steps = value(&mut it, "--max-steps")?.parse()?,
            "--max-seconds" => args.max_seconds = Some(value(&mut it, "--max-seconds")?.parse()?),
            "--watch" => args.watch.push(u64::from_str_radix(value(&mut it, "--watch")?.trim_start_matches("0x"), 16)?),
            "--trace" => args.trace = value(&mut it, "--trace")?.parse()?,
            "--x0" => args.x0 = hex(&value(&mut it, "--x0")?)?,
            "--json" => args.json = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--json")?)),
            "--imports" => args.imports = Some(value(&mut it, "--imports")?),
            "--verbose" => args.verbose = true,
            "--all-calls" => args.all_calls = true,
            "--press" => {
                let v = value(&mut it, "--press")?;
                args.presses.push(ew_boot::hid::parse_press(&v).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?);
            }
            "--romfs" => args.romfs = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--romfs")?)),
            "--native" => args.native = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--native")?)),
            "--lib" => args.libs.push(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--lib")?)),
            "--save" => args.save = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--save")?)),
            "--nacp" => args.nacp = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--nacp")?)),
            "--language" => args.language = Some(value(&mut it, "--language")?),
            "--snapshot-at" => args.snapshot_at = Some(hex(&value(&mut it, "--snapshot-at")?)?),
            "--snapshot-dir" => args.snapshot_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value(&mut it, "--snapshot-dir")?)),
            "--snapshot-steps" => args.snapshot_steps = value(&mut it, "--snapshot-steps")?.parse()?,
            "--dump" => {
                let v = value(&mut it, "--dump")?;
                let (addr, count) = v
                    .split_once(':')
                    .context("--dump expects ADDR:COUNT")?;
                args.dump = Some((hex(addr)?, count.parse().context("--dump count must be a number")?));
            }
            "-h" | "--help" => {
                println!(
                    "ew-run — execute a decoded module and report where it stops\n\
                     \n\
                     USAGE:\n  ew-run --module <decoded-module-dir> [options]\n\
                     \x20 ew-run --text text.bin [--rodata rodata.bin] [--data data.bin] [options]\n\
                     \n\
                     OPTIONS:\n\
                     \x20 --module DIR     directory holding text.bin, rodata.bin, data.bin\n\
                     \x20 --entry ADDR     start address in hex (default 0, the text start)\n\
                     \x20 --max-steps N    instruction budget for the run (default 20000000)\n\
                     \x20 --trace N        keep N transfer lines for the report (default 64)\n\
                     \x20 --x0 VALUE       initial x0 in hex (default 0)\n\
                     \x20 --json PATH      also write the report as JSON\n\
                     \x20 --imports TEXT   list named imports containing TEXT and exit\n\
                     \x20 --verbose        print the transfer trace\n\
                     \x20 --all-calls      list every import reached, not the first 12\n\
                     \x20 --press B@F[+N]  hold button B (A, B, PLUS, UP, A+B, ...) from presented\n\
                     \x20                  frame F for N frames (default 10); repeatable\n\
                     \x20 --max-seconds N  stop after N seconds of wall-clock time\n\
                     \x20 --watch ADDR     log entry and return of the function at hex ADDR\n\
                     \x20                  (EW_PEEK=addr,... shows memory at each hit)\n\
                     \x20 --romfs DIR      your extracted romfs, mounted read-only for nn::fs\n\
                     \x20 --save DIR       writable save directory (default build/save)\n\
                     \x20 --nacp FILE      the title's control.nacp, for its display version\n\
                     \x20 --language CODE  system language reported to the game (default en-US)\n\
                     \x20 --dump A:N       decode N instructions at hex address A and exit\n"
                );
                std::process::exit(0);
            }
            other => anyhow::bail!("unknown argument `{other}` (try --help)"),
        }
    }

    let module = match (&args.module_dir, &args.text) {
        (Some(dir), None) => Module::from_dir(dir)?,
        (None, Some(text)) => {
            let read = |p: &Option<PathBuf>| -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
                match p {
                    Some(path) => std::fs::read(path)
                        .with_context(|| format!("reading {}", path.display())),
                    None => Ok(Vec::new()),
                }
            };
            Module::new(
                "module",
                std::fs::read(text).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", text.display()))?,
                read(&args.rodata)?,
                read(&args.data)?,
            )
        }
        (Some(_), Some(_)) => anyhow::bail!("use either --module or --text, not both"),
        (None, None) => anyhow::bail!("--module or --text is required (try --help)"),
    };

    println!("module:            {}", module.name);
    println!(
        "image:             text 0x0 ({} bytes), rodata 0x{:x} ({} bytes), data 0x{:x} ({} bytes)",
        module.text.len(),
        module.rodata_addr,
        module.rodata.len(),
        module.data_addr,
        module.data.len()
    );

    if let Some(filter) = &args.imports {
        for export in &module.imports.exports {
            if export.name.contains(filter.as_str()) {
                println!("export 0x{:08x}  {:6}  {}", export.addr, export.size, export.name);
            }
        }
        let mut shown = 0usize;
        for import in &module.imports.jumps {
            if import.name.contains(filter.as_str()) {
                println!("0x{:08x}  {}", import.slot, import.name);
                shown += 1;
            }
        }
        println!("{shown} of {} named imports contain `{filter}`", module.imports.jumps.len());
        return Ok(());
    }

    if let Some((at, count)) = args.dump {
        for i in 0..count {
            let addr = at + (i as u64) * 4;
            let Some(word) = ew_lift::scan::word_at(&module.text, addr) else {
                println!("0x{addr:x}: outside the text segment");
                break;
            };
            let op = ew_lift::decode(word, addr);
            println!("0x{addr:08x}: {word:08x}  {op:?}");
        }
        return Ok(());
    }

    // Without an explicit entry, follow nnSdk's startup order through every
    // entry point the module exports.
    let mut sequence = match args.entry {
        Some(e) => vec![("entry".to_string(), e)],
        None => module.startup_sequence(),
    };
    let (entry_name, entry) = sequence.remove(0);
    println!("entry:             0x{entry:x} ({entry_name})");
    for (name, addr) in &sequence {
        println!("  then:            0x{addr:x} ({name})");
    }
    println!("imports:           {} named jump slots", module.imports.jumps.len());
    println!("relocations:       {} relative, {} relr", module.imports.relatives.len(), module.imports.relr.len());

    let mut settings = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    if let Some(path) = &args.nacp {
        match ew_boot::read_nacp(path) {
            Some((title, version)) => {
                println!("title:             {title} {version} (control.nacp)");
                settings.insert("display_version".to_string(), version);
            }
            None => println!("title:             {} is not a control.nacp", path.display()),
        }
    }
    if let Some(lang) = &args.language {
        settings.insert("language".to_string(), lang.clone());
    }
    let opts = BootOptions {
        settings,
        snapshot_at: args.snapshot_at,
        snapshot_dir: args.snapshot_at.map(|_| args.snapshot_dir.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("build/snapshot"))),
        snapshot_steps: args.snapshot_steps,
        romfs: args.romfs.clone(),
        save_dir: Some(args.save.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("build/save"))),
        entry,
        max_steps: args.max_steps,
        watch: args.watch.clone(),
        // A wall-clock limit: once the game paces itself by the host clock,
        // an instruction budget alone can take arbitrarily long to reach.
        cancel: args.max_seconds.map(|secs| {
            let flag = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
            let f = flag.clone();
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(secs));
                f.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            });
            flag
        }),
        trace: args.trace,
        x0: args.x0,
        then: sequence,
        entry_name,
        libraries: args
            .libs
            .iter()
            .map(|d| ew_boot::Module::from_dir(d))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?,
        native: match &args.native {
            Some(p) => {
                let n = ew_boot::native::Native::load(p).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?;
                println!("native:            {} ({} functions, {} blocks)", p.display(), n.functions, n.blocks());
                Some(std::sync::Arc::new(n))
            }
            None => None,
        },
        ..Default::default()
    };
    for lib in &opts.libraries {
        println!(
            "library:           {} ({} exports, {} imports, init {:?}, init_array {:?})",
            lib.name,
            lib.imports.exports.len(),
            lib.imports.jumps.len(),
            lib.imports.init,
            lib.imports.init_array
        );
    }
    ew_boot::hid::set_script(args.presses.clone());
    let report = boot(&module, &opts)?;

    println!();
    println!("steps:             {}", report.steps);
    println!("function entries:  {}", report.dispatches);
    if args.native.is_some() {
        println!("native entries:    {} ({} handed to the interpreter)", report.native_dispatches, report.native_halts);
    }
    println!("distinct funcs:    {}", report.distinct_functions);
    println!(
        "calls / returns:   {} / {} (max depth {})",
        report.calls, report.returns, report.max_depth
    );
    println!("branches:          {}", report.branches);
    println!(
        "host calls:        {} ({} imports implemented)",
        report.host_calls, report.host_implemented
    );
    println!("guest memory:      {} bytes mapped", report.memory_bytes);
    println!(
        "stack:             sp 0x{:x}, low water 0x{:x}",
        report.final_sp, report.stack_low
    );
    println!();
    for line in &report.thread_states {
        println!("{line}");
    }
    for line in &report.host_log {
        println!("host: {line}");
    }
    if !report.resolved.is_empty() {
        println!("resolved at run time: {}", report.resolved.len());
        for name in &report.resolved {
            println!("  {name}");
        }
    }
    if let Ok(path) = std::env::var("EW_PROC_SLOTS") {
        let text: String = report.proc_slots.iter().map(|(a, n)| format!("{a:x} {n}
")).collect();
        let _ = std::fs::write(path, text);
    }
    if !report.recent.is_empty() {
        println!("last events before the stop:");
        for line in report.recent.iter().rev().take(40).collect::<Vec<_>>().into_iter().rev() {
            println!("  {line}");
        }
    }
    println!("phases completed:  {}", if report.phases.is_empty() { "none".to_string() } else { report.phases.join(", ") });
    println!("relocated slots:   {} changed by the loader", report.relocations_changed);
    println!("stopped:           {} (during {})", report.stop.describe(), report.phase);
    if let Stop::Unsupported { pc, word } = report.stop {
        println!("  blocked at       0x{pc:x} (word 0x{word:08x})");
    }

    if !report.import_calls.is_empty() {
        println!();
        println!("imports reached:");
        for i in report.import_calls.iter().take(if args.all_calls { usize::MAX } else { 12 }) {
            println!("  {:<64} {:>6} call(s) from 0x{:x}", i.name, i.calls, i.first_from);
        }
    }

    if !report.hot.is_empty() {
        println!();
        println!("hottest functions:");
        for h in &report.hot {
            println!(
                "  0x{:<10x} {:>8} entries  {:>10} instructions",
                h.addr, h.entries, h.instructions
            );
        }
    }

    if !report.externals.is_empty() {
        println!();
        println!("transfers outside the text segment:");
        for e in report.externals.iter().take(16) {
            println!("  {} 0x{:x} -> 0x{:x}", e.kind, e.from, e.to);
        }
    }

    if args.verbose && !report.trace.is_empty() {
        println!();
        println!("trace:");
        for line in &report.trace {
            println!("  {line}");
        }
    }

    if let Some(path) = &args.json {
        std::fs::write(path, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?)
            .with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))?;
        println!();
        println!("report:            {}", path.display());
    }

    println!();
    println!("summary: {}", report.headline());
    Ok(())
}

fn value(it: &mut impl Iterator<Item = String>, flag: &str) -> Result<String> {
    it.next().with_context(|| format!("{flag} needs a value"))
}

fn hex(v: &str) -> Result<u64> {
    u64::from_str_radix(v.trim_start_matches("0x"), 16).context("expected a hex address")
}

`crates/ew-boot/src/codec.rs`:

```rs
//! `nn::codec` Opus decoders on the host.
//!
//! nnSdk serves Opus through a system decoder service. The host keeps each
//! decoder's parameters itself and decodes packets to silence of exactly the
//! right length, so the game's audio streaming advances at the rate the data
//! dictates. Producing the real waveform belongs with audio mixing, which the
//! host does not do yet; until then nothing would be heard anyway.
//!
//! Input follows Nintendo's Opus framing: each packet is preceded by an 8-byte
//! header, a big-endian payload size and the encoder's final range. The sample
//! count comes from the packet's own TOC byte (RFC 6716, section 3.1).
//!
//! ADPCM decoding is pure library code and runs as nnSdk's own code.

use crate::hle::{read_bytes, write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const OK: u64 = 0;
/// `nn::codec::ResultOpusInvalidPacket`-style failure for malformed input.
const INVALID_PACKET: u64 = 0x6E1F;

#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)]
struct Decoder {
    rate: u32,
    channels: u32,
    streams: u32,
    stereo: u32,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Decoders(BTreeMap<u64, Decoder>);

fn with<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut BTreeMap<u64, Decoder>) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<Decoders, R>(|d| f(&mut d.0))
}

/// Samples per channel in one Opus packet at `rate`, from its TOC byte.
pub fn packet_samples(packet: &[u8], rate: u32) -> Option<u32> {
    let toc = *packet.first()?;
    let config = toc >> 3;
    // Frame duration in units of 2.5 ms.
    let quarter_ms = match config {
        0..=11 => [4u32, 8, 16, 24][(config % 4) as usize],
        12..=15 => [4u32, 8][(config % 2) as usize],
        _ => [1u32, 2, 4, 8][(config % 4) as usize],
    };
    let frames = match toc & 3 {
        0 => 1,
        1 | 2 => 2,
        _ => (*packet.get(1)? & 0x3F) as u32,
    };
    Some(frames * quarter_ms * rate / 400)
}

fn work_buffer_size(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    // Decoder state is kept on the host; the game reserves one page.
    HostResult::Returned(0x1000)
}

/// `Initialize{,Hardware}OpusDecoder(decoder, rate, channels, buffer, size, ...)`.
fn initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (d, rate, channels) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u32, state.x[2] as u32);
    with(state, |m| m.insert(d, Decoder { rate, channels, streams: 1, stereo: (channels == 2) as u32 }));
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// `Initialize{,Hardware}OpusMultiStreamDecoder(decoder, rate, channels,
/// totalStreams, stereoStreams, mapping, buffer, size, ...)`.
fn initialize_multi(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (d, rate, channels, streams, stereo) =
        (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u32, state.x[2] as u32, state.x[3] as u32, state.x[4] as u32);
    with(state, |m| m.insert(d, Decoder { rate, channels, streams, stereo }));
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

fn finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let d = state.x[0];
    with(state, |m| m.remove(&d));
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

fn reset(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

fn get(state: &mut State, f: fn(&Decoder) -> u32) -> HostResult {
    let d = state.x[0];
    match with(state, |m| m.get(&d).copied()) {
        Some(dec) => HostResult::Returned(f(&dec) as u64),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("Opus decoder 0x{d:x} was never initialised")),
    }
}

fn sample_rate(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    get(state, |d| d.rate)
}
fn channel_count(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    get(state, |d| d.channels)
}
fn total_streams(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    get(state, |d| d.streams)
}
fn stereo_streams(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    get(state, |d| d.stereo)
}

/// `Decode*Interleaved(decoder, size_t* consumed, int* samples, int16* out,
/// size_t outSize, const void* in, size_t inSize)`: one packet.
fn decode(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (d, consumed, samples_out, out, out_size, input, in_size) =
        (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2], state.x[3], state.x[4], state.x[5], state.x[6]);
    let Some(dec) = with(state, |m| m.get(&d).copied()) else {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("Opus decoder 0x{d:x} was never initialised"));
    };
    if in_size < 8 {
        return HostResult::Returned(INVALID_PACKET);
    }
    let header = match read_bytes(state, input, 8) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => return e,
    };
    let size = u32::from_be_bytes([header[0], header[1], header[2], header[3]]) as u64;
    if size == 0 || 8 + size > in_size {
        return HostResult::Returned(INVALID_PACKET);
    }
    let packet = match read_bytes(state, input + 8, size.min(2)) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => return e,
    };
    let Some(per_channel) = packet_samples(&packet, dec.rate) else {
        return HostResult::Returned(INVALID_PACKET);
    };
    let bytes = per_channel as u64 * dec.channels.max(1) as u64 * 2;
    if bytes > out_size {
        return HostResult::Returned(INVALID_PACKET);
    }
    for r in [
        write_bytes(state, out, &vec![0u8; bytes as usize]),
        write_bytes(state, consumed, &(8 + size).to_le_bytes()),
        write_bytes(state, samples_out, &per_channel.to_le_bytes()),
    ] {
        if let Err(e) = r {
            return e;
        }
    }
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult)] = &[
        ("_ZN2nn5codec28GetOpusDecoderWorkBufferSizeEii", work_buffer_size),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec36GetHardwareOpusDecoderWorkBufferSizeEiii", work_buffer_size),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec39GetOpusMultiStreamDecoderWorkBufferSizeEiiii", work_buffer_size),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec47GetHardwareOpusMultiStreamDecoderWorkBufferSizeEiiiii", work_buffer_size),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec21InitializeOpusDecoderEPNS0_15OpusDecoderTypeEiiPvm", initialize),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec29InitializeHardwareOpusDecoderEPNS0_23HardwareOpusDecoderTypeEiiPvmi", initialize),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec32InitializeOpusMultiStreamDecoderEPNS0_26OpusMultiStreamDecoderTypeEiiiiPKhPvm", initialize_multi),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec40InitializeHardwareOpusMultiStreamDecoderEPNS0_34HardwareOpusMultiStreamDecoderTypeEiiiiPKhPvmi", initialize_multi),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec19FinalizeOpusDecoderEPNS0_15OpusDecoderTypeE", finalize),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec27FinalizeHardwareOpusDecoderEPNS0_23HardwareOpusDecoderTypeE", finalize),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec30FinalizeOpusMultiStreamDecoderEPNS0_26OpusMultiStreamDecoderTypeE", finalize),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec38FinalizeHardwareOpusMultiStreamDecoderEPNS0_34HardwareOpusMultiStreamDecoderTypeE", finalize),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec16ResetOpusDecoderEPNS0_15OpusDecoderTypeE", reset),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec24ResetHardwareOpusDecoderEPNS0_23HardwareOpusDecoderTypeE", reset),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec27ResetOpusMultiStreamDecoderEPNS0_26OpusMultiStreamDecoderTypeE", reset),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec35ResetHardwareOpusMultiStreamDecoderEPNS0_34HardwareOpusMultiStreamDecoderTypeE", reset),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec24GetOpusDecoderSampleRateEPKNS0_15OpusDecoderTypeE", sample_rate),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec32GetHardwareOpusDecoderSampleRateEPKNS0_23HardwareOpusDecoderTypeE", sample_rate),
        ("_ZN2nn5codec35GetOpusMultiStreamDecoderSampleRateEPKNS0_26OpusMultiStreamDecoderTypeE", sample_rate),

        assert_eq!(packet_samples(&[(16 << 3) | 3, 4], 48_000), Some(480));
