`crates/ew-boot/src/hle.rs`:

```rs
//! Host implementations for imported functions.
//!
//! Every entry here is a claim that the host can provide the exact semantics of
//! that symbol, so the set is deliberately small: the C memory and string
//! routines, whose behaviour is fully specified. Anything else stays
//! unimplemented and stops the run with its name.
//!
//! Two Nintendo runtime initialisers are also modelled, and both are marked as
//! assumptions rather than facts, because their exact side effects live in a
//! module this project does not translate yet.

use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// Result of a host call.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum HostResult {
    /// Returned `x0` to the caller.
    Returned(u64),
    /// Cannot be provided; the run stops with this reason.
    Unavailable(String),
    /// Continue at a guest address with the registers as the handler left
    /// them and the caller's return address intact: a tail call into guest
    /// code, which is how a host vtable forwards to the game's own functions.
    Jump(u64),
    /// The calling guest thread must wait. The scheduler parks it with its
    /// registers as the handler left them and calls `resume` (with those
    /// registers loaded) whenever it next considers the thread; `resume`
    /// returns the call's result or blocks again. `timed` marks a wait that
    /// the passage of time alone can end, which is how a deadlock is told
    /// apart from a sleep.
    Block { resume: Handler, timed: bool },
}

/// Results compare by value; two blocks compare by their `timed` flag only,
/// because a function pointer has no stable identity to compare.
impl PartialEq for HostResult {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        match (self, other) {
            (HostResult::Returned(a), HostResult::Returned(b)) => a == b,
            (HostResult::Unavailable(a), HostResult::Unavailable(b)) => a == b,
            (HostResult::Jump(a), HostResult::Jump(b)) => a == b,
            (HostResult::Block { timed: a, .. }, HostResult::Block { timed: b, .. }) => a == b,
            _ => false,
        }
    }
}

pub type Handler = fn(&mut State) -> HostResult;

/// The set of imported symbols the host can serve.
///
/// A name can be registered exactly, or as a prefix so that C++ overload sets
/// such as the RELRO protection functions are covered by one entry instead of
/// one entry per mangled signature.
pub struct HostServices {
    handlers: BTreeMap<String, (Handler, &'static str)>,
    prefixes: Vec<(String, Handler, &'static str)>,
}

impl HostServices {
    pub fn new() -> HostServices {
        HostServices { handlers: BTreeMap::new(), prefixes: Vec::new() }
    }

    /// The functions EmblemWeave actually implements today.
    pub fn defaults() -> HostServices {
        let mut s = HostServices::new();
        for (name, handler, claim) in [
            ("memcpy", memcpy as Handler, "standard C memcpy semantics"),
            ("memmove", memmove as Handler, "standard C memmove semantics"),
            ("memset", memset as Handler, "standard C memset semantics"),
            ("memcmp", memcmp as Handler, "standard C memcmp semantics"),
            ("bcmp", memcmp as Handler, "memcmp semantics, boolean result unused"),
            ("memchr", memchr as Handler, "standard C memchr semantics"),
            ("strlen", strlen as Handler, "standard C strlen semantics"),
            ("strnlen", strnlen as Handler, "standard C strnlen semantics"),
            ("strcmp", strcmp as Handler, "standard C strcmp semantics"),
            ("strncmp", strncmp as Handler, "standard C strncmp semantics"),
            ("strcpy", strcpy as Handler, "standard C strcpy semantics"),
            ("strncpy", strncpy as Handler, "standard C strncpy semantics"),
            ("strchr", strchr as Handler, "standard C strchr semantics"),
            ("strrchr", strrchr as Handler, "standard C strrchr semantics"),
            ("strstr", strstr as Handler, "standard C strstr semantics"),
            (
                "__nnmusl_init_dso",
                init_dso as Handler,
                "assumption: registers TLS and atexit for a shared object, which this module is not",
            ),
            (
                "__nnmusl_fini_dso",
                init_dso as Handler,
                "assumption: paired teardown of the initialiser above",
            ),
        ] {
            s.register(name, handler, claim);
        }

        // nn::ro memory protection. The flat guest address space has no page
        // permissions, so protecting RELRO cannot fail and has nothing to do;
        // reporting success is the exact behaviour in this memory model, not a
        // shortcut around a missing feature.
        s.register_prefix(
            "_ZN2nn2ro12ProtectRelroE",
            protect_relro as Handler,
            "the flat guest address space has no page permissions, so protection succeeds trivially",
        );
        s.register_prefix(
            "_ZN2nn2ro14UnprotectRelroE",
            protect_relro as Handler,
            "paired with ProtectRelro in the flat guest address space",
        );

        // C runtime registration. The host never exits through the guest's
        // exit path, so registering a handler and returning success is the
        // complete behaviour available in this model.
        for name in ["atexit", "at_quick_exit", "__cxa_finalize"] {
            s.register(
                name,
                register_exit as Handler,
                "registers an exit handler; the host has no guest exit path to run it from yet",
            );
        }
        s.register_prefix(
            "__cxa_atexit",
            register_exit as Handler,
            "same contract as atexit for C++ static destructors",
        );

        // The single-threaded operating system services live in their own
        // module because every one of them has a stated concurrency contract.
        crate::services::register(&mut s);
        crate::math::register(&mut s);
        crate::cxx::register(&mut s);
        crate::alloc::register(&mut s);
        crate::pmr::register(&mut s);
        crate::fs::register(&mut s);
        crate::lmem::register(&mut s);
        // Multi-threaded nn::os supersedes the single-threaded handlers of the
        // same names, so it registers last.
        crate::threads::register(&mut s);
        crate::system::register(&mut s);
        crate::libc::register(&mut s);
        crate::gfx::register(&mut s);
        crate::nvn::register(&mut s);
        crate::nvn_mem::register(&mut s);
        crate::nvn_tex::register(&mut s);
        crate::nvn_win::register(&mut s);
        crate::nvn_cmd::register(&mut s);
        crate::nvn_state::register(&mut s);
        crate::nvn_prog::register(&mut s);
        crate::hid::register(&mut s);
        crate::kernel::register(&mut s);
        crate::audio::register(&mut s);
        crate::codec::register(&mut s);
        crate::prepo::register(&mut s);
        crate::movie::register(&mut s);
        s
    }

    pub fn register(&mut self, name: &str, handler: Handler, claim: &'static str) {
        self.handlers.insert(name.to_string(), (handler, claim));
    }

    /// Register a handler for every symbol starting with `prefix`. Lookup
    /// prefers the longest matching prefix, and re-registering the same prefix
    /// replaces the earlier handler.
    pub fn register_prefix(&mut self, prefix: &str, handler: Handler, claim: &'static str) {
        self.prefixes.retain(|(p, _, _)| p != prefix);
        self.prefixes.push((prefix.to_string(), handler, claim));
    }

    fn resolve(&self, name: &str) -> Option<(Handler, &'static str)> {
        if let Some((handler, claim)) = self.handlers.get(name) {
            return Some((*handler, *claim));
        }
        self.prefixes
            .iter()
            .filter(|(prefix, _, _)| name.starts_with(prefix.as_str()))
            .max_by_key(|(prefix, _, _)| prefix.len())
            .map(|(_, handler, claim)| (*handler, *claim))
    }


    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Handler> {
        self.resolve(name).map(|(h, _)| h)
    }

    pub fn claim(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
        self.resolve(name).map(|(_, c)| c)
    }

    pub fn names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.handlers
            .keys()
            .cloned()
            .chain(self.prefixes.iter().map(|(p, _, _)| format!("{p}*")))
            .collect()
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.handlers.len() + self.prefixes.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.handlers.is_empty()
    }
}

impl Default for HostServices {
    fn default() -> Self {
        HostServices::defaults()
    }
}

// Guest memory helpers. A fault is reported with the address, never masked.

/// The guest address of a host function created at run time, by name. The
/// same name always yields the same address. Calling it dispatches to the
/// service registered under `name`, or stops the run naming it.
pub(crate) fn dynamic_stub(state: &mut State, name: &str) -> Result<u64, HostResult> {
    if let Some(i) = state.host.dyn_stubs.iter().position(|n| n == name) {
        return Ok(state.host.dyn_base + i as u64 * 16);
    }
    let i = state.host.dyn_stubs.len() as u64;
    if state.host.dyn_base == 0 || i >= state.host.dyn_capacity {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "no room for another run-time host function ({name}); {} already exist",
            state.host.dyn_stubs.len()
        )));
    }
    state.host.dyn_stubs.push(name.to_string());
    Ok(state.host.dyn_base + i * 16)
}

pub(crate) fn read_bytes(state: &State, addr: u64, len: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, HostResult> {
    let (Ok(start), Ok(end)) = (usize::try_from(addr), usize::try_from(addr.saturating_add(len))) else {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("host read of {len} bytes at 0x{addr:x} wraps")));
    };
    if end > state.mem.len() {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "host read of {len} bytes at 0x{addr:x} is outside guest memory"
        )));
    }
    Ok(state.mem[start..end].to_vec())
}

pub(crate) fn write_bytes(state: &mut State, addr: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    let (Ok(start), Ok(end)) = (usize::try_from(addr), usize::try_from(addr.saturating_add(bytes.len() as u64))) else {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("host write at 0x{addr:x} wraps")));
    };
    if end > state.mem.len() {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "host write of {} bytes at 0x{addr:x} is outside guest memory",
            bytes.len()
        )));
    }
    state.mem[start..end].copy_from_slice(bytes);
    Ok(())
}

fn memcpy(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (dst, src, n) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    match read_bytes(state, src, n) {
        Ok(bytes) => match write_bytes(state, dst, &bytes) {
            Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(dst),
            Err(e) => e,
        },
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn memmove(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    memcpy(state)
}

fn memset(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (dst, value, n) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u8, state.x[2]);
    let bytes = vec![value; n as usize];
    match write_bytes(state, dst, &bytes) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(dst),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn memcmp(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (a, b, n) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    let (left, right) = match (read_bytes(state, a, n), read_bytes(state, b, n)) {
        (Ok(l), Ok(r)) => (l, r),
        (Err(e), _) | (_, Err(e)) => return e,
    };
    let order = match left.iter().zip(right.iter()).find(|(x, y)| x != y) {
        Some((x, y)) => x.cmp(y),
        None => std::cmp::Ordering::Equal,
    };
    let result = match order {
        std::cmp::Ordering::Less => -1i64,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => 0,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => 1,
    };
    HostResult::Returned(result as u64)
}

fn memchr(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (addr, needle, n) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u8, state.x[2]);
    match read_bytes(state, addr, n) {
        Ok(bytes) => match bytes.iter().position(|b| *b == needle) {
            Some(i) => HostResult::Returned(addr + i as u64),
            None => HostResult::Returned(0),
        },
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

/// Read a NUL-terminated string, with a hard cap so a bad pointer cannot walk
/// the whole address space.
pub(crate) fn c_string(state: &State, addr: u64, max: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, HostResult> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..max {
        let byte = read_bytes(state, addr + i, 1)?;
        if byte[0] == 0 {
            return Ok(out);
        }
        out.push(byte[0]);
    }
    Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
        "host string read at 0x{addr:x} has no terminator within {max} bytes"
    )))
}

fn strlen(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let addr = state.x[0];
    match c_string(state, addr, 1 << 20) {
        Ok(s) => HostResult::Returned(s.len() as u64),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn strnlen(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (addr, max) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    match c_string(state, addr, max.max(1)) {
        Ok(s) => HostResult::Returned(s.len() as u64),
        // An unterminated string is exactly what strnlen reports as `max`.
        Err(_) => HostResult::Returned(max),
    }
}

fn strcmp(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (a, b) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let (left, right) = match (c_string(state, a, 1 << 20), c_string(state, b, 1 << 20)) {
        (Ok(l), Ok(r)) => (l, r),
        (Err(e), _) | (_, Err(e)) => return e,
    };
    let order = left.cmp(&right);
    let result = match order {
        std::cmp::Ordering::Less => -1i64,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => 0,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => 1,
    };
    HostResult::Returned(result as u64)
}

fn strncmp(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (a, b, n) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    let (left, right) = if n == 0 {
        (Vec::new(), Vec::new())
    } else {
        // At most n bytes, stopping at a terminator: a string needs no
        // terminator within the compared length.
        let bounded = |at: u64| -> Result<Vec<u8>, HostResult> {
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            for i in 0..n.min(1 << 20) {
                let c = read_bytes(state, at + i, 1)?[0];
                if c == 0 {
                    break;
                }
                out.push(c);
            }
            Ok(out)
        };
        match (bounded(a), bounded(b)) {
            (Ok(l), Ok(r)) => (l, r),
            (Err(e), _) | (_, Err(e)) => return e,
        }
    };
    let order = left.cmp(&right);
    let result = match order {
        std::cmp::Ordering::Less => -1i64,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => 0,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => 1,
    };
    HostResult::Returned(result as u64)
}

fn strcpy(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (dst, src) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    match c_string(state, src, 1 << 20) {
        Ok(mut s) => {
            s.push(0);
            match write_bytes(state, dst, &s) {
                Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(dst),
                Err(e) => e,
            }
        }
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn strncpy(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (dst, src, n) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    match c_string(state, src, 1 << 20) {
        Ok(s) => {
            out.extend_from_slice(&s);
            out.push(0);
            out.resize(n as usize, 0);
        }
        Err(e) => return e,
    }
    match write_bytes(state, dst, &out) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(dst),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn strchr(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (addr, needle) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u8);
    match c_string(state, addr, 1 << 20) {
        Ok(s) => {
            // The terminator is a valid match for a zero needle.
            match s.iter().position(|b| *b == needle) {
                Some(i) => HostResult::Returned(addr + i as u64),
                None if needle == 0 => HostResult::Returned(addr + s.len() as u64),
                None => HostResult::Returned(0),
            }
        }
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn strrchr(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (addr, needle) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as u8);
    match c_string(state, addr, 1 << 20) {
        Ok(s) => match s.iter().rposition(|b| *b == needle) {
            Some(i) => HostResult::Returned(addr + i as u64),
            None if needle == 0 => HostResult::Returned(addr + s.len() as u64),
            None => HostResult::Returned(0),
        },
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn strstr(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (hay, needle) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let (h, n) = match (c_string(state, hay, 1 << 20), c_string(state, needle, 1 << 20)) {
        (Ok(h), Ok(n)) => (h, n),
        (Err(e), _) | (_, Err(e)) => return e,
    };
    if n.is_empty() {
        return HostResult::Returned(hay);
    }
    if n.len() > h.len() {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    match h.windows(n.len()).position(|w| w == n.as_slice()) {
        Some(i) => HostResult::Returned(hay + i as u64),
        None => HostResult::Returned(0),
    }
}

/// `__nnmusl_init_dso` / `__nnmusl_fini_dso`.
///
/// Assumption stated in the claim: these set up per-shared-object C runtime
/// state. The module being translated is the program image, not a shared
/// object, so there is nothing to register. If the guest depends on something
/// this skips, the next stop will say so instead of hiding it.
fn init_dso(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nn::ro::ProtectRelro` and `nn::ro::UnprotectRelro`.
fn protect_relro(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `atexit`, `at_quick_exit`, `__cxa_atexit` and `__cxa_finalize`.
fn register_exit(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn state_with(bytes: &[u8], at: u64) -> State {
        let mut s = State::default();
        s.mem[at as usize..at as usize + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
        s
    }

    #[test]

        assert_eq!(&s.mem[0x200..0x205], b"hello");

        let mut s = State::default();
        s.x[0] = 0x300;
        s.x[1] = 0xAB;
        s.x[2] = 3;

        assert_eq!(&s.mem[0x300..0x303], &[0xAB, 0xAB, 0xAB]);

    }

        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        s.x[1] = 0x104;

    }

        let result = memcpy(&mut s);
        match result {
            HostResult::Unavailable(msg) => assert!(msg.contains("0x"), "{msg}"),
            other => panic!("expected a reported fault, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

        let s = HostServices::defaults();
        for name in ["memcpy", "memset", "strlen", "strcmp", "__nnmusl_init_dso"] {
            assert!(s.get(name).is_some(), "missing {name}");
            assert!(s.claim(name).is_some());
        }
        assert!(s.get("nn::os::CreateThread").is_none());

    #[test]

        assert!(s.get("_ZN2nn2ro14UnprotectRelroEPKv").is_some());
        assert!(s.claim("_ZN2nn2ro12ProtectRelroEPKvS2_S2_").unwrap().contains("flat"));
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-boot/src/imports.rs`:

```rs
//! Import discovery from the module's own dynamic-link metadata.
//!
//! A retail NSO carries everything needed to name every external symbol it
//! calls: `MOD0` in `.rodata` points at an ELF-style dynamic array, whose
//! `DT_SYMTAB`, `DT_STRTAB` and `DT_JMPREL` tables describe each jump slot by
//! name. Reading them is what turns "branched to address zero" into "called
//! `nn::os::LockMutex`".
//!
//! `MOD0` stores its fields relative to the `MOD0` structure itself, not to the
//! module base. That detail is the difference between finding the dynamic array
//! and reading garbage, so it is applied explicitly here.

use crate::Module;
use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const DT_NULL: u64 = 0;
const DT_PLTRELSZ: u64 = 2;
const DT_PLTGOT: u64 = 3;
const DT_HASH: u64 = 4;
const DT_STRTAB: u64 = 5;
const DT_SYMTAB: u64 = 6;
const DT_RELA: u64 = 7;
const DT_RELASZ: u64 = 8;
const DT_SYMENT: u64 = 11;
const DT_STRSZ: u64 = 10;
const DT_JMPREL: u64 = 23;
const DT_INIT: u64 = 12;
const DT_FINI: u64 = 13;
const DT_INIT_ARRAY: u64 = 25;
const DT_INIT_ARRAYSZ: u64 = 27;
const DT_RELRSZ: u64 = 35;
const DT_RELR: u64 = 36;

/// One external symbol the module imports, addressed through a jump slot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Import {
    pub slot: u64,
    pub name: String,
    /// Raw ELF relocation type, kept so `R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT` and data imports
    /// can be told apart later.
    pub reloc: u32,
}

/// A symbol the module defines and exports, such as `nnMain`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Export {
    pub addr: u64,
    pub size: u64,
    pub name: String,
    /// ELF symbol type: 1 object, 2 function.
    pub kind: u8,
}

/// Everything the dynamic table says about this module.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct ImportTable {
    pub mod0: Option<u64>,
    pub dynamic: Option<u64>,
    pub symtab: Option<u64>,
    pub strtab: Option<u64>,
    pub jmprel: Option<u64>,
    pub got: Option<u64>,
    pub bss_start: Option<u64>,
    pub bss_end: Option<u64>,
    pub jumps: Vec<Import>,
    /// Symbols the module defines, sorted by address.
    pub exports: Vec<Export>,
    pub init: Option<u64>,
    pub fini: Option<u64>,
    /// `DT_INIT_ARRAY` and its entry count.
    pub init_array: Option<(u64, u64)>,
    /// Data-symbol relocations (vtables, typeinfo) that would need the other
    /// module's data to satisfy.
    pub data_imports: usize,
    pub relative_relocs: usize,
    /// `R_AARCH64_RELATIVE` fixups as (slot, addend). With the image at base
    /// zero, the loader writes the addend itself into the slot.
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub relatives: Vec<(u64, u64)>,
    /// Slots listed by the compact `DT_RELR` table: each holds a link-time
    /// address, to which the loader adds the load base.
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub relr: Vec<u64>,
    /// Named data relocations (`R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT`, `R_AARCH64_ABS64`) as
    /// (slot, symbol, addend): pointers to another module's objects.
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub data_binds: Vec<(u64, String, u64)>,
    /// Reasons a table could not be read, so a partial result never looks whole.
    pub notes: Vec<String>,
}

impl ImportTable {
    /// Address of an exported symbol by exact name.
    pub fn export(&self, name: &str) -> Option<u64> {
        self.exports.iter().find(|e| e.name == name).map(|e| e.addr)
    }

    /// Slot address to symbol name, for reporting.
    pub fn by_slot(&self) -> BTreeMap<u64, String> {
        self.jumps.iter().map(|i| (i.slot, i.name.clone())).collect()
    }

    pub fn name_at(&self, slot: u64) -> Option<&str> {
        self.jumps
            .iter()
            .find(|i| i.slot == slot)
            .map(|i| i.name.as_str())
    }
}

/// A read-only view over the module image that maps guest addresses onto the
/// segment that contains them.
struct View<'a> {
    segments: [(u64, &'a [u8]); 3],
}

impl<'a> View<'a> {
    fn new(module: &'a Module) -> View<'a> {
        View {
            segments: [
                (0, module.text.as_slice()),
                (module.rodata_addr, module.rodata.as_slice()),
                (module.data_addr, module.data.as_slice()),
            ],
        }
    }

    fn slice(&self, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
        for (base, bytes) in self.segments {
            if bytes.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let end = base + bytes.len() as u64;
            if addr >= base && addr + len as u64 <= end {
                let off = (addr - base) as usize;
                return Some(&bytes[off..off + len]);
            }
        }
        None
    }

    fn u8(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<u8> {
        self.slice(addr, 1).map(|b| b[0])
    }

    fn u16(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<u16> {
        self.slice(addr, 2).map(|b| u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]]))
    }

    fn u32(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<u32> {
        self.slice(addr, 4)
            .map(|b| u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))
    }

    fn u64(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.slice(addr, 8).map(|b| {
            let mut v = [0u8; 8];
            v.copy_from_slice(b);
            u64::from_le_bytes(v)
        })
    }

    fn cstr(&self, addr: u64, max: usize) -> Option<String> {
        for (base, bytes) in self.segments {
            if bytes.is_empty() || addr < base {
                continue;
            }
            let off = usize::try_from(addr - base).ok()?;
            if off >= bytes.len() {
                continue;
            }
            // Clamp to the segment: a name at the end of .rodata is short, not
            // missing, and asking for a fixed window would reject it.
            let avail = &bytes[off..(off + max).min(bytes.len())];
            let end = avail.iter().position(|b| *b == 0)?;
            return Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&avail[..end]).to_string());
        }
        None
    }
}

/// Locate `MOD0` and read the dynamic table it points at.
pub fn read(module: &Module) -> ImportTable {
    let view = View::new(module);
    let mut table = ImportTable::default();

    let Some(mod0) = find_mod0(&view, module) else {
        table.notes.push("no MOD0 structure in .rodata".to_string());
        return table;
    };
    table.mod0 = Some(mod0);

    // MOD0 fields are offsets from the MOD0 structure itself.
    let field = |offset: u64| view.u32(mod0 + offset).map(|v| mod0.wrapping_add(v as u64));
    let Some(dynamic) = field(4) else {
        table.notes.push("MOD0 is truncated".to_string());
        return table;
    };
    table.dynamic = Some(dynamic);
    table.bss_start = field(8);
    table.bss_end = field(0x0C);

    let mut tags: BTreeMap<u64, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
    for i in 0..256u64 {
        let at = dynamic + i * 16;
        let (Some(tag), Some(value)) = (view.u64(at), view.u64(at + 8)) else {
            table.notes.push(format!("dynamic array truncated at 0x{at:x}"));
            break;
        };
        if tag == DT_NULL {
            break;
        }
        tags.entry(tag).or_insert(value);
    }
    if tags.is_empty() {
        table.notes.push("dynamic array is empty".to_string());
        return table;
    }

    table.symtab = tags.get(&DT_SYMTAB).copied();
    table.strtab = tags.get(&DT_STRTAB).copied();
    table.jmprel = tags.get(&DT_JMPREL).copied();
    table.got = tags.get(&DT_PLTGOT).copied();
    let strsz = tags.get(&DT_STRSZ).copied().unwrap_or(0) as usize;
    let syment = tags.get(&DT_SYMENT).copied().unwrap_or(24);

    let (Some(symtab), Some(strtab)) = (table.symtab, table.strtab) else {
        table.notes.push("dynamic table has no symbol or string table".to_string());
        return table;
    };
    if syment != 24 {
        table
            .notes
            .push(format!("unexpected symbol entry size {syment}"));
    }

    let symbol_name = |index: u64| -> Option<String> {
        let name_off = view.u32(symtab + index * syment)? as u64;
        if strsz > 0 && name_off >= strsz as u64 {
            return None;
        }
        view.cstr(strtab + name_off, 512)
    };

    if let (Some(jmprel), Some(size)) = (table.jmprel, tags.get(&DT_PLTRELSZ).copied()) {
        for i in 0..size / 24 {
            let at = jmprel + i * 24;
            let (Some(offset), Some(info)) = (view.u64(at), view.u64(at + 8)) else {
                break;
            };
            let symbol = info >> 32;
            let reloc = (info & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32;
            if symbol == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(name) = symbol_name(symbol) {
                table.jumps.push(Import { slot: offset, name, reloc });
            }
        }
        table.jumps.sort_by_key(|i| i.slot);
    } else {
        table.notes.push("no jump-slot relocation table".to_string());
    }

    // The general relocation table names the data symbols (C++ vtables and
    // typeinfo for the exception runtime) and counts relative fixups.
    if let (Some(rela), Some(size)) = (tags.get(&DT_RELA).copied(), tags.get(&DT_RELASZ).copied()) {
        for i in 0..size / 24 {
            let at = rela + i * 24;
            let Some(info) = view.u64(at + 8) else { break };
            let reloc = (info & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32;
            let symbol = info >> 32;
            match reloc {
                1027 => {
                    // R_AARCH64_RELATIVE
                    table.relative_relocs += 1;
                    if let (Some(offset), Some(addend)) = (view.u64(at), view.u64(at + 16)) {
                        table.relatives.push((offset, addend));
                    }
                }
                1025 | 257 if symbol != 0 => {
                    table.data_imports += 1;
                    if let (Some(offset), Some(addend), Some(name)) = (view.u64(at), view.u64(at + 16), symbol_name(symbol)) {
                        table.data_binds.push((offset, name, addend));
                    }
                }
                _ if symbol != 0 => table.data_imports += 1,
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    // DT_RELR: an address entry relocates one slot and sets the cursor after
    // it; a bitmap entry (low bit set) relocates the following 63 slots whose
    // bits are set, then advances the cursor past them.
    if let (Some(relr), Some(size)) = (tags.get(&DT_RELR).copied(), tags.get(&DT_RELRSZ).copied()) {
        let mut cursor = 0u64;
        for i in 0..size / 8 {
            let Some(entry) = view.u64(relr + i * 8) else { break };
            if entry & 1 == 0 {
                table.relr.push(entry);
                cursor = entry + 8;
            } else {
                let mut bits = entry >> 1;
                let mut at = cursor;
                while bits != 0 {
                    if bits & 1 != 0 {
                        table.relr.push(at);
                    }
                    bits >>= 1;
                    at += 8;
                }
                cursor += 63 * 8;
            }
        }
        table.relative_relocs += table.relr.len();
    }
    table.init = tags.get(&DT_INIT).copied();
    table.fini = tags.get(&DT_FINI).copied();
    if let (Some(at), Some(size)) = (tags.get(&DT_INIT_ARRAY).copied(), tags.get(&DT_INIT_ARRAYSZ).copied()) {
        table.init_array = Some((at, size / 8));
    }

    // The symbol count comes from the SysV hash table's chain length. Without
    // one, the string table conventionally follows the symbol table.
    let count = tags
        .get(&DT_HASH)
        .and_then(|&h| view.u32(h + 4))
        .map(|n| n as u64)
        .or_else(|| (strtab > symtab).then(|| (strtab - symtab) / syment));
    match count {
        Some(count) => {
            for i in 1..count.min(1 << 20) {
                let at = symtab + i * syment;
                let (Some(info), Some(shndx), Some(value), Some(size)) =
                    (view.u8(at + 4), view.u16(at + 6), view.u64(at + 8), view.u64(at + 16))
                else {
                    break;
                };
                if shndx == 0 || value == 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(name) = symbol_name(i) {
                    table.exports.push(Export { addr: value, size, name, kind: info & 0xF });
                }
            }
            table.exports.sort_by_key(|e| e.addr);
        }
        None => table.notes.push("symbol count unknown; exports not read".to_string()),
    }

    if tags.get(&DT_HASH).is_none() && table.jumps.is_empty() {
        table.notes.push("no symbol hash table to validate names against".to_string());
    }

    table
}

fn find_mod0(view: &View, module: &Module) -> Option<u64> {
    let ro = &module.rodata;
    let mut at = 0usize;
    while at + 0x20 <= ro.len() {
        let hit = ro[at..].windows(4).position(|w| w == b"MOD0")? + at;
        // Validate: the dynamic pointer must land inside the image and the
        // first entries must be plain tags. A string match alone is not proof.
        if let Some(field) = view.u32(module.rodata_addr + hit as u64 + 4) {
            let base = module.rodata_addr + hit as u64;
            let dynamic = base.wrapping_add(field as u64);
            if dynamic >= 0x1000 && view.u64(dynamic).is_some() {
                return Some(base);
            }
        }
        at = hit + 4;
    }
    None
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn words_to_bytes(words: &[u32]) -> Vec<u8> {
        words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect()
    }

    /// Synthesize a module with MOD0, a dynamic array, two symbols and one jump
    /// slot, so the parse path is exercised without the game's data.
    fn synthetic() -> Module {
        // Four words of text put rodata at page one, so absolute table addresses
        // below are relative to that base.
        const RO: u64 = 0x1000;
        let text = words_to_bytes(&[0xD65F03C0; 4]);
        let mut ro = vec![0u8; 0x100];
        ro[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"MOD0");
        // dynamic array at MOD0+0x40
        let dynamic = 0x40u32;
        ro[4..8].copy_from_slice(&dynamic.to_le_bytes());
        let dyn_at = dynamic as usize;
        let entries = [
            (DT_SYMTAB, RO + 0xA0),
            (DT_STRTAB, RO + 0x200),
            (DT_STRSZ, 0x40),
            (DT_JMPREL, RO + 0x280),
            (DT_PLTRELSZ, 24),
            (DT_SYMENT, 24),
            (DT_NULL, 0),
        ];
        for (i, (tag, value)) in entries.iter().enumerate() {
            let at = dyn_at + i * 16;
            ro[at..at + 8].copy_from_slice(&tag.to_le_bytes());
            ro[at + 8..at + 16].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
        ro.resize(0x400, 0);
        // symbols at 0xA0: index 1 has name offset 8 in strtab
        let sym = 0xA0 + 24;
        ro[sym..sym + 4].copy_from_slice(&8u32.to_le_bytes()); // name at strtab+8
        // strtab at 0x200
        ro[0x200..0x200 + 4].copy_from_slice(b"\0nn\0");
        let name = b"nn::os::Test";
        ro[0x208..0x208 + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name);
        // jmprel at 0x280: slot 0x1234, symbol 1, type 1026
        let jmprel = 0x280;
        ro[jmprel..jmprel + 8].copy_from_slice(&0x1234u64.to_le_bytes());
        ro[jmprel + 8..jmprel + 16].copy_from_slice(&((1u64 << 32) | 1026).to_le_bytes());
        ro[jmprel + 16..jmprel + 24].copy_from_slice(&0i64.to_le_bytes());
        Module::new("test", text, ro, Vec::new())
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_a_jump_slot() {
        let m = synthetic();
        let table = read(&m);
        assert_eq!(table.jumps.len(), 1, "{:?}", table.notes);
        assert_eq!(table.jumps[0].slot, 0x1234);
        assert_eq!(table.jumps[0].name, "nn::os::Test");
        assert_eq!(table.name_at(0x1234), Some("nn::os::Test"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_metadata_is_reported_not_invented() {
        let m = Module::new("empty", vec![0u8; 0x10], vec![0u8; 0x10], Vec::new());
        let table = read(&m);
        assert!(table.jumps.is_empty());
        assert!(table.notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("MOD0")));
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-boot/src/kernel.rs`:

```rs
//! Supervisor calls: the kernel interface under nnSdk's own code.
//!
//! Most of the title's system calls go through the host's `nn::*` services.
//! Library code that runs as the title's own code (the C++ runtime in `sdk`)
//! reaches the kernel directly with `svc`. The calls served here are the ones
//! that code needs: lock and condition-variable arbitration on guest memory,
//! the system tick, thread identity, sleeping and debug output.
//!
//! Lock words follow the kernel's protocol: 0 when free, otherwise the owner's
//! handle, with bit 30 set while other threads wait. A waiter blocks in the
//! host scheduler and takes the lock once its word is free; an unlock frees the
//! word, which wakes them.

use crate::hle::{read_bytes, write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;

/// Bit 30 of a lock word: other threads are waiting.
const WAITERS: u32 = 0x4000_0000;
/// Kernel result codes.
const OK: u64 = 0;
const TIMED_OUT: u64 = 0xEA01;

fn r32(state: &State, a: u64) -> Result<u32, HostResult> {
    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes(read_bytes(state, a, 4)?.try_into().unwrap()))
}

fn w32(state: &mut State, a: u64, v: u32) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    write_bytes(state, a, &v.to_le_bytes())
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($e:expr) => {
        match $e {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(e) => return e,
        }
    };
}

/// The running thread's handle, from its thread-local region.
fn my_handle(state: &State) -> u32 {
    r32(state, state.tpidrro + crate::sched::TLS_HANDLE).unwrap_or(0)
}

/// `svc 0x1A ArbitrateLock(ownerHandle, address, tag)`: wait until the lock at
/// `address` is free, then take it with `tag`.
fn arbitrate_lock(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (addr, tag) = (state.x[1], state.x[2] as u32);
    let word = t!(r32(state, addr));
    if word & !WAITERS == 0 {
        t!(w32(state, addr, tag | (word & WAITERS)));
        return HostResult::Returned(OK);
    }
    if word & !WAITERS == tag {
        // Already ours (the owner released and handed it over).
        return HostResult::Returned(OK);
    }
    if state.x[0] != 0 {
        state.host.log.push(format!(
            "kernel: lock 0x{addr:x} held by 0x{:x} (word 0x{word:x}); thread 0x{tag:x} waits",
            state.x[0] as u32
        ));
        state.x[0] = 0;
    }
    HostResult::Block { resume: arbitrate_lock, timed: false }
}

/// `svc 0x1B ArbitrateUnlock(address)`: free the lock so a waiter can take it.
fn arbitrate_unlock(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let addr = state.x[0];
    // Waiters re-check when the scheduler next considers them.
    t!(w32(state, addr, 0));
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// Condition variables are keyed by guest address; a signal counts as a
/// wake-up token the waiters take in turn.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Keys {
    tokens: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, u64>,
}

fn keys<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Keys) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<Keys, R>(f)
}

/// `svc 0x1C WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic(mutexAddr, key, tag, timeoutNs)`:
/// release the mutex, wait for a signal on `key`, then retake the mutex.
fn wait_key(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (mutex, key) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    // First entry: release the mutex and mark this thread as waiting.
    let word = t!(r32(state, mutex));
    if word & !WAITERS == my_handle(state) {
        t!(w32(state, mutex, 0));
    }
    keys(state, |k| {
        k.tokens.entry(key).or_insert(0);
    });
    wait_key_resume(state)
}

fn wait_key_resume(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (mutex, key, tag, timeout) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2] as u32, state.x[3] as i64);
    let woken = keys(state, |k| match k.tokens.get_mut(&key) {
        Some(n) if *n > 0 => {
            *n -= 1;
            true
        }
        _ => false,
    });
    if !woken {
        if timeout == 0 {
            return HostResult::Returned(TIMED_OUT);
        }
        return HostResult::Block { resume: wait_key_resume, timed: timeout > 0 };
    }
    let word = t!(r32(state, mutex));
    if word & !WAITERS != 0 && word & !WAITERS != tag {
        return HostResult::Block { resume: retake_mutex, timed: false };
    }
    t!(w32(state, mutex, tag));
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

fn retake_mutex(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (mutex, tag) = (state.x[0], state.x[2] as u32);
    let word = t!(r32(state, mutex));
    if word & !WAITERS != 0 && word & !WAITERS != tag {
        return HostResult::Block { resume: retake_mutex, timed: false };
    }
    t!(w32(state, mutex, tag));
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// `svc 0x1D SignalProcessWideKey(key, count)`: wake `count` waiters, or all
/// of them for a negative count.
fn signal_key(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (key, count) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as i32);
    keys(state, |k| {
        let n = k.tokens.entry(key).or_insert(0);
        *n = if count < 0 { u32::MAX as u64 } else { *n + count as u64 };
    });
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// `svc 0x1E GetSystemTick()`.
fn get_system_tick(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(crate::threads::now_ticks())
}

/// `svc 0x0B SleepThread(ns)`: yields; the scheduler runs the others.
fn sleep_thread(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// `svc 0x27 OutputDebugString(str, len)`: kept in the host log.
fn output_debug_string(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (p, n) = (state.x[0], state.x[1].min(4096));
    if let Ok(b) = read_bytes(state, p, n) {
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&b).trim_end().to_string();
        state.host.log.push(format!("debug: {text}"));
    }
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

/// `svc 0x26 Break(reason, arg, size)`: the guest asked to stop.
fn break_(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Unavailable(format!("the guest called svcBreak (reason 0x{:x}, 0x{:x}, 0x{:x})", state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]))
}

/// `svc 0x25 GetThreadId(handle)`: returns the id in x1.
fn get_thread_id(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let handle = state.x[1] as u32;
    let me = my_handle(state);
    state.x[1] = if handle == 0xFFFF_8000 { me as u64 } else { handle as u64 };
    HostResult::Returned(OK)
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult, &'static str)] = &[
        ("svc:0xb", sleep_thread, "yields to the other guest threads"),
        ("svc:0x1a", arbitrate_lock, "waits until the lock word is free, then takes it"),
        ("svc:0x1b", arbitrate_unlock, "frees the lock word"),
        ("svc:0x1c", wait_key, "condition wait on a guest address"),
        ("svc:0x1d", signal_key, "condition signal on a guest address"),
        ("svc:0x1e", get_system_tick, "the host clock at 19.2 MHz"),
        ("svc:0x25", get_thread_id, "the thread's handle serves as its id"),
        ("svc:0x26", break_, "stops the run with the guest's reason"),
        ("svc:0x27", output_debug_string, "kept in the host log"),
    ];
    for (name, handler, claim) in table {
        s.register(name, *handler, claim);
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-boot/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! `ew-boot` — the whole-program dispatcher.
//!
//! `ew-lift` recovers one function at a time and `ew-lift`'s emitter returns to
//! a dispatcher at every edge that leaves a function. This crate is that
//! dispatcher, running the recovered code against a mapped module image so the
//! project can answer a question that static analysis cannot: what does the game
//! actually do when it starts, and where does it stop?
//!
//! Three properties are deliberate:
//!
//! * every stop is a typed reason with an address, so a blocker is a fact and
//!   not an opinion;
//! * memory is a flat buffer sized from the module image, and an access outside
//!   it is a fault reported with the address, never a silent zero;
//! * an instruction the decoder does not model stops the run. Nothing is skipped
//!   to make progress look better than it is.
//!
//! The runner uses the reference interpreter, not the emitted C. That is stated
//! plainly because it matters: the C emitter is verified function by function,
//! while this runner is the tool that exposes which function to look at next.

use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};
use ew_lift::{cfg, scan, Op, State};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
use std::path::Path;

pub mod alloc;
pub mod audio;
pub mod audio_update;
pub mod codec;
pub mod prepo;
pub mod movie;
pub mod cxx;
pub mod fs;
pub mod gfx;
pub mod hash;
pub mod hid;
pub mod hle;
pub mod imports;
pub mod kernel;
pub mod libc;
pub mod lmem;
pub mod math;
pub mod native;

/// A fast hasher for the run loop's integer keys (guest addresses and call
/// ids): a multiply and a rotate, as rustc's own FxHash. The standard
/// library's SipHash costs more than the work done per function entry.
#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FastHasher(u64);

impl std::hash::Hasher for FastHasher {
    fn finish(&self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
    fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        for &b in bytes {
            self.write_u64(b as u64);
        }
    }
    fn write_u64(&mut self, x: u64) {
        self.0 = (self.0.rotate_left(5) ^ x).wrapping_mul(0x51_7c_c1_b7_27_22_0a_95);
    }
    fn write_u32(&mut self, x: u32) {
        self.write_u64(x as u64);
    }
    fn write_usize(&mut self, x: usize) {
        self.write_u64(x as u64);
    }
}

pub type FastMap<K, V> = HashMap<K, V, std::hash::BuildHasherDefault<FastHasher>>;
pub type FastSet<K> = std::collections::HashSet<K, std::hash::BuildHasherDefault<FastHasher>>;
pub mod nvn;
pub mod nvn_mem;
pub mod nvn_tex;
pub mod nvn_win;
pub mod nvn_cmd;
pub mod nvn_state;
pub mod nvn_prog;
pub mod pmr;
pub mod sched;
pub mod services;
pub mod system;
pub mod threads;

pub use hle::{HostResult, HostServices};
pub use imports::{Import, ImportTable};

/// Guest stack size reserved below the module image.
pub const STACK_SIZE: u64 = 1 << 20;
/// Guest heap size reserved above the stack.
pub const HEAP_SIZE: u64 = 4 << 30;
/// Extra zero-filled room for `.bss` when the real size is unknown.
pub const BSS_SLACK: u64 = 4 << 20;

/// Return address installed in `x30` before entry. It is deliberately outside
/// any module image and page-aligned, so returning from the entry function is
/// unambiguous rather than looking like a jump into code.
pub const RETURN_SENTINEL: u64 = 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFC;
/// Room for host functions created at run time, such as NVN procedures.
const DYNAMIC_STUBS: u64 = 4096;

const PAGE: u64 = 0x1000;

/// Main-module imports a library may satisfy: the C++ standard library, whose
/// code is pure and self-contained. Everything else stays with the host
/// services, which name what they do not provide.
pub const LIBRARY_PREFIXES: &[&str] =
    &[
        "_ZNSt3__1", "_ZNKSt3__1", "_ZSt", "_ZTVNSt3__1", "_ZTINSt3__1", "_ZTSNSt3__1",
        "_ZN2nn4util", "_ZNK2nn4util",
        "_ZN2nn3hid20ControllerSupportArg",
        "_ZN2nn5audio", "_ZNK2nn5audio",
        "_ZN2nn5codec", "_ZNK2nn5codec",
        "__cxa_demangle", "__dynamic_cast", "qsort",
        "_ZNSt13exception_ptr", "_ZNKSt13exception_ptr",
    ];

/// Where a library module sits in guest memory.
struct Placed<'a> {
    module: &'a Module,
    base: u64,
}

fn align_up(value: u64, align: u64) -> u64 {
    (value + align - 1) & !(align - 1)
}

/// Title metadata from a `control.nacp`: the first title name and the display
/// version. Returns `None` for a file that is not a NACP.
pub fn read_nacp(path: &std::path::Path) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    let d = std::fs::read(path).ok()?;
    if d.len() < 0x4000 {
        return None;
    }
    let text = |b: &[u8]| {
        let end = b.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(b.len());
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..end]).into_owned()
    };
    let title = text(&d[0..0x200]);
    let version = text(&d[0x3060..0x3070]);
    (!version.is_empty()).then_some((title, version))
}

/// A decompressed module laid out at the addresses its code expects.
///
/// The text segment is placed at address 0. Nintendo's linker links NSO modules
/// against a zero base and applies load relocations at run time, so a zero base
/// keeps PC-relative references, and every unrelocated pointer stored in `.data`,
/// pointing at the right place.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Module {
    pub name: String,
    pub text: Vec<u8>,
    pub rodata: Vec<u8>,
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    pub rodata_addr: u64,
    pub data_addr: u64,
    /// `.bss` range from `MOD0` when the module carries one.
    pub bss_start: Option<u64>,
    pub bss_end: Option<u64>,
    /// Dynamic-link metadata: every external symbol this module calls.
    pub imports: ImportTable,
}

impl Module {
    pub fn new(name: &str, text: Vec<u8>, rodata: Vec<u8>, data: Vec<u8>) -> Module {
        let rodata_addr = align_up(text.len() as u64, PAGE);
        let data_addr = align_up(rodata_addr + rodata.len() as u64, PAGE);
        Module {
            name: name.to_string(),
            text,
            rodata,
            data,
            rodata_addr,
            data_addr,
            bss_start: None,
            bss_end: None,
            imports: ImportTable::default(),
        }
    }

    /// A module from decompressed segments, with its dynamic tables read.
    pub fn from_segments(name: &str, text: Vec<u8>, rodata: Vec<u8>, data: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Module> {
        if text.len() % 4 != 0 {
            bail!("text segment length {} is not a multiple of 4", text.len());
        }
        let mut module = Module::new(name, text, rodata, data);
        module.imports = imports::read(&module);
        module.bss_start = module.imports.bss_start;
        module.bss_end = module.imports.bss_end;
        Ok(module)
    }

    /// Load `text.bin`, `rodata.bin` and `data.bin` from a decoded module
    /// directory. `data.bin` is optional because a module can have no `.data`.
    pub fn from_dir(dir: &Path) -> Result<Module> {
        let name = dir
            .file_name()
            .map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "module".to_string());
        let text = std::fs::read(dir.join("text.bin"))
            .with_context(|| format!("reading {}", dir.join("text.bin").display()))?;
        let rodata = read_optional(&dir.join("rodata.bin"))?;
        let data = read_optional(&dir.join("data.bin"))?;
        if text.len() % 4 != 0 {
            bail!(
                "text segment length {} is not a multiple of 4 words",
                text.len()
            );
        }
        let mut module = Module::new(&name, text, rodata, data);
        module.imports = imports::read(&module);
        module.bss_start = module.imports.bss_start;
        module.bss_end = module.imports.bss_end;
        Ok(module)
    }

    /// Best entry address for this module.
    ///
    /// A retail NSO program module starts `.text` with a 0x40 byte header rather
    /// than code: a flag word, the address of `MOD0`, and a `ret` stub. When that
    /// pattern is present the entry stub follows the header, which is where the
    /// loader starts the main thread. Modules that begin with code return 0.
    /// The calls nnSdk's `nn::init::Start` makes into a program module, in
    /// order, as far as this module provides them: `nninitStartup` (which sets
    /// up the allocator the static constructors use), the module's own entry
    /// (relocation protection and C++ static initialisation), then `nnMain`.
    pub fn startup_sequence(&self) -> Vec<(String, u64)> {
        let mut seq = Vec::new();
        if let Some(a) = self.imports.export("nninitStartup") {
            seq.push(("nninitStartup".to_string(), a));
        }
        seq.push(("module entry".to_string(), self.entry_hint()));
        if let Some(a) = self.imports.export("nnMain") {
            seq.push(("nnMain".to_string(), a));
        }
        seq
    }

    pub fn entry_hint(&self) -> u64 {
        if self.text.len() < 0x44 {
            return 0;
        }
        let first = u32::from_le_bytes([self.text[0], self.text[1], self.text[2], self.text[3]]);
        let decodes = !matches!(
            ew_lift::decode(first, 0),
            Op::Unsupported { .. } | Op::UnsupportedBitfield { .. }
        );
        if decodes {
            return 0;
        }
        // The header stores 32-bit image offsets, not 64-bit pointers.
        let mut raw = [0u8; 4];
        raw.copy_from_slice(&self.text[4..8]);
        let second = u32::from_le_bytes(raw) as u64;
        let ro_end = self.rodata_addr + self.rodata.len() as u64;
        if second >= self.rodata_addr && second < ro_end {
            return 0x40;
        }
        0
    }

    /// End of the loadable image: data end, or bss end when the module declares
    /// one past it.
    pub fn image_end(&self) -> u64 {
        let data_end = self.data_addr + self.data.len() as u64;
        match self.bss_end {
            Some(end) if end > data_end => end,
            _ => data_end,
        }
    }
}

fn read_optional(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    match std::fs::read(path) {
        Ok(bytes) => Ok(bytes),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(Vec::new()),
        Err(e) => Err(e).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", path.display())),
    }
}

/// How far to run, and how much detail to keep.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct BootOptions {
    /// Guest address execution starts at. Text starts at 0, which is where the
    /// loader enters an NSO program module.
    pub entry: u64,
    /// Hard instruction budget for the whole run.
    pub max_steps: u64,
    /// Hard cap on dispatcher iterations (function entries).
    pub max_dispatches: usize,
    /// Instruction cap for one recovered function.
    pub max_insns: usize,
    /// Number of event lines to keep for the human-readable trace.
    pub trace: usize,
    /// Initial `x0`. The loader passes a launch-parameter pointer; callers that
    /// do not have one pass 0 and read the fault instead of guessing.
    pub x0: u64,
    /// Functions to call, in order, each time the previous one returns. This is
    /// how the run follows nnSdk's `nn::init::Start`: module initialisation,
    /// then `nnMain`, on one continuous guest state.
    pub then: Vec<(String, u64)>,
    /// Name of the first phase, for the report.
    pub entry_name: String,
    /// Bytes of guest heap arena. The memory is zero-initialised, which the
    /// host OS commits lazily, so an untouched gigabyte costs nothing.
    pub heap_bytes: u64,
    /// The user's extracted romfs, mounted read-only by `nn::fs::MountRom`.
    pub romfs: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    /// Writable directory backing `nn::fs::MountSaveData`.
    pub save_dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    /// System settings for the host services: `language`, `display_version`,
    /// `user_name`.
    pub settings: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Capture the guest state the first time the dispatcher reaches this
    /// address, into `snapshot_dir`, then log `snapshot_steps` instructions.
    pub snapshot_at: Option<u64>,
    pub snapshot_dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    pub snapshot_steps: usize,
    /// Set from another thread to stop the run at the next dispatch.
    pub cancel: Option<std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>>,
    /// Updated with the instruction count as the run proceeds, for a UI.
    pub progress: Option<std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>>,
    /// The game's code compiled ahead of time (`ew-native`): run natively
    /// wherever it has the block, interpreted everywhere else.
    pub native: Option<std::sync::Arc<native::Native>>,
    /// Other modules of the program (the title's `sdk`), loaded after the
    /// main image. Their exports satisfy the main module's imports that the
    /// host does not serve and whose names start with one of
    /// [`LIBRARY_PREFIXES`]; their own imports bind to the main module first.
    pub libraries: Vec<Module>,
    /// Run each library's DT_INIT before the program. Off by default: nnSdk's
    /// initialisers build on its own `nn::os` start-up, which the host serves
    /// instead, so library code is used for routines that need no statics.
    pub init_libraries: bool,
    /// Addresses to watch: each time a function is entered at one of them,
    /// its first five arguments and caller go to the host log (up to 64 each).
    pub watch: Vec<u64>,
}

impl Default for BootOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        BootOptions {
            entry: 0,
            max_steps: 20_000_000,
            max_dispatches: usize::MAX,
            max_insns: 1024,
            trace: 64,
            x0: 0,
            then: Vec::new(),
            entry_name: "entry".to_string(),
            heap_bytes: HEAP_SIZE,
            romfs: None,
            save_dir: None,
            settings: Default::default(),
            snapshot_at: None,
            snapshot_dir: None,
            snapshot_steps: 20_000,
            cancel: None,
            progress: None,
            native: None,
            libraries: Vec::new(),
            init_libraries: false,
            watch: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// Why the run stopped.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Stop {
    /// The entry function returned to the sentinel address.
    EntryReturned,
    /// Execution left the text segment: an import, a call into another module or
    /// a computed pointer that is not code.
    LeftText {
        pc: u64,
        from: u64,
        /// What the address points at, when it is inside a mapped segment.
        segment: Option<String>,
        /// First eight bytes at the address when it is inside the image.
        word: Option<u64>,
    },
    /// The decoder does not model the instruction at `pc`.
    Unsupported { pc: u64, word: u32 },
    /// The interpreter rejected the instruction, usually a guest memory fault.
    Fault { pc: u64, message: String },
    /// The guest set its own halt flag (a `brk` style stop).
    Halted { pc: u64, reason: String },
    /// The run reached the instruction budget with code still executing.
    StepBudget,
    /// The run reached the dispatch budget.
    DispatchBudget,
    /// Every live guest thread waits on something only another thread could
    /// provide. `waits` names each waiter and the call it is parked in.
    Deadlock { waits: String },
    /// Every guest thread, including the main thread, has exited.
    AllThreadsExited,
    /// The caller cancelled the run.
    Cancelled,
    /// One function ran its per-entry budget without leaving, which means a spin
    /// loop or a block set that does not contain the exit.
    SpinLimit { pc: u64 },
    /// The guest called an imported function. `import` is the symbol name read
    /// from the module's own dynamic table, so the blocker is always named.
    Blocked {
        import: String,
        pc: u64,
        from: u64,
        /// x0..x7 at the call, which is usually enough to see what was wanted.
        args: [u64; 8],
    },
    /// An implemented host function rejected the call, usually a bad pointer.
    HostFault {
        import: String,
        from: u64,
        message: String,
    },
}

impl Stop {
    /// One line a human can act on.
    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Stop::EntryReturned => "the entry function returned".to_string(),
            Stop::Deadlock { waits } => format!("deadlock: every guest thread is waiting ({waits})"),
            Stop::AllThreadsExited => "every guest thread exited".to_string(),
            Stop::Cancelled => "cancelled by the user".to_string(),
            Stop::LeftText { pc, from, segment, word } => {
                let mut s = format!("left the text segment at 0x{pc:x} (from 0x{from:x})");
                match segment {
                    Some(seg) => s.push_str(&format!(", inside {seg}")),
                    None => s.push_str(", outside the module image"),
                }
                if let Some(w) = word {
                    s.push_str(&format!(", holding 0x{w:016x}"));
                }
                s
            }
            Stop::Unsupported { pc, word } => {
                format!("unsupported instruction 0x{word:08x} at 0x{pc:x}")
            }
            Stop::Fault { pc, message } => format!("{message} at 0x{pc:x}"),
            Stop::Halted { pc, reason } => format!("guest halted at 0x{pc:x}: {reason}"),
            Stop::StepBudget => "instruction budget exhausted".to_string(),
            Stop::DispatchBudget => "dispatch budget exhausted".to_string(),
            Stop::SpinLimit { pc } => {
                format!("no control-flow exit from the block set at 0x{pc:x} within the per-entry budget")
            }
            Stop::Blocked { import, from, .. } => {
                format!("called {import} at 0x{from:x}, which the runtime does not implement")
            }
            Stop::HostFault { import, from, message } => {
                format!("host {import} failed at 0x{from:x}: {message}")
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A call or return the dispatcher resolved.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct TransferRecord {
    pub from: u64,
    pub to: u64,
    /// `call`, `return` or `branch`.
    pub kind: &'static str,
}

/// A function that owns a large share of the executed instructions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct HotFunction {
    pub addr: u64,
    pub entries: u64,
    pub instructions: u64,
}

/// One imported function the guest called.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ImportCall {
    pub name: String,
    pub calls: u64,
    pub first_from: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct BootReport {
    pub module: String,
    pub entry: u64,
    pub steps: u64,
    pub dispatches: u64,
    /// Dispatches run by the native library, and the times it handed an
    /// address back to the interpreter.
    pub native_dispatches: u64,
    pub native_halts: u64,
    pub distinct_functions: usize,
    pub calls: u64,
    pub returns: u64,
    pub branches: u64,
    pub max_depth: u32,
    pub final_sp: u64,
    pub stack_low: u64,
    pub stop: Stop,
    pub trace: Vec<String>,
    pub hot: Vec<HotFunction>,
    pub externals: Vec<TransferRecord>,
    pub memory_bytes: u64,
    /// Imported symbols found in the module's dynamic table.
    pub import_count: usize,
    /// Imports the run reached, in call order, with call counts.
    pub import_calls: Vec<ImportCall>,
    pub bss_bytes: u64,
    /// Host functions the run executed successfully.
    pub host_calls: u64,
    /// Host functions available to this run.
    pub host_implemented: usize,
    /// Startup phases that ran to completion, in order.
    pub phases: Vec<String>,
    /// The phase that was running when the run stopped.
    pub phase: String,
    /// Relative relocation slots whose stored value differed from the addend.
    pub relocations_changed: u64,
    /// Guest threads that ran, including the main thread, and context switches.
    pub threads: u64,
    pub switches: u64,
    /// The last events before the stop (host calls with arguments and results,
    /// calls and returns), oldest first.
    pub recent: Vec<String>,
    /// Host-level events (files opened, mounts), in order.
    pub host_log: Vec<String>,
    /// Every guest thread at the stop.
    pub thread_states: Vec<String>,
    /// Names the game resolved to host functions at run time (NVN procedures),
    /// in the order it first asked for them.
    pub resolved: Vec<String>,
    /// Image slots (data and bss) holding a run-time host function's address,
    /// with that function's name: the game's own procedure tables.
    pub proc_slots: Vec<(u64, String)>,
}

impl BootReport {
    /// A short, honest summary suitable for a UI banner.
    pub fn headline(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "{} instructions, {} function entries, {} distinct functions, stopped because {}",
            self.steps,
            self.dispatches,
            self.distinct_functions,
            self.stop.describe()
        )
    }
}

/// One recovered function plus its instruction index, held for the whole run.
struct Cached {
    compiled: ew_lift::interpreter::Compiled,
}

/// Run the module from `opts.entry` for as long as the guest code allows, using
/// the default host services.
pub fn boot(module: &Module, opts: &BootOptions) -> Result<BootReport> {
    boot_with(module, opts, &HostServices::defaults())
}

/// Run with an explicit set of host services.
pub fn boot_with(
    module: &Module,
    opts: &BootOptions,
    services: &HostServices,
) -> Result<BootReport> {
    let text = &module.text;
    if opts.entry % 4 != 0 || opts.entry as usize + 4 > text.len() {
        bail!("entry 0x{:x} is not inside the text segment", opts.entry);
    }

    // Layout: image, import stubs, stack, heap. Everything is inside one flat
    // buffer, so a read or write outside it faults in the interpreter with the
    // address that caused it.
    // Libraries follow the main image, each on a 1 MiB boundary.
    let mut next_base = align_up(module.image_end(), 0x10_0000);
    let placed: Vec<Placed> = opts
        .libraries
        .iter()
        .map(|m| {
            let base = next_base;
            next_base = align_up(base + m.image_end(), 0x10_0000);
            Placed { module: m, base }
        })
        .collect();
    let image_end = if placed.is_empty() { align_up(module.image_end(), PAGE) } else { next_base };
    // Every symbol each module defines, at its loaded address. The main module
    // comes first, so a symbol it defines (operator new, for one) wins.
    let mut symbols: HashMap<String, u64> = HashMap::new();
    for e in &module.imports.exports {
        symbols.entry(e.name.clone()).or_insert(e.addr);
    }
    for p in &placed {
        for e in &p.module.imports.exports {
            symbols.entry(e.name.clone()).or_insert(p.base + e.addr);
        }
    }
    let library_symbol = |name: &str| -> Option<u64> {
        if module.imports.export(name).is_some() || !LIBRARY_PREFIXES.iter().any(|p| name.starts_with(p)) {
            return None;
        }
        placed.iter().find_map(|p| p.module.imports.export(name).map(|a| p.base + a))
    };
    // Main imports the host does not serve go to a library when one has them.
    let main_binds: Vec<Option<u64>> = module
        .imports
        .jumps
        .iter()
        .map(|j| if services.get(&j.name).is_some() { None } else { library_symbol(&j.name) })
        .collect();
    // Library imports: another module's symbol, or a host stub by name.
    let mut lib_binds: Vec<(u64, Option<u64>, String)> = Vec::new();
    for p in &placed {
        for j in &p.module.imports.jumps {
            let target = if services.get(&j.name).is_some() { None } else { symbols.get(&j.name).copied() };
            lib_binds.push((p.base + j.slot, target, j.name.clone()));
        }
    }
    let jumps = &module.imports.jumps;
    // Sixteen bytes per stub keeps every entry distinct and aligned, and one
    // final stub stands for a slot the guest reached without a binding.
    // Host functions with no import slot (vtable entries of host-built
    // objects) get stubs after the imports.
    let names: Vec<String> = jumps
        .iter()
        .map(|j| j.name.clone())
        .chain(pmr::SYNTHETIC.iter().map(|n| n.to_string()))
        .chain(lib_binds.iter().filter(|b| b.1.is_none()).map(|b| b.2.clone()))
        .collect();
    let stub_bytes = align_up((names.len() as u64 + 1 + DYNAMIC_STUBS) * 16, PAGE);
    let stub_base = image_end;
    let unresolved_stub = stub_base + names.len() as u64 * 16;
    let stack_base = stub_base + stub_bytes;
    let stack_top = stack_base + STACK_SIZE;
    let heap_base = stack_top;
    let memory_bytes = align_up(heap_base + opts.heap_bytes, PAGE);
    let mut memory = vec![0u8; memory_bytes as usize];
    memory[..text.len()].copy_from_slice(text);
    let ro = module.rodata_addr as usize;
    memory[ro..ro + module.rodata.len()].copy_from_slice(&module.rodata);
    let da = module.data_addr as usize;
    memory[da..da + module.data.len()].copy_from_slice(&module.data);
    for p in &placed {
        let m = p.module;
        let b = p.base as usize;
        memory[b..b + m.text.len()].copy_from_slice(&m.text);
        let ro = b + m.rodata_addr as usize;
        memory[ro..ro + m.rodata.len()].copy_from_slice(&m.rodata);
        let da = b + m.data_addr as usize;
        memory[da..da + m.data.len()].copy_from_slice(&m.data);
        for &(slot, addend) in &m.imports.relatives {
            write_u64(&mut memory, p.base + slot, p.base + addend);
        }
        for &slot in &m.imports.relr {
            let at = (p.base + slot) as usize;
            if at + 8 <= memory.len() {
                let v = u64::from_le_bytes(memory[at..at + 8].try_into().unwrap());
                write_u64(&mut memory, p.base + slot, v + p.base);
            }
        }
    }

    // Apply the relative relocations exactly as rtld does with a zero load
    // base: the slot receives the addend. Count how many slots this changed, so
    // the report shows whether the image depended on it.
    let mut relocated = 0u64;
    for &(slot, addend) in &module.imports.relatives {
        let at = slot as usize;
        if at + 8 <= memory.len() {
            let mut old = [0u8; 8];
            old.copy_from_slice(&memory[at..at + 8]);
            if u64::from_le_bytes(old) != addend {
                relocated += 1;
            }
            write_u64(&mut memory, slot, addend);
        }
    }

    // Bind every jump slot to its own stub. This is the loader's job in the real
    // system; here the stub address is how the dispatcher recognises an import
    // call and can name it instead of jumping to zero.
    for (i, import) in jumps.iter().enumerate() {
        let target = main_binds[i].unwrap_or(stub_base + i as u64 * 16);
        write_u64(&mut memory, import.slot, target);
    }
    let mut lib_stub = jumps.len() + pmr::SYNTHETIC.len();
    for (slot, target, _) in &lib_binds {
        let addr = match target {
            Some(a) => *a,
            None => {
                lib_stub += 1;
                stub_base + (lib_stub - 1) as u64 * 16
            }
        };
        write_u64(&mut memory, *slot, addr);
    }
    // Named data pointers between modules (vtables, typeinfo, globals).
    let mut data_bound = 0u64;
    for (base, m) in std::iter::once((0u64, module)).chain(placed.iter().map(|p| (p.base, p.module))) {
        for (slot, name, addend) in &m.imports.data_binds {
            if let Some(a) = symbols.get(name) {
                write_u64(&mut memory, base + slot, a + addend);
                data_bound += 1;
            }
        }
        if base != 0 {
            if let Some(got) = m.imports.got {
                write_u64(&mut memory, base + got + 0x10, unresolved_stub);
            }
        }
    }
    let _ = data_bound;
    // GOT[2] is the lazy resolver every unbound slot starts at. Point it at a
    // stub that reports an unresolved binding rather than branching to zero.
    if let Some(got) = module.imports.got {
        write_u64(&mut memory, got + 0x10, unresolved_stub);
    }
    let stub_index: HashMap<u64, usize> = names
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, _)| (stub_base + i as u64 * 16, i))
        .collect();

    let mut state = State { mem: memory, ..State::default() };
    // The heap doubles as the page arena the `nn::os` memory services hand out
    // from, so an allocation is real guest memory the interpreter can load from.
    state.host.alloc_next = heap_base;
    state.host.alloc_end = heap_base + opts.heap_bytes;
    state.host.program_size = image_end;
    state.host.dyn_base = unresolved_stub + 16;
    state.host.dyn_capacity = DYNAMIC_STUBS;
    state.host.romfs_root = opts.romfs.clone();
    state.host.save_root = opts.save_dir.clone();
    state.host.settings = opts.settings.clone();
    state.host.stack_size = STACK_SIZE;
    let synthetic_stubs: Vec<u64> = (0..pmr::SYNTHETIC.len())
        .map(|i| stub_base + (jumps.len() + i) as u64 * 16)
        .collect();
    let exports: Vec<(&str, Option<u64>)> = ["_Znwm", "_ZnwmSt11align_val_t", "_ZdlPv", "_ZdlPvSt11align_val_t"]
        .iter()
        .map(|n| (*n, module.imports.export(n)))
        .collect();
    // Every symbol the module defines is available to host services that
    // forward into the game's own code (operator new, for one).
    for e in &module.imports.exports {
        state.host.named.insert(format!("export.{}", e.name), e.addr);
    }
    // Library exports too, where the main module does not define the name, so
    // a host service can observe a call and then forward it to the library.
    for p in &placed {
        for e in &p.module.imports.exports {
            state.host.named.entry(format!("export.{}", e.name)).or_insert(p.base + e.addr);
        }
    }
    if let Err(e) = pmr::install(&mut state, &synthetic_stubs, &exports) {
        bail!("could not build the host's libc++ objects: {e}");
    }
    state.sp = (stack_top - 0x100) & !0xF;
    state.x[30] = RETURN_SENTINEL;
    state.x[0] = opts.x0;
    state.pc = opts.entry;

    // Code of every module, at its loaded address, for the recompiler.
    let code_end = placed.iter().map(|p| p.base + p.module.text.len() as u64).max().unwrap_or(0).max(text.len() as u64);
    let code_buf: Vec<u8> = if placed.is_empty() { Vec::new() } else { state.mem[..code_end as usize].to_vec() };
    let main_text = text;
    let text: &[u8] = if placed.is_empty() { main_text } else { &code_buf };
    let code_ranges: Vec<(u64, u64)> = std::iter::once((0u64, main_text.len() as u64))
        .chain(placed.iter().map(|p| (p.base, p.base + p.module.text.len() as u64)))
        .collect();
    let in_code = |pc: u64| pc % 4 == 0 && code_ranges.iter().any(|&(lo, hi)| pc >= lo && pc + 4 <= hi);
    let mut boundaries = scan::call_targets(main_text);
    for p in &placed {
        boundaries.extend(scan::call_targets(&p.module.text).into_iter().map(|t| t + p.base));
    }
    let mut segments: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = vec![
        (module.rodata_addr, module.rodata.as_slice()),
        (module.data_addr, module.data.as_slice()),
    ];
    for p in &placed {
        segments.push((p.base + p.module.rodata_addr, p.module.rodata.as_slice()));
        segments.push((p.base + p.module.data_addr, p.module.data.as_slice()));
    }

    let mut cache: FastMap<u64, Cached> = FastMap::default();
    let mut hot: FastMap<u64, (u64, u64)> = FastMap::default();
    let mut trace: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut externals: Vec<TransferRecord> = Vec::new();
    let mut dispatches = 0u64;
    let mut native_dispatches = 0u64;
    let mut native_halts = 0u64;
    let mut skip_native: Option<u64> = None;
    // EW_NATIVE_CHECK=1: every native call is also tried on the side and
    // compared with the interpreter, which stays the one that runs.
    let native_check = opts.native.is_some() && std::env::var("EW_NATIVE_CHECK").is_ok_and(|v| v != "0");
    let mut native_compared = 0u64;
    let mut check_start: Option<native::Regs>;
    let mut calls = 0u64;
    let mut returns = 0u64;
    let mut branches = 0u64;
    let mut depth = 0u32;
    let mut max_depth = 0u32;
    let mut stack_low = state.sp;
    let mut seen_functions: FastSet<u64> = FastSet::default();
    // Host calls are counted by call id: the index of a static import name, or
    // `names.len()` plus the index of a run-time host function. Supervisor
    // calls, which are rare, are counted by name.
    let mut call_counts: FastMap<u32, (u64, u64)> = FastMap::default();
    let mut import_calls: BTreeMap<String, (u64, u64)> = BTreeMap::new();
    // Each stub address resolved once: its call id and handler.
    let mut resolved: FastMap<u64, (u32, Option<hle::Handler>)> = FastMap::default();
    let mut seen_starts = u64::MAX;
    let mut watch_hits: FastMap<u64, u32> = FastMap::default();
    // Return addresses of watched calls still in flight: (function, thread).
    let mut watch_returns: FastMap<u64, (u64, u64)> = FastMap::default();
    let mut host_calls = 0u64;
    // Origin of the last transfer, so a stop outside the text segment can name
    // the instruction that sent control there.
    let mut last_from = opts.entry;

    // The last events before a stop, kept as plain data and only formatted
    // into text for the report: formatting every call costs more than the
    // calls themselves in host-call-heavy code.
    let mut recent: std::collections::VecDeque<Event> = std::collections::VecDeque::new();
    macro_rules! event {
        ($e:expr) => {{
            if recent.len() >= 96 {
                recent.pop_front();
            }
            recent.push_back($e);
        }};
    }
    macro_rules! note {
        ($($arg:tt)*) => {{
            event!(Event::Text(format!($($arg)*)));
        }};
    }

    let mut queue: std::collections::VecDeque<(String, u64)> = opts.then.iter().cloned().collect();
    let mut phases: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut phase = opts.entry_name.clone();
    // Libraries initialise first, as the loader does before any program code
    // runs: each library's DT_INIT constructs its static objects.
    let lib_inits: Vec<(String, u64)> = placed
        .iter()
        .filter(|_| opts.init_libraries)
        .filter_map(|p| p.module.imports.init.map(|i| (format!("{} init", p.module.name), p.base + i)))
        .collect();
    if let Some((first, rest)) = lib_inits.split_first() {
        queue.push_front((phase.clone(), opts.entry));
        for init in rest.iter().rev() {
            queue.push_front(init.clone());
        }
        phase = first.0.clone();
        state.pc = first.1;
        state.x[0] = 0;
    }

    // The main thread is the pseudo thread object the os services already use.
    let main_object = match state.host.take_thread_object() {
        Ok(o) => o,
        Err(e) => bail!("could not create the main thread object: {e}"),
    };
    state.host.threads.insert(
        main_object,
        ew_lift::ThreadInfo { started: true, priority: 44, ..Default::default() },
    );
    // The main thread's thread-local region, holding its kernel handle.
    match sched::new_tls(&mut state, sched::handle_for(0), main_object) {
        Ok(tls) => state.tpidrro = tls,
        Err(e) => bail!("could not create the main thread's thread-local region: {e}"),
    }
    let mut sched = sched::Scheduler::new(main_object, &state);
    macro_rules! adopt {
        () => {{
            if state.host.thread_starts != seen_starts {
                seen_starts = state.host.thread_starts;
                sched.adopt_started(&mut state);
            }
        }};
    }
    // Switch away from the running thread; a stop when nothing can run.
    macro_rules! switch_or_stop {
        ($status:expr) => {
            match sched.switch(&mut state, $status) {
                Ok(()) => continue,
                Err(sched::NoRunnable::Deadlock(waits)) => break Stop::Deadlock { waits },
                Err(sched::NoRunnable::AllExited) => break Stop::AllThreadsExited,
                Err(sched::NoRunnable::Fault { call, message }) => {
                    break Stop::HostFault { import: call, from: 0, message }
                }
            }
        };
    }

    let mut since_poll = 0u32;
    let stop = loop {
        since_poll += 1;
        if since_poll >= 4096 {
            since_poll = 0;
            if let Some(p) = &opts.progress {
                p.store(state.steps, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            }
            if opts.cancel.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)) {
                break Stop::Cancelled;
            }
        }
        if state.steps >= opts.max_steps {
            break Stop::StepBudget;
        }
        if dispatches as usize >= opts.max_dispatches {
            break Stop::DispatchBudget;
        }
        let pc = state.pc;
```
