`crates/ew-boot/src/lmem.rs`:

```rs
//! `nn::lmem` frame heaps.
//!
//! A frame heap is a region the game owns, carved from both ends: positive
//! alignments allocate upward from the head, negative alignments downward from
//! the tail, and `FreeToFrameHeap` releases everything taken from one end (or
//! both) at once. That contract is small enough to implement exactly.
//!
//! State lives in the `HeapHead` the game supplies (or, for the overload without
//! one, at the start of the region, which is where nnSdk places it), tagged with
//! a magic word so a stray handle is reported instead of trusted.

use crate::hle::{read_bytes, write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;

const MAGIC: u64 = 0x4845_4150_4D52_4646; // "FFRMPAEH"
/// Bytes of head state this host keeps.
const HEAD_BYTES: u64 = 0x40;
const OPTION_ZERO_CLEAR: u64 = 1;
const FREE_HEAD: u64 = 1;
const FREE_TAIL: u64 = 2;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Head {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    head: u64,
    tail: u64,
    option: u64,
}

fn load(state: &State, at: u64) -> Result<Head, HostResult> {
    let b = read_bytes(state, at, 48)?;
    let w = |i: usize| u64::from_le_bytes(b[i * 8..i * 8 + 8].try_into().unwrap());
    if w(0) != MAGIC {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{at:x} is not a frame heap this host created")));
    }
    Ok(Head { start: w(1), end: w(2), head: w(3), tail: w(4), option: w(5) })
}

fn store(state: &mut State, at: u64, h: Head) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    let mut b = Vec::with_capacity(48);
    for v in [MAGIC, h.start, h.end, h.head, h.tail, h.option] {
        b.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
    }
    write_bytes(state, at, &b)
}

fn create(state: &mut State, head_at: u64, start: u64, size: u64, option: u64) -> HostResult {
    if start == 0 || size == 0 {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    let h = Head { start, end: start + size, head: start, tail: start + size, option };
    match store(state, head_at, h) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(head_at),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

/// `CreateFrameHeap(void*, size_t, int option, HeapHead*)`.
fn create_with_head(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (addr, size, option, head) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2], state.x[3]);
    create(state, head, addr, size, option)
}

/// `CreateFrameHeap(void*, size_t, int option)`: the head sits at the start of
/// the region, so the usable part begins after it.
fn create_in_place(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (addr, size, option) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    let head = (addr + 15) & !15;
    let start = head + HEAD_BYTES;
    if start >= addr + size {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    create(state, head, start, addr + size - start, option)
}

fn destroy(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let at = state.x[0];
    if let Err(e) = load(state, at) {
        return e;
    }
    match write_bytes(state, at, &[0u8; 8]) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(at),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

/// `AllocateFromFrameHeap(HeapHead*, size_t, int alignment)`. A negative
/// alignment allocates from the tail. Returns null when the heap is full.
fn allocate(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (at, size) = (state.x[0], state.x[1].max(1));
    let alignment = state.x[2] as i32;
    let mut h = match load(state, at) {
        Ok(h) => h,
        Err(e) => return e,
    };
    let align = (alignment.unsigned_abs() as u64).max(4).next_power_of_two();
    let ptr = if alignment >= 0 {
        let p = (h.head + align - 1) & !(align - 1);
        if p + size > h.tail {
            return HostResult::Returned(0);
        }
        h.head = p + size;
        p
    } else {
        let Some(p) = h.tail.checked_sub(size).map(|v| v & !(align - 1)) else {
            return HostResult::Returned(0);
        };
        if p < h.head {
            return HostResult::Returned(0);
        }
        h.tail = p;
        p
    };
    if h.option & OPTION_ZERO_CLEAR != 0 {
        if let Err(e) = write_bytes(state, ptr, &vec![0u8; size as usize]) {
            return e;
        }
    }
    match store(state, at, h) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(ptr),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

/// `FreeToFrameHeap(HeapHead*, FreeMode)`: 1 head, 2 tail, 3 both.
fn free(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (at, mode) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let mut h = match load(state, at) {
        Ok(h) => h,
        Err(e) => return e,
    };
    if mode & FREE_HEAD != 0 {
        h.head = h.start;
    }
    if mode & FREE_TAIL != 0 {
        h.tail = h.end;
    }
    match store(state, at, h) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(0),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    s.register("_ZN2nn4lmem15CreateFrameHeapEPvmiPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE", create_with_head, "frame heap state kept in the caller's HeapHead");
    s.register("_ZN2nn4lmem15CreateFrameHeapEPvmi", create_in_place, "head placed at the start of the region, as nnSdk does");
    s.register("_ZN2nn4lmem16DestroyFrameHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE", destroy, "clears the tag; the memory stays the caller's");
    s.register("_ZN2nn4lmem21AllocateFromFrameHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadEmi", allocate, "head-up for positive alignment, tail-down for negative; null when full; ZeroClear honoured");
    s.register("_ZN2nn4lmem15FreeToFrameHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadENS0_8FreeModeE", free, "releases the head side, the tail side, or both");
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn allocates_from_both_ends_and_frees() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        s.x[0] = 0x1000;
        s.x[1] = 0x1000;
        s.x[2] = OPTION_ZERO_CLEAR;
        s.x[3] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(create_with_head(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0x100));
        s.mem[0x1000..0x2000].fill(0xAA);

        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        s.x[1] = 0x10;
        s.x[2] = 16;
        assert_eq!(allocate(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0x1000));
        assert_eq!(&s.mem[0x1000..0x1010], &[0u8; 16], "ZeroClear");
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        s.x[1] = 0x20;
        s.x[2] = (-32i64) as u64;
        assert_eq!(allocate(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0x1FE0));
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        s.x[1] = 0x2000;
        s.x[2] = 4;
        assert_eq!(allocate(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0), "full heap returns null");

        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        s.x[1] = 3;
        assert_eq!(free(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        s.x[1] = 0x10;
        s.x[2] = 16;
        assert_eq!(allocate(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0x1000));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_foreign_handle_is_reported() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        s.x[0] = 0x500;
        s.x[1] = 1;
        assert!(matches!(free(&mut s), HostResult::Unavailable(_)));
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-boot/src/math.rs`:

```rs
//! The C math library the module imports.
//!
//! nnSdk's C library is musl, so every function here is computed by the `libm`
//! crate, a line-by-line port of musl's libm: the results are the bits the
//! console's own library would produce, not merely "IEEE-correct to an ulp".
//!
//! Calling convention (AAPCS64): floating point arguments arrive in `s0`/`d0`,
//! `s1`/`d1`, ... (the low lanes of `v0`, `v1`, ...), integer and pointer
//! arguments in `x0`, `x1`, ... independently of the float ones. The result is
//! written to `v0` with the rest of the register zeroed, which is what a scalar
//! floating point write does; `x0` is left alone.

use crate::hle::{write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;

fn fa(state: &State, i: usize) -> f32 {
    f32::from_bits(state.v[i][0] as u32)
}

fn da(state: &State, i: usize) -> f64 {
    f64::from_bits(state.v[i][0])
}

fn fr(state: &mut State, v: f32) -> HostResult {
    state.v[0] = [v.to_bits() as u64, 0];
    HostResult::Returned(state.x[0])
}

fn dr(state: &mut State, v: f64) -> HostResult {
    state.v[0] = [v.to_bits(), 0];
    HostResult::Returned(state.x[0])
}

macro_rules! f1 {
    ($($name:ident),* $(,)?) => {$(
        fn $name(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
            let a = fa(s, 0);
            fr(s, libm::$name(a))
        }
    )*};
}
macro_rules! f2 {
    ($($name:ident),* $(,)?) => {$(
        fn $name(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
            let (a, b) = (fa(s, 0), fa(s, 1));
            fr(s, libm::$name(a, b))
        }
    )*};
}
macro_rules! d1 {
    ($($name:ident),* $(,)?) => {$(
        fn $name(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
            let a = da(s, 0);
            dr(s, libm::$name(a))
        }
    )*};
}
macro_rules! d2 {
    ($($name:ident),* $(,)?) => {$(
        fn $name(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
            let (a, b) = (da(s, 0), da(s, 1));
            dr(s, libm::$name(a, b))
        }
    )*};
}

f1!(
    cosf, sinf, tanf, acosf, asinf, atanf, sqrtf, fabsf, floorf, ceilf, truncf, roundf, rintf, expf,
    logf, log2f, log10f, cbrtf, exp2f, sinhf, coshf, tanhf, asinhf, acoshf, atanhf, expm1f, log1pf,
    erff, erfcf, tgammaf, lgammaf, j0f, j1f, y0f, y1f
);
f2!(powf, atan2f, fmodf, fmaxf, fminf, copysignf, hypotf, remainderf, nextafterf, fdimf);
d1!(cos, sin, tan, acos, asin, atan, sqrt, fabs, floor, ceil, trunc, round, exp, exp2, log, log2, log10);
d2!(pow, fmod, atan2);

/// `logbf`, written as musl writes it (the libm crate does not carry it).
fn logbf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let x = fa(s, 0);
    let r = if !x.is_finite() {
        x * x
    } else if x == 0.0 {
        -1.0 / (x * x)
    } else {
        libm::ilogbf(x) as f32
    };
    fr(s, r)
}

fn fmaf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (a, b, c) = (fa(s, 0), fa(s, 1), fa(s, 2));
    fr(s, libm::fmaf(a, b, c))
}

/// `ldexpf(float, int)` and `scalbnf(float, int)`: the integer is in `w0`.
fn ldexpf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (a, e) = (fa(s, 0), s.x[0] as i32);
    fr(s, libm::ldexpf(a, e))
}
fn scalbnf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (a, e) = (fa(s, 0), s.x[0] as i32);
    fr(s, libm::scalbnf(a, e))
}

/// `int ilogbf(float)` returns in `w0`.
fn ilogbf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(libm::ilogbf(fa(s, 0)) as u32 as u64)
}

/// `frexpf(float, int* exp)`.
fn frexpf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (m, e) = libm::frexpf(fa(s, 0));
    if let Err(err) = write_bytes(s, s.x[0], &e.to_le_bytes()) {
        return err;
    }
    fr(s, m)
}

/// `modff(float, float* iptr)`.
fn modff(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (frac, int) = libm::modff(fa(s, 0));
    if let Err(err) = write_bytes(s, s.x[0], &int.to_bits().to_le_bytes()) {
        return err;
    }
    fr(s, frac)
}

/// `remquof(float, float, int* quo)`.
fn remquof(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (r, q) = libm::remquof(fa(s, 0), fa(s, 1));
    if let Err(err) = write_bytes(s, s.x[0], &q.to_le_bytes()) {
        return err;
    }
    fr(s, r)
}

/// `nanf(const char*)`: musl ignores the tag and returns the quiet NaN.
fn nanf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    fr(s, f32::from_bits(0x7FC0_0000))
}

/// `jnf(int, float)` / `ynf(int, float)`.
fn jnf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (n, x) = (s.x[0] as i32, fa(s, 0));
    fr(s, libm::jnf(n, x))
}
fn ynf(s: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (n, x) = (s.x[0] as i32, fa(s, 0));
    fr(s, libm::ynf(n, x))
}

/// Register the C math family the module imports.
pub fn register(services: &mut HostServices) {
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult)] = &[
        ("cosf", cosf), ("sinf", sinf), ("tanf", tanf), ("acosf", acosf), ("asinf", asinf),
        ("atanf", atanf), ("sqrtf", sqrtf), ("fabsf", fabsf), ("floorf", floorf), ("ceilf", ceilf),
        ("truncf", truncf), ("roundf", roundf), ("rintf", rintf), ("expf", expf), ("logf", logf),
        ("log2f", log2f), ("log10f", log10f), ("cbrtf", cbrtf), ("exp2f", exp2f), ("sinhf", sinhf),
        ("coshf", coshf), ("tanhf", tanhf), ("asinhf", asinhf), ("acoshf", acoshf), ("atanhf", atanhf),
        ("expm1f", expm1f), ("log1pf", log1pf), ("logbf", logbf), ("erff", erff), ("erfcf", erfcf),
        ("tgammaf", tgammaf), ("lgammaf", lgammaf), ("j0f", j0f), ("j1f", j1f), ("y0f", y0f),
        ("y1f", y1f), ("jnf", jnf), ("ynf", ynf), ("powf", powf), ("atan2f", atan2f), ("fmodf", fmodf),
        ("fmaxf", fmaxf), ("fminf", fminf), ("copysignf", copysignf), ("hypotf", hypotf),
        ("remainderf", remainderf), ("nextafterf", nextafterf), ("fdimf", fdimf), ("fmaf", fmaf),
        ("ldexpf", ldexpf), ("scalbnf", scalbnf), ("ilogbf", ilogbf), ("frexpf", frexpf),

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn with_f(args: &[f32]) -> State {
        let mut s = State::default();
        for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate() {
            s.v[i] = [a.to_bits() as u64, 0];
        }
        s
    }

    #[test]
    fn arguments_come_from_s_registers_not_x0() {
        let mut s = with_f(&[0.0]);
        s.x[0] = 0x4049_0FDB; // pi as bits: must be ignored
        cosf(&mut s);
        assert_eq!(f32::from_bits(s.v[0][0] as u32), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(s.v[0][1], 0, "a scalar write clears the upper half");
    }

    #[test]
    fn binary_and_mixed_signatures() {
        let mut s = with_f(&[1.5, -2.0]);
        fmaxf(&mut s);
        assert_eq!(f32::from_bits(s.v[0][0] as u32), 1.5);
        let mut s = with_f(&[3.0]);
        s.x[0] = 4;
        ldexpf(&mut s);
        assert_eq!(f32::from_bits(s.v[0][0] as u32), 48.0);
        let mut s = with_f(&[8.0]);
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        frexpf(&mut s);
        assert_eq!(f32::from_bits(s.v[0][0] as u32), 0.5);
        assert_eq!(i32::from_le_bytes(s.mem[0x100..0x104].try_into().unwrap()), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn double_results_land_in_d0() {
        let mut s = State::default();
        s.v[0] = [9.0f64.to_bits(), 0];
        sqrt(&mut s);
        assert_eq!(f64::from_bits(s.v[0][0]), 3.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn results_match_musl() {
        // musl's sinf(1.0f) is 0x3f576aa4.
        let mut s = with_f(&[1.0]);
        sinf(&mut s);
        assert_eq!(s.v[0][0] as u32, 0x3F57_6AA4);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! `nn::movie` video playback.
//!
//! The host does not decode video yet. The game's movie objects can be built
//! and torn down, but opening a movie reports that the media cannot be
//! opened, which the game treats as a movie it cannot play, so it goes on
//! without it. The path asked for is logged.

use crate::hle::{c_string, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;

/// `nn::movie` result for media the extractor cannot open (module 74,
/// description 1): any failure is enough for the game to skip the movie.
const RESULT_MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED: u64 = 74 | (1 << 9);

fn ok(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `MediaExtractor::SetUriMedia(const char* uri, int length)`.
fn set_uri_media(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let uri = c_string(state, state.x[1], 1024).map(|b| String::from_utf8_lossy(&b).into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();
    state.host.log.push(format!("movie: {uri} cannot be played yet; reported as unsupported media"));
    HostResult::Returned(RESULT_MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED)
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult, &'static str)] = &[
        ("_ZN2nn5movie10InitializeEv", ok, "nothing to set up"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie8FinalizeEv", ok, "nothing to tear down"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie13MediaPropertyC1Ev", ok, "an empty property set"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie6BufferC1Ev", ok, "an empty buffer"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie14MediaExtractorC1Ev", ok, "an extractor with no media"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie14MediaExtractorD1Ev", ok, "nothing to release"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie14MediaExtractor10InitializeEPvmm", ok, "accepts its work memory"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie14MediaExtractor8FinalizeEv", ok, "nothing to release"),
        ("_ZN2nn5movie14MediaExtractor11SetUriMediaEPKci", set_uri_media, "video is not decoded yet: the media is reported unsupported"),
        ("_ZN5movie12VideoDecoderC1Ev", ok, "a decoder that is never started"),
        ("_ZN5movie12VideoDecoderD1Ev", ok, "nothing to release"),
        ("_ZN5movie12VideoDecoder8FinalizeEv", ok, "nothing to release"),
        ("_ZN5movie10VideoFrameC1Ev", ok, "an empty frame"),
    ];
    for (name, handler, claim) in table {
        s.register(name, *handler, claim);
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-boot/src/native.rs`:

```rs
//! Native execution: the game's code compiled ahead of time by `ew-native`
//! into `ew_native.dll`, run in place of the reference interpreter.
//!
//! The library's functions take the C `Cpu` of `ew_aarch64.h`; [`Cpu`] mirrors
//! it field for field. A call copies the guest registers in, points the
//! library at guest memory (guest address = offset into `State::mem`), runs
//! one function until control leaves it, a supervisor call, a halt or the end
//! of its instruction budget, and copies the registers back.

use ew_lift::interpreter::State;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::path::Path;

pub type NativeFn = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut Cpu) -> i32;

/// `Cpu` from `ew_aarch64.h`, in the same order.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Cpu {
    pub x: [u64; 31],
    pub v: [[u64; 2]; 32],
    pub sp: u64,
    pub pc: u64,
    pub nzcv: u32,
    pub halted: i32,
    pub halt_reason: [u8; 128],
    pub tpidrro: u64,
    pub tpidr: u64,
    pub fpcr: u64,
    pub fpsr: u64,
    pub counter: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn() -> u64>,
    pub svc: i32,
    pub excl_addr: u64,
    pub excl_valid: i32,
    pub mem_read: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64, u32) -> u64,
    pub mem_write: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64, u64, u32),
    pub mem_ctx: *mut c_void,
    pub mem_base: *mut u8,
    pub mem_size: u64,
    pub budget: i64,
}

/// An access outside guest memory: the library calls back here, and the run
/// stops with the same message the interpreter gives.
struct Fault(Option<String>);

unsafe extern "C" fn mem_read(ctx: *mut c_void, addr: u64, bytes: u32) -> u64 {
    let f = unsafe { &mut *(ctx as *mut Fault) };
    f.0.get_or_insert_with(|| format!("guest read of {bytes} byte(s) at 0x{addr:x} is outside guest memory"));
    0
}

unsafe extern "C" fn mem_write(ctx: *mut c_void, addr: u64, _v: u64, bytes: u32) {
    let f = unsafe { &mut *(ctx as *mut Fault) };
    f.0.get_or_insert_with(|| format!("guest write of {bytes} byte(s) at 0x{addr:x} is outside guest memory"));
}

thread_local! {
    static CLOCK: std::cell::Cell<(Option<fn() -> u64>, u64)> = const { std::cell::Cell::new((None, 0)) };
}

/// The system counter, as the interpreter reads it: the host clock, or the
/// instruction count when there is none.
unsafe extern "C" fn counter() -> u64 {
    CLOCK.with(|c| {
        let (f, steps) = c.get();
        f.map(|f| f()).unwrap_or(steps)
    })
}

/// How a native call ended.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Exit {
    /// Control left the function; `state.pc` is where it went.
    Left,
    /// A supervisor call: `state.svc` is set and `state.pc` is the `svc`.
    Svc,
    /// The instruction budget ran out; `state.pc` is a block to resume at.
    Budget,
    /// The library stopped at something it cannot run (`state.pc`); the
    /// interpreter takes over there.
    Halt(String),
    /// An access outside guest memory.
    Fault(String),
}

pub struct Native {
    _lib: Library,
    blocks: crate::FastMap<u64, NativeFn>,
    pub functions: usize,
    /// Run native functions back to back (`EW_NATIVE_CHAIN=0` turns it off,
    /// so the run loop sees every function entry).
    pub chain: bool,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Native {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "Native {{ {} functions, {} blocks }}", self.functions, self.blocks.len())
    }
}

struct Library(*mut c_void);
unsafe impl Send for Library {}
unsafe impl Sync for Library {}

#[cfg(windows)]
impl Library {
    fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Library, String> {
        use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
        let wide: Vec<u16> = path.as_os_str().encode_wide().chain([0]).collect();
        let h = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::LoadLibraryW(wide.as_ptr()) };
        if h.is_null() {
            return Err(format!("could not load {}: {}", path.display(), std::io::Error::last_os_error()));
        }
        Ok(Library(h as *mut c_void))
    }

    fn symbol(&self, name: &str) -> Option<*const c_void> {
        let c = std::ffi::CString::new(name).ok()?;
        let p = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::GetProcAddress(self.0 as _, c.as_ptr() as _) }?;
        Some(p as *const c_void)
    }
}

#[repr(C)]
struct Entry {
    address: u64,
    f: Option<NativeFn>,
}

impl Native {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Native, String> {
        let lib = Library::open(path)?;
        let shards: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> u32 =
            unsafe { std::mem::transmute(lib.symbol("ew_native_shards").ok_or("ew_native_shards is missing: not an ew-native library")?) };
        let shard: unsafe extern "C" fn(u32, *mut u32) -> *const Entry =
            unsafe { std::mem::transmute(lib.symbol("ew_native_shard").ok_or("ew_native_shard is missing")?) };
        let mut blocks = crate::FastMap::default();
        let mut functions = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for i in 0..unsafe { shards() } {
            let mut n = 0u32;
            let t = unsafe { shard(i, &mut n) };
            if t.is_null() {
                continue;
            }
            for e in unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(t, n as usize) } {
                if let Some(f) = e.f {
                    blocks.insert(e.address, f);
                    functions.insert(f as usize);
                }
            }
        }
        let chain = std::env::var("EW_NATIVE_CHAIN").map_or(true, |v| v != "0");
        Ok(Native { _lib: lib, blocks, functions: functions.len(), chain })
    }

    pub fn blocks(&self) -> usize {
        self.blocks.len()
    }

    pub fn get(&self, pc: u64) -> Option<NativeFn> {
        self.blocks.get(&pc).copied()
    }

    /// Run `f` from `state.pc` for up to `budget` instructions.
    pub fn run(&self, f: NativeFn, state: &mut State, budget: u64) -> Exit {
        let mut fault = Fault(None);
        let mut cpu = Cpu {
            x: state.x,
            v: state.v,
            sp: state.sp,
            pc: state.pc,
            nzcv: state.nzcv,
            halted: 0,
            halt_reason: [0; 128],
            tpidrro: state.tpidrro,
            tpidr: state.tpidr,
            fpcr: state.fpcr,
            fpsr: state.fpsr,
            counter: Some(counter),
            svc: -1,
            excl_addr: state.exclusive.unwrap_or(0),
            excl_valid: state.exclusive.is_some() as i32,
            mem_read,
            mem_write,
            mem_ctx: &mut fault as *mut Fault as *mut c_void,
            mem_base: state.mem.as_mut_ptr(),
            mem_size: state.mem.len() as u64,
            budget: budget.min(i64::MAX as u64) as i64,
        };
        CLOCK.with(|c| c.set((state.host.clock, state.steps)));
        // Chain: when control leaves for another native function, enter it
        // here rather than going back to the run loop, which only needs to
        // see supervisor calls, host functions, halts and the end of the
        // budget.
        let mut f = f;
        let mut more;
        loop {
            more = unsafe { f(&mut cpu) };
            if more == 0 || cpu.halted != 0 || cpu.svc != -1 || fault.0.is_some() || !self.chain {
                break;
            }
            match self.blocks.get(&cpu.pc) {
                Some(&g) => f = g,
                None => break,
            }
        }
        state.x = cpu.x;
        state.v = cpu.v;
        state.sp = cpu.sp;
        state.pc = cpu.pc;
        state.nzcv = cpu.nzcv;
        state.tpidr = cpu.tpidr;
        state.fpcr = cpu.fpcr;
        state.fpsr = cpu.fpsr;
        state.exclusive = (cpu.excl_valid != 0).then_some(cpu.excl_addr);
        state.steps += budget.saturating_sub(cpu.budget.max(0) as u64);
        if let Some(m) = fault.0 {
            return Exit::Fault(m);
        }
        if cpu.halted != 0 {
            let n = cpu.halt_reason.iter().position(|&b| b == 0).unwrap_or(128);
            return Exit::Halt(String::from_utf8_lossy(&cpu.halt_reason[..n]).into_owned());
        }
        if more == 0 && cpu.svc >= 0 {
            state.svc = Some(cpu.svc as u16);
            state.pc = cpu.pc.wrapping_sub(4);
            return Exit::Svc;
        }
        if cpu.svc == -2 {
            return Exit::Budget;
        }
        Exit::Left
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------- check mode

/// The registers a native call and the interpreter are compared on.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Regs {
    pub x: [u64; 31],
    pub v: [[u64; 2]; 32],
    pub sp: u64,
    pub pc: u64,
    pub nzcv: u32,
}

impl Regs {
    pub fn of(s: &State) -> Regs {
        Regs { x: s.x, v: s.v, sp: s.sp, pc: s.pc, nzcv: s.nzcv }
    }

    /// The first differences from `other`, as text.
    pub fn diff(&self, other: &Regs) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut d = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..31 {
            if self.x[i] != other.x[i] {
                d.push(format!("x{i} native 0x{:x} interpreter 0x{:x}", self.x[i], other.x[i]));
            }
        }
        for i in 0..32 {
            if self.v[i] != other.v[i] {
                d.push(format!("v{i} native {:x}:{:x} interpreter {:x}:{:x}", self.v[i][1], self.v[i][0], other.v[i][1], other.v[i][0]));
            }
        }
        if self.sp != other.sp {
            d.push(format!("sp native 0x{:x} interpreter 0x{:x}", self.sp, other.sp));
        }
        if self.pc != other.pc {
            d.push(format!("pc native 0x{:x} interpreter 0x{:x}", self.pc, other.pc));
        }
        if self.nzcv != other.nzcv {
            d.push(format!("nzcv native {:x} interpreter {:x}", self.nzcv, other.nzcv));
        }
        d
    }
}

/// Guest memory seen through an overlay: reads come from the run's memory
/// unless the native call wrote the byte, writes go to the overlay only.
struct Overlay {
    mem: *const Vec<u8>,
    writes: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, u8>,
    fault: Option<String>,
}

unsafe extern "C" fn overlay_read(ctx: *mut c_void, addr: u64, bytes: u32) -> u64 {
    let o = unsafe { &mut *(ctx as *mut Overlay) };
    let mem = unsafe { &*o.mem };
    let mut v = 0u64;
    for i in 0..bytes as u64 {
        let a = addr.wrapping_add(i);
        let b = match o.writes.get(&a) {
            Some(b) => *b,
            None => match mem.get(a as usize) {
                Some(b) => *b,
                None => {
                    o.fault.get_or_insert_with(|| format!("guest read of {bytes} byte(s) at 0x{addr:x} is outside guest memory"));
                    0
                }
            },
        };
        v |= (b as u64) << (8 * i);
    }
    v
}

unsafe extern "C" fn overlay_write(ctx: *mut c_void, addr: u64, value: u64, bytes: u32) {
    let o = unsafe { &mut *(ctx as *mut Overlay) };
    for i in 0..bytes as u64 {
        o.writes.insert(addr.wrapping_add(i), (value >> (8 * i)) as u8);
    }
}

/// What a native call would do, without changing the run: its exit, final
/// registers and the bytes it wrote. `state` is left as it was.
pub struct Trial {
    pub exit: Exit,
    pub regs: Regs,
    pub writes: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, u8>,
    /// Instructions the call ran.
    pub executed: u64,
}

impl Native {
    pub fn trial(&self, f: NativeFn, state: &mut State, budget: u64) -> Trial {
        let before = Regs::of(state);
        let (excl, tpidr, fpcr, fpsr, steps) = (state.exclusive, state.tpidr, state.fpcr, state.fpsr, state.steps);
        let mut o = Overlay { mem: &state.mem, writes: Default::default(), fault: None };
        let mut cpu = Cpu {
            x: state.x,
            v: state.v,
            sp: state.sp,
            pc: state.pc,
            nzcv: state.nzcv,
            halted: 0,
            halt_reason: [0; 128],
            tpidrro: state.tpidrro,
            tpidr: state.tpidr,
            fpcr: state.fpcr,
            fpsr: state.fpsr,
            counter: Some(counter),
            svc: -1,
            excl_addr: state.exclusive.unwrap_or(0),
            excl_valid: state.exclusive.is_some() as i32,
            mem_read: overlay_read,
            mem_write: overlay_write,
            mem_ctx: &mut o as *mut Overlay as *mut c_void,
            mem_base: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            mem_size: 0,
            budget: budget.min(i64::MAX as u64) as i64,
        };
        CLOCK.with(|c| c.set((state.host.clock, state.steps)));
        let more = unsafe { f(&mut cpu) };
        let mut regs = Regs { x: cpu.x, v: cpu.v, sp: cpu.sp, pc: cpu.pc, nzcv: cpu.nzcv };
        let exit = if let Some(m) = o.fault.take() {
            Exit::Fault(m)
        } else if cpu.halted != 0 {
            Exit::Halt(String::new())
        } else if more == 0 && cpu.svc >= 0 {
            regs.pc = cpu.pc.wrapping_sub(4);
            Exit::Svc
        } else if cpu.svc == -2 {
            Exit::Budget
        } else {
            Exit::Left
        };
        // Leave the run exactly as it was.
        state.x = before.x;
        state.v = before.v;
        state.sp = before.sp;
        state.pc = before.pc;
        state.nzcv = before.nzcv;
        state.exclusive = excl;
        state.tpidr = tpidr;
        state.fpcr = fpcr;
        state.fpsr = fpsr;
        state.steps = steps;
        let executed = budget.saturating_sub(cpu.budget.max(0) as u64);
        Trial { exit, regs, writes: o.writes, executed }
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-boot/src/nvn.rs`:

```rs
//! NVN objects backed by the host's Vulkan device.
//!
//! NVN structures are opaque to the game: it reserves their storage and passes
//! pointers. The host keeps each object's state on the host side, keyed by
//! that pointer, and never invents a result: an object reports success only
//! when the host state behind it exists, and a query whose answer the host
//! cannot establish stops the run naming the query.
//!
//! Procedures are registered under `nvn:<name>`, the names the game resolves
//! through `nvnDeviceGetProcAddress`.

use crate::hle::{read_bytes, write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const NVN_TRUE: u64 = 1;
const NVN_FALSE: u64 = 0;

/// Host-side NVN state for one run.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Nvn {
    /// Builder and object fields, by object address then field name.
    pub fields: BTreeMap<u64, BTreeMap<String, u64>>,
    /// Recorded arguments of generic state setters, by object then procedure.
    pub state: BTreeMap<u64, BTreeMap<String, Vec<u64>>>,
    /// Debug labels the game attached to objects.
    pub labels: BTreeMap<u64, String>,
    /// Device property queries answered, for the report.
    pub queries: BTreeMap<u32, u64>,
}

fn nvn<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Nvn) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<Nvn, R>(f)
}

pub(crate) fn set_field(state: &State, obj: u64, field: &'static str, v: u64) {
    nvn(state, |n| {
        n.fields.entry(obj).or_default().insert(field.to_string(), v);
    })
}

pub(crate) fn field(state: &State, obj: u64, field: &'static str) -> Option<u64> {
    nvn(state, |n| n.fields.get(&obj).and_then(|m| m.get(field).copied()))
}

pub(crate) fn w32(state: &mut State, addr: u64, v: u32) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    write_bytes(state, addr, &v.to_le_bytes())
}

#[allow(dead_code)]
pub(crate) fn r32(state: &State, addr: u64) -> Result<u32, HostResult> {
    let b = read_bytes(state, addr, 4)?;
    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))
}

/// The NVN procedure the guest just called, recovered from the stub address
/// it branched to.
pub(crate) fn called(state: &State) -> String {
    let pc = state.pc;
    if pc < state.host.dyn_base {
        return String::new();
    }
    let i = ((pc - state.host.dyn_base) / 16) as usize;
    state.host.dyn_stubs.get(i).map(|n| n.trim_start_matches("nvn:").to_string()).unwrap_or_default()
}

/// A pure state setter: records its arguments against the object so a later
/// getter, a draw or the report can read them. Used only for procedures that
/// return nothing and whose effect is entirely the state they set.
pub(crate) fn record_state(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let name = called(state);
    let obj = state.x[0];
    let mut args: Vec<u64> = state.x[1..8].to_vec();
    args.extend(state.v[0..4].iter().map(|v| v[0]));
    nvn(state, |n| {
        if name.ends_with("SetDefaults") {
            // A builder starts over: nothing set before applies any more.
            n.state.remove(&obj);
        }
        n.state.entry(obj).or_default().insert(name, args);
    });
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// The getter matching a recorded setter (`...GetX` reads `...SetX`'s first
/// argument). A value the game never set stops the run rather than guessing.
fn read_state(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let name = called(state);
    let obj = state.x[0];
    let set = name.replacen("Get", "Set", 1);
    match nvn(state, |n| n.state.get(&obj).and_then(|m| m.get(&set)).map(|a| a[0])) {
        Some(v) => HostResult::Returned(v),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("{name} read state the game never set with {set}")),
    }
}

/// First argument a builder setter recorded, if the game called it.
fn recorded(state: &State, obj: u64, setter: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    nvn(state, |n| n.state.get(&obj).and_then(|m| m.get(setter)).map(|a| a[0]))
}

fn align_up(v: u64, a: u64) -> u64 {
    v.div_ceil(a) * a
}

/// `nvnQueueBuilderGetQueueMemorySize`: the guest memory the queue asks for,
/// the sum of its command, compute and control areas, page aligned.
fn queue_builder_get_queue_memory_size(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let b = state.x[0];
    let command = recorded(state, b, "nvnQueueBuilderSetCommandMemorySize").unwrap_or(0x1_0000);
    let compute = recorded(state, b, "nvnQueueBuilderSetComputeMemorySize").unwrap_or(0x4_0000);
    let control = recorded(state, b, "nvnQueueBuilderSetControlMemorySize").unwrap_or(0x4000);
    HostResult::Returned(align_up(command + compute + control, 0x1000))
}

/// Host-side record of an initialized NVN object: its kind and the builder
/// state it was created from.
fn adopt_builder(state: &mut State, obj: u64, builder: u64, kind: &'static str) {
    nvn(state, |n| {
        let from = n.state.get(&builder).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        n.state.insert(obj, from);
        n.fields.entry(obj).or_default().insert("kind".into(), kind_id(kind));
    });
}

fn kind_id(kind: &str) -> u64 {
    match kind {
        "queue" => 1,
        "memory_pool" => 2,
        "buffer" => 3,
        "texture" => 4,
        "sampler" => 5,
        "window" => 6,
        "program" => 7,
        "sync" => 8,
        "command_buffer" => 9,
        "texture_pool" => 10,
        "sampler_pool" => 11,
        "event" => 12,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

/// `nvnQueueInitialize(NVNqueue*, const NVNqueueBuilder*)`. The queue executes
/// on the host, so it succeeds whenever the device exists.
fn queue_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (q, b) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    if ew_gfx::device().is_err() {
        return HostResult::Returned(NVN_FALSE);
    }
    adopt_builder(state, q, b, "queue");
    state.host.log.push(format!("gfx: NVN queue 0x{q:x} created"));
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

/// `nvnDlssNetworkBuilderGetOptimalSettings(builder, out x6, optional out)`:
/// the render resolution the upscaler wants for the output resolution. The
/// host upscaler takes any input size, so every size it reports, optimal,
/// smallest and largest, is half the output in each dimension. Writing the
/// same pair to every out pointer keeps the answer consistent whichever order
/// the game reads them in.
fn dlss_get_optimal_settings(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let b = state.x[0];
    let out = nvn(state, |n| n.state.get(&b).and_then(|m| m.get("nvnDlssNetworkBuilderSetOutputResolution")).cloned());
    let Some(out) = out else {
        return HostResult::Unavailable("nvnDlssNetworkBuilderGetOptimalSettings before SetOutputResolution".into());
    };
    let (w, h) = (((out[0] as u32) / 2).max(1), ((out[1] as u32) / 2).max(1));
    let ptrs: Vec<u64> = state.x[1..7].to_vec();
    for (i, p) in ptrs.iter().enumerate() {
        if *p != 0 {
            let v = if i % 2 == 0 { w } else { h };
            if let Err(e) = w32(state, *p, v) {
                return e;
            }
        }
    }
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

/// The host upscaler keeps no network weights in guest memory; the game still
/// reserves a page for it.
fn dlss_storage_size(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0x1000)
}

/// `nvnDlssNetworkInitialize(network, builder)`: the host upscaler exists
/// whenever the device does.
fn dlss_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (net, b) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    adopt_builder(state, net, b, "dlss");
    let res = recorded(state, b, "nvnDlssNetworkBuilderSetOutputResolution");
    state.host.log.push(format!("gfx: upscaler 0x{net:x} for output width {}", res.unwrap_or(0)));
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

fn ok_true(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

fn ok_zero(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nvnDeviceGetCurrentTimestampInNanoseconds(device)`: the host clock.
fn device_timestamp_now(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(crate::threads::now_ticks().saturating_mul(1_000_000_000) / crate::threads::TICK_FREQ)
}

/// `nvnDeviceGetTimestampInNanoseconds(device, const NVNcounterData*)`: the
/// report's timestamp field, which host reports already hold in nanoseconds.
fn device_timestamp_of(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    match read_bytes(state, state.x[1] + 8, 8) {
        Ok(b) => HostResult::Returned(u64::from_le_bytes(b.try_into().unwrap())),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

/// `nvnDeviceGenerateDebugDomainId(device, const char*)`: a fresh id.
fn device_debug_domain(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let id = nvn(state, |n| {
        let e = n.fields.entry(0).or_default().entry("debug_domain".into()).or_insert(0);
        *e += 1;
        *e
    });
    HostResult::Returned(id)
}

/// `nvnDeviceBuilderSetDefaults(NVNdeviceBuilder*)`.
fn device_builder_set_defaults(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let b = state.x[0];
    set_field(state, b, "flags", 0);
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nvnDeviceBuilderSetFlags(NVNdeviceBuilder*, int flags)`.
fn device_builder_set_flags(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (b, flags) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] & 0xFFFF_FFFF);
    set_field(state, b, "flags", flags);
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nvnDeviceBuilderGetFlags(const NVNdeviceBuilder*)`.
fn device_builder_get_flags(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(field(state, state.x[0], "flags").unwrap_or(0))
}

/// `nvnDeviceInitialize(NVNdevice*, const NVNdeviceBuilder*)`: true only when
/// the host's Vulkan device exists.
fn device_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (dev, b) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let flags = field(state, b, "flags").unwrap_or(0);
    match ew_gfx::device() {
        Ok(gpu) => {
            let i = &gpu.info;
            state.host.log.push(format!(
                "gfx: NVN device 0x{dev:x} on {} (Vulkan {}.{}.{}, {}), flags 0x{flags:x}",
                i.name, i.api.0, i.api.1, i.api.2, i.driver
            ));
            set_field(state, dev, "live", 1);
            set_field(state, dev, "flags", flags);
            HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
        }
        Err(e) => {
            state.host.log.push(format!("gfx: NVN device could not be created: {e}"));
            HostResult::Returned(NVN_FALSE)
        }
    }
}

/// `nvnDeviceGetFlags(const NVNdevice*)`.
fn device_get_flags(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(field(state, state.x[0], "flags").unwrap_or(0))
}

/// `nvnXxxSetDebugLabel(obj, const char*)` for every object type: the label is
/// kept for diagnostics.
fn set_debug_label(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (obj, s) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let label = if s == 0 {
        String::new()
    } else {
        match crate::hle::c_string(state, s, 256) {
            Ok(b) => String::from_utf8_lossy(&b).into_owned(),
            Err(e) => return e,
        }
    };
    nvn(state, |n| n.labels.insert(obj, label));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Device properties the host answers, by NVN `DeviceInfo` value. Every entry
/// says where its value comes from; an id that is not listed stops the run.
fn device_property(id: u32) -> Option<(u64, &'static str)> {
    Some(match id {
        // The API version the driver reports. The game's own startup code reads
        // both and discards them (0x5d00c), so these identify the host layer
        // rather than claim a particular console driver.
        0 => (55, "API major version reported by the EmblemWeave NVN layer"),
        1 => (0, "API minor version reported by the EmblemWeave NVN layer"),
        // The NVN device-info numbering. The game's own use confirms the
        // entries it has read so far (19 and 20 align its command and control
        // memory at 0x554f4). Every value is one the host device honours: the
        // host stores commands and descriptors itself, so alignments and sizes
        // only shape how the game lays out its own memory.
        2 => (18, "uniform buffer bindings per stage"),
        3 => (0x1_0000, "largest uniform buffer, bytes"),
        4 => (256, "uniform buffer alignment, bytes"),
        5 => (8, "color render targets"),
        6 => (16, "vertex buffer bindings"),
        7 => (4, "transform feedback buffer bindings"),
        8 => (16, "storage buffer bindings per stage"),
        9 => (32, "texture bindings per stage"),
        10 => (16, "counter report alignment, bytes"),
        11 => (4, "transform feedback buffer alignment, bytes"),
        12 => (4, "transform feedback control alignment, bytes"),
        13 => (4, "indirect draw alignment, bytes"),
        14 => (16, "vertex attributes"),
        15 => (32, "texture descriptor size, bytes"),
        16 => (32, "sampler descriptor size, bytes"),
        17 => (256, "reserved texture descriptors"),
        18 => (256, "reserved sampler descriptors"),
        19 => (4, "command memory alignment, bytes"),
        20 => (8, "control memory alignment, bytes"),
        21 => (0x1_0000, "smallest command memory chunk, bytes"),
        22 => (0x1000, "smallest control memory chunk, bytes"),
        23 => (1, "minimum shader scratch scale factor"),
        24 => (1, "recommended shader scratch scale factor"),
        25 => (0x1000, "shader scratch memory alignment, bytes"),
        26 => (0x2_0000, "shader scratch memory granularity, bytes"),
        27 => (16, "largest texture anisotropy"),
        // Read together at 0x6036d0 and folded into a two-bit feature mask that
        // is tested for zero, so both are capability flags. The host provides
        // neither optional feature.
        42 => (0, "optional feature flag, not provided by the host"),
        90 => (0, "optional feature flag, not provided by the host"),
        // Queue memory defaults. The game sizes its queues as a multiple of
        // these (0x5dac0: compute x8, command x32, control x8). The host queue
        // records commands on the host, so these only set how much guest
        // memory the game reserves; they are kept modest and aligned.
        82 => (0x1_0000, "queue command memory unit (bytes)"),
        85 => (0x4_0000, "queue compute memory unit (bytes)"),
        92 => (0x4000, "queue control memory unit (bytes)"),
        // A count the upscaler setup at 0x1913d58 sizes a table with and skips
        // when zero; the host upscaler has no such entries.
        133 => (0, "upscaler table entries, none on the host"),
        // An upper bound: the game takes the smaller of it and its own figure
        // (0x649944). The texture handle's 20-bit index is the host's limit.
        70 => (1 << 20, "largest descriptor count, the 20-bit handle index"),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// `nvnDeviceGetInteger(const NVNdevice*, NVNdeviceInfo, int*)`.
fn device_get_integer(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (id, out) = ((state.x[1] & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32, state.x[2]);
    let Some((value, _why)) = device_property(id) else {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "nvnDeviceGetInteger asked for device property {id}, whose value the host has not established"
        ));
    };
    nvn(state, |n| n.queries.insert(id, value));
    match w32(state, out, value as u32) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(0),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult, &'static str)] = &[
        ("nvn:nvnDeviceBuilderSetDefaults", device_builder_set_defaults, "builder state kept on the host"),
        ("nvn:nvnDeviceBuilderSetFlags", device_builder_set_flags, "builder state kept on the host"),
        ("nvn:nvnDeviceBuilderGetFlags", device_builder_get_flags, "builder state kept on the host"),
        ("nvn:nvnDeviceInitialize", device_initialize, "true only when the host Vulkan device exists"),
        ("nvn:nvnDeviceGetFlags", device_get_flags, "flags the device was created with"),
        ("nvn:nvnDeviceGetInteger", device_get_integer, "answers only properties the host has established"),
    ];
    for (name, handler, claim) in table {
        s.register(name, *handler, claim);
    }
    s.register("nvn:nvnDlssNetworkBuilderGetOptimalSettings", dlss_get_optimal_settings, "half the output resolution for the host upscaler");
    s.register("nvn:nvnDlssNetworkBuilderGetStorageSize", dlss_storage_size, "one page; the host upscaler keeps its state on the host");
    s.register("nvn:nvnDlssNetworkInitialize", dlss_initialize, "a host upscaler");
    s.register("nvn:nvnDlssNetworkResize", ok_true, "the host upscaler takes any size");
    s.register("nvn:nvnDlssNetworkFinalize", ok_zero, "nothing to release");
    s.register_prefix("nvn:nvnDlssParametersSet", record_state, "upscaler parameters recorded on the host");
    for name in DEVICE_HINTS {
        s.register(&format!("nvn:nvnDevice{name}"), ok_zero, "a hint or debug setting with no effect on host results");
    }
    s.register("nvn:nvnDeviceGetCurrentTimestampInNanoseconds", device_timestamp_now, "the host clock");
    s.register("nvn:nvnDeviceGetTimestampInNanoseconds", device_timestamp_of, "the report's own timestamp");
    s.register("nvn:nvnDeviceGenerateDebugDomainId", device_debug_domain, "a fresh id per call");
    s.register("nvn:nvnDeviceIsExternalDebuggerAttached", ok_zero, "no debugger is attached");
    s.register("nvn:nvnQueueBuilderGetQueueMemorySize", queue_builder_get_queue_memory_size, "sum of the queue's memory areas, page aligned");
    s.register("nvn:nvnQueueInitialize", queue_initialize, "a host queue on the Vulkan device");
    for name in STATE_SETTERS {
        s.register(&format!("nvn:nvn{name}"), record_state, "pure state setter recorded on the host");
    }
    for name in STATE_GETTERS {
        s.register(&format!("nvn:nvn{name}"), read_state, "returns what the matching setter recorded");
    }
    for kind in BUILDERS {
        s.register_prefix(&format!("nvn:nvn{kind}BuilderSet"), record_state, "builder state recorded on the host");
        s.register_prefix(&format!("nvn:nvn{kind}BuilderGet"), read_state, "returns what the matching builder setter recorded");
    }
    for kind in LABELLED {
        s.register(&format!("nvn:nvn{kind}SetDebugLabel"), set_debug_label, "debug labels kept for diagnostics");
    }
}

/// Builders: objects whose setters only accumulate state until an
/// `Initialize` consumes it. Computed builder queries (storage sizes and the
/// like) are registered by exact name and take precedence.
const BUILDERS: &[&str] =
    &["Buffer", "Event", "MemoryPool", "Program", "Queue", "Sampler", "Window", "DlssNetwork"];

const LABELLED: &[&str] = &[
    "Buffer", "CommandBuffer", "Device", "MemoryPool", "Program", "Queue", "SamplerPool", "Sampler", "Sync",
    "TexturePool", "Texture", "Window",
];

/// Procedures whose whole effect is the state they set on their object.
const STATE_SETTERS: &[&str] = &["DeviceSetDepthMode", "DeviceSetWindowOriginMode"];

/// Getters answered from the matching setter's recorded state.
const STATE_GETTERS: &[&str] = &["DeviceGetDepthMode", "DeviceGetWindowOriginMode"];

/// Device calls that tune performance or debugging and change no result the
/// game can observe: fast-clear registrations (the host clears at full rate
/// for every value), the shader cache, checkpoints and the debug callback,
/// which the host never needs to call because it reports faults itself.
const DEVICE_HINTS: &[&str] = &[
    "RegisterFastClearColor",
    "RegisterFastClearColorIndex",
    "RegisterFastClearColori",
    "RegisterFastClearColoriIndex",
    "RegisterFastClearColorui",
    "RegisterFastClearColoruiIndex",
    "RegisterFastClearDepth",
    "RegisterFastClearDepthIndex",
    "RegisterFastClearStencil",
    "RegisterFastClearStencilIndex",
    "SetIntermediateShaderCache",
    "InstallDebugCallback",
    "SetAutomaticCheckpointsEnable",
    "SetAutomaticCheckpointsMask",
    "SetAutomaticCheckpointsSamplingInterval",
    "SetAutomaticCheckpointsByDebugGroup",
    "SetCheckpointCallStacksEnable",
    "SetCheckpointMaxCallStacksDepth",
];

```

`crates/ew-boot/src/nvn_cmd.rs`:

```rs
//! NVN command buffers and queue submission on the host.
//!
//! Commands are recorded on the host, not into the guest memory the game gives
//! the command buffer: every call between `BeginRecording` and `EndRecording`
//! becomes a [`Cmd`] holding its arguments and a copy of any guest memory they
//! point at, so the game is free to reuse its stack and scratch memory. The
//! guest command and control memory is accounted as given and never consumed,
//! which is why the out-of-memory callback never fires.
//!
//! `QueueSubmitCommands` executes the commands in order. Commands whose effect
//! is on memory the game can read back (buffer copies and clears, uniform
//! updates, reports, fences, events) are carried out on guest memory here.
//! Drawing, clearing render targets and texture copies are counted and kept
//! for the renderer; nothing is drawn yet, and the run report says so.

use crate::hle::{read_bytes, write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use crate::nvn::called;
use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, VecDeque};

const NVN_TRUE: u64 = 1;

/// One recorded command.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Cmd {
    /// The procedure, as its index among the run-time host functions.
    pub op: u32,
    pub x: [u64; 7],
    pub v: [u64; 4],
    /// Guest memory the arguments pointed at, copied when recorded.
    pub data: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CommandBuffer {
    pub recording: Option<Vec<Cmd>>,
    pub command_memory: u64,
    pub control_memory: u64,
    pub callback: u64,
    pub callback_data: u64,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Commands {
    pub buffers: BTreeMap<u64, CommandBuffer>,
    /// Finished command sets by handle.
    pub handles: BTreeMap<u64, Vec<Cmd>>,
    /// Handles in creation order, for retiring old ones.
    pub order: VecDeque<u64>,
    pub next_handle: u64,
    /// Totals for the run report.
    pub submitted: u64,
    pub executed: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
}

/// Handles stay valid for this many newer ones; NVN invalidates a handle once
/// its command memory is reused, which happens far sooner in practice.
const LIVE_HANDLES: usize = 1 << 16;

const HANDLE_BASE: u64 = 0x7E00_0000_0000;

fn cmds<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Commands) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<Commands, R>(f)
}

fn op_index(state: &State) -> u32 {
    ((state.pc - state.host.dyn_base) / 16) as u32
}

pub fn op_name(state: &State, op: u32) -> String {
    state.host.dyn_stubs.get(op as usize).map(|n| n.trim_start_matches("nvn:").to_string()).unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Guest memory a command's arguments point at: (pointer argument, count
/// argument or none, bytes per element or fixed size). Indices are into x[].
fn pointer_args(name: &str) -> &'static [(usize, Option<usize>, u64)] {
    match name.trim_start_matches("nvnCommandBuffer") {
        "BindVertexBuffers" | "BindTransformFeedbackBuffers" => &[(3, Some(2), 16)],
        "BindUniformBuffers" | "BindStorageBuffers" | "BindUniformBuffersDeferred" | "BindStorageBuffersDeferred" => {
            &[(4, Some(3), 16)]
        }
        "BindTextures" | "BindImages" | "BindSeparateTextures" | "BindSeparateSamplers" | "BindTexturesDeferred"
        | "BindImagesDeferred" | "BindSeparateTexturesDeferred" | "BindSeparateSamplersDeferred" => &[(4, Some(3), 8)],
        "SetViewports" | "SetScissors" => &[(3, Some(2), 16)],
        "SetDepthRanges" => &[(3, Some(2), 8)],
        "ClearColor" | "ClearColori" | "ClearColorui" => &[(2, None, 16)],
        "SetBlendColor" => &[(1, None, 16)],
        "SetRenderTargets" => &[(2, Some(1), 8), (3, Some(1), 8)],
        "UpdateUniformBuffer" => &[(5, Some(4), 1)],
        "CopyBufferToTexture" => &[(4, None, 24)],
        "CopyTextureToBuffer" => &[(3, None, 24)],
        "CopyTextureToTexture" => &[(3, None, 24), (6, None, 24)],
        "DrawTexture" => &[(2, None, 16), (3, None, 16)],
        "ClearTexture" | "ClearTexturei" | "ClearTextureui" => &[(3, None, 24), (4, None, 16)],
        "BindVertexAttribState" => &[(2, Some(1), 4)],
        "BindVertexStreamState" => &[(2, Some(1), 8)],
        "BindChannelMaskState" | "BindColorState" | "BindPolygonState" => &[(1, None, 4)],
        "BindBlendState" | "BindDepthStencilState" | "BindMultisampleState" => &[(1, None, 8)],
        _ => &[],
    }
}

/// Every recordable `nvnCommandBuffer*` procedure.
fn record(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let name = called(state);
    let cb = state.x[0];
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    for &(ptr, count, size) in pointer_args(&name) {
        let p = state.x[ptr];
        let n = count.map(|c| state.x[c] & 0xFFFF_FFFF).unwrap_or(1);
        if p == 0 || n == 0 {
            data.push(Vec::new());
            continue;
        }
        match read_bytes(state, p, n * size) {
            Ok(b) => data.push(b),
            Err(e) => return e,
        }
    }
    let mut x = [0u64; 7];
    x.copy_from_slice(&state.x[1..8]);
    let v = [state.v[0][0], state.v[1][0], state.v[2][0], state.v[3][0]];
    let cmd = Cmd { op: op_index(state), x, v, data };
    let ok = cmds(state, |c| match c.buffers.get_mut(&cb).and_then(|b| b.recording.as_mut()) {
        Some(list) => {
            list.push(cmd);
            true
        }
        None => false,
    });
    if ok {
        HostResult::Returned(0)
    } else {
        HostResult::Unavailable(format!("{name} on command buffer 0x{cb:x}, which is not recording"))
    }
}

fn cb_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let cb = state.x[0];
    cmds(state, |c| c.buffers.insert(cb, CommandBuffer::default()));
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

fn cb_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let cb = state.x[0];
    cmds(state, |c| c.buffers.remove(&cb));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn with_cb(state: &mut State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut CommandBuffer, &[u64]) -> u64) -> HostResult {
    let cb = state.x[0];
    let args = state.x[1..8].to_vec();
    match cmds(state, |c| c.buffers.get_mut(&cb).map(|b| f(b, &args))) {
        Some(v) => HostResult::Returned(v),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("{} on command buffer 0x{cb:x}, which was never initialized", called(state))),
    }
}

fn add_command_memory(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, a| {
        b.command_memory += a[2];
        0
    })
}

fn add_control_memory(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, a| {
        b.control_memory += a[1];
        0
    })
}

fn command_memory_size(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, _| b.command_memory)
}

fn control_memory_size(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, _| b.control_memory)
}

fn memory_used(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |_, _| 0)
}

fn set_memory_callback(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, a| {
        b.callback = a[0];
        0
    })
}

fn set_memory_callback_data(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, a| {
        b.callback_data = a[0];
        0
    })
}

fn get_memory_callback(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, _| b.callback)
}

fn get_memory_callback_data(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, _| b.callback_data)
}

fn ignore_setting(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |_, _| 0)
}

fn begin_recording(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, _| {
        b.recording = Some(Vec::new());
        0
    })
}

fn is_recording(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    with_cb(state, |b, _| b.recording.is_some() as u64)
}

/// `nvnCommandBufferEndRecording(cb)`: the commands become a handle.
fn end_recording(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let cb = state.x[0];
    let handle = cmds(state, |c| {
        let list = c.buffers.get_mut(&cb)?.recording.take()?;
        c.next_handle += 1;
        let h = HANDLE_BASE + c.next_handle * 0x100;
        c.handles.insert(h, list);
        c.order.push_back(h);
        while c.order.len() > LIVE_HANDLES {
            if let Some(old) = c.order.pop_front() {
                c.handles.remove(&old);
            }
        }
        Some(h)
    });
    match handle {
        Some(h) => HostResult::Returned(h),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("nvnCommandBufferEndRecording on 0x{cb:x}, which is not recording")),
    }
}

/// `nvnDeviceFinalizeCommandHandle(device, handle)`: the game is done with
/// the commands behind a handle, so the host list is dropped.
fn finalize_command_handle(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let h = state.x[1];
    cmds(state, |c| {
        c.handles.remove(&h);
        c.order.retain(|o| *o != h);
    });
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// A storage-backed pool's GPU address is its guest address; anything else
/// cannot be reached from the CPU.
fn guest_of(state: &State, gpu: u64, len: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    state.host.ext.with::<crate::nvn_mem::Memory, _>(|m| {
        m.pools.values().find_map(|p| {
            (p.storage != 0 && gpu >= p.gpu && gpu + len <= p.gpu + p.size).then(|| p.storage + (gpu - p.gpu))
        })
    })
}

fn now_ns() -> u64 {
    crate::threads::now_ticks().saturating_mul(1_000_000_000) / crate::threads::TICK_FREQ
}

/// Run one command. Memory effects happen now; everything else is counted.
fn execute(state: &mut State, cmd: &Cmd, depth: u32) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    let name = op_name(state, cmd.op);
    let short = name.trim_start_matches("nvnCommandBuffer").to_string();
    let x = &cmd.x;
    match short.as_str() {
        "CallCommands" | "CopyCommands" => {
            // (cb, count, const NVNcommandHandle*): the handles were read at
            // record time only as a pointer, so read them now.
            let (n, p) = (x[0] & 0xFFFF_FFFF, x[1]);
            let raw = read_bytes(state, p, n * 8)?;
            for h in raw.chunks(8).map(|c| u64::from_le_bytes(c.try_into().unwrap())) {
                run_handle(state, h, depth + 1)?;
            }
        }
        "CopyBufferToBuffer" => {
            // (cb, src, dst, size, flags)
            let (src, dst, size) = (x[0], x[1], x[2]);
            if let (Some(s), Some(d)) = (guest_of(state, src, size), guest_of(state, dst, size)) {
                let bytes = read_bytes(state, s, size)?;
                write_bytes(state, d, &bytes)?;
            }
        }
        "ClearBuffer" => {
            // (cb, dst, size, value)
            let (dst, size, value) = (x[0], x[1], x[2] as u32);
            if let Some(d) = guest_of(state, dst, size) {
                let bytes: Vec<u8> = value.to_le_bytes().iter().copied().cycle().take(size as usize).collect();
                write_bytes(state, d, &bytes)?;
            }
        }
        "UpdateUniformBuffer" => {
            // (cb, buffer, bufferSize, updateOffset, updateSize, data)
            let (buffer, offset) = (x[0], x[2]);
            let bytes = cmd.data.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
            if let Some(d) = guest_of(state, buffer + offset, bytes.len() as u64) {
                write_bytes(state, d, &bytes)?;
            }
        }
        "ReportValue" => {
            // (cb, value, buffer): a 32-bit report.
            let (value, buffer) = (x[0] as u32, x[1]);
            if let Some(d) = guest_of(state, buffer, 4) {
                write_bytes(state, d, &value.to_le_bytes())?;
            }
        }
        "ReportCounter" => {
            // (cb, counterType, buffer): a 16-byte report of a 64-bit counter
            // and a 64-bit timestamp. The host executes no GPU work, so every
            // counter other than the timestamp reads zero.
            let buffer = x[1];
            if let Some(d) = guest_of(state, buffer, 16) {
                let mut rep = [0u8; 16];
                rep[8..].copy_from_slice(&now_ns().to_le_bytes());
                write_bytes(state, d, &rep)?;
            }
        }
        "SignalEvent" => {
            // (cb, event, mode, location, flags, value)
            crate::nvn_prog::signal(state, x[0], x[1] & 0xFFFF_FFFF, x[4] as u32)?;
        }
        "FenceSync" => {
            let sync = x[0];
            state.host.ext.with::<crate::nvn_mem::Memory, _>(|m| m.signalled.insert(sync, true));
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    cmds(state, |c| *c.executed.entry(short).or_insert(0) += 1);
    Ok(())
}

fn run_handle(state: &mut State, handle: u64, depth: u32) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    if depth > 8 {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable("command handles nest deeper than 8".into()));
    }
    let Some(list) = cmds(state, |c| c.handles.get(&handle).cloned()) else {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("submitted command handle 0x{handle:x} does not exist")));
    };
    for cmd in &list {
        execute(state, cmd, depth)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `nvnQueueSubmitCommands(NVNqueue*, int count, const NVNcommandHandle*)`.
fn queue_submit_commands(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (n, p) = (state.x[1] & 0xFFFF_FFFF, state.x[2]);
    let raw = match read_bytes(state, p, n * 8) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => return e,
    };
    for h in raw.chunks(8).map(|c| u64::from_le_bytes(c.try_into().unwrap())) {
        if let Err(e) = run_handle(state, h, 0) {
            return e;
        }
    }
    cmds(state, |c| c.submitted += n);
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    s.register_prefix("nvn:nvnCommandBuffer", record, "recorded on the host with the memory its arguments point at");
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult, &'static str)] = &[
        ("nvnCommandBufferInitialize", cb_initialize, "a host command list"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferFinalize", cb_finalize, "forgets the command buffer"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferAddCommandMemory", add_command_memory, "accounted; commands are stored on the host"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferAddControlMemory", add_control_memory, "accounted; commands are stored on the host"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetCommandMemorySize", command_memory_size, "memory the game has given"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetControlMemorySize", control_memory_size, "memory the game has given"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetCommandMemoryUsed", memory_used, "host recording consumes none of it"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetControlMemoryUsed", memory_used, "host recording consumes none of it"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetCommandMemoryFree", command_memory_size, "all of it stays free"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetControlMemoryFree", control_memory_size, "all of it stays free"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferSetMemoryCallback", set_memory_callback, "kept; never called, memory never runs out"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferSetMemoryCallbackData", set_memory_callback_data, "kept for GetMemoryCallbackData"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetMemoryCallback", get_memory_callback, "what the game set"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferGetMemoryCallbackData", get_memory_callback_data, "what the game set"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferSetCommandMemoryCallbackEnabled", ignore_setting, "the callback never fires"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferSetControlMemoryCallbackEnabled", ignore_setting, "the callback never fires"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferSetRecordingMode", ignore_setting, "host recording has one mode"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferBeginRecording", begin_recording, "starts a host command list"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferEndRecording", end_recording, "returns a handle to the host command list"),
        ("nvnCommandBufferIsRecording", is_recording, "whether recording is open"),
        ("nvnDeviceFinalizeCommandHandle", finalize_command_handle, "drops the host command list"),
        ("nvnQueueSubmitCommands", queue_submit_commands, "executes memory effects; draws are counted, not rendered"),
    ];
    for (name, handler, claim) in table {
        s.register(&format!("nvn:{name}"), *handler, claim);
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-boot/src/nvn_mem.rs`:

```rs
//! NVN memory pools, buffers, syncs and queue control on the host.
//!
//! NVN memory is guest memory: a pool's storage is a range the game allocated,
//! and the GPU reads it in place. The host renderer reads the same guest bytes
//! when it executes work, so a storage-backed pool's GPU address is its guest
//! address and map/flush/invalidate need no copies. A virtual pool (no storage)
//! gets addresses from a range above guest memory that nothing can map.
//!
//! Work submitted to a queue completes before the submitting call returns,
//! which is why a fence is signalled as soon as it is placed.

use crate::hle::{HostResult, HostServices};
use crate::nvn::{called, field, set_field};
use ew_lift::State;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const NVN_TRUE: u64 = 1;

/// Base of the GPU address range for pools without storage.
const VIRTUAL_BASE: u64 = 0x80_0000_0000;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Pool {
    pub storage: u64,
    pub size: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub gpu: u64,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Memory {
    pub pools: BTreeMap<u64, Pool>,
    pub next_virtual: u64,
    /// Buffers: object to (pool, offset, size).
    pub buffers: BTreeMap<u64, (u64, u64, u64)>,
    /// Syncs that a queue has signalled.
    pub signalled: BTreeMap<u64, bool>,
}

fn mem<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Memory) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<Memory, R>(f)
}

/// Arguments a builder setter recorded (see `nvn::record_state`).
fn recorded_args(state: &State, obj: u64, setter: &str) -> Option<Vec<u64>> {
    state.host.ext.with::<crate::nvn::Nvn, _>(|n| n.state.get(&obj).and_then(|m| m.get(setter)).cloned())
}

/// `nvnMemoryPoolInitialize(NVNmemoryPool*, const NVNmemoryPoolBuilder*)`.
fn pool_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (pool, b) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let Some(storage) = recorded_args(state, b, "nvnMemoryPoolBuilderSetStorage") else {
        return HostResult::Unavailable("nvnMemoryPoolInitialize with no storage or size set".into());
    };
    let (ptr, size) = (storage[0], storage[1]);
    let flags = recorded_args(state, b, "nvnMemoryPoolBuilderSetFlags").map(|a| a[0]).unwrap_or(0);
    if ptr != 0 && ptr.saturating_add(size) > state.mem.len() as u64 {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "nvnMemoryPoolInitialize storage 0x{ptr:x}+0x{size:x} is outside guest memory"
        ));
    }
    let gpu = mem(state, |m| {
        let gpu = if ptr != 0 {
            ptr
        } else {
            let at = VIRTUAL_BASE + m.next_virtual;
            m.next_virtual += size.div_ceil(0x1_0000) * 0x1_0000;
            at
        };
        m.pools.insert(pool, Pool { storage: ptr, size, flags, gpu });
        gpu
    });
    state.host.log.push(format!(
        "gfx: memory pool 0x{pool:x}: 0x{size:x} bytes, flags 0x{flags:x}, GPU address 0x{gpu:x}"
    ));
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

fn pool_query(state: &mut State, f: impl FnOnce(&Pool) -> u64) -> HostResult {
    let pool = state.x[0];
    match mem(state, |m| m.pools.get(&pool).map(f)) {
        Some(v) => HostResult::Returned(v),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("{} on memory pool 0x{pool:x}, which was never initialized", called(state))),
    }
}

fn pool_get_buffer_address(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    pool_query(state, |p| p.gpu)
}

fn pool_map(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    pool_query(state, |p| p.storage)
}

fn pool_get_size(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    pool_query(state, |p| p.size)
}

fn pool_get_flags(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    pool_query(state, |p| p.flags)
}

fn pool_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let pool = state.x[0];
    mem(state, |m| m.pools.remove(&pool));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Flushes and invalidates: the host reads guest memory in place, so caches
/// are already coherent.
fn coherent(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nvnBufferInitialize(NVNbuffer*, const NVNbufferBuilder*)`.
fn buffer_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (buf, b) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let Some(st) = recorded_args(state, b, "nvnBufferBuilderSetStorage") else {
        return HostResult::Unavailable("nvnBufferInitialize with no storage set".into());
    };
    let (pool, offset, size) = (st[0], st[1], st[2]);
    let known = mem(state, |m| {
        let known = m.pools.contains_key(&pool);
        if known {
            m.buffers.insert(buf, (pool, offset, size));
        }
        known
    });
    if !known {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("nvnBufferInitialize on memory pool 0x{pool:x}, which was never initialized"));
    }
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

fn buffer_query(state: &mut State, f: impl FnOnce(&Pool, u64, u64, u64) -> u64) -> HostResult {
    let buf = state.x[0];
    let v = mem(state, |m| {
        let (pool, offset, size) = *m.buffers.get(&buf)?;
        m.pools.get(&pool).map(|p| f(p, pool, offset, size))
    });
    match v {
        Some(v) => HostResult::Returned(v),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("{} on buffer 0x{buf:x}, which was never initialized", called(state))),
    }
}

fn buffer_get_address(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    buffer_query(state, |p, _, off, _| p.gpu + off)
}

fn buffer_map(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    buffer_query(state, |p, _, off, _| if p.storage == 0 { 0 } else { p.storage + off })
}

fn buffer_get_size(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    buffer_query(state, |_, _, _, size| size)
}

fn buffer_get_memory_pool(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    buffer_query(state, |_, pool, _, _| pool)
}

fn buffer_get_memory_offset(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    buffer_query(state, |_, _, off, _| off)
}

fn buffer_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let buf = state.x[0];
    mem(state, |m| m.buffers.remove(&buf));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nvnSyncInitialize(NVNsync*, NVNdevice*)`.
fn sync_initialize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let sync = state.x[0];
    mem(state, |m| m.signalled.insert(sync, false));
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

fn sync_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let sync = state.x[0];
    mem(state, |m| m.signalled.remove(&sync));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nvnQueueFenceSync(NVNqueue*, NVNsync*, condition, flags)`: work before the
/// fence has already completed on the host, so the fence is signalled now.
fn queue_fence_sync(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let sync = state.x[1];
    mem(state, |m| m.signalled.insert(sync, true));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// NVN wait results.
const WAIT_ALREADY_SIGNALED: u64 = 0;
const WAIT_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED: u64 = 2;

/// `nvnSyncWait(const NVNsync*, uint64 timeoutNs)`. A sync no queue has
/// fenced can never signal, so the wait reports its timeout.
fn sync_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let sync = state.x[0];
    let done = mem(state, |m| m.signalled.get(&sync).copied().unwrap_or(false));
    HostResult::Returned(if done { WAIT_ALREADY_SIGNALED } else { WAIT_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED })
}

/// `nvnQueueWaitSync(NVNqueue*, const NVNsync*)`: the queue is in order and
/// synchronous, so a wait on a fence is already satisfied.
fn queue_wait_sync(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(NVN_TRUE)
}

/// `nvnQueueFlush` / `nvnQueueFinish`: submitted work has executed.
fn queue_flush(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `nvnQueueGetError(NVNqueue*, NVNqueueErrorInfo*)`: no GPU error occurred.
fn queue_get_error(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn queue_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let q = state.x[0];
    set_field(state, q, "live", 0);
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Memory-usage counters: the host queue keeps its commands on the host and
/// uses none of the guest memory the game gave it.
fn zero(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

pub fn register(s: &mut HostServices) {
    let _ = field;
    let table: &[(&str, fn(&mut State) -> HostResult, &'static str)] = &[
        ("nvnMemoryPoolInitialize", pool_initialize, "a pool over the game's guest storage, GPU address = guest address"),
        ("nvnMemoryPoolGetBufferAddress", pool_get_buffer_address, "the pool's GPU address"),
        ("nvnMemoryPoolMap", pool_map, "the pool's guest storage"),
        ("nvnMemoryPoolGetSize", pool_get_size, "the size the pool was created with"),
        ("nvnMemoryPoolGetFlags", pool_get_flags, "the flags the pool was created with"),

        ("nvnMemoryPoolInvalidateMappedRange", coherent, "guest memory is read in place, so it is coherent"),

        ("nvnQueueGetTotalComputeMemoryUsed", zero, "host queues use none of the game's queue memory"),
        ("nvnQueueResetMemoryUsageCounts", zero, "nothing to reset"),
    ];

        s.register(&format!("nvn:{name}"), *handler, claim);
```
