`crates/ew-boot/src/threads.rs`:

```rs
//! Multi-threaded `nn::os`: threads, blocking synchronisation, sleeps and timers.
//!
//! Guest threads are scheduled by the dispatcher (see `sched`). A service that
//! has to wait returns [`HostResult::Block`] with a continuation; the scheduler
//! parks the thread and retries the continuation, with that thread's registers
//! loaded, whenever it next considers the thread. Waits are therefore real
//! waits: a mutex held by another thread, an unsignalled event, a condition
//! variable or `WaitThread` all suspend the caller until another thread changes
//! the state, and a run in which every thread waits on something only another
//! thread could provide stops as a deadlock with every waiter named.
//!
//! Continuations keep their private data in caller-saved registers (`x2`..`x7`
//! beyond the call's own arguments), which the AArch64 procedure call standard
//! lets a callee clobber, so the guest cannot observe the bookkeeping.
//!
//! State lives in the guest objects, tagged with magic words, as in `services`.
//! Mutexes record their owner, so ownership errors are reported, not ignored.

use crate::hle::{read_bytes, write_bytes, HostResult, HostServices};
use ew_lift::{State, ThreadInfo};

const CV_NEXT: u64 = 0;
const CV_RELEASED: u64 = 4;
const TIMER_MAGIC: u32 = u32::from_le_bytes(*b"EWTM");
const EVENT_MAGIC: u32 = u32::from_le_bytes(*b"EWEV");
const SEM_MAGIC: u32 = u32::from_le_bytes(*b"EWSM");
const RW_MAGIC: u32 = u32::from_le_bytes(*b"EWRW");

/// The tick frequency every title measures time against.
pub const TICK_FREQ: u64 = 19_200_000;

/// `nn::os::ConditionVariableStatus`.
const CV_NO_TIMEOUT: u64 = 0;
const CV_TIMEOUT: u64 = 1;

// ---- guest object access ----------------------------------------------------

fn r32(state: &State, a: u64) -> Result<u32, HostResult> {
    let b = read_bytes(state, a, 4)?;
    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))
}
fn w32(state: &mut State, a: u64, v: u32) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    write_bytes(state, a, &v.to_le_bytes())
}
fn r64(state: &State, a: u64) -> Result<u64, HostResult> {
    let b = read_bytes(state, a, 8)?;
    Ok(u64::from_le_bytes(b.try_into().unwrap()))
}
fn w64(state: &mut State, a: u64, v: u64) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    write_bytes(state, a, &v.to_le_bytes())
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($e:expr) => {
        match $e {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(e) => return e,
        }
    };
}

fn me(state: &State) -> u64 {
    state.host.thread_object
}

/// Host clock in guest ticks. Monotonic, so a deadline cannot move backwards.
pub fn now_ticks() -> u64 {
    use std::sync::OnceLock;
    static START: OnceLock<std::time::Instant> = OnceLock::new();
    let start = *START.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now);
    let ns = start.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64;
    // Offset so the first tick is not zero, which some titles treat as "unset".
    ns.saturating_mul(TICK_FREQ) / 1_000_000_000 + TICK_FREQ
}

fn ns_to_ticks(ns: u64) -> u64 {
    ((ns as u128 * TICK_FREQ as u128) / 1_000_000_000) as u64
}

fn block(resume: fn(&mut State) -> HostResult) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Block { resume, timed: false }
}
fn block_timed(resume: fn(&mut State) -> HostResult) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Block { resume, timed: true }
}

// ---- mutexes -------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// Mutex state lives on the host, keyed by the guest object's address: the
// guest objects differ in size (nn::os::MutexType is 32 bytes, this SDK's
// pthread_mutex_t is 8, and a condition variable often follows directly), so
// writing state into them would corrupt their neighbours. An address the host
// has not seen is a zeroed static mutex: unlocked and not recursive.

/// (depth, recursive, owner) by mutex address.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Mutexes(std::collections::HashMap<u64, (u32, u32, u64)>);

fn mutex_state(state: &mut State, m: u64) -> Result<(u32, u32, u64), HostResult> {
    Ok(state.host.ext.with::<Mutexes, _>(|x| x.0.get(&m).copied().unwrap_or_default()))
}

/// Record a new depth and owner, keeping the mutex's recursive flag.
fn mutex_hold(state: &mut State, m: u64, depth: u32, owner: u64) {
    state.host.ext.with::<Mutexes, _>(|x| {
        let e = x.0.entry(m).or_default();
        e.0 = depth;
        e.2 = owner;
    });
}

fn mutex_init(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (m, recursive) = (state.x[0], (state.x[1] & 1) as u32);
    state.host.ext.with::<Mutexes, _>(|x| x.0.insert(m, (0, recursive, 0)));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mutex_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let m = state.x[0];
    state.host.ext.with::<Mutexes, _>(|x| x.0.remove(&m));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Take the mutex in `x0` for the current thread, or say who holds it.
fn try_take(state: &mut State, m: u64) -> Result<bool, HostResult> {
    let (depth, recursive, owner) = mutex_state(state, m)?;
    let cur = me(state);
    if depth == 0 {
        mutex_hold(state, m, 1, cur);
        return Ok(true);
    }
    if owner == cur {
        if recursive == 0 {
            return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
                "self-deadlock: thread 0x{cur:x} locked the non-recursive mutex at 0x{m:x} twice"
            )));
        }
        mutex_hold(state, m, depth + 1, cur);
        return Ok(true);
    }
    Ok(false)
}

pub(crate) fn mutex_lock(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    match try_take(state, state.x[0]) {
        Ok(true) => HostResult::Returned(0),
        Ok(false) => block(mutex_lock),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn mutex_try_lock(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    match try_take(state, state.x[0]) {
        Ok(taken) => HostResult::Returned(taken as u64),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn release(state: &mut State, m: u64) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    let (depth, _, owner) = mutex_state(state, m)?;
    let cur = me(state);
    if depth == 0 || owner != cur {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "thread 0x{cur:x} unlocked the mutex at 0x{m:x}, which it does not hold (depth {depth}, owner 0x{owner:x})"
        )));
    }
    mutex_hold(state, m, depth - 1, if depth == 1 { 0 } else { owner });
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn mutex_unlock(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    match release(state, state.x[0]) {
        Ok(()) => HostResult::Returned(0),
        Err(e) => e,
    }
}

fn mutex_locked_by_me(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let m = state.x[0];
    let (depth, _, owner) = t!(mutex_state(state, m));
    HostResult::Returned((depth > 0 && owner == me(state)) as u64)
}

// ---- condition variables: [next_ticket, released] ---------------------

fn cv_init(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let cv = state.x[0];
    t!(w32(state, cv + CV_NEXT, 0));
    t!(w32(state, cv + CV_RELEASED, 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// The next ticket to hand out and the release mark. `ConditionVariableType`
/// is 8 bytes and is often followed directly by its mutex, so both counters
/// live in those 8 bytes; zeroed memory is a valid, empty condition variable.
pub(crate) fn cv_fields(state: &mut State, cv: u64) -> Result<(u32, u32), HostResult> {
    Ok((r32(state, cv + CV_NEXT)?, r32(state, cv + CV_RELEASED)?))
}

pub(crate) fn cv_signal(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let cv = state.x[0];
    let (next, released) = t!(cv_fields(state, cv));
    if released < next {
        t!(w32(state, cv + CV_RELEASED, released + 1));
    }
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

pub(crate) fn cv_broadcast(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let cv = state.x[0];
    let (next, _) = t!(cv_fields(state, cv));
    t!(w32(state, cv + CV_RELEASED, next));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Common wait: take a ticket, release the mutex completely, park.
/// x0 = cv, x1 = mutex; the ticket goes to x2 and the saved depth to x5.
pub(crate) fn cv_enter(state: &mut State) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    let (cv, m) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let (next, _) = cv_fields(state, cv)?;
    w32(state, cv + CV_NEXT, next.wrapping_add(1))?;
    let (depth, _, owner) = mutex_state(state, m)?;
    if depth == 0 || owner != me(state) {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "waited on the condition variable at 0x{cv:x} without holding the mutex at 0x{m:x}"
        )));
    }
    mutex_hold(state, m, 0, 0);
    state.x[2] = next as u64;
    state.x[5] = depth as u64;
    Ok(())
}

/// Reacquire the mutex with its saved depth, then return `x6`.
pub(crate) fn cv_relock(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let m = state.x[1];
    let (depth, _, _) = t!(mutex_state(state, m));
    if depth != 0 {
        return block(cv_relock);
    }
    let cur = me(state);
    mutex_hold(state, m, state.x[5] as u32, cur);
    HostResult::Returned(state.x[6])
}

fn cv_resume(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (cv, ticket) = (state.x[0], state.x[2] as u32);
    let (_, released) = t!(cv_fields(state, cv));
    // Tickets are handed out in order and released in order, so a ticket below
    // the release mark has been signalled.
    if ticket.wrapping_sub(released) as i32 >= 0 {
        return block(cv_resume);
    }
    state.x[6] = CV_NO_TIMEOUT;
    cv_relock(state)
}

fn cv_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(cv_enter(state));
    cv_resume(state)
}

/// `TimedWaitConditionVariable(cv, mutex, TimeSpan)`: deadline kept in x3.
fn cv_timed_resume(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (cv, ticket, deadline) = (state.x[0], state.x[2] as u32, state.x[3]);
    let (next, released) = t!(cv_fields(state, cv));
    if (ticket.wrapping_sub(released) as i32) < 0 {
        state.x[6] = CV_NO_TIMEOUT;
        return cv_relock(state);
    }
    if now_ticks() >= deadline {
        // Withdraw this waiter: the slot it held is skipped by a later signal
        // only if it is the newest; otherwise a signal may land on it, which is
        // the spurious-wakeup latitude the API already grants.
        if ticket.wrapping_add(1) == next {
            t!(w32(state, cv + CV_NEXT, ticket));
        }
        state.x[6] = CV_TIMEOUT;
        return cv_relock(state);
    }
    block_timed(cv_timed_resume)
}

fn cv_timed_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let deadline = now_ticks().saturating_add(ns_to_ticks(state.x[2]));
    t!(cv_enter(state));
    state.x[3] = deadline;
    cv_timed_resume(state)
}

// ---- events, light events, semaphores, reader/writer locks -------------------
// Layouts match `services`: event [magic, signalled, manual-clear],
// light event [signalled], semaphore [magic, count, max], rw [magic, readers, writer].

fn event_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let e = state.x[0];
    if t!(r32(state, e)) != EVENT_MAGIC {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{e:x} is not an initialised event"));
    }
    if t!(r32(state, e + 4)) == 0 {
        return block(event_wait);
    }
    // nn::os::EventClearMode: ManualClear = 0, AutoClear = 1.
    if t!(r32(state, e + 8)) == 1 {
        t!(w32(state, e + 4, 0));
    }
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Light events auto-clear on a successful wait in this model, as `services`
/// implemented them for the single-threaded case.
fn light_event_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let e = state.x[0];
    if t!(r32(state, e)) == 0 {
        return block(light_event_wait);
    }
    t!(w32(state, e, 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn sem_acquire(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let s = state.x[0];
    if t!(r32(state, s)) != SEM_MAGIC {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{s:x} is not an initialised semaphore"));
    }
    let count = t!(r32(state, s + 4));
    if count == 0 {
        return block(sem_acquire);
    }
    t!(w32(state, s + 4, count - 1));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn rw_read(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let l = state.x[0];
    if t!(r32(state, l)) != RW_MAGIC {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{l:x} is not an initialised reader/writer lock"));
    }
    if t!(r32(state, l + 8)) != 0 {
        return block(rw_read);
    }
    let readers = t!(r32(state, l + 4));
    t!(w32(state, l + 4, readers + 1));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn rw_write(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let l = state.x[0];
    if t!(r32(state, l)) != RW_MAGIC {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{l:x} is not an initialised reader/writer lock"));
    }
    if t!(r32(state, l + 4)) != 0 || t!(r32(state, l + 8)) != 0 {
        return block(rw_write);
    }
    t!(w32(state, l + 8, 1));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

// ---- threads -------------------------------------------------------------------

/// `CreateThread(ThreadType*, ThreadFunction, void* arg, void* stack,
/// size_t stackSize, int priority[, int idealCore])`. The game supplies the
/// stack; the thread starts at `StartThread`.
fn create_thread(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (t, entry, arg, stack, size, prio) =
        (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2], state.x[3], state.x[4], state.x[5] as i32);
    if t == 0 || entry == 0 || stack == 0 || size < 0x1000 {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "CreateThread(0x{t:x}, entry 0x{entry:x}, stack 0x{stack:x}+0x{size:x}) has a null or tiny argument"
        ));
    }
    if stack.checked_add(size).is_none_or(|end| end as usize > state.mem.len()) {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("thread stack 0x{stack:x}+0x{size:x} is outside guest memory"));
    }
    state.host.threads.insert(
        t,
        ThreadInfo { entry, arg, stack_top: (stack + size) & !0xF, priority: prio, ..Default::default() },
    );
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn start_thread(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let t = state.x[0];
    match state.host.threads.get_mut(&t) {
        Some(info) => {
            info.started = true;
            state.host.thread_starts += 1;
            HostResult::Returned(0)
        }
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("StartThread on 0x{t:x}, which was never created")),
    }
}

fn wait_thread(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let t = state.x[0];
    match state.host.threads.get(&t) {
        Some(info) if info.exited => HostResult::Returned(0),
        Some(info) if !info.started => HostResult::Unavailable(format!(
            "WaitThread on 0x{t:x}, which was created but never started, would wait forever"
        )),
        Some(_) => block(wait_thread),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("WaitThread on 0x{t:x}, which was never created")),
    }
}

fn destroy_thread(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let t = state.x[0];
    match state.host.threads.get(&t) {
        Some(info) if info.exited || !info.started => {
            state.host.threads.remove(&t);
            HostResult::Returned(0)
        }
        Some(_) => block(destroy_thread),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("DestroyThread on 0x{t:x}, which was never created")),
    }
}

fn set_thread_name(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (t, name) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    if let Some(info) = state.host.threads.get_mut(&t) {
        info.name = name;
    }
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn current_thread(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(me(state))
}

fn thread_priority(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let t = state.x[0];
    HostResult::Returned(state.host.threads.get(&t).map(|i| i.priority as i64 as u64).unwrap_or(44))
}

fn change_priority(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (t, p) = (state.x[0], state.x[1] as i32);
    let old = state.host.threads.get(&t).map(|i| i.priority).unwrap_or(44);
    if let Some(info) = state.host.threads.get_mut(&t) {
        info.priority = p;
    }
    HostResult::Returned(old as i64 as u64)
}

/// `YieldThread()`: park for one scheduling round.
fn yield_thread(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    block(yielded)
}
fn yielded(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// `SleepThread(TimeSpan ns)`: deadline in x1.
fn sleep_thread(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let ns = state.x[0] as i64;
    if ns <= 0 {
        return block(yielded);
    }
    state.x[1] = now_ticks().saturating_add(ns_to_ticks(ns as u64));
    block_timed(sleep_resume)
}
fn sleep_resume(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    if now_ticks() >= state.x[1] {
        HostResult::Returned(0)
    } else {
        block_timed(sleep_resume)
    }
}

fn system_tick(_state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    HostResult::Returned(now_ticks())
}

// ---- timer events: [magic, signalled, manual, active, next u64, period u64] ----

fn timer_init(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let e = state.x[0];
    // nn::os::EventClearMode: ManualClear = 0, AutoClear = 1.
    let mode = (state.x[1] & 1) as u32;
    t!(w32(state, e, TIMER_MAGIC));
    t!(w32(state, e + 4, 0));
    t!(w32(state, e + 8, mode));
    t!(w32(state, e + 12, 0));
    t!(w64(state, e + 16, 0));
    t!(w64(state, e + 24, 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn timer_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(w32(state, state.x[0], 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Fire the timer if its deadline has passed, then report whether it is set.
fn timer_poll(state: &mut State, e: u64) -> Result<bool, HostResult> {
    if r32(state, e)? != TIMER_MAGIC {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{e:x} is not an initialised timer event")));
    }
    if r32(state, e + 12)? != 0 {
        let next = r64(state, e + 16)?;
        let now = now_ticks();
        if now >= next {
            w32(state, e + 4, 1)?;
            let period = r64(state, e + 24)?;
            if period == 0 {
                w32(state, e + 12, 0)?;
            } else {
                let missed = (now - next) / period + 1;
                w64(state, e + 16, next + missed * period)?;
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(r32(state, e + 4)? != 0)
}

fn timer_consume(state: &mut State, e: u64) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    if r32(state, e + 8)? == 1 {
        w32(state, e + 4, 0)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn timer_start(state: &mut State, e: u64, first_ns: u64, period_ns: u64) -> HostResult {
    if t!(r32(state, e)) != TIMER_MAGIC {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{e:x} is not an initialised timer event"));
    }
    state.host.log.push(format!("os: timer 0x{e:x} armed, first {first_ns} ns, period {period_ns} ns"));
    t!(w32(state, e + 12, 1));
    t!(w64(state, e + 16, now_ticks().saturating_add(ns_to_ticks(first_ns))));
    t!(w64(state, e + 24, ns_to_ticks(period_ns)));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn timer_start_periodic(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (e, first, period) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    timer_start(state, e, first, period.max(1))
}
fn timer_start_oneshot(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (e, first) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    timer_start(state, e, first, 0)
}
fn timer_stop(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(w32(state, state.x[0] + 12, 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}
fn timer_signal(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(w32(state, state.x[0] + 4, 1));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}
fn timer_clear(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(w32(state, state.x[0] + 4, 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}
fn timer_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let e = state.x[0];
    if !t!(timer_poll(state, e)) {
        let active = t!(r32(state, e + 12)) != 0;
        return if active { block_timed(timer_wait) } else { block(timer_wait) };
    }
    t!(timer_consume(state, e));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}
fn timer_try_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let e = state.x[0];
    if !t!(timer_poll(state, e)) {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    t!(timer_consume(state, e));
    HostResult::Returned(1)
}

// ---- multi-wait --------------------------------------------------------------
//
// Holders and their links are kept on the host, keyed by the guest objects'
// addresses, so the guest structures' own sizes never matter. A holder waits
// on an event or a system event (an ordinary event or a host timer event).
// WaitAny reports a signalled holder without consuming the signal, as on the
// console: the caller then waits on or clears the object itself.

#[derive(Default)]
struct MultiWaits {
    /// Each multi-wait's linked holders, in link order.
    lists: std::collections::HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>>,
    /// Each holder: (waited object, user data, linked multi-wait).
    holders: std::collections::HashMap<u64, (u64, u64, Option<u64>)>,
}

fn multi<R>(state: &State, f: impl FnOnce(&mut MultiWaits) -> R) -> R {
    state.host.ext.with::<MultiWaits, R>(f)
}

/// Whether an event or system event is signalled, without consuming it.
fn object_signalled(state: &mut State, e: u64) -> Result<bool, HostResult> {
    match r32(state, e)? {
        TIMER_MAGIC => timer_poll(state, e),
        EVENT_MAGIC => Ok(r32(state, e + 4)? != 0),
        // Never initialised by the host: nothing can have signalled it.
        _ => Ok(false),
    }
}

fn mw_init(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let mw = state.x[0];
    multi(state, |m| m.lists.insert(mw, Vec::new()));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mw_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let mw = state.x[0];
    multi(state, |m| m.lists.remove(&mw));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mw_holder_init(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (holder, object) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    multi(state, |m| m.holders.insert(holder, (object, 0, None)));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mw_holder_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let holder = state.x[0];
    multi(state, |m| m.holders.remove(&holder));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mw_link(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (mw, holder) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    let linked = multi(state, |m| {
        let h = m.holders.get_mut(&holder)?;
        h.2 = Some(mw);
        m.lists.entry(mw).or_default().push(holder);
        Some(())
    });
    match linked {
        Some(()) => HostResult::Returned(0),
        None => HostResult::Unavailable(format!("LinkMultiWaitHolder: holder 0x{holder:x} was never initialised")),
    }
}

fn mw_unlink(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let holder = state.x[0];
    multi(state, |m| {
        if let Some(mw) = m.holders.get_mut(&holder).and_then(|h| h.2.take()) {
            if let Some(list) = m.lists.get_mut(&mw) {
                list.retain(|h| *h != holder);
            }
        }
    });
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mw_set_user_data(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (holder, data) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    multi(state, |m| m.holders.entry(holder).or_insert((0, 0, None)).1 = data);
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mw_get_user_data(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let holder = state.x[0];
    HostResult::Returned(multi(state, |m| m.holders.get(&holder).map(|h| h.1).unwrap_or(0)))
}

/// `WaitAny(MultiWaitType*)`: the first linked holder whose object is
/// signalled, else wait.
fn mw_wait_any(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let mw = state.x[0];
    let linked: Vec<(u64, u64)> = multi(state, |m| {
        m.lists.get(&mw).map(|l| l.iter().filter_map(|h| m.holders.get(h).map(|x| (*h, x.0))).collect()).unwrap_or_default()
    });
    let mut timed = false;
    for (holder, object) in linked {
        if t!(object_signalled(state, object)) {
            return HostResult::Returned(holder);
        }
        timed |= t!(r32(state, object)) == TIMER_MAGIC;
    }
    if timed { block_timed(mw_wait_any) } else { block(mw_wait_any) }
}

// ---- system events ----------------------------------------------------------
//
// A system event the host creates (an audio renderer's frame event) is a timer
// event in the guest object, so waits block until the host clock fires it.
// Waits on events the game set up as ordinary events use the event layout.

/// Set up a timer event in a guest object, unarmed.
pub fn init_timer_event(state: &mut State, e: u64, auto_clear: bool) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    w32(state, e, TIMER_MAGIC)?;
    w32(state, e + 4, 0)?;
    w32(state, e + 8, auto_clear as u32)?;
    w32(state, e + 12, 0)?;
    w64(state, e + 16, 0)?;
    w64(state, e + 24, 0)
}

pub fn start_timer_event(state: &mut State, e: u64, first_ns: u64, period_ns: u64) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    match timer_start(state, e, first_ns, period_ns) {
        HostResult::Returned(_) => Ok(()),
        other => Err(other),
    }
}

pub fn stop_timer_event(state: &mut State, e: u64) -> Result<(), HostResult> {
    w32(state, e + 12, 0)
}

fn is_timer(state: &State, e: u64) -> Result<bool, HostResult> {
    Ok(r32(state, e)? == TIMER_MAGIC)
}

fn system_event_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    if t!(is_timer(state, state.x[0])) { timer_wait(state) } else { event_wait(state) }
}

fn system_event_try_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    if t!(is_timer(state, state.x[0])) {
        return timer_try_wait(state);
    }
    let e = state.x[0];
    if t!(r32(state, e)) != EVENT_MAGIC {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{e:x} is not an initialised system event"));
    }
    if t!(r32(state, e + 4)) == 0 {
        return HostResult::Returned(0);
    }
    if t!(r32(state, e + 8)) == 1 {
        t!(w32(state, e + 4, 0));
    }
    HostResult::Returned(1)
}

/// `TimedWaitSystemEvent(event, TimeSpan)`: deadline kept in x3.
fn system_event_timed_resume(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let deadline = state.x[3];
    match system_event_try_wait(state) {
        HostResult::Returned(1) => HostResult::Returned(1),
        HostResult::Returned(_) if now_ticks() >= deadline => HostResult::Returned(0),
        HostResult::Returned(_) => block_timed(system_event_timed_resume),
        other => other,
    }
}

fn system_event_timed_wait(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    state.x[3] = now_ticks().saturating_add(ns_to_ticks(state.x[1]));
    system_event_timed_resume(state)
}

fn system_event_clear(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(w32(state, state.x[0] + 4, 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn system_event_destroy(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(w32(state, state.x[0], 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

// ---- message queues: [magic, capacity, used, head, buffer u64] -------------
//
// Messages live in the buffer the game supplies, as a ring, exactly as the
// console keeps them. A full send or an empty receive blocks the caller.

const MQ_MAGIC: u32 = u32::from_le_bytes(*b"EWMQ");

fn mq(state: &State, q: u64) -> Result<(u32, u32, u32, u64), HostResult> {
    if r32(state, q)? != MQ_MAGIC {
        return Err(HostResult::Unavailable(format!("0x{q:x} is not an initialised message queue")));
    }
    Ok((r32(state, q + 4)?, r32(state, q + 8)?, r32(state, q + 12)?, r64(state, q + 16)?))
}

fn mq_init(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (q, buf, count) = (state.x[0], state.x[1], state.x[2]);
    if count == 0 || buf == 0 {
        return HostResult::Unavailable(format!("message queue 0x{q:x} given buffer 0x{buf:x} of {count} entries"));
    }
    t!(w32(state, q, MQ_MAGIC));
    t!(w32(state, q + 4, count as u32));
    t!(w32(state, q + 8, 0));
    t!(w32(state, q + 12, 0));
    t!(w64(state, q + 16, buf));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

fn mq_finalize(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    t!(w32(state, state.x[0], 0));
    HostResult::Returned(0)
}

/// Push at the back (or the front for `jam`). False when full.
fn mq_push(state: &mut State, q: u64, msg: u64, jam: bool) -> Result<bool, HostResult> {
    let (cap, used, head, buf) = mq(state, q)?;
    if used == cap {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let (slot, head) = if jam { let h = (head + cap - 1) % cap; (h, h) } else { ((head + used) % cap, head) };
    w64(state, buf + slot as u64 * 8, msg)?;
    w32(state, q + 8, used + 1)?;
    w32(state, q + 12, head)?;
    Ok(true)
}

/// Pop from the front into `out`. False when empty.
fn mq_pop(state: &mut State, out: u64, q: u64) -> Result<bool, HostResult> {
    let (cap, used, head, buf) = mq(state, q)?;
    if used == 0 {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let msg = r64(state, buf + head as u64 * 8)?;
    w64(state, out, msg)?;
    w32(state, q + 8, used - 1)?;
    w32(state, q + 12, (head + 1) % cap)?;
    Ok(true)
}

fn mq_send(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (q, msg) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    if t!(mq_push(state, q, msg, false)) { HostResult::Returned(0) } else { block(mq_send) }
}

fn mq_jam(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (q, msg) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    if t!(mq_push(state, q, msg, true)) { HostResult::Returned(0) } else { block(mq_jam) }
}

fn mq_try_send(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (q, msg) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    HostResult::Returned(t!(mq_push(state, q, msg, false)) as u64)
}

fn mq_receive(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (out, q) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    if t!(mq_pop(state, out, q)) { HostResult::Returned(0) } else { block(mq_receive) }
}

fn mq_try_receive(state: &mut State) -> HostResult {
    let (out, q) = (state.x[0], state.x[1]);
    HostResult::Returned(t!(mq_pop(state, out, q)) as u64)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn st() -> State {
        let mut s = State::default();
        s.host.thread_object = 0xA000;
        s
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_held_mutex_blocks_another_thread_until_released() {
        let mut s = st();
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(mutex_init(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(mutex_lock(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.host.thread_object = 0xB000;
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert!(matches!(mutex_lock(&mut s), HostResult::Block { timed: false, .. }));
        assert!(matches!(mutex_unlock(&mut s), HostResult::Unavailable(_)), "B does not own it");
        s.host.thread_object = 0xA000;
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(mutex_unlock(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.host.thread_object = 0xB000;
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(mutex_lock(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn condition_variable_releases_and_reacquires() {
        let mut s = st();
        s.x[0] = 0x200;
        cv_init(&mut s);
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        mutex_init(&mut s);
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        mutex_lock(&mut s);
        // Thread A waits: the mutex is released.
        s.x[0] = 0x200;
        s.x[1] = 0x100;
        let HostResult::Block { resume, .. } = cv_wait(&mut s) else { panic!("should wait") };
        let saved = s.x;
        assert_eq!(u32::from_le_bytes(s.mem[0x104..0x108].try_into().unwrap()), 0);
        // Thread B takes the mutex and signals.
        s.host.thread_object = 0xB000;
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(mutex_lock(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.x[0] = 0x200;
        cv_signal(&mut s);
        // A is released but must wait for the mutex B still holds.
        s.host.thread_object = 0xA000;
        s.x = saved;
        let HostResult::Block { resume, .. } = resume(&mut s) else { panic!("mutex still held") };
        let saved = s.x;
        s.host.thread_object = 0xB000;
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(mutex_unlock(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.host.thread_object = 0xA000;
        s.x = saved;
        assert_eq!(resume(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(CV_NO_TIMEOUT));
        s.x[0] = 0x100;
        assert_eq!(mutex_locked_by_me(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn threads_are_created_started_and_joined() {
        let mut s = st();
        s.mem.resize(0x40000, 0);
        s.x[0] = 0x300;
        s.x[1] = 0x1234;
        s.x[2] = 7;
        s.x[3] = 0x10000;
        s.x[4] = 0x8000;
        s.x[5] = 16;
        assert_eq!(create_thread(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        s.x[0] = 0x300;
        assert!(matches!(wait_thread(&mut s), HostResult::Unavailable(_)), "never started");
        assert_eq!(start_thread(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
        assert!(matches!(wait_thread(&mut s), HostResult::Block { .. }));
        s.host.threads.get_mut(&0x300).unwrap().exited = true;
        assert_eq!(wait_thread(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_one_shot_timer_fires_once() {
        let mut s = st();
        s.x[0] = 0x400;
        s.x[1] = 1; // EventClearMode_AutoClear
        timer_init(&mut s);
        s.x[0] = 0x400;
        s.x[1] = 0;
        timer_start_oneshot(&mut s);
        s.x[0] = 0x400;
        assert_eq!(timer_try_wait(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(1));
        assert_eq!(timer_try_wait(&mut s), HostResult::Returned(0));
    }
}

`crates/ew-format/src/bin/ew_decode.rs`:

```rs
//! ew-decode: decompress an LZ4 NSO0 module into text.bin, rodata.bin and data.bin.
//!
//! Reads the user's own module and writes the segments to a directory; it never
//! modifies the input. ZBIC modules go through `tools/zbic_extract.py`.

use ew_format::nso::{Nso, SegmentKind};

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    if args.len() != 2 {
        eprintln!("usage: ew-decode <module> <out-dir>");
        std::process::exit(2);
    }
    let bytes = match std::fs::read(&args[0]) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("reading {}: {e}", args[0]);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };
    let run = || -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let nso = Nso::parse(&bytes)?;
        let out = std::path::Path::new(&args[1]);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(out)?;
        for (kind, file) in [(SegmentKind::Text, "text.bin"), (SegmentKind::Rodata, "rodata.bin"), (SegmentKind::Data, "data.bin")] {
            let seg = nso.decompress_segment(kind)?;
            std::fs::write(out.join(file), &seg)?;
            println!("{:<7} {} bytes", kind.as_str(), seg.len());
        }
        println!("module  {} bss 0x{:x}", nso.header.module_name, nso.header.bss_size);
        Ok(())
    };
    if let Err(e) = run() {
        eprintln!("{e:#}");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

`crates/ew-format/src/bin/ew_inspect.rs`:

```rs
//! `ew-inspect` — evidence collector for an extracted Fire Emblem: Fortune's
//! Weave dump.
//!
//! It never writes to the game data. It parses the ExeFS modules, decompresses
//! every segment it can, inventories the romfs, probes asset containers, and
//! reports anything that blocks progress as an explicit blocker rather than
//! silently skipping it.

use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};
use ew_format::{Blocker, Compression, ExeFs, GameImage, Inventory, Nso, SegmentKind};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
struct SegmentReport {
    kind: String,
    compression: String,
    stored_bytes: u64,
    declared_bytes: u32,
    decoded_bytes: Option<u64>,
    fingerprint: Option<String>,
    error: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
struct ModuleReport {
    file_name: String,
    module_name: String,
    module_id: String,
    flags: u32,
    file_size: u64,
    image_size: u64,
    segments: Vec<SegmentReport>,
    has_mod0: Option<bool>,
    blocked_by: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
struct Report {
    generated_by: String,
    exefs_root: Option<String>,
    romfs_root: Option<String>,
    modules: Vec<ModuleReport>,
    inventory: Option<Inventory>,
    probes: Vec<ew_format::ProbeResult>,
    blockers: Vec<BlockerLine>,
    notes: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
struct BlockerLine {
    id: String,
    summary: String,
    affects: Vec<String>,
}

fn main() {
    if let Err(e) = run() {
        eprintln!("ew-inspect: {e:#}");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

struct Args {
    exefs: Option<PathBuf>,
    romfs: Option<PathBuf>,
    json: Option<PathBuf>,
    probe: usize,
    inventory: bool,
}

fn parse_args() -> Result<Args> {
    let mut args = Args { exefs: None, romfs: None, json: None, probe: 2, inventory: true };
    let mut it = std::env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--exefs" => args.exefs = Some(PathBuf::from(next(&mut it, "--exefs")?)),
            "--romfs" => args.romfs = Some(PathBuf::from(next(&mut it, "--romfs")?)),
            "--json" => args.json = Some(PathBuf::from(next(&mut it, "--json")?)),
            "--probe" => {
                args.probe = next(&mut it, "--probe")?
                    .parse()
                    .context("--probe expects a number")?
            }
            "--no-inventory" => args.inventory = false,
            "-h" | "--help" => {
                println!(
                    "ew-inspect — inspect an extracted Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave dump\n\
                     \n\
                     USAGE:\n  ew-inspect [--exefs DIR] [--romfs DIR] [--json OUT] [--probe N]\n\
                     \n\
                     With no arguments, the current directory is searched for `exefs/`\n\
                     and `romfs/` subdirectories."
                );
                std::process::exit(0);
            }
            other => bail!("unknown argument `{other}` (try --help)"),
        }
    }
    Ok(args)
}

fn next(it: &mut impl Iterator<Item = String>, flag: &str) -> Result<String> {
    it.next().with_context(|| format!("{flag} needs a value"))
}

fn run() -> Result<()> {
    let mut args = parse_args()?;
    if args.exefs.is_none() && args.romfs.is_none() {
        // Discover a conventional layout: <root>/exefs and <root>/romfs.
        if Path::new("exefs").is_dir() {
            args.exefs = Some(PathBuf::from("exefs"));
        }
        if Path::new("romfs").is_dir() {
            args.romfs = Some(PathBuf::from("romfs"));
        }
    }
    if args.exefs.is_none() && args.romfs.is_none() {
        bail!("nothing to inspect: pass --exefs DIR and/or --romfs DIR (try --help)");
    }

    let mut report = Report {
        generated_by: format!("ew-inspect {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")),
        exefs_root: args.exefs.as_ref().map(|p| p.display().to_string()),
        romfs_root: args.romfs.as_ref().map(|p| p.display().to_string()),
        modules: Vec::new(),
        inventory: None,
        probes: Vec::new(),
        blockers: Vec::new(),
        notes: Vec::new(),
    };

    if let Some(exefs_dir) = &args.exefs {
        let exefs = ExeFs::scan_dir(exefs_dir)?;
        if let Some(npdm) = exefs.read_npdm()? {
            report
                .notes
                .push(format!("NPDM: category={}, name={}", npdm.process_category, npdm.name));
        }
        println!("== ExeFS: {} ==", exefs_dir.display());
        println!(
            "{:<10} {:<10} {:>10} {:>11} {:>7} {:<12} {}",
            "file", "module", "file size", "image size", "flags", "compress", "status"
        );

        let mut blocked_modules = Vec::new();
        for m in &exefs.modules {
            let mut segments = Vec::new();
            let mut decoded_image: Option<GameImage> = None;
            let mut module_error: Option<String> = None;

            if m.is_zbic() {
                blocked_modules.push(m.file_name.clone());
            } else {
                let bytes = std::fs::read(&m.path)?;
                let nso = Nso::parse(&bytes)?;
                let mut parts = Vec::new();
                for kind in SegmentKind::ALL {
                    let seg = nso.header.segment(kind);
                    let comp = nso.header.compression(kind);
                    let stored = stored_len(&nso, kind);
                    match nso.decompress_segment(kind) {
                        Ok(data) => parts.push(SegmentReport {
                            kind: kind.as_str().to_string(),
                            compression: comp_name(comp).to_string(),
                            stored_bytes: stored,
                            declared_bytes: seg.size,
                            decoded_bytes: Some(data.len() as u64),
                            fingerprint: Some(fnv_hex(&data)),
                            error: None,
                        }),
                        Err(e) => {
                            parts.push(SegmentReport {
                                kind: kind.as_str().to_string(),
                                compression: comp_name(comp).to_string(),
                                stored_bytes: stored,
                                declared_bytes: seg.size,
                                decoded_bytes: None,
                                fingerprint: None,
                                error: Some(format!("{e:#}")),
                            });
                            module_error = Some(format!("{}: {e:#}", kind.as_str()));
                        }
                    }
                }
                match nso.to_image() {
                    Ok(img) => decoded_image = Some(img),
                    Err(e) if module_error.is_none() => module_error = Some(format!("{e:#}")),
                    Err(_) => {}
                }
                segments = parts;
            }

            let has_mod0 = decoded_image.as_ref().map(|i| i.find_mod0().is_some());

            if m.is_zbic() {
                // Report the real stored ranges even though the payload cannot
                // be decoded yet, so the cost of the blocker is visible.
                let bytes = std::fs::read(&m.path)?;
                let nso = Nso::parse(&bytes)?;
                segments = SegmentKind::ALL
                    .iter()
                    .map(|kind| {
                        let seg = nso.header.segment(*kind);
                        SegmentReport {
                            kind: kind.as_str().to_string(),
                            compression: "zbic".to_string(),
                            stored_bytes: stored_len(&nso, *kind),
                            declared_bytes: seg.size,
                            decoded_bytes: None,
                            fingerprint: None,
                            error: Some("blocked: ZBIC compression not implemented".to_string()),
                        }
                    })
                    .collect();
            }

            println!(
                "{:<10} {:<10} {:>10} {:>11} {:>7} {:<12} {}",
                m.file_name,
                m.module_name,
                human(m.file_size),
                human(m.image_size()),
                format!("{:02x}", m.flags),
                m.compressions.join("+"),
                if m.is_zbic() {
                    "blocked (ZBIC)"
                } else if module_error.is_some() {
                    "decode error"
                } else {
                    "decoded + verified"
                }
            );

            report.modules.push(ModuleReport {
                file_name: m.file_name.clone(),
                module_name: m.module_name.clone(),
                module_id: m.module_id.clone(),
                flags: m.flags,
                file_size: m.file_size,
                image_size: m.image_size(),
                segments,
                has_mod0,
                blocked_by: if m.is_zbic() { Some(Blocker::ZbicCompression.id().to_string()) } else { None },
            });
        }

        if !blocked_modules.is_empty() {
            report.blockers.push(BlockerLine {
                id: Blocker::ZbicCompression.id().to_string(),
                summary: Blocker::ZbicCompression.summary().to_string(),
                affects: blocked_modules,
            });
        }
        println!();
    }

    if let Some(romfs_dir) = &args.romfs {
        if args.inventory {
            eprintln!("scanning romfs (metadata only)…");
            let inv = Inventory::scan(romfs_dir)?;
            println!("== romfs: {} ==", romfs_dir.display());
            println!(
                "{} files, {} total",
                inv.total_files,
                human(inv.total_bytes)
            );
            println!("\ntop-level directories (by size):");
            for d in inv.dirs.iter().take(12) {
                println!("  {:<14} {:>7} files  {:>10}", d.name, d.files, human(d.bytes));
            }
            println!("\nextensions (by count):");
            for e in inv.extensions.iter().take(12) {
                println!("  .{:<12} {:>7} files  {:>10}", e.ext, e.files, human(e.bytes));
            }
            report.inventory = Some(inv);
        }

        if args.probe > 0 {
            eprintln!("probing asset containers…");
            let probes = ew_format::probe_samples(romfs_dir, args.probe)?;
            println!("\ninner formats (sample of {} per extension):", args.probe);
            for p in &probes {
                println!("  {:<58} {:<12} {}", truncate(&p.relative, 58), p.format.id, p.format.description);
            }
            report.probes = probes;
        }
    }

    if let Some(out) = &args.json {
        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?;
        std::fs::write(out, json).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", out.display()))?;
        println!("\nwrote {}", out.display());
    }

    if !report.blockers.is_empty() {
        println!("\n== blockers ==");
        for b in &report.blockers {
            println!("  {} affects {:?}", b.id, b.affects);
            println!("    {}", b.summary);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn stored_len(nso: &Nso<'_>, kind: SegmentKind) -> u64 {
    let start = nso.header.segment(kind).file_offset as u64;
    let end = match kind {
        SegmentKind::Text => nso.header.segment(SegmentKind::Rodata).file_offset as u64,
        SegmentKind::Rodata => nso.header.segment(SegmentKind::Data).file_offset as u64,
        SegmentKind::Data => nso.bytes_len() as u64,
    };
    end.saturating_sub(start)
}

fn comp_name(c: Compression) -> &'static str {
    match c {
        Compression::None => "none",
        Compression::Lz4 => "lz4",
        Compression::Zbic => "zbic",
    }
}

/// FNV-1a 64-bit: a cheap content fingerprint for the evidence report, so a
/// decoded segment can be compared across runs and machines.
fn fnv_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for b in data {
        h ^= *b as u64;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0x100_0000_01b3);
    }
    format!("{h:016x}")
}

fn human(n: u64) -> String {
    const UNITS: [&str; 4] = ["B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB"];
    let mut v = n as f64;
    let mut u = 0;
    while v >= 1024.0 && u < UNITS.len() - 1 {
        v /= 1024.0;
        u += 1;
    }
    if u == 0 {
        format!("{n} B")
    } else {
        format!("{v:.1} {}", UNITS[u])
    }
}

fn truncate(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    if s.chars().count() <= n {
        s.to_string()
    } else {
        let mut out: String = s.chars().take(n.saturating_sub(1)).collect();
        out.push('…');
        out
    }
}

`crates/ew-format/src/bin/ew_nup.rs`:

```rs
//! ew-nup: list a `.nup` game container, or copy its ExeFS out.
//!
//! usage: ew-nup <file.nup>                 list packages and the ExeFS
//!        ew-nup <file.nup> --exefs <dir>   write the program's ExeFS to <dir>
//!
//! Only reads the container; every file is checked against its SHA-256.

use ew_format::nup::Nup;

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let Some(path) = args.first() else {
        eprintln!("usage: ew-nup <file.nup> [--exefs <dir>]");
        std::process::exit(2);
    };
    if let Err(e) = run(path, args.get(1).map(String::as_str), args.get(2)) {
        eprintln!("ew-nup: {e:#}");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

fn run(path: &str, flag: Option<&str>, out: Option<&String>) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let nup = Nup::open(std::path::Path::new(path))?;
    println!("{} bytes, {} directories, {} files, read in {:?}", nup.size, nup.dirs.len(), nup.files.len(), started.elapsed());
    for p in &nup.packages {
        println!("package {:016X} v{} {:?}: root {}, exefs {}, romfs {}", p.title_id, p.version, p.kind, p.root, p.exefs, p.romfs);
    }
    let pkg = nup.program_package().ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("no base or update package"))?;
    let meta = nup.metadata(pkg)?;
    println!("title: {} {} ({})", meta.title().unwrap_or_default(), meta.display_version().unwrap_or_default(), meta.publisher().unwrap_or_default());
    let exefs = nup.walk(pkg.exefs);
    for (name, i) in &exefs {
        let e = &nup.files[*i as usize];
        println!("  exefs/{name:<16} {:>12} bytes ({} stored{})", e.size, e.stored, if e.compressed { ", zstd" } else { "" });
    }
    println!("romfs: {} files", nup.walk(pkg.romfs).len());
    if flag == Some("--exefs") {
        let dir = std::path::Path::new(out.ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("--exefs needs a directory"))?);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
        for (name, i) in &exefs {
            std::fs::write(dir.join(name), nup.read(*i)?)?;
            println!("wrote {}", dir.join(name).display());
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

`crates/ew-format/src/bin/ew_unzst.rs`:

```rs
//! Decompress a `.zst` file from the game's RomFS, for inspection.
//!
//! usage: ew_unzst <input.zst> <output>
use std::io::Read;

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    if args.len() != 3 {
        eprintln!("usage: ew_unzst <input.zst> <output>");
        std::process::exit(2);
    }
    let input = std::fs::read(&args[1]).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
        eprintln!("reading {}: {e}", args[1]);
        std::process::exit(1)
    });
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let result = ruzstd::StreamingDecoder::new(std::io::Cursor::new(input)).map_err(|e| e.to_string()).and_then(|mut d| d.read_to_end(&mut out).map_err(|e| e.to_string()));
    if let Err(e) = result {
        eprintln!("decompressing {}: {e}", args[1]);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(&args[2], &out) {
        eprintln!("writing {}: {e}", args[2]);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    println!("{} bytes", out.len());
}

`crates/ew-format/src/exefs.rs`:

```rs
//! ExeFS directory handling: the set of NSO modules that make up one title.

use crate::nso::{Nso, NsoHeader};
use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// One module found in an ExeFS directory.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ModuleEntry {
    pub file_name: String,
    pub path: PathBuf,
    /// Internal module name recorded in the NSO (e.g. `app`, `nnrtld`).
    pub module_name: String,
    pub module_id: String,
    pub text_size: u32,
    pub rodata_size: u32,
    pub data_size: u32,
    pub bss_size: u32,
    pub flags: u32,
    pub compressions: Vec<String>,
    pub file_size: u64,
}

impl ModuleEntry {
    pub fn is_zbic(&self) -> bool {
        self.compressions.iter().any(|c| c == "zbic")
    }

    /// Decompressed footprint of the module.
    pub fn image_size(&self) -> u64 {
        self.text_size as u64 + self.rodata_size as u64 + self.data_size as u64
            + self.bss_size as u64
    }
}

/// A parsed ExeFS directory, ordered so the main program comes first.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ExeFs {
    pub root: PathBuf,
    pub modules: Vec<ModuleEntry>,
    /// Whether `main.npdm` was present next to the modules.
    pub has_npdm: bool,
}

impl ExeFs {
    /// Scan a directory that holds extracted ExeFS files. Files are identified
    /// by their `NSO0` magic rather than by name, so renamed dumps still work.
    pub fn scan_dir(root: &Path) -> Result<ExeFs> {
        let mut modules = Vec::new();
        let mut has_npdm = false;

        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(root)
            .with_context(|| format!("reading ExeFS directory {}", root.display()))?
        {
            let entry = entry?;
            let path = entry.path();
            if !entry.file_type()?.is_file() {
                continue;
            }
            let file_name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
            if file_name.ends_with(".npdm") {
                has_npdm = true;
                continue;
            }

            // Only the header and the module name need to be resident to
            // describe a module.
            let file_size = entry.metadata()?.len();
            let mut head = vec![0u8; 0x200];
            let read = {
                use std::io::Read;
                let mut f = std::fs::File::open(&path)?;
                f.read(&mut head)?
            };
            head.truncate(read);
            let header: NsoHeader = match Nso::parse(&head) {
                Ok(n) => n.header,
                // A short read cannot hold the name string, so retry by
                // parsing just the fixed header.
                Err(_) => match Nso::parse(&head[..crate::nso::NSO_HEADER_SIZE.min(head.len())]) {
                    Ok(n) => n.header,
                    Err(_) => continue,
                },
            };

            modules.push(ModuleEntry {
                file_name,
                path,
                module_name: header.module_name.clone(),
                module_id: header.module_id.clone(),
                text_size: header.segments[0].size,
                rodata_size: header.segments[1].size,
                data_size: header.segments[2].size,
                bss_size: header.bss_size,
                flags: header.flags,
                compressions: header
                    .compressions()
                    .into_iter()
                    .map(|c| match c {
                        crate::nso::Compression::None => "none",
                        crate::nso::Compression::Lz4 => "lz4",
                        crate::nso::Compression::Zbic => "zbic",
                    })
                    .map(str::to_string)
                    .collect(),
                file_size,
            });
        }

        // `main` first, then subsdk0..n, then sdk/rtld for readability.
        modules.sort_by_key(|m| {
            let rank = match m.file_name.as_str() {
                "main" => 0,
                "rtld" => 900,
                "sdk" => 901,
                other if other.starts_with("subsdk") => 100,
                _ => 500,
            };
            (rank, m.file_name.clone())
        });

        Ok(ExeFs { root: root.to_path_buf(), modules, has_npdm })
    }

    /// Parse the NPDM that accompanies the modules, if present.
    pub fn read_npdm(&self) -> Result<Option<NpdmInfo>> {
        let path = self.root.join("main.npdm");
        if !path.is_file() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path)?;
        NpdmInfo::parse(&bytes).map(Some)
    }

    pub fn find(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&ModuleEntry> {
        self.modules.iter().find(|m| m.file_name == name)
    }

    /// Modules that can currently be decompressed and lifted.
    pub fn liftable(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &ModuleEntry> {
        self.modules.iter().filter(|m| !m.is_zbic())
    }

    /// Modules blocked on ZBIC support.
    pub fn blocked(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &ModuleEntry> {
        self.modules.iter().filter(|m| m.is_zbic())
    }
}

/// Minimal NPDM (process metadata) description.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct NpdmInfo {
    pub name: String,
    pub mmu_flags: u32,
    pub process_category: String,
    pub main_thread_priority: u8,
    pub default_cpu_id: u8,
    pub address_space_type: u32,
}

impl NpdmInfo {
    pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<NpdmInfo> {
        anyhow::ensure!(bytes.len() >= 0x80, "NPDM too small");
        anyhow::ensure!(&bytes[0..4] == b"META", "NPDM magic mismatch");
        let read_u32 = |o: usize| -> u32 {
            u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[o], bytes[o + 1], bytes[o + 2], bytes[o + 3]])
        };
        let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes[0x20..0x50])
            .trim_end_matches('\0')
            .to_string();
        let category = match read_u32(0x0C) {
            0 => "Regular",
            1 => "System",
            2 => "Application",
            3 => "Applet",
            _ => "Unknown",
        };
        Ok(NpdmInfo {
            name,
            mmu_flags: read_u32(0x08),
            process_category: category.to_string(),
            main_thread_priority: bytes[0x10],
            default_cpu_id: bytes[0x11],
            address_space_type: read_u32(0x0C),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn npdm_parses_category_and_name() {
        let mut v = vec![0u8; 0x80];
        v[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"META");
        v[0x0C..0x10].copy_from_slice(&2u32.to_le_bytes());
        v[0x20..0x2F].copy_from_slice(b"Application\0\0\0\0".split(|_| false).next().unwrap());
        let info = NpdmInfo::parse(&v).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(info.process_category, "Application");
        assert!(info.name.starts_with("Application"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn npdm_rejects_bad_magic() {
        let v = vec![0u8; 0x80];
        assert!(NpdmInfo::parse(&v).is_err());
    }
}

`crates/ew-format/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! `ew-format` — container and asset format layer for EmblemWeave.
//!
//! This crate is the evidence-driven foundation of the project: it parses the
//! Nintendo Switch 2 executable containers found in a retail dump, decompresses
//! their segments, and inventories the extracted romfs. Nothing here contains or
//! redistributes Nintendo content; every function takes the user's own files as
//! input.

pub mod exefs;
pub mod nso;
pub mod nup;
pub mod romfs;

pub use exefs::{ExeFs, ModuleEntry, NpdmInfo};
pub use nso::{Compression, GameImage, Mod0, Nso, NsoHeader, Segment, SegmentKind};
pub use romfs::{probe_samples, FormatGuess, Inventory, ProbeResult};

/// Errors that identify a genuine, documented blocker rather than a bug.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Blocker {
    /// The module's segments use Nintendo's ZBIC Zstandard variant.
    ZbicCompression,
}

impl Blocker {
    /// Stable identifier used in reports and the launcher status panel.
    pub fn id(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Blocker::ZbicCompression => "ZBIC_COMPRESSION",
        }
    }

    pub fn summary(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Blocker::ZbicCompression => {
                "Executable segments use ZBIC compression (Nintendo's modified Zstandard). \
                 Decoding needs a Binary Interpolative Coding FSE table reader."
            }
        }
    }
}

`crates/ew-format/src/nso.rs`:

```rs
//! NSO0 executable container parsing and segment extraction.
//!
//! Header layout used here was established empirically against the retail
//! Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave ExeFS dump: every segment boundary declared by
//! this layout is reproduced exactly by an independent LZ4 decode, and the last
//! segment lands precisely on end-of-file for all five LZ4-compressed modules.
//! See `docs/FEASIBILITY.md` for the evidence table.
//!
//! ```text
//! 0x00  magic "NSO0"
//! 0x04  u32 version
//! 0x08  u32 reserved
//! 0x0C  u32 flags            bit0..2 = text/rodata/data compressed,
//!                            bit3..5 = per-segment hashes present,
//!                            bit7    = ZBIC compression instead of LZ4
//! 0x10  u32 text.file_offset
//! 0x14  u32 text.mem_offset
//! 0x18  u32 text.size        (decompressed)
//! 0x1C  u32 header_size      (0x100 in every observed module)
//! 0x20  u32 rodata.file_offset
//! 0x24  u32 rodata.mem_offset
//! 0x28  u32 rodata.size
//! 0x2C  u32 name_len         (bytes occupied by the module name + NUL)
//! 0x30  u32 data.file_offset
//! 0x34  u32 data.mem_offset
//! 0x38  u32 data.size
//! 0x3C  u32 bss_size
//! 0x40  u8  module_id[0x20]
//! ...   module name at (text.file_offset - name_len)
//! ```

use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::path::Path;

pub const NSO_MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"NSO0";
pub const NSO_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 0x100;

/// Which segment a piece of the module lives in.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum SegmentKind {
    Text,
    Rodata,
    Data,
}

impl SegmentKind {
    pub const ALL: [SegmentKind; 3] = [SegmentKind::Text, SegmentKind::Rodata, SegmentKind::Data];

    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SegmentKind::Text => "text",
            SegmentKind::Rodata => "rodata",
            SegmentKind::Data => "data",
        }
    }

    fn index(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            SegmentKind::Text => 0,
            SegmentKind::Rodata => 1,
            SegmentKind::Data => 2,
        }
    }
}

/// Per-segment byte range in the module image.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Segment {
    /// Offset of the (possibly compressed) segment inside the NSO file.
    pub file_offset: u32,
    /// Offset the segment occupies once loaded into memory.
    pub mem_offset: u32,
    /// Size after decompression.
    pub size: u32,
}

/// Compression applied to a segment.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum Compression {
    /// Stored verbatim.
    None,
    /// Raw LZ4 blocks; decoded length comes from the segment header.
    Lz4,
    /// Nintendo's modified Zstandard stream, magic `ZBIC`, which replaces the
    /// FSE table reader with Binary Interpolative Coding.
    Zbic,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct NsoHeader {
    pub version: u32,
    pub flags: u32,
    pub segments: [Segment; 3],
    pub header_size: u32,
    /// Raw `name_len` field (the module name plus its NUL terminator).
    pub name_len: u32,
    pub bss_size: u32,
    pub module_id: String,
    pub module_name: String,
}

impl NsoHeader {
    pub fn segment(&self, kind: SegmentKind) -> Segment {
        self.segments[kind.index()]
    }

    /// Compression of one segment, derived from the flag word.
    pub fn compression(&self, kind: SegmentKind) -> Compression {
        let bit = 1u32 << kind.index();
        if self.flags & bit == 0 {
            return Compression::None;
        }
        if self.flags & 0x80 != 0 {
            Compression::Zbic
        } else {
            Compression::Lz4
        }
    }

    /// Set of compressions present anywhere in this module.
    pub fn compressions(&self) -> Vec<Compression> {
        let mut v = Vec::new();
        for kind in SegmentKind::ALL {
            let c = self.compression(kind);
            if !v.contains(&c) {
                v.push(c);
            }
        }
        v
    }

    pub fn has_zbic(&self) -> bool {
        self.compressions().contains(&Compression::Zbic)
    }
}

/// A parsed NSO module: header plus the original file bytes.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Nso<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    pub header: NsoHeader,
}

/// A decompressed module image with the three segments laid out by their
/// declared memory offsets, plus zero-initialised `.bss`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct GameImage {
    pub module_name: String,
    pub module_id: String,
    pub text: Vec<u8>,
    pub rodata: Vec<u8>,
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    pub bss_size: u32,
}

impl GameImage {
    pub fn segment(&self, kind: SegmentKind) -> &[u8] {
        match kind {
            SegmentKind::Text => &self.text,
            SegmentKind::Rodata => &self.rodata,
            SegmentKind::Data => &self.data,
        }
    }

    /// Total addressable image size: data end + bss.
    pub fn mapped_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.text.len() + self.rodata.len() + self.data.len() + self.bss_size as usize
    }

    /// Locate the `MOD0` module metadata structure, which normally lives in
    /// rodata and describes the dynamic section, bss and exception frames.
    pub fn find_mod0(&self) -> Option<Mod0> {
        mod0::locate(self.rodata.as_slice())
    }
}

fn u32_at(bytes: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<u32> {
    let end = off + 4;
    if end > bytes.len() {
        bail!("NSO header truncated at 0x{off:x}");
    }
    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[off..end].try_into().expect("4 bytes")))
}

impl<'a> Nso<'a> {
    pub fn parse(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Nso<'a>> {
        if bytes.len() < NSO_HEADER_SIZE {
            bail!("file is smaller than an NSO header ({} bytes)", bytes.len());
        }
        if &bytes[0..4] != NSO_MAGIC {
            bail!("not an NSO0 module (magic {:02x?})", &bytes[0..4]);
        }

        let version = u32_at(bytes, 0x04)?;
        let flags = u32_at(bytes, 0x0C)?;
        let mut segments = [Segment { file_offset: 0, mem_offset: 0, size: 0 }; 3];
        for (i, _kind) in SegmentKind::ALL.iter().enumerate() {
            // Segment entries sit at 0x10 (text), 0x20 (rodata) and 0x30
            // (data); the words at 0x1C, 0x2C and 0x3C hold header_size,
            // name_len and bss_size.
            let base = 0x10 + i * 0x10;
            segments[i] = Segment {
                file_offset: u32_at(bytes, base)?,
                mem_offset: u32_at(bytes, base + 4)?,
                size: u32_at(bytes, base + 8)?,
            };
        }

        let header_size = u32_at(bytes, 0x1C)?;
        let name_len = u32_at(bytes, 0x2C)?;
        let bss_size = u32_at(bytes, 0x3C)?;
        let module_id = hex(&bytes[0x40..0x60]);

        // The module name sits immediately before the text segment.
        let name_end = segments[0].file_offset as usize;
        let name_start = name_end.checked_sub(name_len as usize).unwrap_or(0);
        let module_name = if name_start < name_end && name_end <= bytes.len() {
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes[name_start..name_end])
                .trim_end_matches('\0')
                .to_string()
        } else {
            String::new()
        };

        Ok(Nso {
            bytes,
            header: NsoHeader {
                version,
                flags,
                segments,
                header_size,
                name_len,
                bss_size,
                module_id,
                module_name,
            },
        })
    }

    /// Length of the module file that was parsed.
    pub fn bytes_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len()
    }

    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, NsoHeader)> {
        let bytes = std::fs::read(path)
            .with_context(|| format!("reading NSO module {}", path.display()))?;
        let header = {
            let nso = Nso::parse(&bytes)?;
            nso.header.clone()
        };
        Ok((bytes, header))
    }

    /// Validate that the declared segment ranges describe a sane file: ordered,
    /// in bounds, and ending at end-of-file.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        let mut notes = Vec::new();
        let file_len = self.bytes.len();
        let mut prev_end = 0usize;
        for kind in SegmentKind::ALL {
            let seg = self.header.segment(kind);
            let start = seg.file_offset as usize;
            if start < prev_end {
                bail!("{} segment starts before the previous segment ends", kind.as_str());
            }
            if start > file_len {
                bail!("{} segment offset 0x{start:x} is past end of file", kind.as_str());
            }
            prev_end = start;
        }
        if self.header.bss_size == 0 {
            notes.push("module declares no bss".to_string());
        }
        Ok(notes)
    }

    /// Byte range of a segment's stored (possibly compressed) representation.
    /// The end is bounded by the next segment's file offset, or EOF.
    fn stored_range(&self, kind: SegmentKind) -> Result<(usize, usize)> {
        let start = self.header.segment(kind).file_offset as usize;
        let end = match kind {
            SegmentKind::Text => self.header.segment(SegmentKind::Rodata).file_offset as usize,
            SegmentKind::Rodata => self.header.segment(SegmentKind::Data).file_offset as usize,
            SegmentKind::Data => self.bytes.len(),
        };
        if start > end || end > self.bytes.len() {
            bail!("{} segment range 0x{start:x}..0x{end:x} is invalid", kind.as_str());
        }
        Ok((start, end))
    }

    /// Decompress one segment into its declared size.
    pub fn decompress_segment(&self, kind: SegmentKind) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let (start, end) = self.stored_range(kind)?;
        let stored = &self.bytes[start..end];
        let size = self.header.segment(kind).size as usize;

        match self.header.compression(kind) {
            Compression::None => {
                if stored.len() < size {
                    bail!(
                        "{} segment stores fewer bytes than declared ({} < {})",
                        kind.as_str(),
                        stored.len(),
                        size
                    );
                }
                Ok(stored[..size].to_vec())
            }
            Compression::Lz4 => {
                let out = lz4_flex::block::decompress(stored, size).with_context(|| {
                    format!("LZ4 decode of {} segment failed", kind.as_str())
                })?;
                if out.len() != size {
                    bail!(
                        "{} segment decoded to {} bytes, header declares {}",
                        kind.as_str(),
                        out.len(),
                        size
                    );
                }
                Ok(out)
            }
            Compression::Zbic => bail!(
                "{} segment uses ZBIC (Nintendo Zstandard variant); decoding requires a \
                 BIC-based FSE table reader that is not implemented",
                kind.as_str()
            ),
        }
    }

    /// Decompress every segment, producing a loadable image.
    pub fn to_image(&self) -> Result<GameImage> {
        let text = self.decompress_segment(SegmentKind::Text)?;
        let rodata = self.decompress_segment(SegmentKind::Rodata)?;
        let data = self.decompress_segment(SegmentKind::Data)?;
        Ok(GameImage {
            module_name: self.header.module_name.clone(),
            module_id: self.header.module_id.clone(),
            text,
            rodata,
            data,
            bss_size: self.header.bss_size,
        })
    }
}

/// `MOD0` dynamic-link metadata embedded in a module.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Mod0 {
    pub offset: usize,
    pub dynamic: u32,
    pub bss_start: u32,
    pub bss_end: u32,
    pub eh_frame_hdr_start: u32,
    pub eh_frame_hdr_end: u32,
    pub module_object: u32,
}

mod mod0 {
    use super::Mod0;

    pub fn locate(rodata: &[u8]) -> Option<Mod0> {
        let pos = rodata.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"MOD0")?;
        let at = |o: usize| -> Option<u32> {
            rodata
                .get(pos + o..pos + o + 4)
                .map(|b| u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))
        };
        Some(Mod0 {
            offset: pos,
            dynamic: at(4)?,
            bss_start: at(8)?,
            bss_end: at(0x0C)?,
            eh_frame_hdr_start: at(0x10)?,
            eh_frame_hdr_end: at(0x14)?,
            module_object: at(0x18)?,
        })
    }
}

fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Build a synthetic NSO with three uncompressed segments.
    fn synthetic(text_len: usize, ro_len: usize, da_len: usize, name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        let name_bytes = name.len() + 1;
        let text_off = 0x100 + name_bytes;
        let ro_off = text_off + text_len;
        let da_off = ro_off + ro_len;
        let mut v = vec![0u8; da_off + da_len];
        v[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"NSO0");
        v[0x0C..0x10].copy_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // no compression
        let put = |v: &mut [u8], off: usize, val: u32| {
            v[off..off + 4].copy_from_slice(&val.to_le_bytes())
        };
        put(&mut v, 0x10, text_off as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x14, 0);
        put(&mut v, 0x18, text_len as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x1C, 0x100);
        put(&mut v, 0x20, ro_off as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x24, 0x2000);
        put(&mut v, 0x28, ro_len as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x2C, name_bytes as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x30, da_off as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x34, 0x4000);
        put(&mut v, 0x38, da_len as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x3C, 0x1000); // bss
        v[0x100..0x100 + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        for (i, b) in v.iter_mut().enumerate().skip(text_off) {
            *b = (i & 0xff) as u8;
        }
        v
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_header_fields() {
        let bytes = synthetic(0x40, 0x30, 0x20, "app");
        let nso = Nso::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(nso.header.module_name, "app");
        assert_eq!(nso.header.header_size, 0x100);
        assert_eq!(nso.header.bss_size, 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(nso.header.segment(SegmentKind::Text).size, 0x40);
        assert_eq!(nso.header.segment(SegmentKind::Rodata).mem_offset, 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(nso.header.segment(SegmentKind::Data).mem_offset, 0x4000);
        assert_eq!(nso.header.compression(SegmentKind::Text), Compression::None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn zbic_flag_detection() {
        let mut bytes = synthetic(0x10, 0x10, 0x10, "app");
        // bit0..2 = segments compressed, bit7 = ZBIC instead of LZ4
        bytes[0x0C..0x10].copy_from_slice(&0xbfu32.to_le_bytes());
        let nso = Nso::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert!(nso.header.has_zbic());
        assert_eq!(nso.header.compression(SegmentKind::Text), Compression::Zbic);
        // ZBIC must fail loudly rather than silently returning garbage.
        let err = nso.decompress_segment(SegmentKind::Text).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("ZBIC"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn decompresses_uncompressed_segments() {
        let bytes = synthetic(0x40, 0x30, 0x20, "subsdk9");
        let nso = Nso::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        let image = nso.to_image().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(image.text.len(), 0x40);
        assert_eq!(image.rodata.len(), 0x30);
        assert_eq!(image.data.len(), 0x20);
        assert_eq!(image.module_name, "subsdk9");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_wrong_magic() {
        let mut bytes = synthetic(0x10, 0x10, 0x10, "app");
        bytes[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"NRO0");
        assert!(Nso::parse(&bytes).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn lz4_segment_roundtrip() {
        // Compress a text segment with a real LZ4 block encoder, then decode
        // it back through the container layer.
        let text: Vec<u8> = (0..4096u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect();
        let packed = lz4_flex::block::compress(&text);
        let name = b"app\0".to_vec();
        let text_off = 0x100 + name.len();
        let ro_off = text_off + packed.len();
        let mut v = vec![0u8; ro_off + 0x10];
        v[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"NSO0");
        v[0x0C..0x10].copy_from_slice(&0x01u32.to_le_bytes()); // text compressed, LZ4
        let put = |v: &mut [u8], off: usize, val: u32| {
            v[off..off + 4].copy_from_slice(&val.to_le_bytes())
        };
        put(&mut v, 0x10, text_off as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x18, text.len() as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x1C, 0x100);
        put(&mut v, 0x20, ro_off as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x28, 0x10);
        put(&mut v, 0x2C, name.len() as u32);
        put(&mut v, 0x30, ro_off as u32 + 0x10);
        put(&mut v, 0x38, 0);
        v[0x100..0x104].copy_from_slice(&name);
        v[text_off..text_off + packed.len()].copy_from_slice(&packed);
        let nso = Nso::parse(&v).unwrap();
        let out = nso.decompress_segment(SegmentKind::Text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, text);
    }
}
