`crates/ew-format/src/nup.rs`:

```rs
//! `.nup` game containers: a whole title (ExeFS, RomFS, metadata) in one file,
//! nothing encrypted, each file stored as-is or as one zstd frame.
//!
//! Layout, little endian:
//!
//! * Superblock (0x80 bytes): `"NUP\x01"`, u16 header size (0x80), u16 version
//!   (1), u64 TOC offset, u64 TOC size, SHA-256 of the TOC, u64 data offset,
//!   u64 file size, u32 package count, u32 zero, a 16-byte id, 32 zero bytes.
//! * TOC: `"TOC\x01"`, u32 packages, u64 directories, u64 files, u64 name-pool
//!   offset (relative to the TOC), u64 pool length, u64 zero; then
//!   * packages, 0x40 bytes each: u64 title id, u32 root, ExeFS and RomFS
//!     directory indices, u32 version, u8 kind (0 base, 1 update, 2 add-on),
//!     u8 flags, u16, u32, u64 metadata offset, u32 metadata length, 20 bytes;
//!   * directories, 0x18 bytes each: u32 name offset, u32 name length, u32
//!     first child, u32 child count, u64;
//!   * files, 0x50 bytes each: u32 name offset, u32 name length, u64 size,
//!     u64 data offset (from the start of the file), u64 stored size, SHA-256
//!     of the file's bytes, u8 codec (0 stored, 1 one zstd frame), padding;
//!   * children, u32 each: an index below the directory count is a
//!     directory, otherwise the file `index - directories`;
//!   * the name pool.
//!
//! The reader only ever reads the user's file.

use anyhow::{bail, ensure, Context, Result};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

const SUPER_SIZE: usize = 0x80;
const TOC_HEAD: usize = 0x30;
const PACKAGE_SIZE: usize = 0x40;
const DIR_SIZE: usize = 0x18;
const FILE_SIZE: usize = 0x50;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PackageKind {
    Base,
    Update,
    AddOn,
    Other(u8),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Package {
    pub title_id: u64,
    pub root: u32,
    pub exefs: u32,
    pub romfs: u32,
    pub version: u32,
    pub kind: PackageKind,
    pub meta_offset: u64,
    pub meta_len: u32,
}

/// Title metadata a package carries: tagged records (u32 tag, u32 length,
/// bytes). Tags seen: 1 NPDM, 3 icon (JPEG), 4 display version, 5 title name,
/// 6 publisher.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Metadata {
    pub records: Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)>,
}

impl Metadata {
    fn text(&self, tag: u32) -> Option<String> {
        self.records.iter().find(|(t, _)| *t == tag).map(|(_, b)| String::from_utf8_lossy(b).trim_end_matches('␀').to_string())
    }
    pub fn display_version(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.text(4)
    }
    pub fn title(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.text(5)
    }
    pub fn publisher(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.text(6)
    }
    pub fn icon_jpeg(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {
        self.records.iter().find(|(t, _)| *t == 3).map(|(_, b)| b.as_slice())
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Directory {
    pub name: String,
    pub children: Vec<Node>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Node {
    Dir(u32),
    File(u32),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FileEntry {
    pub name: String,
    pub size: u64,
    pub offset: u64,
    pub stored: u64,
    pub sha256: [u8; 32],
    pub compressed: bool,
}

/// An opened `.nup` container.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Nup {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub size: u64,
    pub packages: Vec<Package>,
    pub dirs: Vec<Directory>,
    pub files: Vec<FileEntry>,
}

fn u16_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 2].try_into().unwrap())
}
fn u32_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 4].try_into().unwrap())
}
fn u64_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 8].try_into().unwrap())
}

impl Nup {
    /// Whether `path` starts with the `.nup` magic.
    pub fn is_nup(path: &Path) -> bool {
        let mut m = [0u8; 4];
        File::open(path).and_then(|mut f| f.read_exact(&mut m)).is_ok() && &m == b"NUP\x01"
    }

    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Nup> {
        let mut f = File::open(path).with_context(|| format!("opening {}", path.display()))?;
        let size = f.metadata()?.len();
        let mut head = [0u8; SUPER_SIZE];
        f.read_exact(&mut head).context("reading the .nup superblock")?;
        ensure!(&head[0..4] == b"NUP\x01", "{} is not a .nup container", path.display());
        ensure!(u16_at(&head, 4) as usize == SUPER_SIZE && u16_at(&head, 6) == 1, "unsupported .nup header");
        let (toc_off, toc_size) = (u64_at(&head, 8), u64_at(&head, 16));
        let declared = u64_at(&head, 0x40);
        ensure!(declared == size, "the .nup declares {declared} bytes but the file has {size}: it is incomplete");
        ensure!(toc_off + toc_size <= size && toc_size < (1 << 31), "the .nup table of contents is out of range");

        let mut toc = vec![0u8; toc_size as usize];
        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(toc_off))?;
        f.read_exact(&mut toc).context("reading the .nup table of contents")?;
        let digest: [u8; 32] = Sha256::digest(&toc).into();
        ensure!(digest == head[24..56], "the .nup table of contents does not match its SHA-256: the file is damaged");

        ensure!(&toc[0..4] == b"TOC\x01", "the .nup table of contents has no TOC header");
        let n_pkg = u32_at(&toc, 4) as usize;
        let n_dir = u64_at(&toc, 8) as usize;
        let n_file = u64_at(&toc, 16) as usize;
        let (pool_off, pool_len) = (u64_at(&toc, 24) as usize, u64_at(&toc, 32) as usize);
        let pkg_at = TOC_HEAD;
        let dir_at = pkg_at + n_pkg * PACKAGE_SIZE;
        let file_at = dir_at + n_dir * DIR_SIZE;
        let child_at = file_at + n_file * FILE_SIZE;
        ensure!(pool_off + pool_len <= toc.len() && child_at <= pool_off, "the .nup table of contents is inconsistent");
        let pool = &toc[pool_off..pool_off + pool_len];
        let name = |off: u32, len: u32| -> Result<String> {
            let (o, l) = (off as usize, len as usize);
            ensure!(o + l <= pool.len(), "a .nup name is outside the name pool");
            Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&pool[o..o + l]).into_owned())
        };

        let packages = (0..n_pkg)
            .map(|i| {
                let p = &toc[pkg_at + i * PACKAGE_SIZE..];
                Package {
                    title_id: u64_at(p, 0),
                    root: u32_at(p, 8),
                    exefs: u32_at(p, 12),
                    romfs: u32_at(p, 16),
                    version: u32_at(p, 20),
                    kind: match p[24] {
                        0 => PackageKind::Base,
                        1 => PackageKind::Update,
                        2 => PackageKind::AddOn,
                        k => PackageKind::Other(k),
                    },
                    meta_offset: u64_at(p, 32),
                    meta_len: u32_at(p, 40),
                }
            })
            .collect();

        let children_len = (pool_off - child_at) / 4;
        let child = |i: usize| -> Result<Node> {
            ensure!(i < children_len, "a .nup directory lists a child outside the table");
            let v = u32_at(&toc, child_at + i * 4) as usize;
            Ok(if v < n_dir { Node::Dir(v as u32) } else { Node::File((v - n_dir) as u32) })
        };
        let mut dirs = Vec::with_capacity(n_dir);
        for i in 0..n_dir {
            let d = &toc[dir_at + i * DIR_SIZE..];
            let (first, count) = (u32_at(d, 8) as usize, u32_at(d, 12) as usize);
            let children = (first..first + count).map(child).collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
            dirs.push(Directory { name: name(u32_at(d, 0), u32_at(d, 4))?, children });
        }
        let mut files = Vec::with_capacity(n_file);
        for i in 0..n_file {
            let e = &toc[file_at + i * FILE_SIZE..];
            let entry = FileEntry {
                name: name(u32_at(e, 0), u32_at(e, 4))?,
                size: u64_at(e, 8),
                offset: u64_at(e, 16),
                stored: u64_at(e, 24),
                sha256: e[32..64].try_into().unwrap(),
                compressed: match e[64] {
                    0 => false,
                    1 => true,
                    c => bail!("file {} uses an unknown .nup codec {c}", i),
                },
            };
            ensure!(entry.offset + entry.stored <= size, "a .nup file's data is outside the container");
            files.push(entry);
        }
        for d in &dirs {
            for c in &d.children {
                match *c {
                    Node::Dir(i) => ensure!((i as usize) < dirs.len(), "bad .nup directory index"),
                    Node::File(i) => ensure!((i as usize) < files.len(), "bad .nup file index"),
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(Nup { path: path.to_path_buf(), size, packages, dirs, files })
    }

    /// The package holding the game program: an update when present (it
    /// carries the newest program and a full RomFS), else the base game.
    pub fn program_package(&self) -> Option<&Package> {
        self.packages
            .iter()
            .find(|p| p.kind == PackageKind::Update)
            .or_else(|| self.packages.iter().find(|p| p.kind == PackageKind::Base))
    }

    /// A package's title metadata.
    pub fn metadata(&self, pkg: &Package) -> Result<Metadata> {
        ensure!(pkg.meta_offset + pkg.meta_len as u64 <= self.size, "the .nup metadata is outside the container");
        let mut f = File::open(&self.path)?;
        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(pkg.meta_offset))?;
        let mut b = vec![0u8; pkg.meta_len as usize];
        f.read_exact(&mut b)?;
        let mut records = Vec::new();
        let mut at = 0usize;
        while at + 8 <= b.len() {
            let (tag, len) = (u32_at(&b, at), u32_at(&b, at + 4) as usize);
            ensure!(at + 8 + len <= b.len(), "a .nup metadata record runs past its end");
            records.push((tag, b[at + 8..at + 8 + len].to_vec()));
            at += 8 + len;
        }
        Ok(Metadata { records })
    }

    /// Every file below directory `dir`, as (path relative to it, file index).
    pub fn walk(&self, dir: u32) -> Vec<(String, u32)> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut stack = vec![(dir, String::new())];
        while let Some((d, prefix)) = stack.pop() {
            for c in &self.dirs[d as usize].children {
                match *c {
                    Node::Dir(i) => stack.push((i, format!("{prefix}{}/", self.dirs[i as usize].name))),
                    Node::File(i) => out.push((format!("{prefix}{}", self.files[i as usize].name), i)),
                }
            }
        }
        out.sort();
        out
    }

    /// A map from relative path to file index for everything below `dir`.
    pub fn index(&self, dir: u32) -> HashMap<String, u32> {
        self.walk(dir).into_iter().collect()
    }

    /// The bytes of a file, decompressed and checked against its SHA-256.
    pub fn read(&self, file: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let e = &self.files[file as usize];
        let mut f = File::open(&self.path)?;
        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(e.offset))?;
        let mut stored = vec![0u8; e.stored as usize];
        f.read_exact(&mut stored)?;
        let data = if e.compressed {
            let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(e.size as usize);
            ruzstd::StreamingDecoder::new(std::io::Cursor::new(&stored[..]))
                .map_err(|err| anyhow::anyhow!("{}: {err}", e.name))?
                .read_to_end(&mut out)
                .with_context(|| format!("decompressing {}", e.name))?;
            out
        } else {
            stored
        };
        ensure!(data.len() as u64 == e.size, "{} decoded to {} bytes, the .nup says {}", e.name, data.len(), e.size);
        let digest: [u8; 32] = Sha256::digest(&data).into();
        ensure!(digest == e.sha256, "{} does not match its SHA-256: the .nup is damaged", e.name);
        Ok(data)
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-format/src/romfs.rs`:

```rs
//! romfs inventory and content probing.
//!
//! The inventory walks the extracted romfs and reports file counts and byte
//! totals per top-level directory and per extension. Probing inspects the bytes
//! of a small sample of files, transparently decompressing standard Zstandard
//! assets so that the *inner* container format is reported rather than the
//! wrapper.

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct DirStat {
    pub name: String,
    pub files: u64,
    pub bytes: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ExtStat {
    pub ext: String,
    pub files: u64,
    pub bytes: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Inventory {
    pub root: PathBuf,
    pub total_files: u64,
    pub total_bytes: u64,
    /// Per top-level directory, largest first.
    pub dirs: Vec<DirStat>,
    /// Per extension, most frequent first.
    pub extensions: Vec<ExtStat>,
}

impl Inventory {
    /// Walk the romfs collecting counts and sizes. Metadata only: no file
    /// contents are read, so this stays cheap on large dumps.
    pub fn scan(root: &Path) -> Result<Inventory> {
        let mut dirs: BTreeMap<String, DirStat> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut exts: BTreeMap<String, ExtStat> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut total_files = 0u64;
        let mut total_bytes = 0u64;

        let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
        while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
            let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {
                Ok(e) => e,
                Err(e) if dir == root => {
                    return Err(e).with_context(|| format!("reading romfs {}", root.display()))
                }
                Err(_) => continue,
            };
            for entry in entries {
                let entry = match entry {
                    Ok(e) => e,
                    Err(_) => continue,
                };
                let path = entry.path();
                let ft = match entry.file_type() {
                    Ok(t) => t,
                    Err(_) => continue,
                };
                if ft.is_dir() {
                    stack.push(path);
                    continue;
                }
                let len = entry.metadata().map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0);

                // Attribute the file to its top-level directory.
                let top = path
                    .strip_prefix(root)
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|rel| rel.components().next())
                    .map(|c| c.as_os_str().to_string_lossy().to_string())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| ".".to_string());
                let d = dirs.entry(top.clone()).or_insert_with(|| DirStat {
                    name: top,
                    files: 0,
                    bytes: 0,
                });
                d.files += 1;
                d.bytes += len;

                let ext = path
                    .extension()
                    .map(|e| e.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "(none)".to_string());
                // Asset names contain dots, so keep only the last suffix.
                let e = exts.entry(ext.clone()).or_insert_with(|| ExtStat {
                    ext,
                    files: 0,
                    bytes: 0,
                });
                e.files += 1;
                e.bytes += len;

                total_files += 1;
                total_bytes += len;
            }
        }

        let mut dirs: Vec<DirStat> = dirs.into_values().collect();
        dirs.sort_by(|a, b| b.bytes.cmp(&a.bytes).then_with(|| a.name.cmp(&b.name)));
        let mut extensions: Vec<ExtStat> = exts.into_values().collect();
        extensions.sort_by(|a, b| b.files.cmp(&a.files).then_with(|| a.ext.cmp(&b.ext)));

        Ok(Inventory { root: root.to_path_buf(), total_files, total_bytes, dirs, extensions })
    }
}

/// What a file's bytes actually are.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct FormatGuess {
    /// Short machine-friendly identifier, e.g. `bfres`, `msbt`, `zstd`.
    pub id: String,
    /// Human-readable description.
    pub description: String,
    /// True when the payload was wrapped in Zstandard and unwrapped for the
    /// probe.
    pub zstd_wrapped: bool,
}

impl FormatGuess {
    fn new(id: &str, description: &str, zstd_wrapped: bool) -> Self {
        FormatGuess {
            id: id.to_string(),
            description: description.to_string(),
            zstd_wrapped,
        }
    }
}

/// Identify a payload from its leading bytes.
pub fn identify(payload: &[u8], name_hint: &str) -> FormatGuess {
    let zstd = payload.len() >= 4 && payload[0..4] == [0x28, 0xb5, 0x2f, 0xfd];
    if zstd {
        return FormatGuess::new("zstd", "Zstandard stream (standard)", false);
    }
    match () {
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"FRES") => FormatGuess::new("bfres", "NintendoWare BFRES resource", false),
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"Gfx2") => FormatGuess::new("bfres2", "NintendoWare BFRES (Switch 2) resource", false),
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"MsgStdBn") => FormatGuess::new("msbt", "Nintendo text message archive", false),
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"MsgPrjBn") => FormatGuess::new("msbt_project", "Nintendo message project", false),
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"BNTX") => FormatGuess::new("bntx", "NintendoWare texture container", false),
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"FSAR") || payload.starts_with(b"BFSAR") => {
            FormatGuess::new("bfsar", "NintendoWare sound archive", false)
        }
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"FSTM") || payload.starts_with(b"FWAV") => {
            FormatGuess::new("bntx_audio", "NintendoWare audio bank", false)
        }
        _ if payload.starts_with(&[0x1a, 0x45, 0xdf, 0xa3]) => {
            FormatGuess::new("webm", "Matroska/WebM container", false)
        }
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"OggS") => FormatGuess::new("ogg", "Ogg container", false),
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"AVA0") || payload.starts_with(b"AVM0") => {
            FormatGuess::new("nvn_shader", "NVN shader container", false)
        }
        _ if payload.starts_with(b"ZBCS") || payload.starts_with(b"ZBIC") => {
            FormatGuess::new("zbic", "Nintendo Zstandard variant (ZBIC)", false)
        }
        _ if name_hint.ends_with(".opus") => {
            FormatGuess::new("opus_bank", "Opus/HCA-style audio stream", false)
        }
        _ if name_hint.ends_with(".lips") => FormatGuess::new("lips", "Lip-sync data", false),
        _ if name_hint.ends_with(".matanimb") => {
            FormatGuess::new("matanimb", "NintendoWare material animation", false)
        }
        _ => FormatGuess::new("unknown", "Unrecognised payload", false),
    }
}

/// Read the first `limit` bytes of a file, unwrapping a standard Zstandard
/// stream if that is what the file holds.
pub fn read_probe_payload(path: &Path, limit: usize) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, bool)> {
    use std::io::{Read, Seek};
    let mut f = std::fs::File::open(path).with_context(|| format!("opening {}", path.display()))?;
    let mut head = vec![0u8; 4];
    let n = f.read(&mut head)?;
    head.truncate(n);
    if head == [0x28, 0xb5, 0x2f, 0xfd] {
        f.rewind()?;
        let bytes = std::fs::read(path)?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(limit);
        let mut dec = ruzstd::StreamingDecoder::new(std::io::Cursor::new(&bytes[..]))
            .with_context(|| format!("opening zstd stream in {}", path.display()))?;
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; limit];
        while out.len() < limit {
            let want = (limit - out.len()).min(buf.len());
            match dec.read(&mut buf[..want]) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(k) => out.extend_from_slice(&buf[..k]),
                Err(e) => return Err(e).with_context(|| format!("zstd decode {}", path.display())),
            }
        }
        return Ok((out, true));
    }
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; limit];
    let k = f.read(&mut buf)?;
    buf.truncate(k);
    Ok((buf, false))
}

/// Probe a sample of files, one per extension encountered.
pub fn probe_samples(root: &Path, per_ext: usize) -> Result<Vec<ProbeResult>> {
    let mut seen: BTreeMap<String, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut results = Vec::new();
    let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {
            Ok(e) => e,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        for entry in entries.flatten() {
            let path = entry.path();
            match entry.file_type() {
                Ok(t) if t.is_dir() => {
                    stack.push(path);
                    continue;
                }
                Ok(_) => {}
                Err(_) => continue,
            }
            let ext = path
                .extension()
                .map(|e| e.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "(none)".to_string());
            let count = seen.entry(ext.clone()).or_insert(0);
            if *count >= per_ext {
                continue;
            }
            if let Ok((payload, wrapped)) = read_probe_payload(&path, 64) {
                let mut guess = identify(&payload, &path.to_string_lossy());
                guess.zstd_wrapped = wrapped;
                if wrapped {
                    // Report both the wrapper and the inner container.
                    guess.description = format!("zstd -> {}", guess.description);
                    if guess.id == "unknown" {
                        guess.id = "zstd-unidentified".to_string();
                    }
                }
                *count += 1;
                results.push(ProbeResult {
                    relative: path
                        .strip_prefix(root)
                        .unwrap_or(&path)
                        .to_string_lossy()
                        .to_string(),
                    format: guess,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    results.sort_by(|a, b| a.relative.cmp(&b.relative));
    Ok(results)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ProbeResult {
    pub relative: String,
    pub format: FormatGuess,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn identifies_common_magics() {
        assert_eq!(identify(b"FRES\0\0\0\0", "x.bfres").id, "bfres");
        assert_eq!(identify(b"MsgStdBn", "x.msbt").id, "msbt");
        assert_eq!(identify(&[0x28, 0xb5, 0x2f, 0xfd, 0, 0], "x.zst").id, "zstd");
        assert_eq!(identify(b"\x1a\x45\xdf\xa3rest", "x.webm").id, "webm");
        assert_eq!(identify(b"", "x.opus").id, "opus_bank");
        assert_eq!(identify(b"????", "x.weird").id, "unknown");
    }

    #[test]
    fn inventory_scans_directory_tree() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ew_inv_{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("Sound/stream")).unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("Msg/CNzh")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("Sound/stream/a.opus"), vec![0u8; 10]).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("Sound/b.opus"), vec![0u8; 5]).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("Msg/CNzh/c.msbt.zst"), vec![0u8; 7]).unwrap();

        let inv = Inventory::scan(&dir).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(inv.total_files, 3);
        assert_eq!(inv.total_bytes, 22);
        assert_eq!(inv.dirs[0].name, "Sound");
        assert_eq!(inv.dirs[0].files, 2);
        let opus = inv.extensions.iter().find(|e| e.ext == "opus").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(opus.files, 2);
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    }
}
```

`crates/ew-gfx/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! The host graphics device behind EmblemWeave's NVN layer.
//!
//! NVN objects the game creates are backed by real Vulkan objects on the host.
//! This crate owns the Vulkan instance, the physical device choice and the
//! logical device with its graphics queue. It is created once per process, on
//! the first `nvnDeviceInitialize`, and every NVN host service reaches it
//! through [`device`].
//!
//! The loader is opened at run time (`ash`'s `loaded` feature), so a machine
//! without Vulkan gets a clear error from `nvnDeviceInitialize` instead of an
//! executable that fails to start.

use ash::vk;
use std::ffi::CStr;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};

/// What the game's NVN layer needs to know about the host device.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DeviceInfo {
    pub name: String,
    pub vendor_id: u32,
    pub device_id: u32,
    /// Vulkan API version the device supports, as `major.minor.patch`.
    pub api: (u32, u32, u32),
    pub driver: String,
    pub queue_family: u32,
    pub max_texture_2d: u32,
    pub min_uniform_alignment: u64,
    pub min_storage_alignment: u64,
}

pub struct Gpu {
    _entry: ash::Entry,
    instance: ash::Instance,
    pub physical: vk::PhysicalDevice,
    pub device: ash::Device,
    pub queue: vk::Queue,
    pub info: DeviceInfo,
}

impl Drop for Gpu {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        unsafe {
            let _ = self.device.device_wait_idle();
            self.device.destroy_device(None);
            self.instance.destroy_instance(None);
        }
    }
}

fn version(v: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32) {
    (vk::api_version_major(v), vk::api_version_minor(v), vk::api_version_patch(v))
}

impl Gpu {
    /// Create the instance and the logical device. Prefers a discrete GPU,
    /// then an integrated one, and requires Vulkan 1.3 and a graphics queue.
    pub fn new() -> Result<Gpu, String> {
        let entry = unsafe { ash::Entry::load() }.map_err(|e| format!("the Vulkan loader could not be opened: {e}"))?;
        let app = vk::ApplicationInfo::default()
            .application_name(c"EmblemWeave")
            .application_version(vk::make_api_version(0, 0, 1, 0))
            .engine_name(c"EmblemWeave NVN")
            .api_version(vk::API_VERSION_1_3);
        let create = vk::InstanceCreateInfo::default().application_info(&app);
        let instance =
            unsafe { entry.create_instance(&create, None) }.map_err(|e| format!("vkCreateInstance failed: {e}"))?;

        let candidates = unsafe { instance.enumerate_physical_devices() }.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let rank = |t: vk::PhysicalDeviceType| match t {
            vk::PhysicalDeviceType::DISCRETE_GPU => 0,
            vk::PhysicalDeviceType::INTEGRATED_GPU => 1,
            _ => 2,
        };
        let mut best: Option<(vk::PhysicalDevice, vk::PhysicalDeviceProperties, u32)> = None;
        for pd in candidates {
            let props = unsafe { instance.get_physical_device_properties(pd) };
            if props.api_version < vk::API_VERSION_1_3 {
                continue;
            }
            let families = unsafe { instance.get_physical_device_queue_family_properties(pd) };
            let Some(qf) = families.iter().position(|f| f.queue_flags.contains(vk::QueueFlags::GRAPHICS | vk::QueueFlags::COMPUTE)) else {
                continue;
            };
            let better = best.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, b, _)| rank(props.device_type) < rank(b.device_type));
            if better {
                best = Some((pd, props, qf as u32));
            }
        }
        let Some((physical, props, queue_family)) = best else {
            unsafe { instance.destroy_instance(None) };
            return Err("no Vulkan 1.3 device with a graphics queue was found".into());
        };

        let priorities = [1.0f32];
        let queues = [vk::DeviceQueueCreateInfo::default().queue_family_index(queue_family).queue_priorities(&priorities)];
        let mut v13 = vk::PhysicalDeviceVulkan13Features::default().dynamic_rendering(true).synchronization2(true);
        let create = vk::DeviceCreateInfo::default().queue_create_infos(&queues).push_next(&mut v13);
        let device = match unsafe { instance.create_device(physical, &create, None) } {
            Ok(d) => d,
            Err(e) => {
                unsafe { instance.destroy_instance(None) };
                return Err(format!("vkCreateDevice failed: {e}"));
            }
        };
        let queue = unsafe { device.get_device_queue(queue_family, 0) };

        let mut driver_props = vk::PhysicalDeviceDriverProperties::default();
        let mut props2 = vk::PhysicalDeviceProperties2::default().push_next(&mut driver_props);
        unsafe { instance.get_physical_device_properties2(physical, &mut props2) };
        let driver = driver_props.driver_name_as_c_str().map(|c| c.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();
        let name = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(props.device_name.as_ptr()) }.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let info = DeviceInfo {
            name,
            vendor_id: props.vendor_id,
            device_id: props.device_id,
            api: version(props.api_version),
            driver,
            queue_family,
            max_texture_2d: props.limits.max_image_dimension2_d,
            min_uniform_alignment: props.limits.min_uniform_buffer_offset_alignment,
            min_storage_alignment: props.limits.min_storage_buffer_offset_alignment,
        };
        Ok(Gpu { _entry: entry, instance, physical, device, queue, info })
    }
}

static GPU: OnceLock<Mutex<Option<Arc<Gpu>>>> = OnceLock::new();

/// The process's host device, created on first use. Creation failures are
/// returned each time rather than cached, so a driver installed later is found.
pub fn device() -> Result<Arc<Gpu>, String> {
    let slot = GPU.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(None));
    let mut guard = slot.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if let Some(g) = guard.as_ref() {
        return Ok(g.clone());
    }
    let g = Arc::new(Gpu::new()?);
    *guard = Some(g.clone());
    Ok(g)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn creates_a_device_when_vulkan_is_present() {
        // Machines without a Vulkan driver report an error instead of a device;
        // either outcome is valid, a panic is not.
        match super::device() {
            Ok(g) => {
                assert!(!g.info.name.is_empty());
                assert!(g.info.api.0 >= 1);
                assert!(g.info.max_texture_2d >= 4096);
            }
            Err(e) => assert!(!e.is_empty()),
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
//! AArch64 (ARMv8-A) instruction decoder for the subset needed by lifted
//! Nintendo Switch 2 modules.
//!
//! This is a *decoder*, not an interpreter: it produces a structured
//! description of each instruction which `lift` turns into C. Anything not
//! recognised is reported as `Op::Unsupported` so the emitted code traps at
//! run time instead of executing a wrong guess.

use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum Cond {
    Eq,
    Ne,
    Cs,
    Cc,
    Mi,
    Pl,
    Vs,
    Vc,
    Hi,
    Ls,
    Ge,
    Lt,
    Gt,
    Le,
    Al,
    Nv,
}

impl Cond {
    pub fn from_bits(b: u32) -> Option<Cond> {
        use Cond::*;
        Some(match b & 0xF {
            0x0 => Eq,
            0x1 => Ne,
            0x2 => Cs,
            0x3 => Cc,
            0x4 => Mi,
            0x5 => Pl,
            0x6 => Vs,
            0x7 => Vc,
            0x8 => Hi,
            0x9 => Ls,
            0xA => Ge,
            0xB => Lt,
            0xC => Gt,
            0xD => Le,
            0xE => Al,
            _ => Nv,
        })
    }

    /// C expression suffix for this condition, used by the emitter.
    pub fn c_suffix(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Cond::Eq => "eq",
            Cond::Ne => "ne",
            Cond::Cs => "cs",
            Cond::Cc => "cc",
            Cond::Mi => "mi",
            Cond::Pl => "pl",
            Cond::Vs => "vs",
            Cond::Vc => "vc",
            Cond::Hi => "hi",
            Cond::Ls => "ls",
            Cond::Ge => "ge",
            Cond::Lt => "lt",
            Cond::Gt => "gt",
            Cond::Le => "le",
            Cond::Al => "al",
            Cond::Nv => "nv",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum LogicalOp {
    And,
    Orr,
    Eor,
    Ands,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum Shift {
    Lsl,
    Lsr,
    Asr,
    Ror,
}

impl Shift {
    fn from_bits(b: u32) -> Shift {
        match b & 3 {
            0 => Shift::Lsl,
            1 => Shift::Lsr,
            2 => Shift::Asr,
            _ => Shift::Ror,
        }
    }
    pub fn c_op(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Shift::Lsl => "<<",
            Shift::Lsr => ">>",
            Shift::Asr => ">>s",
            Shift::Ror => "rors",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum MemMode {
```
