`crates/ew-lift/src/jump_table.rs`:

```rs
//! Jump-table recovery.
//!
//! The compilers used for this title emit the same switch shape every time:
//!
//! ```text
//! cmp   w8, #0x10
//! b.hi  .Ldefault
//! adr   x9, .LJTI              (or adrp x9, page / add x9, x9, #lo)
//! ldrb  w10, [x9, w8, uxtw]    (or ldrh, with lsl #1)
//! add   x9, x9, w10, lsl #2    (or sxtw #2 for signed byte offsets)
//! br    x9
//! ```
//!
//! This module recognises that shape in a decoded instruction window and reads
//! the actual entries out of the text image, so an indirect `br` becomes a set
//! of concrete successor blocks. Anything that does not fit is left alone and
//! reported as an unresolved edge: a wrong table would silently corrupt the
//! graph, which is worse than an honest gap.

use crate::aarch64::{decode, Cond, Op, Shift};
use crate::scan::{word_at, Insn};
use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct JumpTable {
    /// Address of the first table entry in the text image.
    pub table: u64,
    /// Base address that entry offsets are relative to (the `adr` target).
    pub base: u64,
    pub entries: usize,
    pub entry_bytes: u8,
    pub shift: u8,
    pub signed: bool,
    pub default: Option<u64>,
    pub targets: Vec<u64>,
}

/// Constants established by a function prologue, used to seed register
/// resolution. Compilers frequently build one table base in the prologue and
/// reuse it for every switch in the function.
pub type Known = std::collections::BTreeMap<u8, u64>;

/// Collect simple constant register values from a linear scan.
pub fn prologue_constants(text: &[u8], start: u64, max_insns: usize) -> Known {
    let mut known = Known::new();
    let mut addr = start;
    for _ in 0..max_insns {
        let word = match crate::scan::word_at(text, addr) {
            Some(w) => w,
            None => break,
        };
        match decode(word, addr) {
            Op::Adr { rd, target } => {
                known.insert(rd, target);
            }
            Op::AddSubImm { rd, rn, imm, sub: false, .. } if rd == rn => {
                if let Some(v) = known.get(&rn).copied() {
                    known.insert(rd, v.wrapping_add(imm as u64));
                }
            }
            Op::MoveWide { rd, imm, shift, kind: 0, is64 } => {
                let v = if is64 {
                    (imm as u64) << shift
                } else {
                    ((imm as u64) << shift) & 0xFFFF_FFFF
                };
                known.insert(rd, v);
            }
            Op::LoadStore { rt, .. } | Op::LoadStoreReg { rt, .. } | Op::LoadLiteral { rt, .. } => {
                known.remove(&rt);
            }
            Op::LoadStorePair { rt, rt2, .. } => {
                known.remove(&rt);
                known.remove(&rt2);
            }
            Op::LogicalReg { rd, .. }
            | Op::LogicalImm { rd, .. }
            | Op::AddSubReg { rd, .. }
            | Op::AddSubExt { rd, .. }
            | Op::MultiplyAdd { rd, .. }
            | Op::MulLong { rd, .. }
            | Op::CondSelect { rd, .. }
            | Op::DataProc2 { rd, .. } => {
                known.remove(&rd);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        addr += 4;
    }
    known
}

/// Slice backwards to the nearest definition of `reg` and return the constant
/// it was built from.
///
/// Walking forwards and requiring *every* write in the window to be understood
/// was wrong: a function reuses its scratch registers, so any later unrelated
/// write to the same number erased a perfectly good table base. Slicing stops at
/// the first definition, which is the one that actually reaches the use, and
/// follows it through `adr`/`adrp` plus `add` immediate pairs.
fn resolve_register(insns: &[Insn], reg: u8, known: &Known) -> Option<u64> {
    if reg == 31 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut tracked = reg;
    let mut addend: i64 = 0;
    for insn in insns.iter().rev() {
        match insn.op {
            Op::Adr { rd, target } if rd == tracked => {
                return Some((target as i64).wrapping_add(addend) as u64);
            }
            Op::AddSubImm { rd, rn, imm, sub: false, set_flags: false, .. } if rd == tracked => {
                if rn == 31 {
                    return None;
                }
                addend = addend.wrapping_add(imm as i64);
                tracked = rn;
            }
            Op::MoveWide { rd, imm, shift, kind: 0, .. } if rd == tracked => {
                return Some(((imm as i64) << shift).wrapping_add(addend) as u64);
            }
            Op::AddSubImm { rd, .. }
            | Op::LogicalReg { rd, .. }
            | Op::LogicalImm { rd, .. }
            | Op::AddSubReg { rd, .. }
            | Op::AddSubExt { rd, .. }
            | Op::MultiplyAdd { rd, .. }
            | Op::MulLong { rd, .. }
            | Op::CondSelect { rd, .. }
            | Op::DataProc2 { rd, .. }
            | Op::MoveWide { rd, .. }
            | Op::Adr { rd, .. }
            | Op::LoadLiteral { rt: rd, .. }
            | Op::LoadStore { rt: rd, .. }
            | Op::LoadStoreReg { rt: rd, .. }
                if rd == tracked =>
            {
                return None;
            }
            Op::LoadStorePair { rt, rt2, .. } if rt == tracked || rt2 == tracked => return None,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    known.get(&reg).copied().or_else(|| {
        // A base recorded by the prologue scan resolves directly.
        if tracked == reg { None } else { known.get(&tracked).copied().map(|v| (v as i64).wrapping_add(addend) as u64) }
    })
}

/// Mapped read-only segments besides text, as (module address, bytes). Jump
/// tables are usually emitted into rodata, so reading one requires the module
/// image rather than the text file alone.
pub type Segments<'a> = &'a [(u64, &'a [u8])];

fn slice_at<'a>(text: &'a [u8], segments: Segments<'a>, at: u64, len: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
    let off = at as usize;
    if off.saturating_add(len) <= text.len() {
        return Some(&text[off..off + len]);
    }
    for (base, data) in segments {
        if at >= *base {
            let rel = (at - *base) as usize;
            if rel.saturating_add(len) <= data.len() {
                return Some(&data[rel..rel + len]);
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

fn read_entry(text: &[u8], segments: Segments, at: u64, bytes: u8) -> Option<u64> {
    let raw = slice_at(text, segments, at, bytes as usize)?;
    Some(match bytes {
        1 => raw[0] as u64,
        2 => u16::from_le_bytes([raw[0], raw[1]]) as u64,
        4 => u32::from_le_bytes([raw[0], raw[1], raw[2], raw[3]]) as u64,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// Recognise a jump table whose `br` is the last instruction of `insns`.
pub fn detect(
    text: &[u8],
    segments: Segments,
    known: &Known,
    insns: &[Insn],
) -> Option<JumpTable> {
    detect_with_reason(text, segments, known, insns).ok()
}

/// Why a `br` was not recognised as a jump table. Reported by the `ew-tables`
/// diagnostic so a missing instruction pattern is measured, not guessed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Unresolved {
    NotABranch,
    NoIndexAdd,
    BaseUnknown,
    NoTableLoad,
    TableUnknown,
    NoBoundsCheck,
    NoEntries,
    BadDefault,
    BadTarget,
    Empty,
}

impl Unresolved {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Unresolved::NotABranch => "last instruction is not br",
            Unresolved::NoIndexAdd => "no add of a loaded offset to a base",
            Unresolved::BaseUnknown => "table base register is not a known constant",
            Unresolved::NoTableLoad => "no load from the table base",
            Unresolved::TableUnknown => "table address register is not a known constant",
            Unresolved::NoBoundsCheck => "no cmp/subs bound before the branch",
            Unresolved::NoEntries => "bound check is not a hi/cs comparison",
            Unresolved::BadDefault => "default target is not code",
            Unresolved::BadTarget => "a table entry does not land on code",
            Unresolved::Empty => "table has no entries",
        }
    }
}

pub fn detect_with_reason(
    text: &[u8],
    segments: Segments,
    known: &Known,
    insns: &[Insn],
) -> Result<JumpTable, Unresolved> {
    let last = insns.last().ok_or(Unresolved::NotABranch)?;
    let br_reg = match last.op {
        Op::Br { rn } => rn,
        _ => return Err(Unresolved::NotABranch),
    };

    // The instruction that adds the table entry to the base. Compilers use
    // either the extended-register form (`add x9, x9, w8, lsl #2`) or the plain
    // shifted-register form (`add x10, x10, w11, lsl #2`); both appear here.
    // Two shapes are accepted: `add x9, x9, w10, lsl #2`, where the base is the
    // branch register itself, and `add x9, x8, w10, lsl #2`, where the base is a
    // separate register and the branch register is only the sum.
    let (add_idx, index_reg, base_reg, shift, signed) =
        insns.iter().enumerate().rev().find_map(|(i, insn)| match insn.op {
            Op::AddSubExt { rd, rn, rm, option, shift, sub: false, set_flags: false, .. }
                if rd == br_reg && rn != 31 =>
            {
                Some((i, rm, rn, shift as u32, option.is_signed()))
            }
            Op::AddSubReg {
                rd,
                rn,
                rm,
                shift: Shift::Lsl,
                amount,
                sub: false,
                set_flags: false,
                ..
            } if rd == br_reg && rn != 31 => Some((i, rm, rn, amount as u32, false)),
            _ => None,
        })
        .ok_or(Unresolved::NoIndexAdd)?;

    let base = resolve_register(&insns[..add_idx], base_reg, known).ok_or(Unresolved::BaseUnknown)?;

    // The table load: `ldrb wI, [xTable, xIndex, extend]`.
    let (load_idx, table_reg, index_src, entry_bytes) =
        insns[..add_idx].iter().enumerate().rev().find_map(|(i, insn)| match insn.op {
            Op::LoadStoreReg { rt, rn, rm, bytes, load: true, .. } if rt == index_reg => {
                Some((i, rn, rm, bytes))
            }
            _ => None,
        })
        .ok_or(Unresolved::NoTableLoad)?;

    let table = resolve_register(&insns[..load_idx], table_reg, known)
        .ok_or(Unresolved::TableUnknown)?;

    // The index is usually copied into a scratch register first
    // (`mov w8, w0`), and the range check is then emitted against the original
    // argument. Follow that copy, or the bound looks absent when it is right
    // there.
    let mut bound_regs = vec![index_src];
    if let Some(source) = insns[..load_idx].iter().rev().find_map(|insn| match insn.op {
        Op::LogicalReg { rd, rn: 31, rm, shift: Shift::Lsl, amount: 0, op: crate::aarch64::LogicalOp::Orr, set_flags: false, is64, invert: false } if rd == index_src => {
            let _ = is64;
            Some(rm)
        }
        Op::LogicalReg { rd, .. } if rd == index_src => None,
        _ => None,
    }) {
        if source != 31 {
            bound_regs.push(source);
        }
    }

    // `cmp wIndex, #bound` plus the branch that excludes larger values.
    let mut entries = None;
    let mut default = None;
    if let Some((cmp_idx, bound)) = insns[..load_idx].iter().enumerate().rev().find_map(|(i, insn)| {
        match insn.op {
            Op::AddSubImm { rd: 31, rn, imm, sub: true, set_flags: true, .. }
                if bound_regs.contains(&rn) =>
            {
                Some((i, imm as u64))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }) {
        if let Some(Op::BCond { cond, target }) = insns.get(cmp_idx + 1).map(|i| i.op) {
            match cond {
                Cond::Hi => entries = Some(bound + 1),
                Cond::Cs => entries = Some(bound),
                _ => {}
            }
            default = Some(target);
        }
    }

    let entries = entries.ok_or(Unresolved::NoEntries)?;
    if entries == 0 {
        return Err(Unresolved::Empty);
    }
    if entries > 2048 {
        return Err(Unresolved::NoEntries);
    }
    // The default target is part of the same switch, so it has to be real code.
    if let Some(target) = default {
        if word_at(text, target).is_none() {
            return Err(Unresolved::BadDefault);
        }
    }

    let mut targets = Vec::with_capacity(entries as usize);
    for i in 0..entries {
        let at = table
            .checked_add(i * entry_bytes as u64)
            .ok_or(Unresolved::TableUnknown)?;
        let raw = read_entry(text, segments, at, entry_bytes).ok_or(Unresolved::TableUnknown)?;
        let extended = if signed {
            match entry_bytes {
                1 => (raw as u8 as i8) as i64,
                2 => (raw as u16 as i16) as i64,
                _ => (raw as u32 as i32) as i64,
            }
        } else {
            raw as i64
        };
        let target = (base as i64)
            .wrapping_add(extended.wrapping_shl(shift))
            .max(0) as u64;
        // Every successor must be a real, aligned instruction in the image.
        if target % 4 != 0 || word_at(text, target).is_none() || word_at(text, target) == Some(0) {
            return Err(Unresolved::BadTarget);
        }
        targets.push(target);
    }

    targets.sort_unstable();
    targets.dedup();

    Ok(JumpTable {
        table,
        base,
        entries: entries as usize,
        entry_bytes,
        shift: shift as u8,
        signed,
        default,
        targets,
    })
}


/// How far back a jump-table search may look for the code that built the table
/// base. Compilers put that in the function prologue, so the window has to reach
/// past the block that ends in `br`.
pub const CONTEXT_WORDS: u64 = 96;

/// Decode `window` words of context before `addr` and return them followed by
/// the words from `addr` to `end` inclusive.
pub fn context_window(text: &[u8], addr: u64, end: u64) -> Vec<Insn> {
    let mut insns = Vec::new();
    let start = addr.saturating_sub(CONTEXT_WORDS * 4);
    let mut at = start;
    while at <= end {
        if let Some(word) = word_at(text, at) {
            insns.push(Insn { addr: at, word, op: decode(word, at) });
        }
        at += 4;
    }
    insns
}

/// Convenience for address discovery: try to resolve the table that feeds the
/// `br` at `br_addr` using a window of preceding instructions.
pub fn targets_at(text: &[u8], segments: Segments, br_addr: u64) -> Vec<u64> {
    let insns = context_window(text, br_addr, br_addr);
    detect(text, segments, &Known::new(), &insns)
        .map(|t| t.targets)
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Hand-assembled switch in the exact shape clang produces. The table holds
    /// signed byte offsets, scaled by four, relative to `base`.
    fn switch_image() -> Vec<u8> {
        let words: [u32; 10] = [
            0x7100_0D1F, // 0x00: cmp w8, #3
            0x5400_0128, // 0x04: b.hi 0x28 (default)
            0x1000_0109, // 0x08: adr x9, 0x28   (base = table start)
            0x3868_692A, // 0x0c: ldrb w10, [x9, x8, uxtw]
            0x8B2A_C929, // 0x10: add x9, x9, w10, sxtw #2
            0xD61F_0120, // 0x14: br x9
            0xD503_201F, // 0x18: nop
            0xD503_201F, // 0x1c: nop
            0xD503_201F, // 0x20: nop
            0xD503_201F, // 0x24: nop
        ];
        let mut text: Vec<u8> = words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        // Table at 0x28: signed byte offsets relative to 0x28, scaled by four.
        // 6, 8, 10, 12 scale to 0x18, 0x20, 0x28, 0x30.
        text.extend_from_slice(&[6, 8, 10, 12]);
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD5, 0x03, 0x20, 0x1F]); // 0x2c
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD5, 0x03, 0x20, 0x1F]); // 0x30
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD5, 0x03, 0x20, 0x1F]); // 0x34
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD5, 0x03, 0x20, 0x1F]); // 0x38
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD5, 0x03, 0x20, 0x1F]); // 0x3c
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD6, 0x5F, 0x03, 0xC0]); // 0x40: ret
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD6, 0x5F, 0x03, 0xC0]); // 0x44
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD6, 0x5F, 0x03, 0xC0]); // 0x48: ret
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD6, 0x5F, 0x03, 0xC0]); // 0x4c
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD6, 0x5F, 0x03, 0xC0]); // 0x50: ret
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD6, 0x5F, 0x03, 0xC0]); // 0x54
        text.extend_from_slice(&[0xD6, 0x5F, 0x03, 0xC0]); // 0x58: ret
        text
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_a_signed_byte_table() {
        let text = switch_image();
        let insns: Vec<Insn> = (0..6u64)
            .filter_map(|i| {
                let addr = i * 4;
                word_at(&text, addr).map(|word| Insn { addr, word, op: decode(word, addr) })
            })
            .collect();
        let table = detect(&text, &[], &Known::new(), &insns).expect("table must resolve");
        assert_eq!(table.table, 0x28);
        assert_eq!(table.base, 0x28);
        assert_eq!(table.entries, 4);
        assert_eq!(table.entry_bytes, 1);
        assert_eq!(table.shift, 2);
        assert!(table.signed);
        assert_eq!(table.default, Some(0x28));
        assert_eq!(table.targets, vec![0x40, 0x48, 0x50, 0x58]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_a_table_with_a_bad_target() {
        let mut text = switch_image();
        // point the first entry outside the image
        text[0x28] = 0x7F;
        let insns: Vec<Insn> = (0..6u64)
            .filter_map(|i| {
                let addr = i * 4;
                word_at(&text, addr).map(|word| Insn { addr, word, op: decode(word, addr) })
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(detect(&text, &[], &Known::new(), &insns).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn ignores_a_plain_indirect_branch() {
        let text = switch_image();
        let insns: Vec<Insn> = (5..6u64)
            .filter_map(|i| {
                let addr = i * 4;
                word_at(&text, addr).map(|word| Insn { addr, word, op: decode(word, addr) })
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(detect(&text, &[], &Known::new(), &insns).is_none());
    }
}

`crates/ew-lift/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! `ew-lift` — the static recompilation pipeline.
//!
//! Pipeline: decode AArch64 words -> discover dispatchable addresses -> recover
//! basic blocks and their control-flow edges (including jump tables) -> emit C
//! that dispatches between blocks internally and returns to the runtime
//! dispatcher at every edge that leaves the function.
//!
//! Two independent implementations of the same instruction semantics exist on
//! purpose: [`interpreter`] (used as a reference for differential tests) and
//! [`lift`] (the shipped C). Agreement between them is evidence; the interpreter
//! is not part of the product runtime.

pub mod aarch64;
pub mod cfg;
pub mod interpreter;
pub mod jump_table;
pub mod lift;
pub mod scan;
pub mod simd;

pub use aarch64::{decode, Cond, DataOp2, Extend, LogicalOp, MemMode, Op, Shift};
pub use interpreter::{HostArena, Program, State, Transfer};
pub use jump_table::JumpTable;
pub use interpreter::{StepRecord, ThreadInfo};
pub use lift::{
    dispatch_header, emit_campaign, emit_harness, emit_module, emit_simd_campaign, simd_seed_vector,
    RUNTIME_HEADER,
};
pub use scan::{
    discover_starts, discover_starts_in, lift_function, lift_function_in, Block, Edge, EdgeKind,
    Insn, LiftedFunction,
};

use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LiftOptions {
    pub module: String,
    pub entry: u64,
    pub max_functions: usize,
    pub max_insns: usize,
    pub pure_leaf_only: bool,
    /// Keep a block only in the function whose start is the closest one at
    /// or below it. Control flow is followed from every start, so without
    /// this the same code is lifted into every function that reaches it
    /// (about fifty times over for the whole game).
    pub own_blocks: bool,
}

impl Default for LiftOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        LiftOptions {
            module: "module".to_string(),
            entry: 0,
            max_functions: 512,
            // Per-function budget, not a per-block cap. A budget of 256 truncated
            // most real functions before their switch blocks were reached, which
            // made control-flow recovery look far worse than it is. The block
            // ceiling in `cfg` is what stops a bad edge walking the module.
            max_insns: 4096,
            pure_leaf_only: false,
            own_blocks: false,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct LiftReport {
    pub module: String,
    pub text_bytes: usize,
    pub text_words: usize,
    /// All-zero words. AArch64 leaves alignment gaps between functions, so these
    /// are padding, not code. They are excluded from the coverage ratio instead
    /// of being counted as undecoded instructions.
    pub padding_words: usize,
    /// Words that decode to a supported instruction across the whole segment.
    pub decodable_words: usize,
    pub unsupported_words: usize,
    /// Fraction of the real (non-padding) text segment that decodes to
    /// supported instructions.
    pub decode_coverage: f64,
    pub candidate_starts: usize,
    pub lifted_functions: usize,
    pub complete_functions: usize,
    pub pure_leaf_functions: usize,
    pub blocks_lifted: usize,
    pub instructions_lifted: usize,
    pub unsupported_in_lifted: usize,
    pub jump_tables: usize,
    pub jump_table_targets: usize,
    pub unresolved_edges: usize,
    /// Functions left partial because their instruction budget ran out.
    pub incomplete_budget: usize,
    /// Functions left partial because a block had no terminator.
    pub incomplete_unterminated: usize,
    /// Functions left partial because an indirect edge could not be resolved.
    pub incomplete_indirect: usize,
    pub limitations: Vec<String>,
}

/// Lift a text segment.
pub fn lift_text(text: &[u8], opts: &LiftOptions) -> (LiftReport, Vec<LiftedFunction>) {
    lift_text_in(text, &[], opts)
}

/// Lift a text segment with the rest of the module image available, so jump
/// tables stored in rodata can be resolved.
pub fn lift_text_in(
    text: &[u8],
    segments: jump_table::Segments,
    opts: &LiftOptions,
) -> (LiftReport, Vec<LiftedFunction>) {
    let text_words = text.len() / 4;
    let mut decodable = 0usize;
    let mut padding = 0usize;
    for (addr, word) in scan::words(text) {
        if word == 0 {
            padding += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if !matches!(
            decode(word, addr),
            Op::Unsupported { .. } | Op::UnsupportedBitfield { .. }
        ) {
            decodable += 1;
        }
    }
    let real_words = text_words.saturating_sub(padding);

    // Computed once: rebuilding the call-target set per function would be
    // quadratic in the size of the module. Prologue entries are boundaries too,
    // and without them the traversal walks straight into the next function and
    // exhausts its budget on code it does not own.
    let mut boundaries = scan::call_targets(text);
    boundaries.extend(scan::prologue_starts(text, 262_144));

    let candidates =
        discover_starts_in(text, segments, opts.entry, opts.max_functions.saturating_mul(8).max(64));
    let candidate_count = candidates.len();

    let mut sorted: Vec<u64> = candidates.clone();
    sorted.sort_unstable();
    sorted.dedup();
    let region_owner = |a: u64| match sorted.binary_search(&a) {
        Ok(i) => sorted[i],
        Err(0) => u64::MAX,
        Err(i) => sorted[i - 1],
    };
    let mut funcs = Vec::new();
    for start in candidates {
        if funcs.len() >= opts.max_functions {
            break;
        }
        if let Some(mut f) = cfg::build(text, segments, start, opts.max_insns, &boundaries) {
            if opts.pure_leaf_only && !f.is_pure_leaf() {
                continue;
            }
            if opts.own_blocks {
                f.blocks.retain(|b| region_owner(b.addr) == start);
                if f.blocks.is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
            }
            funcs.push(f);
        }
    }

    let report = LiftReport {
        module: opts.module.clone(),
        text_bytes: text.len(),
        text_words,
        padding_words: padding,
        decodable_words: decodable,
        unsupported_words: real_words.saturating_sub(decodable),
        decode_coverage: if real_words == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            decodable as f64 / real_words as f64
        },
        candidate_starts: candidate_count,
        lifted_functions: funcs.len(),
        complete_functions: funcs.iter().filter(|f| f.complete).count(),
        pure_leaf_functions: funcs.iter().filter(|f| f.is_pure_leaf()).count(),
        blocks_lifted: funcs.iter().map(|f| f.blocks.len()).sum(),
        instructions_lifted: funcs.iter().map(|f| f.insn_count()).sum(),
        unsupported_in_lifted: funcs.iter().map(|f| f.unsupported).sum(),
        jump_tables: funcs.iter().map(|f| f.jump_tables).sum(),
        jump_table_targets: funcs.iter().map(|f| f.jump_table_targets).sum(),
        unresolved_edges: funcs.iter().map(|f| f.unresolved_edges).sum(),
        incomplete_budget: funcs.iter().filter(|f| !f.complete && f.budget_exhausted).count(),
        incomplete_unterminated: funcs
            .iter()
            .filter(|f| !f.complete && !f.budget_exhausted && f.unterminated_blocks > 0)
            .count(),
        incomplete_indirect: funcs
            .iter()
            .filter(|f| !f.complete && !f.budget_exhausted && f.unresolved_edges > 0)
            .count(),
        limitations: vec![
            "indirect branches without a recognisable table remain unresolved and return to the dispatcher"
                .to_string(),
            "function entry points are inferred from call and branch targets, not from debug metadata"
                .to_string(),
            "SIMD/FP instructions are still decoded as unsupported and trap when reached".to_string(),
            "zero words are counted as padding and excluded from the coverage ratio".to_string(),
        ],
    };
    (report, funcs)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn words_to_bytes(words: &[u32]) -> Vec<u8> {
        words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn lifts_synthetic_segment_and_reports_coverage() {
        // The zero word is alignment padding, so the coverage ratio is measured
        // over the four real words and is therefore total.
        let text = words_to_bytes(&[
            0x9100_4020, // 0x00: add x0, x1, #0x10
            0xAA01_03E0, // 0x04: mov x0, x1
            0xD65F03C0,  // 0x08: ret
            0x0000_0000, // 0x0c: unsupported
            0xD65F03C0,  // 0x10: ret
        ]);
        let opts = LiftOptions { module: "synthetic".into(), ..Default::default() };
        let (report, funcs) = lift_text(&text, &opts);
        assert_eq!(report.text_words, 5);
        assert_eq!(report.padding_words, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.unsupported_words, 0);
        assert_eq!(report.decodable_words, 4);
        assert!((report.decode_coverage - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert_eq!(report.lifted_functions, funcs.len());
        assert!(funcs.iter().any(|f| f.addr == 0 && f.complete));
        assert_eq!(report.blocks_lifted, 1, "one block, ending at the ret");
    }

    /// `ldadd x9, x8, [x8]` stores old + x9 and returns the old value in x8.
    /// The emitter once stored `x9 & (old + x9)` and returned x9.
    #[test]
    fn atomic_add_returns_the_old_value() {
        let text = words_to_bytes(&[0xF829_0108, 0xD65F03C0]);
        let opts = LiftOptions { module: "t".into(), ..Default::default() };
        let (_, funcs) = lift_text(&text, &opts);
        let c = emit_module("t", &funcs);
        assert!(c.contains("ew_u64 new_ = old_ + v_;"), "{c}");
        assert!(c.contains("ew_u64 v_ = (EW_R(cpu, 9, 0)) & ~0ULL;"), "{c}");
        assert!(c.contains("old_);"), "the destination gets the old value: {c}");
    }

    /// Differential test: the interpreter and the emitter share only the decoder.
    #[test]
    fn interpreter_follows_branches() {
        let text = words_to_bytes(&[
            0xAA02_03E0, // 0x00: mov x0, x2
            0xB500_0040, // 0x04: cbnz x0, 0x0c
            0xAA03_03E0, // 0x08: mov x0, x3
            0xD65F03C0, // 0x0c: ret
            0xD65F03C0, // 0x10: ret (unreached)
        ]);
        let f = lift_function(&text, 0, 256).unwrap();
        assert!(f.complete);
        assert_eq!(f.blocks.len(), 3);
        let mut st = State::patterned();
        interpreter::run_function(&mut st, &f, 64).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(st.x[0], st.x[2], "cbz taken skips the mov x0, x3");
        assert_eq!(st.pc, st.x[30], "left the function through ret");
    }
}

```

`crates/ew-lift/src/lift.rs`:

```rs
//! C emission for lifted AArch64 functions.
//!
//! The generated code is intentionally boring: one statement per guest
//! instruction, an explicit guest stack pointer, and a return to the dispatcher
//! at every control-flow edge. That keeps the translation auditable, which
//! matters far more than dispatch speed at this stage. Unsupported instructions
//! become `ew_halt()` calls with the guest address, never a silent guess.

use crate::aarch64::{DataOp2, FpBinop, FpRound, FpUnop, LogicalOp, MemMode, Op, Shift};
use crate::scan::{Insn, LiftedFunction};

/// Support header emitted next to every generated translation unit.
pub const RUNTIME_HEADER: &str = concat!(r#"/* ew_aarch64.h — generated by ew-lift. Shared by lifted code and the runtime.
 *
 * Guest registers are explicit so translations stay readable and auditable.
 * x31 is context dependent (XZR or SP), which the EW_R/EW_W macros encode.
 */
#ifndef EW_AARCH64_H
#define EW_AARCH64_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

typedef uint64_t ew_u64;
typedef int64_t  ew_i64;
typedef uint32_t ew_u32;
typedef int32_t  ew_i32;
typedef uint8_t  ew_u8;

typedef struct Cpu {
    ew_u64 x[31];          /* x0..x30 */
    ew_u64 v[32][2];       /* V0..V31: [0] low eight bytes, [1] high eight */
    ew_u64 sp;
    ew_u64 pc;
    ew_u32 nzcv;           /* bit3=N bit2=Z bit1=C bit0=V */
    int    halted;
    char   halt_reason[128];
    ew_u64 tpidrro;        /* thread pointers */
    ew_u64 tpidr;
    ew_u64 fpcr;
    ew_u64 fpsr;
    ew_u64 (*counter)(void); /* system counter, 19.2 MHz; NULL: none */
    int    svc;            /* pending supervisor call number, -1 when none, -2 out of budget */
    ew_u64 excl_addr;      /* exclusive monitor: reserved address */
    int    excl_valid;     /* and whether a reservation is held */
    /* Guest memory access. Supplied by the runtime; the harness may stub it. */
    ew_u64 (*mem_read)(void *ctx, ew_u64 addr, unsigned bytes);
    void   (*mem_write)(void *ctx, ew_u64 addr, ew_u64 value, unsigned bytes);
    void   *mem_ctx;
    /* Native runs: guest memory as one host block (guest address = offset),
     * read and written directly; NULL sends every access to the callbacks. */
    ew_u8  *mem_base;
    ew_u64 mem_size;
    /* Instructions left before the function returns to the run loop, checked
     * at every block so a long loop still lets other guest threads run. */
    ew_i64 budget;
} Cpu;

/* The index expression clamps 31 to 0 so the unused branch of these ternaries
 * never forms an out-of-bounds access at compile time. */
#define EW_IDX(i) (((i) == 31) ? 0 : (i))
#define EW_R(cpu, i, spok)                                                     \
    (((i) == 31) ? (((spok) && (i) == 31) ? (cpu)->sp : 0ULL) : (cpu)->x[EW_IDX(i)])
#define EW_W(cpu, i, spok, v)                                                  \
    do {                                                                       \
        ew_u64 ew_v_ = (v);                                                    \
        if ((i) == 31) {                                                       \
            if (spok) { (cpu)->sp = ew_v_; }                                   \
        } else {                                                               \
            (cpu)->x[EW_IDX(i)] = ew_v_;                                       \
        }                                                                      \
    } while (0)

#define EW_M32(v) ((ew_u64)(ew_u32)(v))
#define EW_M(cpu_is64, v) ((cpu_is64) ? (ew_u64)(v) : EW_M32(v))

static inline void ew_halt(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 pc, const char *why)
{
    cpu->halted = 1;
    cpu->pc = pc;
    snprintf(cpu->halt_reason, sizeof(cpu->halt_reason), "pc=0x%llx %s",
             (unsigned long long)pc, why);
}

/* System registers, numbered by the 15-bit field of mrs/msr. Values match the
 * interpreter's read_sysreg. */
static inline int ew_mrs(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 pc, ew_u32 reg, ew_u64 *out)
{
    switch (reg) {
    case 0x5E83: *out = cpu->tpidrro; return 1;          /* tpidrro_el0 */
    case 0x5E82: *out = cpu->tpidr; return 1;            /* tpidr_el0 */
    case 0x5F01: case 0x5F02:                            /* cntpct, cntvct */
        *out = cpu->counter ? cpu->counter() : 0; return 1;
    case 0x5F00: *out = 19200000ULL; return 1;           /* cntfrq_el0 */
    case 0x5A20: *out = cpu->fpcr; return 1;
    case 0x5A21: *out = cpu->fpsr; return 1;
    case 0x5A10: *out = (ew_u64)cpu->nzcv << 28; return 1;
    case 0x5801: *out = 0x8444C004ULL; return 1;         /* ctr_el0 */
    case 0x5807: *out = 4; return 1;                     /* dczid_el0 */
    default: ew_halt(cpu, pc, "mrs from a system register that is not modelled"); return 0;
    }
}

static inline int ew_msr(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 pc, ew_u32 reg, ew_u64 v)
{
    switch (reg) {
    case 0x5E82: cpu->tpidr = v; return 1;
    case 0x5A20: cpu->fpcr = v; return 1;
    case 0x5A21: cpu->fpsr = v; return 1;
    case 0x5A10: cpu->nzcv = (ew_u32)((v >> 28) & 0xF); return 1;
    default: ew_halt(cpu, pc, "msr to a system register that is not modelled"); return 0;
    }
}

/* Vector register access. Writing a scalar width zeroes the upper bytes, which
 * is the architectural rule for every SIMD/FP and V-register write. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_vget(Cpu *cpu, unsigned i, unsigned bytes)
{
    ew_u64 lo = cpu->v[i & 31u][0];
    ew_u64 keep = (bytes >= 8u) ? ~(ew_u64)0 : (((ew_u64)1 << (bytes * 8u)) - 1u);
    return lo & keep;
}

static inline void ew_vset(Cpu *cpu, unsigned i, unsigned bytes, ew_u64 value)
{
    unsigned idx = i & 31u;
    ew_u64 keep = (bytes >= 8u) ? ~(ew_u64)0 : (((ew_u64)1 << (bytes * 8u)) - 1u);
    cpu->v[idx][0] = value & keep;
    cpu->v[idx][1] = 0;
}

static inline void ew_vset128(Cpu *cpu, unsigned i, ew_u64 lo, ew_u64 hi)
{
    unsigned idx = i & 31u;
    cpu->v[idx][0] = lo;
    cpu->v[idx][1] = hi;
}

static inline ew_u64 ew_load(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 addr, unsigned bytes)
{
    if (cpu->mem_base && addr <= cpu->mem_size && bytes <= cpu->mem_size - addr) {
        ew_u64 v = 0;
        memcpy(&v, cpu->mem_base + addr, bytes); /* the host is little endian */
        return v;
    }
    return cpu->mem_read(cpu->mem_ctx, addr, bytes);
}

static inline void ew_store(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 addr, ew_u64 value, unsigned bytes)
{
    if (cpu->mem_base && addr <= cpu->mem_size && bytes <= cpu->mem_size - addr) {
        memcpy(cpu->mem_base + addr, &value, bytes);
        return;
    }
    cpu->mem_write(cpu->mem_ctx, addr, value, bytes);
}

static inline void ew_flags_nz(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 v, int is64)
{
    ew_u32 n = is64 ? (ew_u32)(v >> 63) : (ew_u32)((v >> 31) & 1);
    ew_u32 z = (v == 0) ? 1u : 0u;
    cpu->nzcv = (n << 3) | (z << 2); /* logical ops clear C and V */
}

static inline void ew_flags_add(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 a, ew_u64 b, ew_u64 r, int is64)
{
    ew_u32 c, v, n, z;
    if (is64) {
        c = (r < a);
        v = (ew_u32)((((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 63) & 1);
        n = (ew_u32)(r >> 63);
        z = (r == 0);
    } else {
        ew_u32 a32 = (ew_u32)a, b32 = (ew_u32)b, r32 = (ew_u32)r;
        c = (r32 < a32);
        v = ((a32 ^ r32) & (b32 ^ r32)) >> 31;
        n = r32 >> 31;
        z = (r32 == 0);
    }
    cpu->nzcv = (n << 3) | (z << 2) | (c << 1) | v;
}

static inline void ew_flags_sub(Cpu *cpu, ew_u64 a, ew_u64 b, ew_u64 r, int is64)
{
    ew_u32 c, v, n, z;
    if (is64) {
        c = (a >= b);
        v = (ew_u32)((((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 63) & 1);
        n = (ew_u32)(r >> 63);
        z = (r == 0);
    } else {
        ew_u32 a32 = (ew_u32)a, b32 = (ew_u32)b, r32 = (ew_u32)r;
        c = (a32 >= b32);
        v = ((a32 ^ b32) & (a32 ^ r32)) >> 31;
        n = r32 >> 31;
        z = (r32 == 0);
    }
    cpu->nzcv = (n << 3) | (z << 2) | (c << 1) | v;
}

static inline ew_u64 ew_shift(ew_u64 v, unsigned kind, unsigned amount, int is64)
{
    unsigned width = is64 ? 64u : 32u;
    amount %= width;
    v = is64 ? v : EW_M32(v);
    switch (kind) {
    case 0: return EW_M(is64, v << amount);
    case 1: return EW_M(is64, v >> amount);
    case 2: return is64 ? (ew_u64)((ew_i64)v >> amount)
                        : EW_M32((ew_u32)((int32_t)(ew_u32)v >> amount));
    default:
        return is64 ? (v >> amount) | (v << ((width - amount) % width))
                    : EW_M32(((ew_u32)v >> amount) | ((ew_u32)v << ((width - amount) % width)));
    }
}

static inline ew_u64 ew_ones(unsigned n)
{
    return (n >= 64u) ? ~(ew_u64)0 : ((((ew_u64)1) << n) - 1u);
}

/* Operand extension, matching the AArch64 `option` field. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_extend(ew_u64 v, unsigned option)
{
    switch (option & 7u) {
    case 0: return (ew_u64)(ew_u8)v;
    case 1: return (ew_u64)(uint16_t)v;
    case 2: return (ew_u64)(ew_u32)v;
    case 3: return v;
    case 4: return (ew_u64)(ew_i64)(int8_t)v;
    case 5: return (ew_u64)(ew_i64)(int16_t)v;
    case 6: return (ew_u64)(ew_i64)(int32_t)(ew_u32)v;
    default: return v;
    }
}

static inline ew_u64 ew_rbit(ew_u64 v, int is64)
{
    ew_u64 r = 0;
    unsigned bits = is64 ? 64u : 32u;
    unsigned i;
    for (i = 0; i < bits; i++) {
        if ((v >> i) & 1u) r |= (ew_u64)1 << (bits - 1u - i);
    }
    return is64 ? r : EW_M32(r);
}

/* Reverse the byte order inside each `group`-byte unit. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_rev_within(ew_u64 v, unsigned group, int is64)
{
    unsigned bits = is64 ? 64u : 32u;
    unsigned base = 0;
    ew_u64 out = 0;
    while (base < bits) {
        unsigned j;
        for (j = 0; j < group; j++) {
            ew_u64 byte = (v >> (base + j * 8u)) & 0xFFu;
            out |= byte << (base + (group - 1u - j) * 8u);
        }
        base += group * 8u;
    }
    return is64 ? out : EW_M32(out);
}

static inline ew_u64 ew_clz(ew_u64 v, int is64)
{
    unsigned bits = is64 ? 64u : 32u;
    unsigned n = 0;
    ew_u64 x = is64 ? v : EW_M32(v);
    while (n < bits && ((x >> (bits - 1u - n)) & 1u) == 0) n++;
    return n;
}

/* CLS counts the leading bits equal to the sign bit, minus one. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_cls(ew_u64 v, int is64)
{
    ew_u64 x = is64 ? (v ^ (ew_u64)((ew_i64)v >> 1))
                    : EW_M32((ew_u32)v ^ (ew_u32)((int32_t)(ew_u32)v >> 1));
    ew_u64 z = ew_clz(x, is64);
    return z > 0 ? z - 1u : 0u;
}

/* Sign-extend a value whose sign bit is at `top` inside a 32/64-bit result. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_sext(ew_u64 v, unsigned top, int is64)
{
    unsigned s = 63u - (top & 63u);
    ew_u64 r = (ew_u64)((ew_i64)(v << s) >> s);
    return is64 ? r : EW_M32(r);
}

/* sbfm / bfm / ubfm, which also cover sbfx, ubfx, sbfiz, ubfiz, bfi, bfxil,
 * lsl, lsr and asr with an immediate. opc: 0 sbfm, 1 bfm, 2 ubfm. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_bitfield(ew_u64 src, ew_u64 dst, unsigned immr,
                                 unsigned imms, unsigned opc, int is64)
{
    unsigned bits = is64 ? 64u : 32u;
    unsigned width, shift;
    ew_u64 field, result;

    if ((immr & (bits - 1u)) <= (imms & (bits - 1u))) {
        /* extracting: the field moves down to bit 0 */
        width = (imms & (bits - 1u)) - (immr & (bits - 1u)) + 1u;
        shift = 0u;
        field = (src >> (immr & (bits - 1u))) & ew_ones(width);
    } else {
        /* inserting: the field wraps and moves up */
        width = (imms & (bits - 1u)) + 1u;
        shift = bits - (immr & (bits - 1u));
        field = (src & ew_ones(width)) << shift;
    }

    if (opc == 2u) {
        result = EW_M(is64, field);
    } else if (opc == 0u) {
        result = ew_sext(field, shift + width - 1u, is64);
    } else {
        ew_u64 mask = ew_ones(width) << shift;
        result = EW_M(is64, (dst & ~mask) | field);
    }
    return result;
}

/* udiv/sdiv trap nothing: division by zero yields zero, and the signed
 * overflow case wraps, matching AArch64 rather than the C undefined cases. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_udiv(ew_u64 a, ew_u64 b)
{
    return b ? a / b : 0u;
}

static inline ew_u64 ew_sdiv(ew_u64 a, ew_u64 b, int is64)
{
    if (!b) return 0u;
    if (is64) {
        if (a == 0x8000000000000000ULL && b == ~(ew_u64)0) return a;
        return (ew_u64)((ew_i64)a / (ew_i64)b);
    }
    {
        ew_u32 a32 = (ew_u32)a, b32 = (ew_u32)b;
        if (a32 == 0x80000000u && b32 == 0xFFFFFFFFu) return EW_M32(a32);
        return EW_M32((ew_u32)((int32_t)a32 / (int32_t)b32));
    }
}

/* crc32b/h/w/x and crc32cb/h/w/x. The checksum is CRC-32 with no pre- or
 * post-inversion, continuing from the value in the first operand and absorbing
 * `bytes` bytes of the second from its low end. `poly` is the reflected
 * polynomial: 0xEDB88320 for the IEEE form, 0x82F63B78 for Castagnoli. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_crc32(ew_u64 crc, ew_u64 data, unsigned bytes, ew_u32 poly)
{
    ew_u32 c = (ew_u32)crc;
    unsigned i, b;
    for (i = 0; i < bytes; i++) {
        c ^= (ew_u32)(data & 0xFFu);
        for (b = 0; b < 8; b++) {
            c = (c & 1u) ? ((c >> 1) ^ poly) : (c >> 1);
        }
        data >>= 8;
    }
    return EW_M32(c);
}

static inline int ew_cond(Cpu *cpu, unsigned cond);

/* csel/csinc/csinv/csneg: kind 1..4 selects the "else" operand form. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_condsel(Cpu *cpu, unsigned cond, ew_u64 a, ew_u64 b,
                                unsigned kind, int is64)
{
    ew_u64 r;
    if (ew_cond(cpu, cond)) {
        r = a;
    } else {
        switch (kind) {
        case 1:  r = b; break;
        case 2:  r = b + 1; break;
        case 3:  r = ~b; break;
        default: r = (ew_u64)(0 - b); break;
        }
    }
    return is64 ? r : EW_M32(r);
}

static inline int ew_cond(Cpu *cpu, unsigned cond)
{
    ew_u32 n = (cpu->nzcv >> 3) & 1, z = (cpu->nzcv >> 2) & 1;
    ew_u32 c = (cpu->nzcv >> 1) & 1, v = cpu->nzcv & 1;
    switch (cond) {
    case 0:  return (int)z;
    case 1:  return !z;
    case 2:  return (int)c;
    case 3:  return !c;
    case 4:  return (int)n;
    case 5:  return !n;
    case 6:  return (int)v;
    case 7:  return !v;
    case 8:  return c && !z;
    case 9:  return !c || z;
    case 10: return n == v;
    case 11: return n != v;
    case 12: return !z && (n == v);
    case 13: return z || (n != v);
    default: return 1;
    }
}

/* Scalar floating point. Values move as bit patterns in both directions, so
 * signed zeros, denormals and NaN payloads survive unchanged. */
static inline float ew_sget(Cpu *cpu, unsigned i)
{
    ew_u32 bits = (ew_u32)(cpu->v[i & 31u][0] & 0xFFFFFFFFu);
    float f;
    memcpy(&f, &bits, sizeof f);
    return f;
}

static inline void ew_sset(Cpu *cpu, unsigned i, float f)
{
    ew_u32 bits;
    memcpy(&bits, &f, sizeof bits);
    ew_vset(cpu, i, 4, bits);
}

static inline double ew_dget(Cpu *cpu, unsigned i)
{
    ew_u64 bits = cpu->v[i & 31u][0];
    double d;
    memcpy(&d, &bits, sizeof d);
    return d;
}

static inline void ew_dset(Cpu *cpu, unsigned i, double d)
{
    ew_u64 bits;
    memcpy(&bits, &d, sizeof bits);
    ew_vset(cpu, i, 8, bits);
}

/* fmax and fmin with the architectural NaN rule: one NaN loses to the number,
 * and the two signed zeros keep a fixed sign instead of comparing equal. */
static inline float ew_fmax32(float a, float b)
{
    if (a != a) return b;
    if (b != b) return a;
    if (a == b) return (a == 0.0f && signbit(a) != signbit(b)) ? 0.0f : a;
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

static inline float ew_fmin32(float a, float b)
{
    if (a != a) return b;
    if (b != b) return a;
    if (a == b) return (a == 0.0f && signbit(a) != signbit(b)) ? -0.0f : a;
    return a < b ? a : b;
}

static inline double ew_fmax64(double a, double b)
{
    if (a != a) return b;
    if (b != b) return a;
    if (a == b) return (a == 0.0 && signbit(a) != signbit(b)) ? 0.0 : a;
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

static inline double ew_fmin64(double a, double b)
{
    if (a != a) return b;
    if (b != b) return a;
    if (a == b) return (a == 0.0 && signbit(a) != signbit(b)) ? -0.0 : a;
    return a < b ? a : b;
}

/* FP compare writes NZCV exactly as the architecture does: unordered sets C
 * and V, equal sets Z and C, less than sets N and greater sets C. */
static inline void ew_fp_flags(Cpu *cpu, int unordered, int eq, int lt, int gt)
{
    if (unordered) cpu->nzcv = 0x3u;
    else if (eq)    cpu->nzcv = 0x6u;
    else if (lt)    cpu->nzcv = 0x8u;
    else if (gt)    cpu->nzcv = 0x2u;
}

/* mode: 0 nearest even, 1 nearest away, 2 toward +inf, 3 toward -inf, 4 zero */
static inline double ew_round_mode(double v, unsigned mode)
{
    switch (mode) {
    case 0:  return rint(v);
    case 1:  return round(v);
    case 2:  return ceil(v);
    case 3:  return floor(v);
    default: return trunc(v);
    }
}

/* Float to integer with architectural saturation: NaN becomes zero and an out
 * of range value clamps, because a C cast out of range is undefined. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_fp_to_int(double v, unsigned mode, int is64, int uns)
{
    double r;
    if (v != v) return 0;
    r = ew_round_mode(v, mode);
    if (uns) {
        double limit = is64 ? 18446744073709551616.0 : 4294967296.0;
        if (r <= 0.0) return 0;
        if (r >= limit) return is64 ? ~(ew_u64)0 : (ew_u64)0xFFFFFFFFu;
        return (ew_u64)r;
    }
    if (is64) {
        if (r >= 9223372036854775808.0) return (ew_u64)0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull;
        if (r <= -9223372036854775808.0) return (ew_u64)0x8000000000000000ull;
        return (ew_u64)(ew_i64)r;
    }
    if (r >= 2147483648.0) return (ew_u64)0x7FFFFFFFu;
    if (r <= -2147483648.0) return (ew_u64)0x80000000u;
    return (ew_u64)(ew_u32)(ew_i32)r;
}

/* Fixed-point integer to floating point: the integer scaled by 2^-fbits. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_int_to_fp_fixed(ew_u64 raw, int src_is64, int uns, int dest_is64, int fbits)
{
    double v;
    if (src_is64) {
        v = uns ? (double)raw : (double)(ew_i64)raw;
    } else {
        v = uns ? (double)(ew_u32)raw : (double)(ew_i32)(ew_u32)raw;
    }
    v = ldexp(v, -fbits);
    if (dest_is64) {
        ew_u64 bits;
        memcpy(&bits, &v, sizeof bits);
        return bits;
    } else {
        float f = (float)v;
        ew_u32 bits;
        memcpy(&bits, &f, sizeof bits);
        return bits;
    }
}

/* Integer to floating point, returning the destination bit pattern. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_int_to_fp(ew_u64 raw, int src_is64, int uns, int dest_is64)
{
    double v;
    if (src_is64) {
        v = uns ? (double)raw : (double)(ew_i64)raw;
    } else {
        v = uns ? (double)(ew_u32)raw : (double)(ew_i32)(ew_u32)raw;
    }
    if (dest_is64) {
        ew_u64 bits;
        memcpy(&bits, &v, sizeof bits);
        return bits;
    } else {
        float f = (float)v;
        ew_u32 bits;
        memcpy(&bits, &f, sizeof bits);
        return bits;
    }
}

/* High half of a 64x64 multiply, built from 32-bit pieces so the emitted C
 * needs no 128-bit integer type (MSVC has none). */
static inline ew_u64 ew_umulh(ew_u64 a, ew_u64 b)
{
    ew_u64 al = a & 0xFFFFFFFFu, ah = a >> 32, bl = b & 0xFFFFFFFFu, bh = b >> 32;
    ew_u64 ll = al * bl, lh = al * bh, hl = ah * bl, hh = ah * bh;
    ew_u64 mid = (ll >> 32) + (lh & 0xFFFFFFFFu) + (hl & 0xFFFFFFFFu);
    return hh + (lh >> 32) + (hl >> 32) + (mid >> 32);
}

static inline ew_u64 ew_smulh(ew_u64 a, ew_u64 b)
{
    ew_u64 h = ew_umulh(a, b);
    if ((ew_i64)a < 0) h -= b;
    if ((ew_i64)b < 0) h -= a;
    return h;
}

/* The fmov immediate is three exponent bits with a bias of three and four
 * fraction bits in sixteenths. */
static inline ew_u64 ew_fmov_imm(unsigned imm8, int is64)
{
    int sign = (int)((imm8 >> 7) & 1u);
    int field = (int)((((imm8 >> 6) ^ 1u) << 2) | ((imm8 >> 4) & 3u));
    double frac = (double)(imm8 & 0xFu) / 16.0;
    double value = (1.0 + frac) * ldexp(1.0, field - 3);
    if (sign) value = -value;
    if (is64) {
        ew_u64 bits;
        memcpy(&bits, &value, sizeof bits);
        return bits;
    } else {
        float f = (float)value;
        ew_u32 bits;
        memcpy(&bits, &f, sizeof bits);
        return bits;
    }
}

"#,
    include_str!("ew_simd.h"),
    "
#endif /* EW_AARCH64_H */
"
);

fn fp_binop_name(op: FpBinop) -> &'static str {
    match op {
        FpBinop::Mul => "fmul",
        FpBinop::Div => "fdiv",
        FpBinop::Add => "fadd",
        FpBinop::Sub => "fsub",
        FpBinop::Max => "fmax",
        FpBinop::Min => "fmin",
        FpBinop::MaxNm => "fmaxnm",
        FpBinop::MinNm => "fminnm",
        FpBinop::NegMul => "fnmul",
    }
}

fn fp_unop_name(op: FpUnop) -> &'static str {
    match op {
        FpUnop::Neg => "fneg",
        FpUnop::Abs => "fabs",
        FpUnop::Sqrt => "fsqrt",
        FpUnop::RoundN => "frintn",
        FpUnop::RoundP => "frintp",
        FpUnop::RoundM => "frintm",
        FpUnop::RoundZ => "frintz",
        FpUnop::RoundA => "frinta",
        FpUnop::RoundX => "frintx",
        FpUnop::RoundI => "frinti",
        FpUnop::Cvt => "fcvt",
    }
}

fn fp_round_fp_name(round: FpRound, is64: bool) -> &'static str {
    let _ = is64;
    match round {
        FpRound::NearestEven => "fcvtns",
        FpRound::NearestAway => "fcvtas",
        FpRound::PlusInf => "fcvtps",
        FpRound::MinusInf => "fcvtms",
        FpRound::Zero => "fcvtzs",
    }
}

fn fp_round_name(round: FpRound, unsigned: bool, dest_is64: bool) -> &'static str {
    let _ = dest_is64;
    match (round, unsigned) {
        (FpRound::NearestEven, false) => "fcvtns",
        (FpRound::NearestEven, true) => "fcvtnu",
        (FpRound::NearestAway, false) => "fcvtas",
        (FpRound::NearestAway, true) => "fcvtau",
        (FpRound::PlusInf, false) => "fcvtps",
        (FpRound::PlusInf, true) => "fcvtpu",
        (FpRound::MinusInf, false) => "fcvtms",
        (FpRound::MinusInf, true) => "fcvtmu",
        (FpRound::Zero, false) => "fcvtzs",
        (FpRound::Zero, true) => "fcvtzu",
    }
}

fn reg_read(i: u8, sp_ok: bool) -> String {
    format!("EW_R(cpu, {i}, {})", if sp_ok { 1 } else { 0 })
}

fn reg_write(i: u8, sp_ok: bool, value: &str) -> String {
    format!("EW_W(cpu, {i}, {}, {value});", if sp_ok { 1 } else { 0 })
}

fn masked(is64: bool, expr: &str) -> String {
    if is64 {
        expr.to_string()
    } else {
        format!("EW_M32({expr})")
    }
}

/// Emit a byte-for-byte transfer between guest memory and a SIMD/FP register.
/// Sixteen-byte transfers move both halves explicitly, because the generated C
/// has no 128-bit integer type to lean on.
fn vector_transfer_line(reg: u8, addr: &str, bytes: u8, load: bool) -> String {
    if load {
        if bytes == 16 {
            format!(
                "      {{ ew_u64 lo_ = ew_load(cpu, {addr}, 8); ew_u64 hi_ = ew_load(cpu, ({addr}) + 8, 8); ew_vset128(cpu, {reg}, lo_, hi_); }}\n"
            )
        } else {
            format!("      ew_vset(cpu, {reg}, {bytes}, ew_load(cpu, {addr}, {bytes}));\n")
        }
    } else if bytes == 16 {
        format!(
            "      {{ ew_u64 lo_ = cpu->v[{reg} & 31u][0]; ew_u64 hi_ = cpu->v[{reg} & 31u][1]; ew_store(cpu, {addr}, lo_, 8); ew_store(cpu, ({addr}) + 8, hi_, 8); }}\n"
        )
    } else {
        format!("      ew_store(cpu, {addr}, ew_vget(cpu, {reg}, {bytes}), {bytes});\n")
    }
}

fn emit_vector_transfer(
    out: &mut String,
    a: u64,
    rt: u8,
    bytes: u8,
    load: bool,
    ea: &str,
    writeback: Option<(u8, i64, String)>,
) {
    out.push_str(&format!(
        "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} v{rt}, [{ea}] ({bytes} bytes) */\n    {{ ew_u64 ea_ = {ea};\n",
        if load { "ldr" } else { "str" }
    ));
    out.push_str(&vector_transfer_line(rt, "ea_", bytes, load));
    match writeback {
        Some((rn, offset, base)) => out.push_str(&format!(
            "      EW_W(cpu, {rn}, 1, ({base}) + {}); }}\n",
            offset as i64
        )),
        None => out.push_str("    }\n"),
    }
}

fn emit_insn(
    out: &mut String,
    insn: &Insn,
    func: &LiftedFunction,
    table: Option<&crate::jump_table::JumpTable>,
) {
    let a = insn.addr;
    match insn.op {
        Op::Nop => out.push_str(&format!("    /* 0x{a:x}: nop */\n")),
        Op::B { target } => {
            // A branch inside the recovered block set continues in this
            // function; a branch out of it hands control to the dispatcher.
            let next = if func.contains(target) { "continue;" } else { "return 1;" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: b 0x{target:x} */\n    cpu->pc = 0x{target:x}ULL;\n    {next}\n"
            ));
        }
        Op::Bl { target } => {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: bl 0x{target:x} */\n    cpu->x[30] = 0x{:x}ULL;\n    cpu->pc = 0x{target:x}ULL;\n    return 1;\n",
                a + 4
            ));
        }
        Op::BCond { cond, target } => {
            let next = if func.contains(target) { "continue;" } else { "return 1;" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: b.{} 0x{target:x} */\n    if (ew_cond(cpu, {})) {{ cpu->pc = 0x{target:x}ULL; {next} }}\n",
                cond.c_suffix(),
                cond as u32
            ));
        }
        Op::CompareBranchZero { rt, target, nonzero, is64 } => {
            let v = masked(is64, &reg_read(rt, false));
            let cond = if nonzero { "!=" } else { "==" };
            let next = if func.contains(target) { "continue;" } else { "return 1;" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rt}, 0x{target:x} */\n    if (({v} {cond} 0ULL)) {{ cpu->pc = 0x{target:x}ULL; {next} }}\n",
                if nonzero { "cbnz" } else { "cbz" }
            ));
        }
        Op::TestBitBranch { rt, bit, target, nonzero } => {
            let v = reg_read(rt, false);
            // tbnz branches when the bit is set, tbz when it is clear.
            let cond = if nonzero { "!=" } else { "==" };
            let next = if func.contains(target) { "continue;" } else { "return 1;" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rt}, #{bit}, 0x{target:x} */\n    if (((({v} >> {bit}) & 1ULL) {cond} 0ULL)) {{ cpu->pc = 0x{target:x}ULL; {next} }}\n",
                if nonzero { "tbnz" } else { "tbz" }
            ));
        }
        Op::Br { rn } => {
            match table {
                // A resolved table turns an indirect branch into a dispatch on
                // the branch register, so the next block runs in this function.
                Some(t) => {
                    out.push_str(&format!(
                        "    /* 0x{a:x}: br x{rn} via jump table 0x{:x}, {} entries */\n    switch ({}) {{\n",
                        t.table,
                        t.entries,
                        reg_read(rn, false)
                    ));
                    for target in &t.targets {
                        let next = if func.contains(*target) { "continue;" } else { "return 1;" };
                        out.push_str(&format!(
                            "    case 0x{target:x}ULL: cpu->pc = 0x{target:x}ULL; {next}\n"
                        ));
                    }
                    out.push_str("    default: return 1; /* table target not recovered */\n    }\n");
                }
                None => out.push_str(&format!(
                    "    /* 0x{a:x}: br x{rn} (unresolved) */\n    cpu->pc = {};\n    return 1;\n",
                    reg_read(rn, false)
                )),
            }
        }
        Op::Blr { rn } => out.push_str(&format!(
            "    /* 0x{a:x}: blr x{rn} */\n    cpu->x[30] = 0x{:x}ULL;\n    cpu->pc = {};\n    return 1;\n",
            a + 4,
            reg_read(rn, false)
        )),
        Op::Ret { rn } => out.push_str(&format!(
            "    /* 0x{a:x}: ret x{rn} */\n    cpu->pc = {};\n    return 1;\n",
            reg_read(rn, false)
        )),
        Op::Adr { rd, target } => out.push_str(&format!(
            "    /* 0x{a:x}: adr x{rd}, 0x{target:x} */\n    {}\n",
            reg_write(rd, false, &format!("0x{target:x}ULL"))
        )),
        Op::MoveWide { rd, imm, shift, kind, is64 } => {
            let cur = masked(is64, &reg_read(rd, false));
            let expr = match kind {
                0 => format!("0x{:x}ULL", (imm as u64) << shift),
                1 => format!("~0x{:x}ULL", (imm as u64) << shift),
                _ => format!("(({cur} & ~(0xFFFFULL << {shift})) | (0x{:x}ULL << {shift}))", imm),
            };
            let mnemonic = match kind {
                0 => "movz",
                1 => "movn",
                _ => "movk",
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {mnemonic} x{rd}, #0x{imm:x}, lsl #{shift} */\n    {}\n",
                reg_write(rd, false, &masked(is64, &expr))
            ));
        }
        Op::AddSubImm { rd, rn, imm, sub, set_flags, is64 } => {
            // With S=0, rd/rn 31 means SP; with S=1 it means XZR.
            let sp_ok = !set_flags;
            let a_expr = reg_read(rn, sp_ok);
            let op_str = if sub { "-" } else { "+" };
            let r_expr = masked(is64, &format!("({a_expr} {op_str} 0x{imm:x}ULL)"));
            let mnemonic = match (sub, set_flags) {
                (false, false) => "add",
                (true, false) => "sub",
                (false, true) => "adds",
                (true, true) => "subs",
            };
            let flag_fn = if sub { "ew_flags_sub" } else { "ew_flags_add" };
            out.push_str(&format!("    /* 0x{a:x}: {mnemonic} x{rd}, x{rn}, #0x{imm:x} */\n"));
            if set_flags {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "    {{ ew_u64 a_ = {a_expr}; ew_u64 r_ = {r_expr}; {flag_fn}(cpu, a_, 0x{imm:x}ULL, r_, {}); {}\n",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 },
                    reg_write(rd, sp_ok, "r_")
                ));
                out.pop();
                out.push_str("}\n");
            } else {
                out.push_str(&format!("    {{ ew_u64 r_ = {r_expr}; {} }}\n", reg_write(rd, sp_ok, "r_")));
            }
        }
        Op::AddSubReg { rd, rn, rm, shift, amount, sub, set_flags, is64 } => {
            let a_expr = reg_read(rn, false);
            let b_expr = format!(
                "ew_shift({}, {}, {}, {})",
                reg_read(rm, false),
                shift as u32,
                amount,
                if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
            );
            let op_str = if sub { "-" } else { "+" };
            let r_expr = masked(is64, &format!("(a_ {op_str} b_)"));
            let flag_fn = if sub { "ew_flags_sub" } else { "ew_flags_add" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rd}, x{rn}, x{rm}, {} #{amount} */\n    {{ ew_u64 a_ = {a_expr}; ew_u64 b_ = {b_expr}; ew_u64 r_ = {r_expr};",
                if sub { "sub" } else { "add" },
                shift_name(shift)
            ));
            if set_flags {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    " {flag_fn}(cpu, a_, b_, r_, {});",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                ));
            }
            out.push_str(&format!(" {} }}\n", reg_write(rd, false, "r_")));
        }
        Op::AddSubExt { rd, rn, rm, option, shift, sub, set_flags, is64 } => {
            let a_expr = reg_read(rn, false);
            let b_expr = format!(
                "(ew_extend({}, {}) << {shift})",
                reg_read(rm, false),
                option as u32
            );
            let op_str = if sub { "-" } else { "+" };
            let r_expr = masked(is64, &format!("(a_ {op_str} b_)"));
            let flag_fn = if sub { "ew_flags_sub" } else { "ew_flags_add" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {mnemonic} x{rd}, x{rn}, x{rm}, extend {opt}, lsl #{shift} */\n    {{ ew_u64 a_ = {a_expr}; ew_u64 b_ = {b_expr}; ew_u64 r_ = {r_expr};",
                mnemonic = if sub { "sub" } else { "add" },
                opt = option as u32
            ));
            if set_flags {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    " {flag_fn}(cpu, a_, b_, r_, {});",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                ));
            }
            out.push_str(&format!(" {} }}\n", reg_write(rd, false, "r_")));
        }
        Op::Bitfield { rd, rn, immr, imms, opc, is64 } => {
            let mnemonic = match opc {
                0 => "sbfm",
                1 => "bfm",
                _ => "ubfm",
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {mnemonic} x{rd}, x{rn}, #immr {immr}, #imms {imms} */\n    {{ ew_u64 src_ = {}; ew_u64 dst_ = {}; {} }}\n",
                reg_read(rn, false),
                reg_read(rd, false),
                reg_write(
                    rd,
                    false,
                    &format!(
                        "ew_bitfield(src_, dst_, {immr}, {imms}, {opc}, {})",
                        if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                    )
                )
            ));
        }
        Op::LogicalImm { rd, rn, imm, op, set_flags, is64 } => {
            let a_expr = reg_read(rn, false);
            let sym = match op {
                LogicalOp::And => "&",
                LogicalOp::Orr => "|",
                LogicalOp::Eor => "^",
                LogicalOp::Ands => "&",
            };
            let r_expr = masked(is64, &format!("(a_ {sym} 0x{imm:x}ULL)"));
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rd}, x{rn}, #0x{imm:x} */\n    {{ ew_u64 a_ = {a_expr}; ew_u64 r_ = {r_expr};",
                logical_name(op)
            ));
            if set_flags || op == LogicalOp::Ands {
                out.push_str(&format!(" ew_flags_nz(cpu, r_, {});", if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }));
            }
            out.push_str(&format!(" {} }}\n", reg_write(rd, false, "r_")));
        }
        Op::LogicalReg { rd, rn, rm, shift, amount, op, set_flags, is64, invert } => {
            let a_expr = reg_read(rn, false);
            let b_expr = format!(
                "ew_shift({}, {}, {}, {})",
                reg_read(rm, false),
                shift as u32,
                amount,
                if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
            );
            let b_expr = if invert { masked(is64, &format!("(~{b_expr})")) } else { b_expr };
            let sym = match op {
                LogicalOp::And => "&",
                LogicalOp::Orr => "|",
                LogicalOp::Eor => "^",
                LogicalOp::Ands => "&",
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rd}, x{rn}, x{rm} */\n    {{ ew_u64 a_ = {a_expr}; ew_u64 b_ = {b_expr}; ew_u64 r_ = {};",
                logical_name(op),
                masked(is64, &format!("(a_ {sym} b_)"))
            ));
            if set_flags || op == LogicalOp::Ands {
                out.push_str(&format!(" ew_flags_nz(cpu, r_, {});", if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }));
            }
            out.push_str(&format!(" {} }}\n", reg_write(rd, false, "r_")));
        }
        Op::MulLong { rd, rn, rm, ra, sub, unsigned } => {
            let product = if unsigned {
                format!(
                    "((ew_u64)EW_M32({}) * (ew_u64)EW_M32({}))",
                    reg_read(rn, false),
                    reg_read(rm, false)
                )
            } else {
                format!(
                    "((ew_u64)((ew_i64)(int32_t)EW_M32({}) * (ew_i64)(int32_t)EW_M32({})))",
                    reg_read(rn, false),
                    reg_read(rm, false)
                )
            };
            let op_str = if sub { "-" } else { "+" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rd}, w{rn}, w{rm}, x{ra} */\n    {{ ew_u64 acc_ = {}; ew_u64 p_ = {product}; {} }}\n",
                match (unsigned, sub) {
                    (false, false) => "smaddl",
                    (false, true) => "smsubl",
                    (true, false) => "umaddl",
                    (true, true) => "umsubl",
                },
                reg_read(ra, false),
                reg_write(rd, false, &format!("(acc_ {op_str} p_)"))
            ));
        }
        Op::DataProc2 { rd, rn, rm, op, is64 } => {
            let a_expr = reg_read(rn, false);
            let b_expr = reg_read(rm, false);
            let expr = match op {
                DataOp2::Udiv => format!("ew_udiv({a_expr}, {b_expr})"),
                DataOp2::Sdiv => format!(
                    "ew_sdiv({a_expr}, {b_expr}, {})",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                ),
                DataOp2::Lslv => format!(
                    "ew_shift({a_expr}, 0, (unsigned){b_expr}, {})",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                ),
                DataOp2::Lsrv => format!(
                    "ew_shift({a_expr}, 1, (unsigned){b_expr}, {})",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                ),
                DataOp2::Asrv => format!(
                    "ew_shift({a_expr}, 2, (unsigned){b_expr}, {})",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                ),
                DataOp2::Rorv => format!(
                    "ew_shift({a_expr}, 3, (unsigned){b_expr}, {})",
                    if is64 { 1 } else { 0 }
                ),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rd}, x{rn}, x{rm} */\n    {{ ew_u64 r_ = {}; {} }}\n",
                op.c_name(),
                masked(is64, &expr),
                reg_write(rd, false, "r_")
            ));
        }
        Op::MultiplyAdd { rd, rn, rm, ra, sub, is64 } => {
            let op_str = if sub { "-" } else { "+" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rd}, x{rn}, x{rm}, x{ra} */\n    {{ ew_u64 prod_ = {} * {}; ew_u64 acc_ = {}; ew_u64 r_ = {}; {} }}\n",
                if sub { "msub" } else { "madd" },
                reg_read(rn, false),
                reg_read(rm, false),
                reg_read(ra, false),
                masked(is64, &format!("(acc_ {op_str} prod_)")),
                reg_write(rd, false, "r_")
            ));
        }
        Op::CondSelect { rd, rn, rm, cond, kind, is64 } => {
            let alt = match kind {
                0 => "1".to_string(),
                1 => "2".to_string(),
                2 => "3".to_string(),
                _ => "4".to_string(),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: cs{} ({alt}) x{rd}, x{rn}, x{rm}, {} */\n",
                cond.c_suffix(),
                cond as u32
            ));
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    {{ ew_u64 a_ = {}; ew_u64 b_ = {}; ew_u64 r_ = ew_condsel(cpu, {}, a_, b_, {alt}, {}); {} }}\n",
                reg_read(rn, false),
                reg_read(rm, false),
                cond as u32,
                if is64 { 1 } else { 0 },
                reg_write(rd, false, "r_")
            ));
        }
        Op::LoadStore { rt, rn, offset, bytes, load, signed, mode, is64 } => {
            let base = reg_read(rn, true);
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rt}, [x{rn}, #{offset}] ({} bytes{}) */\n",
                match (load, signed) {
                    (false, _) => "str",
                    (true, false) => "ldr",
                    (true, true) => "ldrs",
                },
                bytes,
                if signed { ", sign extended" } else { "" }
            ));
            // Post-indexed forms address `base` and write back afterwards;
            // offset/pre-indexed forms address `base + offset`.
            let ea = match mode {
                MemMode::PostIndex => base.clone(),
                _ => format!("({base} + {})", offset as i64),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!("    {{ ew_u64 ea_ = {ea};\n"));
            if load {
                let value = if signed {
                    masked(is64, &format!("ew_sext(v_, {}, {})", bytes * 8 - 1, is64 as u32))
                } else {
                    masked(is64, "v_")
                };
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "      ew_u64 v_ = ew_load(cpu, ea_, {bytes}); {} }}\n",
                    reg_write(rt, false, &value)
                ));
            } else {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "      ew_store(cpu, ea_, {}, {bytes}); }}\n",
                    masked(is64, &reg_read(rt, false))
                ));
            }
            // Index writeback for pre/post indexed forms.
            match mode {
                MemMode::PreIndex | MemMode::PostIndex => {
                    out.push_str(&format!(
                        "    {}\n",
                        reg_write(rn, true, &format!("({base} + {offset})"))
                    ));
                }
                MemMode::Offset => {}
            }
        }
        Op::LoadStorePair { rt, rt2, rn, offset, load, mode, is64 } => {
            let base = reg_read(rn, true);
            let width = if is64 { 8 } else { 4 };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rt}, x{rt2}, [x{rn}, #{offset}] */\n",
                if load { "ldp" } else { "stp" }
            ));
            let ea = match mode {
                MemMode::PostIndex => base.clone(),
                _ => format!("({base} + {offset})"),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!("    {{ ew_u64 ea_ = {ea};\n"));
            if load {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "      ew_u64 v1_ = ew_load(cpu, ea_, {width});\n      ew_u64 v2_ = ew_load(cpu, ea_ + {width}, {width});\n      {} {}\n",
                    reg_write(rt, false, &masked(is64, "v1_")),
                    reg_write(rt2, false, &masked(is64, "v2_"))
                ));
            } else {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "      ew_store(cpu, ea_, {}, {width});\n      ew_store(cpu, ea_ + {width}, {}, {width});\n",
                    masked(is64, &reg_read(rt, false)),
                    masked(is64, &reg_read(rt2, false))
                ));
            }
            out.push_str("    }\n");
            if mode != MemMode::Offset {
                out.push_str(&format!("    {}\n", reg_write(rn, true, &format!("({base} + {offset})"))));
            }
        }
        Op::LoadPairSigned { rt, rt2, rn, offset, mode } => {
            let base = reg_read(rn, true);
            let ea = match mode {
                MemMode::PostIndex => base.clone(),
                _ => format!("({base} + {offset})"),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: ldpsw x{rt}, x{rt2}, [x{rn}, #{offset}] */
    {{ ew_u64 ea_ = {ea};
      ew_u64 v1_ = (ew_u64)(ew_i64)(ew_i32)(ew_u32)ew_load(cpu, ea_, 4);
      ew_u64 v2_ = (ew_u64)(ew_i64)(ew_i32)(ew_u32)ew_load(cpu, ea_ + 4, 4);
      {} {}
    }}
",
                reg_write(rt, false, "v1_"),
                reg_write(rt2, false, "v2_")
            ));
            if mode != MemMode::Offset {
                out.push_str(&format!("    {}
", reg_write(rn, true, &format!("({base} + {offset})"))));
            }
        }
        Op::LoadStoreReg { rt, rn, rm, option, shift, bytes, load, signed, is64 } => {
            let base = reg_read(rn, true);
            let ea = format!(
                "({base} + (ew_extend({}, {}) << {shift}))",
                reg_read(rm, false),
                option as u32
            );
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {mnemonic} x{rt}, [x{rn}, x{rm}, extend {opt}, lsl #{shift}] */\n    {{ ew_u64 ea_ = {ea};\n",
                mnemonic = match (load, signed) {
                    (false, _) => "str",
                    (true, false) => "ldr",
                    (true, true) => "ldrs",
                },
                opt = option as u32
            ));
            if load {
                let value = if signed {
                    masked(is64, &format!("ew_sext(v_, {}, {})", bytes * 8 - 1, is64 as u32))
                } else {
                    masked(is64, "v_")
                };
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "      ew_u64 v_ = ew_load(cpu, ea_, {bytes}); {} }}\n",
                    reg_write(rt, false, &value)
                ));
            } else {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "      ew_store(cpu, ea_, {}, {bytes}); }}\n",
                    masked(is64, &reg_read(rt, false))
                ));
            }
        }
        Op::BitScan { rd, rn, op, is64 } => {
            let src = reg_read(rn, false);
            let expr = match op {
                crate::aarch64::BitScan::Rbit => format!("ew_rbit({src}, {})", is64 as u32),
                crate::aarch64::BitScan::Rev => {
                    if is64 {
                        format!("ew_rev_within({src}, 8, 1)")
                    } else {
                        format!("ew_rev_within({src}, 4, 0)")
                    }
                }
                crate::aarch64::BitScan::Rev32 => {
                    format!("ew_rev_within({src}, 4, {})", is64 as u32)
                }
                crate::aarch64::BitScan::Rev16 => {
                    format!("ew_rev_within({src}, 2, {})", is64 as u32)
                }
                crate::aarch64::BitScan::Clz => format!("ew_clz({src}, {})", is64 as u32),
                crate::aarch64::BitScan::Cls => format!("ew_cls({src}, {})", is64 as u32),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rd}, x{rn} */\n    {{ ew_u64 r_ = {}; {} }}\n",
                op.c_name(),
                masked(is64, &expr),
                reg_write(rd, false, "r_")
            ));
        }
        Op::Crc32 { rd, rn, rm, bytes, castagnoli } => {
            let width = match bytes {
                1 => "b",
                2 => "h",
                4 => "w",
                _ => "x",
            };
            let poly = if castagnoli { "0x82F63B78u" } else { "0xEDB88320u" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: crc32{width}{} w{rd}, w{rn}, w{rm} */\n    {{ ew_u64 r_ = ew_crc32({}, {}, {bytes}, {poly}); {} }}\n",
                if castagnoli { "c" } else { "" },
                reg_read(rn, false),
                reg_read(rm, bytes == 8),
                reg_write(rd, false, "r_")
            ));
        }
        Op::CondCompare { rn, rm, imm5, immediate, cond, nzcv, sub, is64 } => {
            let a_expr = reg_read(rn, false);
            let b = if immediate {
                format!("{}ULL", imm5)
            } else {
                reg_read(rm, false)
            };
            let flags = if sub { "ew_flags_sub" } else { "ew_flags_add" };
            let arith = if sub { "-" } else { "+" };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {name} x{rn}, {rhs}, #{nzcv}, {cond} */\n    {{ ew_u64 a_ = {a_expr}; ew_u64 b_ = {b}; ew_u64 r_ = EW_M({m64}, a_ {arith} b_); if (ew_cond(cpu, {cond_bit})) {{ {flags}(cpu, a_, b_, r_, {m64}); }} else {{ cpu->nzcv = {nzcv}u; }} }}\n",
                name = if sub { "ccmp" } else { "ccmn" },
                rhs = if immediate { format!("#{imm5}") } else { format!("x{rm}") },
                cond = cond.c_suffix(),
                cond_bit = cond as u32,
                m64 = if is64 { 1 } else { 0 },
                nzcv = nzcv,
            ));
        }
        Op::AtomicRmw { rs, rt, rn, op, order, bytes } => {
            let width = bytes as u32 * 8;
            // The operand at the access width; the old value is loaded at that
            // width already, and it is what the destination register gets.
            let mask = if bytes == 8 { "~0ULL".to_string() } else { format!("0x{:x}ULL", (1u64 << width) - 1) };
            let op_expr = match op {
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::Add => "old_ + v_".to_string(),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::Clr => "old_ & ~v_".to_string(),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::Eor => "old_ ^ v_".to_string(),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::Set => "old_ | v_".to_string(),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::SMax => format!(
                    "(ew_sext(old_, {t}, 1) > ew_sext(v_, {t}, 1)) ? old_ : v_",
                    t = width - 1
                ),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::SMin => format!(
                    "(ew_sext(old_, {t}, 1) < ew_sext(v_, {t}, 1)) ? old_ : v_",
                    t = width - 1
                ),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::UMax => "(old_ > v_) ? old_ : v_".to_string(),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::UMin => "(old_ < v_) ? old_ : v_".to_string(),
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::Swap => "v_".to_string(),
            };
            let mnemonic = match op {
                crate::aarch64::AtomicOp::Swap => "swp".to_string(),
                other => format!("ld{}", other.c_name()),
            };
            let ordering = match (order.acquire, order.release) {
                (true, true) => "al",
                (true, false) => "a",
                (false, true) => "l",
                (false, false) => "",
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {mnemonic}{ordering} x{rs}, x{rt}, [x{rn}] ({bytes} bytes) */\n    {{ ew_u64 ea_ = {base}; ew_u64 old_ = ew_load(cpu, ea_, {bytes}); ew_u64 v_ = ({operand}) & {mask}; ew_u64 new_ = {op_expr}; ew_store(cpu, ea_, new_, {bytes}); {dest} }}\n",
                base = reg_read(rn, true),
                operand = reg_read(rs, false),
                dest = reg_write(rt, false, "old_"),
            ));
        }
        Op::VectorLoadStore { rt, rn, offset, bytes, load, mode } => {
            let base = reg_read(rn, true);
            let ea = match mode {
                MemMode::PostIndex => base.clone(),
                _ => format!("({base} + {})", offset as i64),
            };
            let writeback = if mode == MemMode::Offset {
                None
            } else {
                Some((rn, offset, base.clone()))
            };
            emit_vector_transfer(out, a, rt, bytes, load, &ea, writeback);
        }
        Op::VectorLoadStoreReg { rt, rn, rm, option, shift, bytes, load } => {
            let ea = format!(
                "({} + (ew_extend({}, {}) << {shift}))",
                reg_read(rn, true),
                reg_read(rm, false),
                option as u32
            );
            emit_vector_transfer(out, a, rt, bytes, load, &ea, None);
        }
        Op::VectorLoadStorePair { rt, rt2, rn, offset, bytes, load, mode } => {
            let base = reg_read(rn, true);
            let ea = match mode {
                MemMode::PostIndex => base.clone(),
                _ => format!("({base} + {})", offset as i64),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    /* 0x{a:x}: {} x{rt}, x{rt2}, [x{rn}] ({} bytes each) */\n    {{ ew_u64 ea_ = {ea};\n",
