`crates/ew-runtime/src/hle.rs`:

```rs
//! HLE (high-level emulation) registry for Nintendo SDK services.
//!
//! A service is registered as either implemented or unimplemented. Unimplemented
//! services fail loudly and carry the reason they are blocked, so the runtime can
//! never appear to boot further than it actually has.
//!
//! The service list below is drawn from the symbol names present in the retail
//! `app`/`nnSdk` rodata (e.g. `nn::os::AllocateMemoryPages`,
//! `nn::mem::StandardAllocator::Finalize`), not from guesswork.

use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum HleResult {
    /// A host implementation exists and is exercised by tests.
    Implemented(String),
    /// No implementation yet; the guest call fails explicitly.
    Unimplemented(String),
}

impl HleResult {
    pub fn is_implemented(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, HleResult::Implemented(_))
    }

    pub fn reason(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            HleResult::Implemented(r) | HleResult::Unimplemented(r) => r,
        }
    }
}

/// Registry of guest-visible services.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct HleRegistry {
    entries: BTreeMap<String, HleResult>,
}

impl HleRegistry {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        HleRegistry::default()
    }

    /// The service set the runtime knows about.
    ///
    /// Implemented entries mirror the handlers `ew-boot` actually registers, so
    /// this list cannot claim less than the runtime delivers. Anything the
    /// single-threaded host cannot provide stays blocked with the reason.
    pub fn with_defaults() -> Self {
        let mut r = HleRegistry::new();
        for (name, claim) in [
            (
                "nn::os::AllocateMemoryPages",
                "pages come from the arena above the guest stack, 4 KiB aligned and bounded",
            ),
            (
                "nn::os::FreeMemoryPages",
                "the arena is a bump allocator, so a freed page is not handed out again",
            ),
            (
                "nn::os::SetMemoryHeapSize",
                "the heap is fixed by the dispatcher layout, and the call succeeds without resizing it",
            ),
            (
                "nn::os::Mutex",
                "single guest thread: an uncontended lock succeeds, recursion is counted and a self-deadlock is reported",
            ),
            (
                "nn::os::Event",
                "single guest thread: signalling is exact, and waiting on a clear event is reported instead of hanging",
            ),
            (
                "nn::os::ThreadLocalStorage",
                "one slot table belonging to the only guest thread",
            ),
        ] {
            r.register(name, HleResult::Implemented(claim.to_string()));
        }
        for (name, reason) in [
            (
                "nn::os::CreateThread",
                "the host runs one guest thread, so starting another one needs a scheduler",
            ),
            ("nn::mem::StandardAllocator", "allocator semantics must match nnSdk exactly"),
            ("nn::nvn::Device", "NVN2 graphics device is not implemented"),
            ("nn::nvn::MemoryPool", "NVN2 memory pools are not implemented"),
            ("nn::nvn::Window", "NVN2 window/swapchain is not implemented"),
            ("nn::vi::Display", "display service is not implemented"),
            ("nn::audio::AudioOut", "audio output is not implemented"),
            ("nn::hid::AppletResource", "input service is not implemented"),
            ("nn::fs::FileSystem", "romfs/save filesystem service is not implemented"),
        ] {
            r.register(name, HleResult::Unimplemented(reason.to_string()));
        }
        r
    }

    pub fn register(&mut self, name: &str, status: HleResult) {
        self.entries.insert(name.to_string(), status);
    }

    pub fn status(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&HleResult> {
        self.entries.get(name)
    }

    pub fn statuses(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (String, HleResult)> + '_ {
        self.entries.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
    }

    pub fn implemented_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.values().filter(|v| v.is_implemented()).count()
    }

    pub fn unimplemented_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.values().filter(|v| !v.is_implemented()).count()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn defaults_separate_what_runs_from_what_does_not() {
        let r = HleRegistry::with_defaults();
        assert!(r.implemented_count() >= 5, "the single-threaded os services run");
        assert!(r.unimplemented_count() >= 9);
        let nvn = r.status("nn::nvn::Device").unwrap();
        assert!(!nvn.is_implemented());
        assert!(nvn.reason().contains("NVN2"));
        let pages = r.status("nn::os::AllocateMemoryPages").unwrap();
        assert!(pages.is_implemented());
        assert!(pages.reason().contains("arena"));
        let create = r.status("nn::os::CreateThread").unwrap();
        assert!(!create.is_implemented(), "a second thread still needs a scheduler");
    }

    #[test]
    fn registration_is_replaceable() {
        let mut r = HleRegistry::new();
        r.register("test", HleResult::Unimplemented("no".into()));
        assert_eq!(r.unimplemented_count(), 1);
        r.register("test", HleResult::Implemented("yes".into()));
        assert_eq!(r.implemented_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(r.status("test").unwrap().reason(), "yes");
    }
}

`crates/ew-runtime/src/image.rs`:

```rs
//! Guest memory bus with explicit region bounds.
//!
//! Nintendo Switch 2 modules are loaded at fixed addresses; a translation that
//! silently reads outside a mapped region is a bug that corrupts emulation
//! state. Every access is range-checked and reported.

use anyhow::{bail, Result};
use serde::Serialize;

/// One loadable module's memory footprint.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ModuleLayout {
    /// ExeFS file name, e.g. `main`, `sdk`.
    pub name: String,
    /// Internal module name, e.g. `app`, `nnSdk`.
    pub module_name: String,
    pub text: u64,
    pub rodata: u64,
    pub data: u64,
    pub bss: u64,
    /// Whether the module's code can already be lifted and dispatched.
    pub liftable: bool,
}

impl ModuleLayout {
    pub fn total(&self) -> u64 {
        self.text + self.rodata + self.data + self.bss
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Perm {
    Read,
    ReadWrite,
    /// `.text` is executable and read-only.
    ReadExecute,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Region {
    name: String,
    base: u64,
    data: Vec<u8>,
    perm: Perm,
}

/// The guest physical address space.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct GuestMemory {
    regions: Vec<Region>,
}

impl GuestMemory {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        GuestMemory::default()
    }

    /// Map a zero-filled region.
    pub fn map(&mut self, name: &str, base: u64, size: u64, perm: Perm) -> Result<()> {
        if size == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let size = usize::try_from(size).map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("region too large"))?;
        let end = base.saturating_add(size as u64);
        for r in &self.regions {
            let r_end = r.base + r.data.len() as u64;
            if base < r_end && r.base < end {
                bail!("region {name} overlaps {}", r.name);
            }
        }
        self.regions.push(Region { name: name.to_string(), base, data: vec![0u8; size], perm });
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Map a region and copy initial contents into it.
    pub fn map_with(&mut self, name: &str, base: u64, bytes: &[u8], perm: Perm) -> Result<()> {
        self.map(name, base, bytes.len() as u64, perm)?;
        let region = self
            .regions
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|r| r.name == name && r.base == base)
            .expect("just mapped");
        region.data[..bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn region_for(&self, addr: u64, len: u64) -> Result<&Region> {
        let end = addr
            .checked_add(len)
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("address overflow at 0x{addr:x}+{len}"))?;
        for r in &self.regions {
            let r_end = r.base + r.data.len() as u64;
            if addr >= r.base && end <= r_end {
                return Ok(r);
            }
        }
        bail!("unmapped guest memory access at 0x{addr:x} ({len} bytes)")
    }

    /// Guest read of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes (little endian).
    pub fn read(&self, addr: u64, bytes: usize) -> Result<u64> {
        if !matches!(bytes, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8) {
            bail!("unsupported access width {bytes}");
        }
        let r = self.region_for(addr, bytes as u64)?;
        let off = (addr - r.base) as usize;
        let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
        buf[..bytes].copy_from_slice(&r.data[off..off + bytes]);
        Ok(u64::from_le_bytes(buf))
    }

    pub fn write(&mut self, addr: u64, value: u64, bytes: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if !matches!(bytes, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8) {
            bail!("unsupported access width {bytes}");
        }
        let (base, perm) = {
            let r = self.region_for(addr, bytes as u64)?;
            (r.base, r.perm)
        };
        if perm == Perm::ReadExecute {
            bail!("write to read-only region at 0x{addr:x}");
        }
        let r = self
            .regions
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|r| r.base == base)
            .expect("region found above");
        let off = (addr - r.base) as usize;
        r.data[off..off + bytes].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes()[..bytes]);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copy out a slice of guest memory (used by tooling and tests).
    pub fn slice(&self, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Result<&[u8]> {
        let r = self.region_for(addr, len as u64)?;
        let off = (addr - r.base) as usize;
        Ok(&r.data[off..off + len])
    }

    pub fn region_names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.regions.iter().map(|r| r.name.clone()).collect()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn mem() -> GuestMemory {
        let mut m = GuestMemory::new();
        m.map("text", 0, 0x100, Perm::ReadExecute).unwrap();
        m.map("data", 0x1000, 0x100, Perm::ReadWrite).unwrap();
        m
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_and_writes_within_region() {
        let mut m = mem();
        m.write(0x1000, 0xdead_beef, 4).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.read(0x1000, 4).unwrap(), 0xdead_beef);
        assert_eq!(m.read(0x1002, 2).unwrap(), 0xdead);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_out_of_bounds_access() {
        let m = mem();
        assert!(m.read(0x10FE, 8).is_err(), "straddles the end of the region");
        assert!(m.read(0x2000, 4).is_err());
        assert!(m.read(u64::MAX - 1, 8).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn text_is_not_writable() {
        let mut m = mem();
        let err = m.write(0x10, 0, 4).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("read-only"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_overlapping_mappings() {
        let mut m = mem();
        assert!(m.map("clash", 0x80, 0x100, Perm::ReadWrite).is_err());
        assert!(m.map("fine", 0x2000, 0x10, Perm::ReadWrite).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn copies_initial_contents() {
        let mut m = GuestMemory::new();
        m.map_with("rodata", 0x100, b"MOD0", Perm::Read).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.slice(0x100, 4).unwrap(), b"MOD0");
    }
}

`crates/ew-runtime/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! `ew-runtime` — the native runtime's host service layer.
//!
//! The runtime has two halves:
//!
//! * **Guest execution** — lifted C (see `ew-lift`) executing guest instructions,
//!   with a dispatcher that resolves `pc` to a lifted function.
//! * **Host services** — this crate: the guest memory bus, module layout, and the
//!   HLE registry for Nintendo SDK services.
//!
//! Memory and HLE live here because they are the parts that must be *correct*
//! before any of the game can run, and because they can be tested without a
//! display, an audio device, or the game itself.
//!
//! Everything unimplemented is recorded as [`Blocked`] and returns an explicit
//! failure to the guest. Nothing here pretends a service works.

use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub mod hle;
pub mod image;

pub use hle::{HleRegistry, HleResult};
pub use image::{GuestMemory, ModuleLayout};

/// Why a host service cannot be provided yet.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Blocked {
    pub service: String,
    pub reason: String,
}

impl Blocked {
    pub fn new(service: &str, reason: &str) -> Self {
        Blocked { service: service.to_string(), reason: reason.to_string() }
    }
}

/// Overall runtime readiness, reported by the launcher and diagnostics.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Default)]
pub struct Readiness {
    /// Modules whose code has been lifted and can be dispatched.
    pub liftable_modules: Vec<String>,
    /// Modules that cannot be lifted yet.
    pub blocked_modules: Vec<String>,
    pub blocked_services: Vec<Blocked>,
    /// True only when a complete, verified boot path exists.
    pub bootable: bool,
}

impl Readiness {
    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
        if self.bootable {
            "bootable".to_string()
        } else {
            format!(
                "not bootable ({} blocked module(s), {} blocked service(s))",
                self.blocked_modules.len(),
                self.blocked_services.len()
            )
        }
    }
}

/// Load an ExeFS directory into a set of guest module layouts.
pub fn plan_modules(exefs: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Vec<ModuleLayout>> {
    let scan = ew_format::ExeFs::scan_dir(exefs)
        .with_context(|| format!("scanning {}", exefs.display()))?;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for m in &scan.modules {
        out.push(ModuleLayout {
            name: m.file_name.clone(),
            module_name: m.module_name.clone(),
            text: m.text_size as u64,
            rodata: m.rodata_size as u64,
            data: m.data_size as u64,
            bss: m.bss_size as u64,
            liftable: !m.is_zbic(),
        });
    }
    if out.is_empty() {
        bail!("no NSO modules found in {}", exefs.display());
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Summarise what can and cannot run, given a module plan.
pub fn readiness(modules: &[ModuleLayout], hle: &HleRegistry) -> Readiness {
    let mut r = Readiness::default();
    for m in modules {
        if m.liftable {
            r.liftable_modules.push(m.name.clone());
        } else {
            r.blocked_modules.push(m.name.clone());
        }
    }
    for (name, status) in hle.statuses() {
        if let HleResult::Unimplemented(reason) = status {
            r.blocked_services.push(Blocked::new(&name, &reason));
        }
    }
    // Boot requires every module to be liftable and every service implemented.
    r.bootable = !r.liftable_modules.is_empty()
        && r.blocked_modules.is_empty()
        && r.blocked_services.is_empty();
    r
}

/// Guest address space description, used for diagnostics.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct AddressSpace {
    pub regions: BTreeMap<String, AddressRange>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize)]
pub struct AddressRange {
    pub start: u64,
    pub len: u64,
}

impl AddressRange {
    pub fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start.saturating_add(self.len)
    }
    pub fn contains(&self, addr: u64) -> bool {
        addr >= self.start && addr < self.end()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn readiness_reports_the_current_truth() {
        let modules = vec![
            ModuleLayout {
                name: "main".into(),
                module_name: "app".into(),
                text: 0x100,
                rodata: 0x100,
                data: 0x100,
                bss: 0x100,
                liftable: false,
            },
            ModuleLayout {
                name: "sdk".into(),
                module_name: "nnSdk".into(),
                text: 0x100,
                rodata: 0x100,
                data: 0x100,
                bss: 0x100,
                liftable: true,
            },
        ];
        let hle = HleRegistry::with_defaults();
        let r = readiness(&modules, &hle);
        assert!(!r.bootable, "the game module is not liftable yet");
        assert_eq!(r.blocked_modules, vec!["main".to_string()]);
        assert!(r.blocked_services.iter().any(|b| b.service.contains("nvn")));
        assert!(r.describe().contains("not bootable"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn range_containment() {
        let r = AddressRange { start: 0x1000, len: 0x100 };
        assert!(r.contains(0x1000));
        assert!(r.contains(0x10FF));
        assert!(!r.contains(0x1100));
    }
}

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`:

```md
# EmblemWeave architecture

## Principles

1. **Evidence over assumption.** Format layouts in this project were derived from the dump and then verified by construction (decode boundaries must land exactly where the header says).
2. **Loud failure.** Unsupported instructions and unimplemented services trap with an address and a reason. No silent no-ops, no fake successes.
3. **Two implementations of instruction semantics, and an outside judge.** The C emitter is the product; the interpreter exists to disagree with it when it is wrong. Because both share one decoder, a third, independent CPU model (Unicorn, development only) checks the interpreter instruction by instruction.
4. **The launcher is not the runtime.** They share a format layer and nothing else.

## Components

```
                +----------------------------------------------+
                |  apps/eblemweave   (launcher, egui/eframe)   |
                |  data detection, settings, diagnostics       |
                +---------------------+------------------------+
                                      |
                +---------------------v------------------------+
                |  crates/ew-boot                               |
                |  dispatcher, module image, imports, host calls|
                +---------------------+------------------------+
                                      |
                +---------------------v------------------------+
                |  crates/ew-runtime                            |
                |  guest memory bus, module plan, HLE registry  |
                +---------------------+------------------------+
                                      |
   +--------------------+   +---------v----------+   +---------------------+
   | crates/ew-format   |   | crates/ew-lift     |   | tools/              |
   | NSO0, ExeFS, romfs |-->| decoder, interpreter|  | zbic_extract.py     |
   | inventory, probes  |   | C emitter, CFG scan |  | (ZBIC bridge)       |
   +--------------------+   +--------------------+   +---------------------+
                                      |
                                      v
                       build/lift/app_lift.c + ew_aarch64.h
                       (compiled by the host C toolchain)
```

### `ew-format` containers and assets

* `nso`: the verified NSO0 header, per-segment compression detection, `.bss`, `MOD0` discovery.
* `exefs`: module discovery by magic (renamed dumps still work), NPDM parsing, liftability classification.
* `romfs`: metadata-only inventory and content probing that unwraps standard Zstandard to report the *inner* container.

### `ew-lift` static recompilation

* `aarch64`: decoder producing a typed `Op`. Unknown words become `Op::Unsupported`, never a guess.
* `scan`: discovery of dispatchable addresses (entry, branch targets, call targets, call return sites) and linear block lifting.
* `lift`: C emission, one statement per guest instruction, return-to-dispatcher at every control-flow edge.
* `interpreter`: reference semantics for differential testing.

Generated code shape:

```c
int ew_fn_00081468(Cpu *cpu)
{
    cpu->pc = 0x81468ULL;
    /* 0x81468: sub sp, sp, #0x40 */
    { ew_u64 r_ = (EW_R(cpu, 31, 1) - 0x40ULL); EW_W(cpu, 31, 1, r_); }
    ...
}
```

`x31` is context-dependent (XZR or SP); the `EW_R`/`EW_W` macros encode that rule, and the index expression clamps 31 so the unused branch of the ternary is never an out-of-bounds access.

### `ew-boot` the whole-program dispatcher

* `Module`: maps `text`, `rodata`, and `data` at the addresses the code expects,
  and derives the entry stub from the loader header at the start of `.text`.
* `imports`: reads `MOD0`, the dynamic array, the symbol table, and the jump slot
  relocations, which is how every external call gets a name.
* `hle`: the host service registry and the C memory and string routines. A
  handler either returns a value in `x0` or reports why it cannot serve the call.
* `services`: the single-threaded `nn::os` families (mutex, event, reader/writer
  lock, semaphore, page allocation, thread-local storage, thread queries). State
  lives in the caller's guest object with a magic tag, so no handler needs global
  state and two runs cannot see each other.
* `math`: the C math library, whose results are exact because IEEE 754 is.
* `cxx`: the libc++ entry points the module imports (`std::random_device`,
  the static-initialisation guards, `__hash_memory`, `__next_prime`, nothrow
  `operator new`).
* `pmr`: `std::pmr` with a real `new_delete_resource` object whose vtable
  forwards into the game's own `operator new` and `operator delete`.
* `threads` and `sched`: multi-threaded `nn::os` (owner-tracking mutexes,
  condition variables, events, timer events, thread lifecycle, sleep) and the
  round-robin scheduler that runs guest threads on one interpreter.
* `fs`: `nn::fs` over host directories. RomFS is mounted read-only; save data
  lives in a separate writable folder; paths cannot leave their mount.
* `lmem`: `nn::lmem` frame heaps, state kept in the caller's heap head.
* `system`: `nn::oe`, `nn::account`, `nn::time`, `nn::aoc` and `nn::diag`,
  answered from launcher settings and the title's `control.nacp`.
* `libc`: the musl C runtime: formatted I/O with AAPCS64 varargs, `sscanf`,
  `strto*`, stdio over `nn::fs`, pthreads on the scheduler, `rand`, `errno`.
* `math`: musl's libm (through the `libm` crate), arguments in `s`/`d`
  registers, results in `v0`.
* `boot`: the dispatch loop. It follows nnSdk's startup order
  (`nninitStartup`, module entry, `nnMain`), runs recovered functions, executes
  host services, switches threads, and stops with a typed reason.

The stop reason is the product of this crate. A run that ends with
`called std::__1::__hash_memory` has proved which service to build next.

A host service must state a contract that is true in the host's model. Mutexes
can be exact because exactly one guest thread exists; `CreateThread` cannot be,
so it is absent and stops the run by name instead of dropping work.

### `ew-runtime` host services

* `image::GuestMemory`: region-bounded guest bus. Reads/writes outside a mapped region are errors; `.text` is not writable.
* `hle::HleRegistry`: service table where every entry is `Implemented` or `Unimplemented(reason)`. The default set is drawn from symbol names actually present in the dump.
* `readiness`: single source of truth for "can this boot yet?", currently **no**.
  Its implemented entries mirror the handlers `ew-boot` registers, so the list
  cannot claim less than the runtime delivers.

### Blocking host services and the scheduler

A host handler is `fn(&mut State) -> HostResult`. Besides returning a value or
reporting that it cannot serve a call, it can:

* `Jump(addr)`: tail-call guest code with the registers it prepared, which is
  how a host vtable forwards to the game's own functions;
* `Block { resume, timed }`: park the calling thread. The scheduler saves the
  thread's registers and later calls `resume` with them loaded. Continuations
  keep private state in caller-saved registers, which the procedure call
  standard lets a callee clobber.

Each guest thread has its own register file, TLS table and exclusive monitor
(cleared on every switch, as an exception return does). Threads rotate every
200,000 instructions, when a call blocks, or when a function exhausts its
budget in a spin-wait. When every thread waits on something only another thread
could provide, the run stops as a deadlock that names each waiter.

### Verification layers

| Layer | Compares | Catches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tools/verify_cfg.sh` | interpreter vs compiled C, whole functions | emitter mistakes |
| `tools/verify_simd.sh` | interpreter vs compiled C, every vector encoding on edge-case inputs | vector-unit mistakes in either implementation |
| `tools/oracle_lockstep.py` | interpreter vs Unicorn, one instruction at a time from a real game snapshot | decoder mistakes, which the other two cannot see |

### Dispatcher contract

Lifted modules export `ew_func_entry <module>_functions[]` mapping guest addresses to functions. The dispatch loop is:

```
while !cpu->halted:
    fn = lookup(cpu->pc)
    if fn is None: halt("unmapped pc")
    fn(&cpu)
```

Each function returns `1` to continue dispatch and `0` after a trap, so a missing implementation stops the guest instead of corrupting state.

## The launcher

`apps/eblemweave` is organised by responsibility: `config` (versioned, atomic
settings), `theme` (palettes, type and spacing tokens), `widgets` (shared
components), `gamedata` (detection and validation), `jobs` (background work with
staged progress and cancellation) and one module per page under `pages/`. Long
operations never run on the interface thread.

## Planned platform layer

| Area | Plan |
| --- | --- |
| Graphics | NVN2 device emulation over **Vulkan** (primary) with D3D12 as a later option; BFSHA shader translation to SPIR-V; BFRES resource upload |
| Audio | `nn::audio::AudioOut` over WASAPI, Opus decode for the 108k `.opus` streams |
| Input | `nn::hid` mapped to SDL3/XInput with per-device profiles and glyph detection |
| Save data | `nn::fs` save mount backed by atomic files under the user's config directory |
| Timing | Guest tick derived from a monotonic host clock; render rate decoupled from simulation rate |

## Directory layout

```
crates/ew-format    containers, romfs, probes
crates/ew-lift      decoder, interpreter, C emitter, ew-lift CLI
crates/ew-boot      dispatcher, module image, import naming, host services
crates/ew-runtime   guest memory, HLE registry, readiness
apps/eblemweave     launcher
tools/              zbic_extract.py, verification scripts, assembler probes
docs/               feasibility, architecture, status, legal
```

`docs/ENGINE.md`:

```md
# EmblemWeave's own engine

EmblemWeave plays the game today through [fefw-recomp](https://github.com/Goldoire/fefw-recomp). The goal is to replace it with
EmblemWeave's own runtime, in Rust, built on the recompiler in `crates/ew-lift` and the host services in `crates/ew-boot`, so the
whole path from your dump to a running game is EmblemWeave's. fefw-recomp stays the reference while that happens: where it has
already worked something out (how a service behaves, how NVN maps to Vulkan), EmblemWeave reads its code and docs, which its
GPL-3.0 licence allows, and writes its own version.

The order is set by what blocks playing, not by what is most visible.

## 1. Native execution (in progress)

The runtime ran the game's code on the reference interpreter, roughly a hundred times too slow to play. The game's code is now
compiled ahead of time:

* `ew-native --module work/decoded/main --out build/native` lifts the whole main module, emits it as C in shards, compiles them
  in parallel with clang and links `ew_native.dll`.
* `ew-run --native build/native/ew_native.dll` runs every function the library has natively and interprets the rest. A native
  function can be entered at any of its blocks, so calls return into native code.
* Guest memory is read and written directly; every block charges its instructions to a budget, so guest threads are still
  rotated by the scheduler; supervisor calls, the system counter, exclusive monitors and halts behave as in the interpreter.
* `EW_NATIVE_CHECK=1` runs each native call on the side and compares its registers and stores with the interpreter, narrowing a
  difference down to the first block where the two part. It found the first native bug (a function entered mid-way restarted
  at its entry) and now passes the boot's first 300 million instructions.

Where it stands (10 November 2026, RX 7900 XT PC, 16 threads, 32 GB):

* The whole main module builds: 807,604 functions, 10.6 million instructions, 530 C files, compiled in about 16 minutes
  (8 jobs at below-normal priority, bounded by memory) into a 757 MB library; later builds only recompile files that changed.
* `EW_NATIVE_CHECK=1` finds no difference from the interpreter over the boot's first billion instructions. On the way it
  found two bugs in the generated code: functions restarting at their entry, and the LSE atomics (`ldadd` and friends)
  storing and returning the wrong values.
* A billion boot instructions take 12 s native against 22 s interpreted. Native functions call each other directly; what is
  left is the run loop's work around host calls: hot loops in the game call host functions (a shuffle calls the C
  library's random number generator every iteration), and every such call goes through the full run loop.

Next: serve simple host calls from inside native code without the full run loop (keeping the scheduler's view of new
threads correct); compile the SDK module too (it needs the lifter to work at the module's load address); `-O2` for hot
code.

## 2. Frame loop at speed

With native code, run the game headless to the title screen and into play, fixing the services it reaches (the audio
renderer's voice release is the last known blocker), as the interpreter runs did, but in minutes rather than hours.

## 3. Graphics

The game draws with NVN. EmblemWeave already tracks NVN's devices, memory pools, textures, programs, state and command buffers
(`nvn_*.rs`). Next:

1. A Vulkan device and window (the `ew-gfx` crate) presenting the game's colour buffers.
2. Textures: the Switch's block-linear layouts and its compressed formats, uploaded to Vulkan.
3. Shaders: the game's Maxwell/Ampere shader binaries translated to SPIR-V. This is the largest single piece; fefw-recomp uses
   Ryujinx's translator (MIT) offline, and EmblemWeave can do the same as a build step before writing its own.
4. Draw calls, render targets, blending, depth and the rest of the pipeline state.

## 4. Audio and input

The audio renderer already runs the game's voices; its mixed output goes to the sound device. Keyboard and controller input go
to the game's HID state (`hid.rs`), with the bindings from the launcher's Controls page.

## 5. Launcher

When the runtime can play, the launcher's **Play** starts it instead of fefw-recomp, and **Build the game** builds
`ew_native.dll` and the shader cache. Saves and mods carry over as they are (the save layout and the mods folder are shared).
Cheats need one change: fefw-recomp maps the game's memory at the game's own addresses, while EmblemWeave's runtime holds it in
one host block, so the runtime will publish where that block is and the cheat engine will add the offset.

```

`docs/FEASIBILITY.md`:

```md
# EmblemWeave technical feasibility report

**Target:** *Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave* (Nintendo Switch 2), Title ID `04007EF01F8AE000`, v131072
**Goal:** a native Windows x64 build that executes the game's own code, built by [XiØN](https://github.com/XiONDiGiTaL)
**Report date:** 8 November 2026
**Status of this report:** every claim below was measured against the user's own dump. Numbers are reproducible with the tools in this repository.

---

## 1. What the dump actually is

The supplied package is **not** a Switch 1 title. Three independent facts establish this:

| Evidence | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Package magic | `NUP\x01` at offset 0, the Nintendo Switch 2 package container |
| Title ID | `04007EF0...`, where the `0x0400` application prefix is reserved for Switch 2 titles (Switch 1 uses `0x0100`) |
| Executable format | NSO0 modules with 64 MiB+ rodata and Switch 2 process metadata, segmented differently from Switch 1 |

The `NUP` is an encrypted retail package and was **not** usable directly. A decrypted view of the content already existed on this machine at
`E:\Switch2\Games\.nup-convert-h_e2mfw5\.nup-nsp-f_aicmw_\`, containing a decrypted PFS0 (NSP) and an extracted ExeFS/romfs. EmblemWeave consumes that extracted material and never touches, modifies, or redistributes the original package.

### Executable modules (measured, `ew-inspect`)

| ExeFS file | Module name | File size | Image size | Flags | Compression | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | `app` | 11.5 MiB | 34.7 MiB | `0xbf` | **ZBIC** | decoded (see §2.2) |
| `subsdk0` | `dlss` | 40.4 MiB | 43.6 MiB | `0x3f` | LZ4 | decoded + verified |
| `subsdk1` | `cuda` | 6.0 MiB | 20.3 MiB | `0x3f` | LZ4 | decoded + verified |
| `subsdk2` | `movie` | 520.9 KiB | 890.9 KiB | `0x3f` | LZ4 | decoded + verified |
| `rtld` | `nnrtld` | 10.3 KiB | 124.3 KiB | `0x3f` | LZ4 | decoded + verified |
| `sdk` | `nnSdk` | 7.5 MiB | 16.4 MiB | `0x3f` | LZ4 | decoded + verified |

`main.npdm` reports process category **Application**, confirming `main` is the game program. The game's own logic therefore lives in `app`: **27,546,352 bytes of AArch64 text**, 5,532,760 bytes of rodata and 2,265,808 bytes of data, plus `0x109d30` of bss.

## 2. Format findings

### 2.1 NSO0 segment layout

The Switch 1 header layout does **not** describe these files. The layout below was derived empirically and then confirmed by construction: an independent LZ4 decode of every segment reproduces the header's declared boundaries exactly, and the final segment ends precisely at end-of-file for all five LZ4 modules.

```
0x00  "NSO0"                 0x20  rodata.file_offset
0x04  u32 version            0x24  rodata.mem_offset
0x08  u32 reserved           0x28  rodata.size
0x0C  u32 flags              0x2C  u32 name_len
0x10  u32 text.file_offset   0x30  data.file_offset
0x14  u32 text.mem_offset    0x34  data.mem_offset
0x18  u32 text.size          0x38  data.size
0x1C  u32 header_size        0x3C  u32 bss_size
                             0x40  u8 module_id[0x20]
module name at (text.file_offset - name_len), NUL terminated
```

Flag bits `0..2` mark the text/rodata/data segments as compressed, `3..5` mark segment hashes, and **bit 7 selects ZBIC instead of LZ4**.

Verification (`rtld`, the smallest module):

| Segment | Declared size | Stored bytes consumed | Ends at | Header next-offset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | `0x2740` | `0x1f67` | `0x206e` | `0x206e` ✓ |
| rodata | `0x9e4` | `0x6eb` | `0x2759` | `0x2759` ✓ |
| data | `0xc008` | `0x1bb` | `0x2914` | EOF `0x2914` ✓ |

The decoded `rtld` rodata yields real symbols, e.g. `_ZN2nn4init5StartEmmPFvvES2_S2_` and `nnrtld.nss`, so the decode is not merely plausible-looking bytes.

### 2.2 ZBIC: Nintendo's modified Zstandard

`app` uses compression flag bit 7. Its text segment begins with the ASCII magic `ZBIC` where a standard Zstandard frame would carry `28 B5 2F FD`. The frame header that follows declares a content size of `0x01a452f0` = 27,546,352, which matches the header's text size exactly.

Public documentation and implementations agree that ZBIC is otherwise Zstandard (1.5.7) with `FSE_readNCount` replaced by a Binary Interpolative Coding reader. Because a decoder is publicly available (`kinnay/zbic`, Atmosphère, `alula/beetool`, and the Ghidra Switch Loader), the game module **is** recoverable today:

```
main: module='app' flags=0xbf zbic=True bss=0x109d30
  text   stored=  9917392 decoded= 27546352 (declared  27546352) OK
  rodata stored=  1809272 decoded=  5532760 (declared   5532760) OK
  data   stored=   298704 decoded=  2265808 (declared   2265808) OK
```

Every decoded size matches the declaration, so `tools/zbic_extract.py` is a trustworthy bridge until a Rust ZBIC decoder replaces it (see §6).

### 2.3 romfs

252,686 files totalling **27.0 GiB** across 17 top-level directories, dominated by audio:

| Extension | Files | Likely content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.opus` | 108,201 | voice/music streams |
| `.lips` | 107,436 | lip-sync data |
| `.zst` | 34,122 | standard Zstandard-wrapped assets (`.bfres`, `.bfsha`, `.msbt`, …) |
| `.matanimb` | 604 | material animation |
| `.webm` | 82 | movies |
| `.msbt.zst` | 6,289 (`.zst` total) | dialogue/message tables |

`Shaders/*.bfsha.zst` and `Graphics/**/*.bfres.zst` confirm the expected NintendoWare pipeline: BFRES models, BFSHA shader archives, BAKE audio, MSBT text. `rodata` in `app` contains `Emblem`/`Fortune` strings and NintendoSDK symbols, further confirming identity.

## 3. Is static recompilation the right approach?

| Option | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| **A. Static recompilation (chosen)** | The only route that yields a native executable with no original binary at run time. Requires an AArch64→C lifter plus a Horizon/NVN2 runtime. |
| **B. Full decompilation to source** | Not tractable: 27.5 MB of text with stripped symbols and heavy inlining. Viable only for small, hot subsystems later. |
| **C. Hybrid** | **Recommended end state.** Static recompilation for bulk code, hand-written native implementations for the platform layer (graphics, audio, input, filesystem), and reconstructed high-level code where behaviour must be cleanly reimplemented. |

Frameworks examined: N64Recomp and XenonRecomp target different ISAs (MIPS/PPC) and cannot be reused; McSema/Remill lift to LLVM IR but supply no Switch loader, no service layer and no graphics; Ghidra is the right tool for *analysis*, not for producing runnable translations. Public Switch recompilation projects (`ssbu-recomp`, `smo-recomp`, `dkb-pc-recomp`) are title-specific and confirm the shape of the work: lifter + per-title runtime + shader translation.

**Recommendation: Option C**, with the lifter and runtime built here as the reusable core.

## 4. Verified progress

| Milestone | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Container parsing | All 6 modules parsed; segment boundaries verified to EOF |
| Code extraction | 6/6 modules decoded (app via ZBIC bridge), sizes match declarations |
| Decoder coverage | **86.18 %** of `app` text decodes to supported instructions (6,886,588 words; 951,908 unsupported) |
| Lifting | 1,352 register-only blocks (2,783 instructions) lifted with 0 unsupported instructions in the lifted set |
| Emitted C compiles | `zig cc -std=c99 -Wall`: clean build of `app_lift.c` |
| Execution | Lifted guest `0x81468` executed natively; results **bit-identical** to the independent interpreter (x5=`cf1bbcdcbfa56300`, x6=`cf1bbcdcbf9b0000`, x7=`cf1bbcdcbb000000`, pc=`0x814dc`) |
| Memory/HLE layer | Range-checked guest bus and explicit HLE registry, 9 tests |

## 5. Major obstacles (honest list)

1. **CFG recovery.** Blocks currently end at the first control-flow instruction; conditional branches mark a block partial and the runtime halts instead of guessing. Jump tables and indirect branches are the next lift milestone.
2. **14 % undecoded text.** SIMD/FP, bitfield-extract and system instructions are not yet modelled. Each becomes either an emitter case or a documented trap.
3. **No service layer.** Nothing in `nn::os`, `nn::mem`, `nn::fs`, `nn::hid`, `nn::audio`, `nn::vi` or `nn::nvn` is implemented. Nine blocked services are listed in the runtime registry, each with a reason.
4. **NVN2 graphics.** The renderer needs Switch 2 (Ampere-class) shader translation to SPIR-V. Public work exists but is incomplete; mesh shaders, VRS and sparse virtual textures are open problems.
5. **Threading and scheduling.** The guest's synchronisation primitives must be mapped onto the host without changing observable ordering.
6. **No C toolchain on this machine by default.** Verification used `zig cc` from a Python wheel. Release engineering needs a pinned LLVM/MSVC toolchain.

## 6. Milestones ahead

| Phase | Work | Exit criterion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3a | Port ZBIC decoding to Rust (remove Python bridge) | `ew-format` decodes `app` with no external tool |
| 3b | CFG recovery: basic blocks, conditional successors, jump tables | ≥95 % of text reachable; blocks no longer partial |
| 3c | Widen instruction coverage (SIMD/FP, bitfield, system) | ≥99 % decodable |
| 3d | `nn::os`/`nn::mem` HLE with a guest heap and threads | `app` reaches its own initialisation and reports a clean failure at the first unimplemented service |
| 4 | NVN2 device + shader translation to Vulkan | First clear colour rendered from the game's own init path |
| 5 | Filesystem, audio, input HLE | First boot to title screen |
| 6 | Gameplay validation matrix | Save/load, battle, cutscene, transition parity |
| 7 | PC enhancements (widescreen, frame pacing, remapping) | Feature-complete settings surface |

EmblemWeave ships **no** Nintendo code, assets, keys or firmware. It requires the user's own dump and never modifies it. See [LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md).

# Legal and distribution position

## Independent project

EmblemWeave is an independent [XiØN](https://github.com/XiONDiGiTaL) project. It is **not** affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Nintendo, Intelligent Systems, or any of their subsidiaries. ## Bring your own game data

EmblemWeave ships no Nintendo content. It contains:

* no game executables, NSO modules or NCA/NSP/NUP containers,
* no textures, models, shaders, audio, movies or fonts from the game,
* no encryption keys, tickets, certificates or firmware,

The supplied `.nup` package is encrypted retail content. This project consumed an already-decrypted, already-extracted view present on the machine (ExeFS + romfs). No circumvention of the package's protection was performed by this project, and no keys are stored or embedded here.

# EmblemWeave status

**Summary: the game is playable through the engine.** EmblemWeave builds and
runs the game with [fefw-recomp](https://github.com/Goldoire/fefw-recomp)
(GPL-3.0, at `engine/fefw-recomp`): on this PC (AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT) the
retail game, update 131072, runs at about 60 fps with sound, from the
launcher's **Build the game** and **Play**. The rest of this page covers
EmblemWeave's own Rust recompiler and runtime, a research path that now
runs the game's frame loop past the autosave notice and the opening movie
into its first map load, with draws counted rather than rendered.

A 25-minute headless run reaches 27.9 billion instructions and then stops
where the game aborts: its pool of sound handles fills up, because the host
audio renderer never reports a voice's wave buffers as played, so no handle is
ever released. That is the next blocker.

Last verified: 9 November 2026, retail `main` module of version 1.1.0, release build.

| **Partial** | Works for the cases listed; the rest is reported, never guessed |

## What changed in this milestone

1. **Into the frame loop.** Two decoder bugs (`csinv` and `fmov` immediates)
   were silently corrupting the game's arithmetic. Fixing them, keeping mutex
   and condition-variable state from overwriting neighbouring objects, and
   adding multi-wait, play reports, `std::thread` and a movie layer took the
   boot from 1.4 billion instructions to the frame loop, the autosave notice
   and the first map load.
2. **Debugging tools.** `ew-run --watch ADDR` logs a function's arguments and
   return value (with `EW_PEEK` memory dumps), `--press` scripts input,
   `--all-calls` lists every import reached, and `ew_unzst` unpacks a RomFS
   `.zst` file.

### Earlier in this milestone

1. **The NVN layer.** Device, queues, memory, textures, samplers, render state,
   programs, window and command buffers are served on the host. Device
   properties come from the game's own use; texture formats come from the
   game's BNTX-to-NVN table, which confirmed the numbering.
2. **The title's `sdk` module.** Loaded beside `main` with RELR relocations;
   the C++ standard library and other library code now run as the title's own
   code. This alone took the run from 3.6 million to 17 million instructions.
3. **System instructions and supervisor calls.** `mrs`/`msr`, `svc` and
   `ldpsw`, with per-thread TLS and kernel lock arbitration.
4. **A real heap.** Three allocator objects previously shared one heap and
   could hand out overlapping memory; each now has its own free list.
5. **Input and audio start-up**, message queues and system events.
6. **Launcher**: the exact xiondigital.net palette, Arcade with its grid, the
   FE scheme, a new wordmark and crest, liquid-glass controls, and command-line
   options that make the screenshots reproducible.

## Known limitations

1. **The dispatcher interprets.** The emitted C is verified but the runtime
   still executes the reference interpreter (about 15 million guest
   instructions per second in a release build). Wiring the dispatcher to the
   compiled code is the main performance step.
2. **Nothing is drawn.** Command buffers are recorded and their memory
   effects carried out, but draws, clears of render targets and texture copies
   are not executed on the GPU, and the game's shaders (compiled for the
   console's GPU) are not translated yet.
3. **ZBIC needs an external decoder.** The bridge runs the GPL-2.0 `zbic`
   package out of process. A clean-room Rust decoder is planned.
4. **Floating point environment.** Only round to nearest is modelled; the
   flush-to-zero and default-NaN mode bits are accepted but not applied.
5. **Time zone.** Calendar conversion is UTC.
6. **Optimised native builds.** The launcher compiles the translation at `-O0`
   to prove it builds; the largest lifted functions take many minutes at `-O1`.
7. **Emitted C size.** 4,000 functions produce about 213 MB of C. The launcher
   splits it into shards balanced by instruction count and compiles them in
   parallel, but the largest functions still take minutes at `-O1`; the emitter
   needs to produce tighter code before the whole game is compiled.
8. **Function boundaries are inferred**, not proven, because the module has no
   symbol table for its internal functions.

## Next actions, in order

1. **Audio renderer updates.** Serve the renderer's update protocol so voices
   report played samples and consumed wave buffers. The game's sound handles
   are released only then, and today their pool runs out during the first map
   load. Exit criterion: the long run passes the map load without the abort.
2. **Rendering.** Execute recorded clears and copies on Vulkan and present the
   swap textures in a window: exit criterion, the game's first frame on screen.
   Then shader translation from the console GPU's binaries, draws, and texture
   decoding (block-linear, BC, ASTC).
3. **Run the compiled code.** The interpreter runs about 8 million instructions
   per second; dispatching into the native translation is the main speed step.
4. **Audio mixing** to WASAPI, and voice state updates.
5. **Movies**: VP9 decoding for `Movie/Product/*.webm` and the cut scenes.
6. **Gameplay validation** from the first battle map on.

## Reproducing these results

```powershell
# decode the main module once
python tools/zbic_extract.py <exefs> work/decoded main

# workspace tests
cargo test --workspace

# decode the sdk module (LZ4) once
target\release\ew-decode <exefs>\sdk work\decoded\sdk

# run the game and print the stop report
target\release\ew-run --module work\decoded\main --lib work\decoded\sdk --romfs <romfs> --nacp <control.nacp> --max-steps 2500000000

# differential verification on your data
bash tools/verify_cfg.sh
bash tools/verify_simd.sh work/decoded/main/text.bin 400

# lockstep against the independent CPU from a snapshot
target\release\ew-run --module work\decoded\main --romfs <romfs> --snapshot-at 0x6c500 --snapshot-steps 30000
python tools/oracle_lockstep.py build/snapshot
```

# Code adapted from other projects

EmblemWeave is GPL-3.0-only. This file lists source code adapted from other free-software projects, with where it came from and
under which licence. Libraries used as dependencies are listed in [LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md).

## fefw-recomp

[Goldoire/fefw-recomp](https://github.com/Goldoire/fefw-recomp), GPL-3.0. A native PC port of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave by static
recompilation. Every file adapted from it carries a header naming the original file.

It is included whole as a git submodule at `engine/fefw-recomp`, pinned to a known commit, and is EmblemWeave's game engine: its

`tools/capture_pages.ps1`:

```ps1
# Capture launcher pages to docs/screenshots for the README.
#
# Sends no keystrokes or clicks: each page is opened with `--page <name>`, and
# the boot captures use `--boot-test`. Each capture is taken with PrintWindow,
# which renders only the launcher's own window, so nothing else on the screen
# can ever appear in a screenshot. The title strip and the invisible resize
# border are cropped off.
param(
    [string]$Exe = "$PSScriptRoot\..\target\release\EmblemWeave.exe",
    [string]$OutDir = "$PSScriptRoot\..\docs\screenshots",
    [string[]]$Only = @(),
    [int]$Crop = 32,
    [int]$Border = 8,
    [int]$BootSeconds = 45,
    [switch]$SkipBoot
)

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
Add-Type @"
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public struct EWP_RECT { public int Left, Top, Right, Bottom; }
public class EWP_Win {
    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool GetWindowRect(IntPtr h, out EWP_RECT r);
    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetWindowPos(IntPtr h, IntPtr after, int x, int y, int cx, int cy, uint flags);
    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool PrintWindow(IntPtr h, IntPtr hdc, uint flags);
}
"@

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $OutDir | Out-Null

function Open-Launcher([string[]]$launchArgs) {
    $p = Start-Process -FilePath $Exe -ArgumentList $launchArgs -WorkingDirectory (Split-Path $Exe) -PassThru
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 40 -and $p.MainWindowHandle -eq 0; $i++) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250; $p.Refresh() }
    # Size the window without raising it or taking focus (SWP_NOZORDER 0x4, SWP_NOACTIVATE 0x10).
    [EWP_Win]::SetWindowPos($p.MainWindowHandle, [IntPtr]::Zero, 40, 40, 1280, 900, 0x14) | Out-Null
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    return $p
}

function Save-Shot($p, [string]$name) {
    $h = $p.MainWindowHandle
    # Raise it above other windows for a moment (no input is sent): a window
    # that is fully covered does not draw, and would capture as black.
    [EWP_Win]::SetWindowPos($h, [IntPtr](-1), 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x3) | Out-Null
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 900
    $r = New-Object EWP_RECT
    [EWP_Win]::GetWindowRect($h, [ref]$r) | Out-Null
    $fw = $r.Right - $r.Left; $fh = $r.Bottom - $r.Top
    $full = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $fw, $fh
    $g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($full)
    $hdc = $g.GetHdc()
    # PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT (2): includes GPU-composited content.
    $ok = [EWP_Win]::PrintWindow($h, $hdc, 2)
    $g.ReleaseHdc($hdc); $g.Dispose()
    if (-not $ok) { $full.Dispose(); Write-Error "PrintWindow failed for $name"; return }
    $rect = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle $Border, $Crop, ($fw - 2 * $Border), ($fh - $Crop - $Border)
    $shot = $full.Clone($rect, $full.PixelFormat)
    $path = Join-Path $OutDir "$name.png"
    $shot.Save($path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
    $shot.Dispose(); $full.Dispose()
    [EWP_Win]::SetWindowPos($h, [IntPtr](-2), 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x3) | Out-Null
    Write-Output "$path $($rect.Width)x$($rect.Height)"
}

$pages = [ordered]@{
    "overview" = "Overview"; "setup" = "Game Setup"; "recompilation" = "Recompilation"
    "graphics" = "Graphics"; "audio" = "Audio"; "controls" = "Controls"
    "appearance" = "Appearance"; "diagnostics" = "Diagnostics"; "about" = "About"
}
foreach ($file in $pages.Keys) {
    if ($Only.Count -gt 0 -and $Only -notcontains $file) { continue }
    $p = Open-Launcher @("--page", "`"$($pages[$file])`"")
    Save-Shot $p $file
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id
}

if (-not $SkipBoot) {
    # A boot test: running, finished, then its diagnostics.
    $p = Open-Launcher @("--boot-test")
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
    Save-Shot $p "boot-running"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds $BootSeconds
    Save-Shot $p "boot-done"
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id
    $p = Open-Launcher @("--boot-test", "--page", "Diagnostics")
    Start-Sleep -Seconds ($BootSeconds + 3)
    Save-Shot $p "diagnostics-run"
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id
}

`tools/capture_window.ps1`:

# Capture the EmblemWeave launcher window to a PNG.
#
# The launcher is a GPU-composited window, so the only dependable way to read it
# is to raise it above every other window and copy its rectangle off the screen.
param(
    [string]$Out = "C:\ewtarget\shot.png",
    [string]$ProcessName = "eblemweave"
)

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
Add-Type @"
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public struct EW_RECT { public int Left, Top, Right, Bottom; }
public class EW_Win {
    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetForegroundWindow(IntPtr h);
    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool GetWindowRect(IntPtr h, out EW_RECT r);
    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool ShowWindow(IntPtr h, int n);
    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetWindowPos(IntPtr h, IntPtr after, int x, int y, int cx, int cy, uint flags);
}
"@

$proc = Get-Process -Name $ProcessName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $_.MainWindowHandle -ne 0 } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $proc) { Write-Error "no window for $ProcessName"; exit 1 }

$h = $proc.MainWindowHandle
[EW_Win]::ShowWindow($h, 9) | Out-Null
# SWP_NOSIZE 0x1, SWP_SHOWWINDOW 0x40, HWND_TOPMOST -1, then move to the corner.
[EW_Win]::SetWindowPos($h, [IntPtr](-1), 40, 40, 0, 0, 0x1 -bor 0x40) | Out-Null
[EW_Win]::SetForegroundWindow($h) | Out-Null
Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 900

$r = New-Object EW_RECT
[EW_Win]::GetWindowRect($h, [ref]$r) | Out-Null
$w = $r.Right - $r.Left
$hgt = $r.Bottom - $r.Top
$bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $w, $hgt
$g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)
$g.CopyFromScreen($r.Left, $r.Top, 0, 0, $bmp.Size)
$bmp.Save($Out, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
$g.Dispose(); $bmp.Dispose()
# Drop topmost again so the window behaves normally afterwards.
[EW_Win]::SetWindowPos($h, [IntPtr](-2), 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x1 -bor 0x2) | Out-Null
Write-Output "$Out ${w}x${hgt}"

`tools/cutout_logo.py`:

```py
"""Cut the EmblemWeave logo render out of its white background.

1. The outer background is a flood fill from the image border over light,
   low-saturation pixels.
2. The gaps enclosed inside and between letters are found separately, from
   pixels that are light and also smooth: background white is flat, while the
   silver letter faces are textured, so a face never joins the gap it touches.
   Enclosed regions that are compact, bright and flat become background; long
   thin runs (the silver rail along the bar) stay.
3. Around the background (grown a few pixels to take in antialiased edges),
   colour-to-alpha against white turns the soft edge into transparency, and
   only a narrow halo next to the logo keeps any alpha, so the backdrop's faint
   grey gradient does not survive as a haze.

Usage: python tools/cutout_logo.py <render> <out.png>
"""
import sys
from collections import deque

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageFilter

src, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
rgb = np.asarray(Image.open(src).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32)
h, w, _ = rgb.shape
mx, mn = rgb.max(axis=2), rgb.min(axis=2)
light = (mn > 175) & ((mx - mn) < 34)


def box(a, r=2):
    """Mean over a (2r+1) square, edges replicated."""
    p = np.pad(a, r, mode="edge")
    c = np.cumsum(np.cumsum(p, axis=0), axis=1)
    c = np.pad(c, ((1, 0), (1, 0)))
    k = 2 * r + 1
    return (c[k:, k:] - c[:-k, k:] - c[k:, :-k] + c[:-k, :-k]) / (k * k)


lum = rgb.mean(axis=2)
flat = np.sqrt(np.maximum(box(lum * lum) - box(lum) ** 2, 0.0)) < 5.0


def regions(mask):
    """Connected regions of `mask`, as lists of (y, x)."""
    seen = np.zeros((h, w), bool)
    for sy in range(h):
        for sx in range(w):
            if not mask[sy, sx] or seen[sy, sx]:
                continue
            seen[sy, sx] = True
            pixels = [(sy, sx)]
            q = deque(pixels)
            while q:
                y, x = q.popleft()
                for dy, dx in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
                    ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx
                    if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and mask[ny, nx] and not seen[ny, nx]:
                        seen[ny, nx] = True
                        pixels.append((ny, nx))
                        q.append((ny, nx))
            yield pixels


bg = np.zeros((h, w), bool)
for pixels in regions(light):
    ys, xs = zip(*pixels)
    if min(ys) == 0 or min(xs) == 0 or max(ys) == h - 1 or max(xs) == w - 1:
        bg[ys, xs] = True

for pixels in regions(light & flat & ~bg):
    if len(pixels) <= 40:
        continue
    ys, xs = zip(*pixels)
    region = rgb[ys, xs]
    tall, wide = max(ys) - min(ys) + 1, max(xs) - min(xs) + 1
    compact = max(tall, wide) < 8 * min(tall, wide)
    if compact and region.min(axis=1).mean() > 195 and region.std(axis=0).mean() < 24:
        bg[ys, xs] = True


def grow(mask, times):
    img = Image.fromarray((mask * 255).astype(np.uint8))
    for _ in range(times):
        img = img.filter(ImageFilter.MaxFilter(3))
    return np.asarray(img) > 0


edge = grow(bg, 2)
halo = grow(~bg, 7)

# Colour-to-alpha against white.
a = np.clip((255.0 - mn) / 255.0 * 1.25, 0.0, 1.0)
safe = np.maximum(a, 1e-3)[..., None]
unmixed = np.clip((rgb - 255.0 * (1.0 - safe)) / safe, 0, 255)
alpha = np.where(edge, a, 1.0)
alpha = np.where(bg & ~halo, 0.0, alpha)
alpha = np.where(alpha < 0.05, 0.0, alpha)
colour = np.where(edge[..., None], unmixed, rgb)

rgba = np.dstack([colour, alpha * 255.0]).astype(np.uint8)
img = Image.fromarray(rgba, "RGBA")
img = img.crop(img.getbbox())
img.save(out)
print(out, img.size)

```

`tools/elf_text.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the .text section of a static ELF object as raw bytes.

Used by the verification scripts to turn a compiled AArch64 object into the flat
guest image the lifter consumes. This is deliberately a few lines of struct
unpacking rather than a dependency: the toolchain already produces the object,
and all that is needed is the section bytes.
"""

import struct
import sys


def text_section(path):
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    if data[:4] != b"\x7fELF" or data[4] != 2:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: not a 64-bit ELF object")
    shoff = struct.unpack_from("<Q", data, 0x28)[0]
    shentsize = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, 0x3A)[0]
    shnum = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, 0x3C)[0]
    shstrndx = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, 0x3E)[0]

    def header(i):
        # name, type, flags, addr, offset, size
        return struct.unpack_from("<IIQQQQ", data, shoff + i * shentsize)

    _, _, _, _, names_off, _ = header(shstrndx)
    for i in range(shnum):
        name, _typ, _flags, _addr, offset, size = header(i)
        end = data.index(b"\0", names_off + name)
        if data[names_off + name:end] == b".text":
            return data[offset:offset + size]
    raise SystemExit(f"{path}: no .text section")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        raise SystemExit("usage: elf_text.py <object.o> <out.bin>")
    section = text_section(sys.argv[1])
    open(sys.argv[2], "wb").write(section)
    print(f"{len(section)} bytes of .text -> {sys.argv[2]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/fp_probe.c`:

```c
/* Floating point probe for the differential campaign.
 *
 * The point is to test the lifter against real clang instruction selection,
 * not against hand written assembly. One function performs every scalar
 * floating point operation the lifter models, and each result is written to a
 * volatile sink so the optimiser cannot fold or delete it. No library call is
 * emitted: every operation here lowers to a hardware instruction, which is
 * exactly what the guest code contains.
 *
 * tools/verify_fp.sh compiles this file for AArch64, lifts the .text segment and
 * compares the emitted C against the reference interpreter register by register.
 */

static volatile float  g_float;
static volatile double g_double;
static volatile int    g_int32;
static volatile unsigned g_uint32;

float fp_sweep(float a, float b, int i, unsigned u, double p, double q)
{
    /* Two source arithmetic, both precisions. */
    g_float = a + b;
    g_float = a - b;
    g_float = a * b;
    g_float = a / b;
    g_double = p + q;
    g_double = p - q;
    g_double = p * q;
    g_double = p / q;

    /* One source: sign, magnitude, square root. */
    g_float = -a;
    g_float = __builtin_fabsf(a);
    g_float = __builtin_sqrtf(a);
    g_double = -p;
    g_double = __builtin_fabs(p);
    g_double = __builtin_sqrt(p);

    /* Three source: multiply accumulate and its negated forms. */
    g_float = a * b + a;
    g_float = -(a * b) - b;
    g_double = p * q + p;
    g_double = -(p * q) - q;

    /* Maximum and minimum, which compile to a compare plus select. */
    g_float = a > b ? a : b;
    g_float = a < b ? a : b;
    g_double = p > q ? p : q;
    g_double = p < q ? p : q;

    /* The rounding family. */
    g_float = __builtin_roundf(a);
    g_float = __builtin_floorf(a);
    g_float = __builtin_ceilf(a);
    g_float = __builtin_truncf(a);
    g_float = __builtin_rintf(a);
    g_double = __builtin_round(p);
    g_double = __builtin_floor(p);
    g_double = __builtin_ceil(p);
    g_double = __builtin_trunc(p);
    g_double = __builtin_rint(p);

    /* Precision conversion in both directions. */
    g_double = (double)a;
    g_float = (float)p;

    /* Floating point to integer, both widths. The unsigned forms are absent on
     * purpose: clang lowers them through a SIMD scalar rounding instruction
     * (`fcvtzs s0, s1`) that this decoder does not model yet, and a probe that
     * silently traps would not be a probe. */
    g_int32 = (int)a;
    g_int32 = (int)p;
    g_int32 = (int)__builtin_rintf(a);
    g_int32 = (int)__builtin_rint(p);

    /* Integer to floating point, signed and unsigned, both widths. */
    g_float = (float)i;
    g_float = (float)u;
    g_double = (double)i;
    g_double = (double)u;

    /* Short immediates. */
    g_float = 1.0f;
    g_float = 0.5f;
    g_float = -2.0f;
    g_float = 3.0f;
    g_double = 1.0;
    g_double = 2.0;

    /* Movement between the register files without conversion. */
    g_float = __builtin_bit_cast(float, (unsigned)i);
    g_int32 = __builtin_bit_cast(int, a);
    g_double = __builtin_bit_cast(double, (unsigned long long)u);
    g_int32 = (int)__builtin_bit_cast(unsigned long long, p);

    return g_float + (float)g_double + (float)g_int32 + (float)g_uint32;
}

```

`tools/make_icon.ps1`:

```ps1
# Generate the EmblemWeave application icon.
#
# The in-app mark is drawn live in egui and recolours per scheme. A window and
# taskbar icon has to be a bitmap, so this script renders the same crest once in
# the Emblem palette (gold monogram, steel shield, teal ribbon) and writes it to
# apps/eblemweave/assets/icon.png, which the launcher loads at startup.
#
# Run from the repository root:
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/make_icon.ps1

param([int]$Size = 256)

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing

$out = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\apps\eblemweave\assets\icon.png"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $out) | Out-Null

$bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $Size, $Size
$g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)
$g.SmoothingMode = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode]::AntiAlias
$g.InterpolationMode = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode]::HighQualityBicubic
$g.Clear([System.Drawing.Color]::Transparent)

function U([double]$x, [double]$y) {
    New-Object System.Drawing.PointF ([single]($x * $Size)), ([single]($y * $Size))
}

# Palette: the Emblem scheme, matching apps/eblemweave/src/theme.rs.
$metal      = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0xcd, 0xd2, 0xdb)
$metalDeep  = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0xb6, 0xbc, 0xc8)
$edge       = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0x63, 0x67, 0x70)
$gold       = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0xc9, 0xa2, 0x27)
$goldHi     = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0xe9, 0xcd, 0x6b)
$royal      = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0x1d, 0x48, 0xaf)
$weave      = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0x30, 0x9f, 0xad)
$weaveHi    = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0x8f, 0xdc, 0xdf)

# Shield outline: straight top edge, vertical shoulders, quarter-ellipse point.
$pts = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[System.Drawing.PointF]
$n = 40
for ($i = 0; $i -le $n; $i++) {
    $t = $i / $n
    $pts.Add((U (0.14 + 0.72 * $t) 0.075))
}
for ($i = 1; $i -le $n; $i++) {
    $t = $i / $n
    if ($t -le 0.46) { $hw = 1.0 } else { $u = ($t - 0.46) / 0.54; $hw = [math]::Sqrt([math]::Max(0.0, 1 - $u * $u)) }
    $pts.Add((U (0.5 + 0.36 * $hw) (0.075 + 0.875 * $t)))
}
for ($i = $n - 1; $i -ge 1; $i--) {
    $t = $i / $n
    if ($t -le 0.46) { $hw = 1.0 } else { $u = ($t - 0.46) / 0.54; $hw = [math]::Sqrt([math]::Max(0.0, 1 - $u * $u)) }
    $pts.Add((U (0.5 - 0.36 * $hw) (0.075 + 0.875 * $t)))
}
$outline = $pts.ToArray()

function Inset([System.Drawing.PointF[]]$poly, [double]$amount) {
    $cx = 0.5 * $Size; $cy = 0.57 * $Size
    $r = @()
    foreach ($p in $poly) {
        $r += New-Object System.Drawing.PointF ([single]($cx + ($p.X - $cx) * (1 - $amount))), ([single]($cy + ($p.Y - $cy) * (1 - $amount)))
    }
    return $r
}

# Drop shadow, dark keyline, light rim, engraved ring, pale field.
$shadow = Inset $outline -0.012
$shadowBrush = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush ([System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(120, 0, 0, 0))
$g.FillPolygon($shadowBrush, $shadow)

$edgeBrush = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush $edge
$g.FillPolygon($edgeBrush, $outline)

$rim = Inset $outline 0.028
$metalBrush = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush $metal
$g.FillPolygon($metalBrush, $rim)

$ring = Inset $outline 0.062
$deepBrush = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush $metalDeep
$g.FillPolygon($deepBrush, $ring)
$edgePen = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen $edge, ([single]([math]::Max(1.0, $Size * 0.006)))
$g.DrawPolygon($edgePen, $ring)

$field = Inset $outline 0.082
$g.FillPolygon($metalBrush, $field)
$pin = Inset $outline 0.048
$royalPen = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen ([System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(140, $royal)), ([single]([math]::Max(1.0, $Size * 0.005)))
$g.DrawPolygon($royalPen, $pin)

# The ribbon, sampled through the same cubic as the live mark.
$p0 = U 0.175 0.630; $c1 = U 0.330 0.820; $c2 = U 0.690 0.815; $p1 = U 0.835 0.585
$band = @()
for ($i = 0; $i -le 60; $i++) {
    $t = $i / 60.0
    $u = 1 - $t
    $x = $p0.X * $u * $u * $u + $c1.X * 3 * $u * $u * $t + $c2.X * 3 * $u * $t * $t + $p1.X * $t * $t * $t
    $y = $p0.Y * $u * $u * $u + $c1.Y * 3 * $u * $u * $t + $c2.Y * 3 * $u * $t * $t + $p1.Y * $t * $t * $t
    $band += New-Object System.Drawing.PointF ([single]$x), ([single]$y)
}
$half = $Size * 0.040
$weavePen = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen ([System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(0xff, 0x05, 0x05, 0x06)), ([single]($half * 2 * 1.3))
$weavePen.LineJoin = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LineJoin]::Round
$g.DrawLines($weavePen, $band)
$fillPen = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen $weave, ([single]($half * 2))
$fillPen.LineJoin = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LineJoin]::Round
$g.DrawLines($fillPen, $band)
$hiPen = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen ([System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(200, $weaveHi)), ([single]($half * 0.8))
$hiPen.LineJoin = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LineJoin]::Round
$g.DrawLines($hiPen, $band)

# The monogram: gold face with a royal keyline, W in front of E.
function Glyph([string]$text, [double]$cx, [double]$cy, [double]$em, [double]$dx, [double]$dy) {
    $family = New-Object System.Drawing.FontFamily "Georgia"
    $path = New-Object System.Drawing.Drawing2D.GraphicsPath
    $fmt = [System.Drawing.StringFormat]::GenericTypographic
    $path.AddString($text, $family, [int][System.Drawing.FontStyle]::Bold, [single]($em * $Size), (U $cx $cy), $fmt)
    # Centre the glyph on its own bounds rather than on its advance.
    $b = $path.GetBounds()
    $m = New-Object System.Drawing.Drawing2D.Matrix
    $m.Translate([single](($cx * $Size) + $dx - $b.X - $b.Width / 2), [single](($cy * $Size) + $dy - $b.Y - $b.Height / 2))
    $path.Transform($m)
    return $path
}

$keyline = [single]([math]::Max(1.4, $Size * 0.010))
$ePath = Glyph "E" 0.355 0.455 0.455 0 0
$wPath = Glyph "W" 0.640 0.520 0.505 0 0

$shadowPen = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen ([System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(150, 0, 0, 0)), $keyline
foreach ($path in @($ePath, $wPath)) {
    $m = New-Object System.Drawing.Drawing2D.Matrix
    $m.Translate([single]($Size * 0.012), [single]($Size * 0.016))
    $copy = $path.Clone()
    $copy.Transform($m)
    $g.DrawPath($shadowPen, $copy)
}

$royalOutline = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen $royal, ($keyline * 1.5)
$goldBrush = New-Object System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LinearGradientBrush(
    (U 0 0.25), (U 0 0.65), $goldHi, $gold)
foreach ($path in @($ePath, $wPath)) {
    $g.DrawPath($royalOutline, $path)
    $g.FillPath($goldBrush, $path)
}

$bmp.Save($out, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
$g.Dispose(); $bmp.Dispose()
Write-Output "wrote $out (${Size}x${Size})"
